`crates/jidr-backend/src/crash.rs`:

```rs
//! Crash detection (D9): notice when an emulator dies or stops answering,
//! save its logs, report. Never restarts it.

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::time::Duration;

use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use tokio::time::{sleep, timeout};

use crate::aosp::{self, AospBackend};
use crate::{InstanceInfo, grpc};

/// Consecutive failed heartbeats before a live process counts as hung.
const HEARTBEAT_FAILURES: u32 = 3;
const HEARTBEAT_EVERY: Duration = Duration::from_secs(5);

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum CrashKind {
    /// The process exited without being asked to stop.
    Exited,
    /// The process is alive but gRPC stopped answering.
    Unresponsive,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct CrashReport {
    pub avd: String,
    pub pid: u32,
    pub kind: CrashKind,
    pub reason: String,
    pub exit_code: Option<i32>,
    pub at: DateTime<Utc>,
    /// The saved crash log (reason + the emulator's own log).
    pub log: Option<PathBuf>,
}

impl AospBackend {
    /// Resolves when the instance crashes. The daemon aborts this future
    /// before stopping a device on purpose.
    pub async fn crash_watch(&self, info: &InstanceInfo, log_dir: &Path) -> CrashReport {
        let (kind, exit_code) = self.watch(info).await;
        let reason = match (&kind, exit_code) {
            (CrashKind::Exited, Some(c)) => format!("emulator exited with status {c}"),
            (CrashKind::Exited, None) => {
                "emulator was killed by a signal or disappeared".to_string()
            }
            (CrashKind::Unresponsive, _) => format!(
                "emulator stopped answering gRPC ({} missed heartbeats)",
                HEARTBEAT_FAILURES
            ),
        };
        tracing::warn!(avd = %info.avd, pid = info.pid, %reason, "emulator crashed");
        let at = Utc::now();
        let log = save_crash_log(info, log_dir, &reason, at);
        CrashReport {
            avd: info.avd.clone(),
            pid: info.pid,
            kind,
            reason,
            exit_code,
            at,
            log,
        }
    }

    async fn watch(&self, info: &InstanceInfo) -> (CrashKind, Option<i32>) {
        let mut failures = 0;
        let mut controller = None;
        loop {
            // Process exit: the exit watcher for owned instances, polling otherwise.
            match self.exit_watch(info.pid) {
                Some(mut rx) => {
                    if let Ok(Ok(state)) =
                        timeout(HEARTBEAT_EVERY, rx.wait_for(Option::is_some)).await
                    {
                        let code = (*state).flatten();
                        return (CrashKind::Exited, code);
                    }
                }
                None => {
                    sleep(HEARTBEAT_EVERY).await;
                    if !aosp::process_alive(info.pid).await {
                        return (CrashKind::Exited, None);
                    }
                }
            }
            // Heartbeat.
            if controller.is_none() {
                controller = grpc::connect(info).await.ok().map(|(c, _)| c);
            }
            let ok = match controller.as_mut() {
                Some(c) => timeout(HEARTBEAT_EVERY, c.get_status(()))
                    .await
                    .is_ok_and(|r| r.is_ok()),
                None => false,
            };
            if ok {
                failures = 0;
            } else {
                failures += 1;
                controller = None;
                if failures >= HEARTBEAT_FAILURES && aosp::process_alive(info.pid).await {
                    return (CrashKind::Unresponsive, None);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

fn save_crash_log(
    info: &InstanceInfo,
    log_dir: &Path,
    reason: &str,
    at: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    std::fs::create_dir_all(log_dir).ok()?;
    let path = log_dir.join(format!("crash-{}.log", at.format("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")));
    let emulator_log = info
        .log_path
        .as_ref()
        .and_then(|p| std::fs::read_to_string(p).ok())
        .unwrap_or_else(|| {
            "(no emulator log: the instance was adopted after a daemon restart)".into()
        });
    let text = format!(
        "Jidr crash report\navd: {}\npid: {}\nat: {at}\nreason: {reason}\nemulator log: {}\n\n--- emulator log ---\n{emulator_log}",
        info.avd,
        info.pid,
        info.log_path
            .as_ref()
            .map(|p| p.display().to_string())
            .unwrap_or_default(),
    );
    std::fs::write(&path, text).ok()?;
    Some(path)
}

`crates/jidr-backend/src/discovery.rs`:

```rs
//! The emulator's discovery files (`pid_<pid>.ini`): one per running emulator,
//! holding its ports, AVD and gRPC token.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

/// A parsed discovery file.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Discovery {
    pub path: PathBuf,
    pub pid: u32,
    pub values: HashMap<String, String>,
}

impl Discovery {
    pub fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&str> {
        self.values.get(key).map(String::as_str)
    }

    pub fn grpc_token(&self) -> Option<&str> {
        self.get("grpc.token")
    }

    pub fn grpc_port(&self) -> Option<u16> {
        self.get("grpc.port")?.parse().ok()
    }

    pub fn console_port(&self) -> Option<u16> {
        self.get("port.serial")?.parse().ok()
    }

    pub fn adb_port(&self) -> Option<u16> {
        self.get("port.adb")?.parse().ok()
    }

    pub fn avd_id(&self) -> Option<&str> {
        self.get("avd.id")
    }

    pub fn avd_dir(&self) -> Option<PathBuf> {
        self.get("avd.dir").map(PathBuf::from)
    }

    /// The ports the emulator actually bound.
    pub fn ports(&self) -> Option<crate::Ports> {
        let console = self.console_port()?;
        Some(crate::Ports {
            console,
            adb: self.adb_port().unwrap_or(console + 1),
            grpc: self.grpc_port()?,
        })
    }
}

pub fn parse(path: &Path, text: &str) -> Option<Discovery> {
    let pid = path
        .file_name()?
        .to_str()?
        .strip_prefix("pid_")?
        .strip_suffix(".ini")?
        .parse()
        .ok()?;
    let values = text
        .lines()
        .filter_map(|l| l.split_once('='))
        .map(|(k, v)| (k.trim().to_string(), v.trim().to_string()))
        .collect();
    Some(Discovery {
        path: path.to_path_buf(),
        pid,
        values,
    })
}

/// Directories the emulator may write discovery files to, most likely first.
pub fn discovery_dirs() -> Vec<PathBuf> {
    let mut dirs = Vec::new();
    if let Some(d) = std::env::var_os("JIDR_DISCOVERY_DIR") {
        dirs.push(PathBuf::from(d));
    }
    if cfg!(target_os = "macos") {
        if let Some(h) = dirs::home_dir() {
            dirs.push(h.join("Library/Caches/TemporaryItems/avd/running"));
        }
    } else {
        if let Some(r) = std::env::var_os("XDG_RUNTIME_DIR") {
            dirs.push(PathBuf::from(r).join("avd/running"));
        }
        if let Ok(user) = std::env::var("USER") {
            dirs.push(PathBuf::from(format!("/tmp/android-{user}/avd/running")));
        }
        dirs.push(std::env::temp_dir().join("avd/running"));
    }
    dirs
}

/// All readable discovery files.
pub fn scan() -> Vec<Discovery> {
    discovery_dirs()
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|d| std::fs::read_dir(d).ok())
        .flat_map(|rd| rd.flatten())
        .filter_map(|e| {
            let p = e.path();
            let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&p).ok()?;
            parse(&p, &text)
        })
        .collect()
}

/// The discovery file of the emulator we launched: same pid, or (if the
/// launcher forked) the gRPC port we reserved for it. The console port is not
/// enough: stale files from crashed or foreign emulators reuse it, and the
/// emulator may not even get the console port it asked for.
pub fn find(pid: u32, grpc: u16) -> Option<Discovery> {
    select(scan(), pid, grpc)
}

fn select(found: Vec<Discovery>, pid: u32, grpc: u16) -> Option<Discovery> {
    found
        .into_iter()
        .find(|d| d.pid == pid || d.grpc_port() == Some(grpc))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn parses_a_discovery_file() {
        let text = "emulator.version=35.6.11.0\nport.serial=5554\nport.adb=5555\navd.id=Pixel\ngrpc.port=8554\ngrpc.token=abc==\navd.dir=/x/Pixel.avd\n";
        let d = parse(Path::new("/r/pid_61264.ini"), text).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(d.pid, 61264);
        assert_eq!(d.console_port(), Some(5554));
        assert_eq!(d.adb_port(), Some(5555));
        assert_eq!(d.grpc_port(), Some(8554));
        assert_eq!(
            d.grpc_token(),
            Some("abc=="),
            "base64 padding survives split_once"
        );
        assert_eq!(d.avd_id(), Some("Pixel"));
        assert!(parse(Path::new("/r/other.ini"), text).is_none());
    }

    /// Regression: a stale discovery file with the same console port (left by
    /// Android Studio or a previous boot) was picked, so we used its gRPC token
    /// and the boot never completed.
    #[test]
    fn stale_file_with_same_console_is_ignored() {
        let stale = parse(
            Path::new("/r/pid_100.ini"),
            "port.serial=5554\ngrpc.port=8554\ngrpc.token=old\n",
        )
        .unwrap();
        let ours = parse(
            Path::new("/r/pid_200.ini"),
            "port.serial=5554\ngrpc.port=9100\ngrpc.token=new\n",
        )
        .unwrap();
        let both = || vec![stale.clone(), ours.clone()];
        assert_eq!(select(both(), 200, 9100).unwrap().grpc_token(), Some("new"));
        // Launcher forked (pid differs): our gRPC port still identifies it.
        assert_eq!(select(both(), 999, 9100).unwrap().grpc_token(), Some("new"));
        assert!(select(vec![stale.clone()], 999, 9100).is_none());
    }

    /// Regression: two emulators launched concurrently by different processes
    /// both asked for console 5554; the loser silently bound 5556 and we
    /// talked to the wrong emulator's console. The discovery file's ports win.
    #[test]
    fn actual_ports_come_from_the_discovery_file() {
        let d = parse(
            Path::new("/r/pid_5.ini"),
            "port.serial=5556\nport.adb=5557\ngrpc.port=9100\n",
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            d.ports(),
            Some(crate::Ports {
                console: 5556,
                adb: 5557,
                grpc: 9100
            })
        );
        let partial = parse(Path::new("/r/pid_6.ini"), "port.serial=5558\n").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(partial.ports(), None, "no gRPC port, no instance");
    }
}

`crates/jidr-backend/src/fake.rs`:

```rs
//! An in-memory backend for daemon, client and CLI tests: no emulator, but
//! the same lifecycle, with hooks to hold a start, trigger a crash and see
//! what was launched.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::path::Path;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::Duration;

use async_trait::async_trait;
use chrono::Utc;
use jidr_core::{Cancel, JidrError, JidrResult};
use tokio::sync::{Notify, Semaphore};

use crate::crash::{CrashKind, CrashReport};
use crate::{Backend, BootProgress, BootStage, InstanceInfo, LaunchOptions, LaunchSpec};

#[derive(Debug, Default)]
struct FakeState {
    next: u16,
    running: HashMap<u32, String>,
    crashes: HashMap<u32, Arc<Notify>>,
    launches: Vec<(String, LaunchOptions)>,
    specs: Vec<LaunchSpec>,
    fail_next: Option<JidrError>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct FakeBackend {
    state: Mutex<FakeState>,
    gate: Mutex<Option<Arc<Semaphore>>>,
}

impl FakeBackend {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }

    fn lock(&self) -> std::sync::MutexGuard<'_, FakeState> {
        self.state.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
    }

    /// From now on each start waits for one permit: `gate.add_permits(1)`.
    pub fn gate_starts(&self) -> Arc<Semaphore> {
        let sem = Arc::new(Semaphore::new(0));
        *self.gate.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) = Some(sem.clone());
        sem
    }

    /// The next start fails with `err`.
    pub fn fail_next_start(&self, err: JidrError) {
        self.lock().fail_next = Some(err);
    }

    /// Simulates the emulator `pid` dying.
    pub fn crash(&self, pid: u32) {
        let mut s = self.lock();
        s.running.remove(&pid);
        if let Some(n) = s.crashes.get(&pid) {
            n.notify_one();
        }
    }

    /// Every start so far: AVD and options.
    pub fn launches(&self) -> Vec<(String, LaunchOptions)> {
        self.lock().launches.clone()
    }

    /// Every start so far: what the daemon asked to launch.
    pub fn specs(&self) -> Vec<LaunchSpec> {
        self.lock().specs.clone()
    }

    pub fn running(&self) -> Vec<u32> {
        self.lock().running.keys().copied().collect()
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl Backend for FakeBackend {
    async fn start(
        &self,
        spec: &LaunchSpec,
        opts: &LaunchOptions,
        progress: BootProgress<'_>,
        cancel: &Cancel,
    ) -> JidrResult<InstanceInfo> {
        {
            let mut s = self.lock();
            if s.running.values().any(|a| a == &spec.avd) {
                return Err(JidrError::busy(format!("{} is already running", spec.avd)));
            }
            s.launches.push((spec.avd.clone(), opts.clone()));
            s.specs.push(spec.clone());
            if let Some(err) = s.fail_next.take() {
                return Err(err);
            }
        }
        progress(BootStage::Spawned);
        let gate = self.gate.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).clone();
        if let Some(gate) = gate {
            loop {
                cancel.check()?;
                if let Ok(Ok(permit)) =
                    tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_millis(50), gate.acquire()).await
                {
                    permit.forget();
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        cancel.check()?;
        for stage in [
            BootStage::GrpcReady,
            BootStage::AdbOnline,
            BootStage::Booted,
        ] {
            progress(stage);
        }
        let mut s = self.lock();
        s.next += 1;
        let pid = 4_000_000 + u32::from(s.next);
        let console = 5554 + 2 * s.next;
        s.running.insert(pid, spec.avd.clone());
        s.crashes.insert(pid, Arc::new(Notify::new()));
        Ok(InstanceInfo {
            avd: spec.avd.clone(),
            pid,
            console_port: console,
            adb_port: console + 1,
            grpc_port: 20_000 + s.next,
            adb_serial: format!("emulator-{console}"),
            grpc_token: format!("fake-token-{pid}"),
            started_at: Utc::now(),
            log_path: None,
        })
    }

    async fn stop(&self, instance: &InstanceInfo) -> JidrResult<()> {
        self.lock().running.remove(&instance.pid);
        Ok(())
    }

    async fn is_alive(&self, instance: &InstanceInfo) -> bool {
        self.lock().running.contains_key(&instance.pid)
    }

    async fn adopt(&self, _avd_home: &Path) -> Vec<InstanceInfo> {
        Vec::new()
    }

    async fn wait_for_crash(&self, instance: &InstanceInfo, _log_dir: &Path) -> CrashReport {
        let notify = self.lock().crashes.get(&instance.pid).cloned();
        match notify {
            Some(n) => n.notified().await,
            None => std::future::pending::<()>().await,
        }
        CrashReport {
            avd: instance.avd.clone(),
            pid: instance.pid,
            kind: CrashKind::Exited,
            reason: "fake crash".into(),
            exit_code: Some(139),
            at: Utc::now(),
            log: None,
        }
    }
}

`crates/jidr-backend/src/grpc.rs`:

```rs
//! Authenticated gRPC clients for a running emulator.

use std::time::Duration;

use jidr_core::{ErrorCode, JidrError, JidrResult, ResultExt};
use jidr_proto::{BearerToken, Controller, Snapshots};
use tonic::transport::Endpoint;

use crate::InstanceInfo;

/// Connects to `127.0.0.1:<port>` with the bearer token.
pub async fn connect_port(port: u16, token: &str) -> JidrResult<(Controller, Snapshots)> {
    let token = BearerToken::new(token).ctx(ErrorCode::Unexpected, "invalid gRPC token")?;
    let channel = Endpoint::from_shared(format!("http://127.0.0.1:{port}"))
        .ctx(ErrorCode::Unexpected, "gRPC endpoint")?
        .connect_timeout(Duration::from_secs(5))
        .tcp_nodelay(true)
        .connect()
        .await
        .map_err(|e| JidrError::sdk(format!("cannot reach emulator gRPC on port {port}: {e}")))?;
    Ok(jidr_proto::clients(channel, token))
}

pub async fn connect(instance: &InstanceInfo) -> JidrResult<(Controller, Snapshots)> {
    connect_port(instance.grpc_port, &instance.grpc_token).await
}

/// Maps a gRPC status to a Jidr error.
pub fn status_error(what: &str, s: tonic::Status) -> JidrError {
    let code = match s.code() {
        tonic::Code::NotFound => ErrorCode::NotFound,
        tonic::Code::InvalidArgument => ErrorCode::Usage,
        tonic::Code::Unavailable | tonic::Code::DeadlineExceeded => ErrorCode::Sdk,
        _ => ErrorCode::Sdk,
    };
    JidrError::new(code, format!("{what}: {}", s.message()))
        .with_data(serde_json::json!({"grpc_code": format!("{:?}", s.code())}))
}

//! Backend trait and the AOSP emulator backend (spawn, discovery, gRPC/console
//! clients, ports, boot wait, crash detection).

pub mod adopt;
pub mod aosp;
pub mod console;
pub mod crash;
pub mod discovery;

/// What to launch.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct LaunchSpec {
    /// AVD id.
    pub avd: String,
    /// `ANDROID_AVD_HOME` (Jidr's own AVD home).
    pub avd_home: PathBuf,
    /// `ANDROID_SDK_ROOT`: the SDK holding the system image.
    pub sdk_root: PathBuf,
    /// The system image directory, passed as `-sysdir`. The emulator from
    /// Android Studio's SDK rejects Jidr's private SDK as `ANDROID_SDK_ROOT`
    /// ("Broken AVD system path") when it holds only system images, so the
    /// image is always named explicitly.
    pub sysdir: PathBuf,
    /// The `emulator` binary.
    pub emulator: PathBuf,
    /// The `adb` binary.
    pub adb: PathBuf,
    /// Directory for per-boot emulator logs.
    pub log_dir: PathBuf,
}

/// How to launch. `ramdisk` is the hook the root engine uses for Magisk.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct LaunchOptions {
    /// Extra emulator arguments, appended last.
    pub extra_args: Vec<String>,
    /// `-ramdisk <path>`: boot a patched per-device ramdisk.
    pub ramdisk: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// `-no-snapshot-load`: ignore the quick-boot snapshot.
    pub cold_boot: bool,
    /// `-wipe-data`.
    pub wipe: bool,
    /// `-gpu` mode; `None` = `host` on macOS (ADR-0001), `swiftshader_indirect` elsewhere.
    pub gpu: Option<String>,
    /// `-camera-back`: `emulated`, `virtualscene`, `none` or `webcamN` (R7, D36).
    pub camera_back: Option<String>,
    /// `-camera-front`: same values.
    pub camera_front: Option<String>,
    /// Guest audio to the host; `false` adds `-no-audio`.
    pub audio: bool,
    /// Save the quick-boot snapshot when stopped (D29); `false` adds `-no-snapshot-save`.
    pub snapshot_save: bool,
    pub boot_timeout: Duration,
}

    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            extra_args: Vec::new(),
            ramdisk: None,
            camera_back: None,
            camera_front: None,
            cold_boot: false,
            wipe: false,
            gpu: None,
            audio: true,
            snapshot_save: true,
            boot_timeout: Duration::from_secs(300),
        }
    }

/// A valid `-camera-back` / `-camera-front` value.
pub fn valid_camera(v: &str) -> bool {
    matches!(v, "emulated" | "virtualscene" | "none")
        || v.strip_prefix("webcam")
            .is_some_and(|n| !n.is_empty() && n.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()))
}

pub fn default_gpu() -> &'static str {
    if cfg!(target_os = "macos") {
        "host"
    } else {
        "swiftshader_indirect"
    }

/// Boot progress, reported as it happens.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum BootStage {
    Spawned,
    GrpcReady,
    AdbOnline,
    Booted,
}

impl BootStage {
    /// Rough progress for job reporting.
    pub fn progress(self) -> f32 {
        match self {
            Self::Spawned => 0.1,
            Self::GrpcReady => 0.3,
            Self::AdbOnline => 0.5,
            Self::Booted => 1.0,
        }
    }
}

/// A running emulator instance.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct InstanceInfo {
    pub avd: String,
    pub pid: u32,
    pub console_port: u16,
    pub adb_port: u16,
    pub grpc_port: u16,
    pub adb_serial: String,
    /// Bearer token for gRPC (`-grpc-use-token`). Never logged.
    pub grpc_token: String,
    pub started_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    /// The emulator's stdout/stderr log for this boot (`None` when adopted).
    pub log_path: Option<PathBuf>,
}

impl InstanceInfo {
    pub fn ports(&self) -> Ports {
        Ports {
            console: self.console_port,
            adb: self.adb_port,
            grpc: self.grpc_port,
        }
    }

    pub fn runtime(&self) -> DeviceRuntime {
        DeviceRuntime {
            pid: self.pid,
            console_port: self.console_port,
            adb_serial: self.adb_serial.clone(),
            grpc_port: self.grpc_port,
            started_at: self.started_at,
        }
    }
}

pub type BootProgress<'a> = &'a (dyn Fn(BootStage) + Send + Sync);

/// A device backend. Object-safe so the daemon can run against a fake.
#[async_trait]
pub trait Backend: Send + Sync + std::fmt::Debug {
    /// Launches and waits until the device has booted.
    async fn start(
        &self,
        spec: &LaunchSpec,
        opts: &LaunchOptions,
        progress: BootProgress<'_>,
        cancel: &Cancel,
    ) -> JidrResult<InstanceInfo>;

    /// Shuts the device down gracefully (saving the quick-boot snapshot when
    /// it was launched with `snapshot_save`), killing it if it hangs.
    async fn stop(&self, instance: &InstanceInfo) -> JidrResult<()>;

    /// True if the instance's process is still running.
    async fn is_alive(&self, instance: &InstanceInfo) -> bool;

    /// Emulators still running Jidr AVDs under `avd_home` (daemon restart).
    async fn adopt(&self, avd_home: &Path) -> Vec<InstanceInfo>;

    /// Resolves when the instance crashes (D9: report, never restart).
    async fn wait_for_crash(&self, instance: &InstanceInfo, log_dir: &Path) -> CrashReport;
}

`crates/jidr-backend/src/ports.rs`:

```rs
//! Port allocation (D9: dynamic, no cap). Console ports are even and the adb
//! port is console + 1. adb auto-discovers consoles 5554–5584; beyond that the
//! device is reached with `adb connect 127.0.0.1:<adb>`.

use std::collections::HashSet;
use std::net::TcpListener;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

use jidr_core::{JidrError, JidrResult};

pub const FIRST_CONSOLE: u16 = 5554;
/// Last console port adb scans by itself.
pub const LAST_AUTO_CONSOLE: u16 = 5584;
/// Upper bound of our search (not a device cap: ~220 pairs).
pub const LAST_CONSOLE: u16 = 5998;

/// Ports for one emulator instance.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Ports {
    pub console: u16,
    pub adb: u16,
    pub grpc: u16,
}

impl Ports {
    /// True if adb finds this instance without `adb connect`.
    pub fn auto_discovered(&self) -> bool {
        self.console <= LAST_AUTO_CONSOLE
    }

    /// The adb serial for this instance.
    pub fn adb_serial(&self) -> String {
        if self.auto_discovered() {
            format!("emulator-{}", self.console)
        } else {
            format!("127.0.0.1:{}", self.adb)
        }
    }
}

/// Hands out free ports and remembers them until released, so two
/// concurrent starts in the same daemon never race for a pair.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct PortAllocator {
    reserved: Arc<Mutex<HashSet<u16>>>,
}

fn free(port: u16) -> bool {
    TcpListener::bind(("127.0.0.1", port)).is_ok()
}

impl PortAllocator {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }

    pub fn allocate(&self) -> JidrResult<Ports> {
        self.allocate_avoiding(&HashSet::new())
    }

    /// Like `allocate`, also skipping `in_use` (ports live emulators hold
    /// according to their discovery files: a bind test on 127.0.0.1 can
    /// miss a port bound on another address).
    pub fn allocate_avoiding(&self, in_use: &HashSet<u16>) -> JidrResult<Ports> {
        let mut reserved = self.reserved.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        let console = (FIRST_CONSOLE..=LAST_CONSOLE)
            .step_by(2)
            .find(|p| {
                ![*p, p + 1]
                    .iter()
                    .any(|q| reserved.contains(q) || in_use.contains(q))
                    && free(*p)
                    && free(p + 1)
            })
            .ok_or_else(|| JidrError::busy("no free emulator console port pair"))?;
        let grpc = (0..20)
            .find_map(|_| {
                let p = TcpListener::bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
                    .ok()?
                    .local_addr()
                    .ok()?
                    .port();
                (!reserved.contains(&p) && p != console && p != console + 1).then_some(p)
            })
            .ok_or_else(|| JidrError::busy("no free gRPC port"))?;
        reserved.extend([console, console + 1, grpc]);
        Ok(Ports {
            console,
            adb: console + 1,
            grpc,
        })
    }

    /// Reserves ports already used by an adopted instance.
    pub fn claim(&self, ports: Ports) {
        let mut reserved = self.reserved.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        reserved.extend([ports.console, ports.adb, ports.grpc]);
    }

    pub fn release(&self, ports: Ports) {
        let mut reserved = self.reserved.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        for p in [ports.console, ports.adb, ports.grpc] {
            reserved.remove(&p);
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn allocations_are_distinct_until_released() {
        let a = PortAllocator::new();
        let p1 = a.allocate().unwrap();
        let p2 = a.allocate().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(p1.console % 2, 0);
        assert_eq!(p1.adb, p1.console + 1);
        assert_ne!(p1.console, p2.console);
        assert_ne!(p1.grpc, p2.grpc);
        a.release(p1);
        let p3 = a.allocate().unwrap();
        assert_ne!(
            p3.console, p2.console,
            "still-reserved pair is never handed out"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn skips_busy_ports() {
        let a = PortAllocator::new();
        let first = a.allocate().unwrap();
        // Hold the port before releasing the reservation, so other test
        // processes can't race us for it.
        let Ok(_hold) = TcpListener::bind(("127.0.0.1", first.console)) else {
            return;
        };
        a.release(first);
        assert_ne!(a.allocate().unwrap().console, first.console);
    }

    /// Regression: two leaked emulators both asked for console 5554; ports
    /// a live emulator reports in its discovery file are skipped.
    #[test]
    fn skips_ports_live_emulators_hold() {
        let a = PortAllocator::new();
        let first = a.allocate().unwrap();
        a.release(first);
        let held: HashSet<u16> = [first.console].into();
        assert_ne!(a.allocate_avoiding(&held).unwrap().console, first.console);
    }

    #[test]
    fn serials_past_adb_scan_range_use_tcp() {
        let low = Ports {
            console: 5554,
            adb: 5555,
            grpc: 1,
        };
        let high = Ports {
            console: 5586,
            adb: 5587,
            grpc: 1,
        };
        assert_eq!(low.adb_serial(), "emulator-5554");
        assert!(!high.auto_discovered());
        assert_eq!(high.adb_serial(), "127.0.0.1:5587");
    }
}

`crates/jidr-backend/src/testing.rs`:

```rs
//! Emulator cleanup for tests that boot real emulators. Not used by the
//! product: there, emulators outlive the daemon on purpose (re-adoption).
//!
//! Three layers, so no test leaves an emulator behind whatever happens:
//! 1. [`AvdGuard`]: kills the AVD's emulator when dropped (pass, failure, panic).
//! 2. A reaper process per test process, in its own process group: when the
//!    test process dies (SIGKILL, Ctrl-C, nextest timeout, where `Drop` never
//!    runs) it kills every emulator whose AVD the test registered.
//! 3. [`kill_orphans`]: at startup, kills orphaned emulators (parent gone)
//!    left by earlier runs of test AVDs with a given prefix.
//!
//! Test AVD names carry the test process id ([`unique_avd`]) so a cleanup
//! never touches another run's emulators.

use std::io::Write;
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::process::{Command, Stdio};
use std::sync::OnceLock;

/// `<base>-<pid>`: an AVD name unique to this test process.
pub fn unique_avd(base: &str) -> String {
    format!("{base}-{}", std::process::id())
}

/// Pids of processes running AVD `avd` (`-avd <avd>` in their command line:
/// the `emulator` launcher or qemu). Test AVD names are unique per process,
/// so an exact match can't hit anyone else's emulator.
fn emulator_pids(avd: &str) -> Vec<u32> {
    let Ok(out) = Command::new("ps").args(["-axo", "pid=,command="]).output() else {
        return Vec::new();
    };
    String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout)
        .lines()
        .filter_map(|l| {
            let mut parts = l.split_whitespace();
            let pid: u32 = parts.next()?.parse().ok()?;
            let args: Vec<&str> = parts.collect();
            args.windows(2)
                .any(|w| w[0] == "-avd" && w[1] == avd)
                .then_some(pid)
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Kills every emulator running `avd` (SIGKILL: tests don't need a snapshot).
pub fn kill_avd(avd: &str) {
    for pid in emulator_pids(avd) {
        let _ = Command::new("kill").args(["-9", &pid.to_string()]).status();
    }
}

/// Kills orphaned emulators (reparented to launchd/init) whose AVD starts
/// with `prefix`: leftovers of earlier, killed test runs.
pub fn kill_orphans(prefix: &str) -> usize {
    let Ok(out) = Command::new("ps")
        .args(["-axo", "pid=,ppid=,command="])
        .output()
    else {
        return 0;
    };
    let mut killed = 0;
    for l in String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout).lines() {
        let mut parts = l.split_whitespace();
        let (Some(pid), Some(ppid)) = (parts.next(), parts.next()) else {
            continue;
        };
        let args: Vec<&str> = parts.collect();
        let orphan = ppid == "1";
        let emulator = args.first().is_some_and(|c| c.contains("qemu-system"));
        let ours = args
            .windows(2)
            .any(|w| w[0] == "-avd" && w[1].starts_with(prefix));
        if orphan
            && emulator
            && ours
            && Command::new("kill")
                .args(["-9", pid])
                .status()
                .is_ok_and(|s| s.success())
        {
            killed += 1;
        }
    }
    killed
}

struct Reaper {
    list: PathBuf,
}

/// Starts (once per process) the watcher that cleans up after this process.
fn reaper() -> Option<&'static Reaper> {
    static REAPER: OnceLock<Option<Reaper>> = OnceLock::new();
    REAPER
        .get_or_init(|| {
            let me = std::process::id();
            let list = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("jidr-test-reaper-{me}.avds"));
            std::fs::write(&list, "").ok()?;
            // Waits for this process to exit, then kills the listed AVDs'
            // emulators by exact `-avd <name>` match.
            let script = format!(
                r#"while kill -0 {me} 2>/dev/null; do sleep 2; done
while IFS= read -r avd; do
  [ -n "$avd" ] || continue
  ps -axo pid=,command= | awk -v a="$avd" '{{ for (i = 2; i < NF; i++) if ($i == "-avd" && $(i+1) == a) print $1 }}' | xargs kill -9 2>/dev/null
done < "{list}"
rm -f "{list}""#,
                list = list.display()
            );
            let mut cmd = Command::new("sh");
            cmd.args(["-c", &script]).stdin(Stdio::null()).stdout(Stdio::null()).stderr(Stdio::null());
            #[cfg(unix)]
            {
                use std::os::unix::process::CommandExt;
                // Its own process group: a Ctrl-C to the test run doesn't kill it.
                cmd.process_group(0);
            }
            cmd.spawn().ok()?;
            Some(Reaper { list })
        })
        .as_ref()
}

/// Ensures `avd`'s emulator dies with the test: on drop, and via the reaper
/// if the test process is killed.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct AvdGuard {
    avd: String,
}

impl AvdGuard {
    pub fn new(avd: &str) -> Self {
        if let Some(r) = reaper()
            && let Ok(mut f) = std::fs::OpenOptions::new().append(true).open(&r.list)
        {
            let _ = writeln!(f, "{avd}");
        }
        Self {
            avd: avd.to_string(),
        }
    }
}

impl Drop for AvdGuard {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        kill_avd(&self.avd);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// A stand-in process with `-avd <name>` in its command line dies when
    /// its guard drops.
    #[test]
    fn guard_kills_its_avd_on_drop() {
        let avd = unique_avd("jidr_guard_test");
        let mut child = Command::new("sh")
            .args(["-c", "sleep 300; :", "emulator", "-avd", &avd])
            .stdout(Stdio::null())
            .stderr(Stdio::null())
            .spawn()
            .unwrap();
        std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(300));
        assert_eq!(emulator_pids(&avd), vec![child.id()]);
        drop(AvdGuard::new(&avd));
        std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(300));
        assert!(child.try_wait().unwrap().is_some(), "the guard killed it");
        assert!(emulator_pids(&avd).is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn unique_names_carry_the_pid() {
        assert!(unique_avd("x").ends_with(&std::process::id().to_string()));
    }
}

#![allow(dead_code)]

pub struct Fixture {

    pub paths: JidrPaths,
    pub avds: AvdManager,
    pub image_sdk: Sdk,

/// Creates AVD `<base>-<pid>` and a launch spec for it. Orphaned emulators
/// of earlier, killed runs are cleaned up first.

    jidr_backend::testing::kill_orphans(&format!("{base}-"));
    let name_owned = jidr_backend::testing::unique_avd(base);
    let name = name_owned.as_str();

        name: name.into(),

        overrides: Default::default(),

    let spec = LaunchSpec {
        avd: name.into(),
        avd_home: paths.avd_home(),
        sdk_root: image_sdk.root.clone(),
        sysdir: image_sdk.image_dir(&test_image()),
        emulator: tools.emulator(),

        log_dir: paths.device_logs(name),

        avds,
        image_sdk,

`crates/jidr-backend/tests/launch_emulator.rs`:

```rs
//! Boots a real emulator: battery over gRPC, stop with a quick-boot snapshot,
//! cold boot with a custom `-ramdisk` through `LaunchOptions`, quick boot.
#![cfg(feature = "emulator")]
#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]

mod common;

use std::sync::Mutex;
use std::time::Instant;

use jidr_backend::{AospBackend, Backend, BootStage, LaunchOptions, grpc};
use jidr_core::Cancel;
use jidr_sdk::ConfigIni;

#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
async fn boot_battery_stop_ramdisk_quickboot() {
    let f = common::fixture("jidr_backend_e2e");
    let (spec, avds) = (&f.spec, &f.avds);
    let quiet = LaunchOptions {
        audio: false,
        ..Default::default()
    };
    let backend = AospBackend::new();

    // 1. First boot.
    let stages = Mutex::new(Vec::new());
    let t = Instant::now();
    let inst = backend
        .start(
            spec,
            &quiet,
            &|s| stages.lock().unwrap().push(s),
            &Cancel::new(),
        )
        .await
        .unwrap();
    println!("first boot: {:.1} s", t.elapsed().as_secs_f64());
    assert_eq!(
        *stages.lock().unwrap(),
        vec![
            BootStage::Spawned,
            BootStage::GrpcReady,
            BootStage::AdbOnline,
            BootStage::Booted
        ]
    );
    assert!(backend.is_alive(&inst).await);

    // 2. Battery over gRPC.
    let (mut ctl, _) = grpc::connect(&inst).await.unwrap();
    let battery = ctl.get_battery(()).await.unwrap().into_inner();
    assert!(battery.has_battery);
    assert!((0..=100).contains(&battery.charge_level), "{battery:?}");

    // 3. Graceful stop saves the quick-boot snapshot (D29).
    backend.stop(&inst).await.unwrap();
    assert!(!backend.is_alive(&inst).await);
    let snap = avds.dir(&spec.avd).join("snapshots/default_boot");
    assert!(
        snap.is_dir(),
        "quick-boot snapshot missing at {}",
        snap.display()
    );

    // 4. Cold boot with a custom ramdisk via LaunchOptions (the root engine's hook).
    let custom = f.tmp.path().join("custom-ramdisk.img");
    std::fs::copy(
        f.image_sdk
            .image_dir(&common::test_image())
            .join("ramdisk.img"),
        &custom,
    )
    .unwrap();
    let opts = LaunchOptions {
        ramdisk: Some(custom.clone()),
        cold_boot: true,
        camera_back: Some("emulated".into()),
        ..quiet.clone()
    };
    let inst = backend
        .start(spec, &opts, &|_| {}, &Cancel::new())
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let hw = ConfigIni::read(&avds.dir(&spec.avd).join("hardware-qemu.ini")).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        hw.get("hw.camera.back"),
        Some("emulated"),
        "camera option applied (R7)"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        hw.get("disk.ramdisk.path"),
        Some(custom.to_str().unwrap()),
        "emulator used our ramdisk"
    );
    backend.stop(&inst).await.unwrap();

    // 5. Quick boot from the snapshot.
    let t = Instant::now();
    let inst = backend
        .start(
            spec,
            &quiet,
            &|s| println!("  quick boot {s:?} at {:.1} s", t.elapsed().as_secs_f64()),
            &Cancel::new(),
        )
        .await
        .unwrap();
    println!("quick boot: {:.1} s", t.elapsed().as_secs_f64());
    backend.stop(&inst).await.unwrap();

    assert!(
        !avds.is_running(&spec.avd),
        "stopped AVD must not look locked"
    );
    avds.delete(&spec.avd).unwrap();
}

`crates/jidr-backend/tests/resilience_emulator.rs`:

```rs
//! Resilience on a real emulator: double launch refused, console commands,
//! re-adoption by a fresh backend (daemon restart), crash detection.
#![cfg(feature = "emulator")]
#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]

mod common;

use std::time::Duration;

use jidr_backend::console::{self, GsmLine};
use jidr_backend::{AospBackend, Backend, Console, CrashKind, LaunchOptions};
use jidr_core::{Cancel, ErrorCode};

#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
async fn double_launch_console_adopt_crash() {
    let f = common::fixture("jidr_resilience");
    let quiet = LaunchOptions {
        audio: false,
        snapshot_save: false,
        ..Default::default()
    };
    let backend = AospBackend::new();
    let inst = backend
        .start(&f.spec, &quiet, &|_| {}, &Cancel::new())
        .await
        .unwrap();

    // Cleanup check: a deliberately failing run must not leak its emulator.
    assert!(
        std::env::var_os("JIDR_TEST_FAIL_AFTER_BOOT").is_none(),
        "deliberate failure after boot (JIDR_TEST_FAIL_AFTER_BOOT)"
    );

    // Double launch refused while it runs.
    let err = backend
        .start(&f.spec, &quiet, &|_| {}, &Cancel::new())
        .await
        .unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(err.code, ErrorCode::Busy, "{err}");

    // Telnet console.
    let token = console::default_token_path();
    let mut c = Console::connect(inst.console_port, token.as_deref())
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(c.avd_name().await.unwrap(), f.spec.avd);
    c.network_speed("edge").await.unwrap();
    c.network_delay("gprs").await.unwrap();
    c.gsm_signal(10, None).await.unwrap();
    c.gsm_state(GsmLine::Data, "roaming").await.unwrap();
    c.power_ac(false).await.unwrap();
    drop(c);

    // A fresh backend (daemon restart) re-adopts the running emulator.
    let restarted = AospBackend::new();
    let adopted = restarted.adopt_running(&f.paths.avd_home()).await;
    let again = adopted
        .iter()
        .find(|i| i.pid == inst.pid)
        .expect("instance re-adopted");
    assert_eq!(again.grpc_port, inst.grpc_port);
    assert_eq!(again.grpc_token, inst.grpc_token);
    assert_eq!(again.adb_serial, inst.adb_serial);
    assert!(restarted.is_alive(again).await);

    // Crash: kill -9 behind the backend's back.
    let crash_dir = f.paths.device_logs(&f.spec.avd);
    let watcher = {
        let (inst, dir) = (inst.clone(), crash_dir.clone());
        tokio::spawn(async move { backend.crash_watch(&inst, &dir).await })
    };
    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(1)).await;
    std::process::Command::new("kill")
        .args(["-9", &inst.pid.to_string()])
        .status()
        .unwrap();
    let report = tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(30), watcher)
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(report.kind, CrashKind::Exited);
    assert_eq!(report.pid, inst.pid);
    let log = report.log.expect("crash log saved");
    let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&log).unwrap();
    assert!(text.contains("reason: emulator was killed"), "{text}");
    assert!(text.contains("--- emulator log ---"));
    println!("crash report: {} ({})", report.reason, log.display());

    // The adopted path (no exit watcher) also notices the death.
    let adopted_report = tokio::time::timeout(
        Duration::from_secs(30),
        restarted.crash_watch(again, &crash_dir),
    )
    .await
    .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(adopted_report.kind, CrashKind::Exited);

    f.avds.delete(&f.spec.avd).unwrap();
}

`crates/jidr-client/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! Jidr daemon protocol client used by the CLI, the GUI and the MCP server.
//!
//! ```no_run
//! # async fn demo() -> jidr_core::JidrResult<()> {
//! let paths = jidr_core::JidrPaths::discover()?;
//! let client = jidr_client::Client::connect_or_spawn(&paths, "cli", &Default::default()).await?;
//! let devices = client.call("device.list", serde_json::json!({})).await?;
//! let booted = client.run("device.start", serde_json::json!({"device": "Phone"}), |_| {}).await?;
//! # Ok(()) }
//! ```

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::process::Stdio;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};
use std::time::Duration;

use jidr_core::rpc::{EVENT_METHOD, Event, HelloResult, Response, RpcError};
use jidr_core::{ErrorCode, JidrError, JidrPaths, JidrResult, Job, JobState, ResultExt};
use serde::Serialize;
use serde::de::DeserializeOwned;
use serde_json::{Value, json};
use tokio::io::{AsyncBufReadExt, AsyncWriteExt, BufReader};
use tokio::net::UnixStream;
use tokio::net::unix::OwnedWriteHalf;
use tokio::sync::{Mutex, broadcast, oneshot};
use tokio::task::JoinHandle;
use uuid::Uuid;

/// The client version sent in `hello`; must equal the daemon's.
pub const VERSION: &str = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION");
/// How long to wait for a freshly spawned daemon's socket.
const SPAWN_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(15);

type Pending = Arc<std::sync::Mutex<HashMap<u64, oneshot::Sender<Response>>>>;

/// How to start the daemon when none is running (D4: on demand).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct SpawnOptions {
    /// The `jidr` binary. Default: `$JIDR_DAEMON_BIN`, then the `jidr` shipped
    /// with the current executable ([`bundled_jidr`]), then `jidr` on `PATH`.
    pub program: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// Replace a daemon of another version instead of failing with `daemon_stale`.
    pub restart_stale: bool,
    /// How long to wait for a spawned daemon (default 15 s).
    pub timeout: Option<Duration>,
}

impl SpawnOptions {
    pub fn program(&self) -> PathBuf {
        if let Some(p) = &self.program {
            return p.clone();
        }
        if let Some(p) = std::env::var_os("JIDR_DAEMON_BIN") {
            return PathBuf::from(p);
        }
        std::env::current_exe()
            .ok()
            .and_then(|exe| bundled_jidr(&exe))
            .unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from("jidr"))
    }
}

/// The `jidr` binary shipped with `exe`: `Contents/Helpers/jidr` in the macOS
/// app bundle, else a `jidr` next to it. Never `exe` itself: on the default
/// case-insensitive APFS volume, `Jidr.app/Contents/MacOS/jidr` *is* the GUI
/// `MacOS/Jidr`, and spawning the GUI as the daemon makes every copy spawn
/// another one.
pub fn bundled_jidr(exe: &Path) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    let dir = exe.parent()?;
    [dir.join("../Helpers/jidr"), dir.join("jidr")]
        .into_iter()
        .find(|p| p.is_file() && !same_file(p, exe))
}

/// Whether two paths name the same file on disk (case aliases included).
#[cfg(unix)]
fn same_file(a: &Path, b: &Path) -> bool {
    use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;
    match (std::fs::metadata(a), std::fs::metadata(b)) {
        (Ok(a), Ok(b)) => a.dev() == b.dev() && a.ino() == b.ino(),
        _ => false,
    }
}

#[cfg(not(unix))]
fn same_file(a: &Path, b: &Path) -> bool {
    matches!((std::fs::canonicalize(a), std::fs::canonicalize(b)), (Ok(a), Ok(b)) if a == b)
}

pub struct Client {
    writer: Mutex<OwnedWriteHalf>,
    pending: Pending,
    events: broadcast::Sender<Event>,
    next: AtomicU64,
    reader: JoinHandle<()>,
    hello: HelloResult,
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for Client {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("Client")
            .field("daemon", &self.hello)
            .finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

impl Drop for Client {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.reader.abort();
    }
}

fn is_unavailable(e: &std::io::Error) -> bool {
    matches!(
        e.kind(),
        std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound | std::io::ErrorKind::ConnectionRefused
    )
}

impl Client {
    /// Connects to a running daemon and says hello.
    pub async fn connect(socket: &Path, client: &str) -> JidrResult<Self> {
        let stream = UnixStream::connect(socket).await.map_err(|e| {
            JidrError::new(
                ErrorCode::Unexpected,
                format!("no Jidr daemon at {}: {e}", socket.display()),
            )
            .with_data(json!({ "unavailable": is_unavailable(&e) }))
        })?;
        Self::handshake(stream, client).await
    }

    async fn handshake(stream: UnixStream, client: &str) -> JidrResult<Self> {
        let (r, w) = stream.into_split();
        let pending: Pending = Arc::default();
        let (events, _) = broadcast::channel(1024);
        let reader = tokio::spawn(read_loop(
            BufReader::new(r),
            pending.clone(),
            events.clone(),
        ));
        let mut c = Self {
            writer: Mutex::new(w),
            pending,
            events,
            next: AtomicU64::new(1),
            reader,
            hello: HelloResult {
                version: String::new(),
                protocol: String::new(),
                pid: 0,
            },
        };
        let hello = c
            .call("hello", json!({ "version": VERSION, "client": client }))
            .await?;
        c.hello = serde_json::from_value(hello).ctx(ErrorCode::Unexpected, "bad hello reply")?;
        Ok(c)
    }

    /// Connects, starting the daemon first if none is running. With
    /// `restart_stale`, a daemon of another version is asked to exit and
    /// replaced (its running emulators are re-adopted by the new one).
    pub async fn connect_or_spawn(
        paths: &JidrPaths,
        client: &str,
        opts: &SpawnOptions,
    ) -> JidrResult<Self> {
        let socket = paths.socket();
        match Self::connect(&socket, client).await {
            Ok(c) => return Ok(c),
            Err(e) if e.code == ErrorCode::DaemonStale && opts.restart_stale => {
                shutdown_daemon(&socket).await?;
            }
            Err(e) if is_unavailable_err(&e) => {}
            Err(e) => return Err(e),
        }
        spawn_daemon(paths, opts)?;
        let wait = opts.timeout.unwrap_or(SPAWN_TIMEOUT);
        let deadline = tokio::time::Instant::now() + wait;
        loop {
            match Self::connect(&socket, client).await {
                Ok(c) => return Ok(c),
                Err(e) if !is_unavailable_err(&e) => return Err(e),
                Err(_) if tokio::time::Instant::now() >= deadline => {
                    return Err(JidrError::unexpected(format!(
                        "the Jidr daemon did not start within {} s; see {}",
                        wait.as_secs(),
                        paths.logs.join("daemon.log").display()
                    )));
                }
                Err(_) => tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100)).await,
            }
        }
    }

    /// What the daemon said in `hello`.
    pub fn daemon(&self) -> &HelloResult {
        &self.hello
    }

    /// Calls a method; JSON-RPC errors become `JidrError`s with their code.
    pub async fn call(&self, method: &str, params: Value) -> JidrResult<Value> {
        let id = self.next.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
        let (tx, rx) = oneshot::channel();
        self.pending
            .lock()
            .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
            .insert(id, tx);
        let req = json!({ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": id, "method": method, "params": params });
        let mut line =
            serde_json::to_string(&req).ctx(ErrorCode::Unexpected, "encoding request")?;
        line.push('\n');
        {
            let mut w = self.writer.lock().await;
            if let Err(e) = w.write_all(line.as_bytes()).await {
                self.pending
                    .lock()
                    .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
                    .remove(&id);
                return Err(JidrError::unexpected(format!(
                    "daemon connection lost: {e}"
                )));
            }
        }
        let resp = rx
            .await
            .map_err(|_| JidrError::unexpected("the daemon closed the connection"))?;
        match (resp.result, resp.error) {
            (_, Some(e)) => Err(e.to_jidr()),
            (Some(v), None) => Ok(v),
            (None, None) => Ok(Value::Null),
        }
    }

    /// Typed call.
    pub async fn call_as<P: Serialize, R: DeserializeOwned>(
        &self,
        method: &str,
        params: P,
    ) -> JidrResult<R> {
        let params = serde_json::to_value(params).ctx(ErrorCode::Usage, "encoding params")?;
        let v = self.call(method, params).await?;
        serde_json::from_value(v).ctx(ErrorCode::Unexpected, format!("decoding {method} result"))
    }

    /// Calls a method and, if it started a job, follows the job to the end,
    /// reporting each progress update. Returns the job's result.
    pub async fn run(
        &self,
        method: &str,
        params: Value,
        on_progress: impl Fn(&Job),
    ) -> JidrResult<Value> {
        let v = self.call(method, params).await?;
        let Some(job) = pending_job(&v) else {
            return Ok(v);
        };
        let mut last = None;
        loop {
            let j = self.wait_job(job, Some(Duration::from_secs(1))).await?;
            if last.as_ref() != Some(&(j.progress, j.message.clone())) {
                on_progress(&j);
                last = Some((j.progress, j.message.clone()));
            }
            match j.state {
                JobState::Succeeded => return Ok(j.result.unwrap_or(Value::Null)),
                JobState::Failed => {
                    return Err(j
                        .error
                        .unwrap_or_else(|| JidrError::unexpected(format!("{method} failed"))));
                }
                JobState::Cancelled => return Err(jidr_core::cancel::cancelled()),
                JobState::Pending | JobState::Running => {}
            }
        }
    }

    /// Waits for a job to end, or `timeout` (then returns it as it is).
    pub async fn wait_job(&self, job: Uuid, timeout: Option<Duration>) -> JidrResult<Job> {
        let params = match timeout {
            Some(t) => json!({ "job": job, "timeout_s": t.as_secs().max(1) }),
            None => json!({ "job": job }),
        };
        self.call_as("jobs.wait", params).await
    }

    pub async fn cancel_job(&self, job: Uuid) -> JidrResult<Job> {
        self.call_as("jobs.cancel", json!({ "job": job })).await
    }

    /// Subscribes to events whose topic starts with any of `topics` (all if
    /// empty) and returns a receiver for them.
    pub async fn subscribe(&self, topics: &[&str]) -> JidrResult<broadcast::Receiver<Event>> {
        let rx = self.events.subscribe();
        self.call("events.subscribe", json!({ "topics": topics }))
            .await?;
        Ok(rx)
    }

    /// A receiver for events on this connection (after `subscribe` or
    /// `logcat.follow`).
    pub fn events(&self) -> broadcast::Receiver<Event> {
        self.events.subscribe()
    }
}

/// The job id of a `{job, pending: true}` answer.
pub fn pending_job(v: &Value) -> Option<Uuid> {
    if v.get("pending") != Some(&Value::Bool(true)) {
        return None;
    }
    v.get("job")
        .and_then(Value::as_str)
        .and_then(|s| Uuid::parse_str(s).ok())
}

fn is_unavailable_err(e: &JidrError) -> bool {
    e.data.as_ref().and_then(|d| d.get("unavailable")) == Some(&Value::Bool(true))
}

async fn read_loop(
    mut r: BufReader<tokio::net::unix::OwnedReadHalf>,
    pending: Pending,
    events: broadcast::Sender<Event>,
) {
    let mut line = String::new();
    loop {
        line.clear();
        match r.read_line(&mut line).await {
            Ok(0) | Err(_) => break,
            Ok(_) => {}
        }
        let Ok(v) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(&line) else {
            continue;
        };
        if v.get("method").and_then(Value::as_str) == Some(EVENT_METHOD) {
            if let Some(ev) = v
                .get("params")
                .and_then(|p| serde_json::from_value::<Event>(p.clone()).ok())
            {
                let _ = events.send(ev);
            }
            continue;
        }
        let Ok(resp) = serde_json::from_value::<Response>(v) else {
            continue;
        };
        let Some(id) = resp.id.as_u64() else {
            // A protocol error without an id (e.g. parse error): nothing to route.
            continue;
        };
        if let Some(tx) = pending
            .lock()
            .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
            .remove(&id)
        {
            let _ = tx.send(resp);
        }
    }
    // Wake every waiter: their senders drop here.
    pending.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).clear();
}

/// Asks the daemon at `socket` to exit (allowed before `hello`) and waits for
/// its socket to disappear.
pub async fn shutdown_daemon(socket: &Path) -> JidrResult<()> {
    let mut s = UnixStream::connect(socket).await.ctx(
        ErrorCode::Unexpected,
        format!("connecting to {}", socket.display()),
    )?;
    s.write_all(b"{\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"id\":1,\"method\":\"daemon.shutdown\"}\n")
        .await
        .ctx(ErrorCode::Unexpected, "asking the daemon to exit")?;
    for _ in 0..100 {
        if !socket.exists() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
    }
    Err(JidrError::unexpected("the old daemon did not exit"))
}

/// Starts `jidr daemon` detached from this process and its terminal.
fn spawn_daemon(paths: &JidrPaths, opts: &SpawnOptions) -> JidrResult<()> {
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&paths.logs).ctx(
        ErrorCode::Unexpected,
        format!("creating {}", paths.logs.display()),
    )?;
    let log_path = paths.logs.join("daemon.log");
    let log = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()
        .create(true)
        .append(true)
        .open(&log_path)
        .ctx(
            ErrorCode::Unexpected,
            format!("opening {}", log_path.display()),
        )?;
    let log_err = log
        .try_clone()
        .ctx(ErrorCode::Unexpected, "duplicating log handle")?;
    let program = opts.program();
    let mut cmd = std::process::Command::new(&program);
    cmd.arg("daemon")
        .stdin(Stdio::null())
        .stdout(Stdio::from(log))
        .stderr(Stdio::from(log_err));
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        use std::os::unix::process::CommandExt;
        // Its own process group: Ctrl-C in the user's terminal doesn't reach it.
        cmd.process_group(0);
    }
    cmd.spawn().map_err(|e| {
        JidrError::unexpected(format!(
            "cannot start the daemon ({}): {e}",
            program.display()
        ))
    })?;
    Ok(())
}

/// Turns a raw JSON-RPC error into a `JidrError` (for callers that speak
/// the protocol themselves).
pub fn error_from_rpc(e: &RpcError) -> JidrError {
    e.to_jidr()
}

mod tests {

    use std::path::Path;

    fn touch(p: &Path) {

    }

//! `jidr-client` against an in-process daemon (fake backend).
#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]

use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::Duration;

use jidr_client::{Client, SpawnOptions, shutdown_daemon};
use jidr_core::{ErrorCode, JidrPaths, JobState};
use jidr_daemon::testing::TestDaemon;
use serde_json::json;

#[tokio::test]
async fn calls_jobs_and_errors() {
    let tmp = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let d = TestDaemon::start(tmp.path()).await.unwrap();
    let c = Client::connect(&d.paths.socket(), "test").await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(c.daemon().protocol, "0.1");
    assert_eq!(c.call("device.list", json!({})).await.unwrap(), json!([]));
    c.call("device.create", json!({ "name": "P", "image": "35" }))
        .await
        .unwrap();

    let seen = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
    let s = seen.clone();
    let dev = c
        .run("device.start", json!({ "device": "P" }), move |j| {
            s.lock().unwrap().push(j.state)
        })
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(dev["status"]["state"], "running");
    assert!(!seen.lock().unwrap().is_empty(), "progress reported");

    let e = c
        .call("device.start", json!({ "device": "nope" }))
        .await
        .unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(e.code, ErrorCode::NotFound);
    assert_eq!(e.code.exit_code(), 3);
    let e = c
        .call("device.start", json!({ "devise": "P" }))
        .await
        .unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(e.code, ErrorCode::Usage);
    assert!(e.message.contains("devise"));

    // A failed job surfaces its error code.
    c.call("device.stop", json!({ "device": "P" }))
        .await
        .unwrap();
    d.backend
        .fail_next_start(jidr_core::JidrError::boot_timeout("slow"));
    let e = c
        .run("device.start", json!({ "device": "P" }), |_| {})
        .await
        .unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(e.code, ErrorCode::BootTimeout);

    // Cancel through the client.
    let _gate = d.backend.gate_starts();
    let v = c
        .call("device.start", json!({ "device": "P" }))
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let job = jidr_client::pending_job(&v).unwrap();
    c.cancel_job(job).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        c.wait_job(job, None).await.unwrap().state,
        JobState::Cancelled
    );
    d.stop().await;
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn spawns_jidr_daemon_when_none_is_running() {
    let tmp = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let paths = JidrPaths::under(tmp.path().join("j"));
    // A stand-in `jidr` that records how it was called and never listens.
    let marker = tmp.path().join("args.txt");
    let fake = tmp.path().join("jidr");
    std::fs::write(
        &fake,
        format!("#!/bin/sh\necho \"$@\" > {}\n", marker.display()),
    )
    .unwrap();
    use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
    std::fs::set_permissions(&fake, std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o755)).unwrap();
    let opts = SpawnOptions {
        program: Some(fake),
        restart_stale: false,
        timeout: Some(Duration::from_secs(1)),
    };
    let e = Client::connect_or_spawn(&paths, "test", &opts)
        .await
        .unwrap_err();
    assert!(e.message.contains("did not start"), "{e}");
    // The spawned process may lag behind under load.
    for _ in 0..100 {
        if marker.exists() {
            break;
        }
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
    }
    let log = std::fs::read_to_string(paths.logs.join("daemon.log")).unwrap_or_default();
    let args =
        std::fs::read_to_string(&marker).unwrap_or_else(|_| format!("no marker; log: {log}"));
    assert_eq!(args.trim(), "daemon");
    assert!(paths.logs.join("daemon.log").exists());
}

//! A cancellation flag shared between a job and the work it runs.

use std::sync::Arc;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};

use crate::error::{ErrorCode, JidrError, JidrResult};

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct Cancel(Arc<AtomicBool>);

impl Cancel {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }

    pub fn cancel(&self) {
        self.0.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }

    pub fn is_cancelled(&self) -> bool {
        self.0.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
    }

    /// `Err` (with `data.cancelled = true`) once cancelled.
    pub fn check(&self) -> JidrResult<()> {
        if self.is_cancelled() {
            Err(cancelled())
        } else {
            Ok(())
        }
    }
}

/// The error returned by cancelled work. Its code is `unexpected`; callers
/// recognise it with [`is_cancelled`].
pub fn cancelled() -> JidrError {
    JidrError::new(ErrorCode::Unexpected, "cancelled")
        .with_data(serde_json::json!({"cancelled": true}))
}

pub fn is_cancelled(err: &JidrError) -> bool {
    err.data
        .as_ref()
        .and_then(|d| d.get("cancelled"))
        .and_then(|c| c.as_bool())
        == Some(true)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn clones_share_the_flag() {
        let a = Cancel::new();
        let b = a.clone();
        assert!(a.check().is_ok());
        b.cancel();
        assert!(a.is_cancelled());
        assert!(is_cancelled(&a.check().unwrap_err()));
        assert!(!is_cancelled(&JidrError::sdk("x")));
    }
}

`crates/jidr-core/src/error.rs`:

```rs
//! Error codes shared by the protocol, the CLI (exit codes) and MCP.

use schemars::JsonSchema;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

/// The eight error codes. Each one is also the CLI exit code.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum ErrorCode {
    /// A bug or an error we didn't classify. Exit code 1.
    Unexpected,
    /// Bad arguments or parameters. Exit code 2.
    Usage,
    /// The device, image, profile, job or snapshot doesn't exist. Exit code 3.
    NotFound,
    /// Another operation holds the device lock. Exit code 4.
    Busy,
    /// The device didn't finish booting in time. Exit code 5.
    BootTimeout,
    /// SDK, emulator, download or license problem. Exit code 6.
    Sdk,
    /// Rooting, verifying or reverting root failed. Exit code 7.
    RootFailed,
    /// The client and the running daemon are different versions. Exit code 8.
    DaemonStale,
}

impl ErrorCode {
    pub const ALL: [ErrorCode; 8] = [
        Self::Unexpected,
        Self::Usage,
        Self::NotFound,
        Self::Busy,
        Self::BootTimeout,
        Self::Sdk,
        Self::RootFailed,
        Self::DaemonStale,
    ];

    /// The CLI exit code (0 is success and has no `ErrorCode`).
    pub const fn exit_code(self) -> u8 {
        match self {
            Self::Unexpected => 1,
            Self::Usage => 2,
            Self::NotFound => 3,
            Self::Busy => 4,
            Self::BootTimeout => 5,
            Self::Sdk => 6,
            Self::RootFailed => 7,
            Self::DaemonStale => 8,
        }
    }

    /// The JSON-RPC error code. Usage maps to "invalid params"; the others
    /// live in the implementation-defined server-error range.
    pub const fn rpc_code(self) -> i64 {
        match self {
            Self::Usage => -32602,
            other => -32000 - other.exit_code() as i64,
        }
    }

    pub const fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Unexpected => "unexpected",
            Self::Usage => "usage",
            Self::NotFound => "not_found",
            Self::Busy => "busy",
            Self::BootTimeout => "boot_timeout",
            Self::Sdk => "sdk",
            Self::RootFailed => "root_failed",
            Self::DaemonStale => "daemon_stale",
        }
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Display for ErrorCode {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.write_str(self.as_str())
    }
}

/// The error type every Jidr layer returns across crate boundaries.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema, thiserror::Error)]
#[error("{code}: {message}")]
pub struct JidrError {
    pub code: ErrorCode,
    pub message: String,
    /// Structured details, e.g. `{"holder": "...", "op": "..."}` for `busy`.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub data: Option<serde_json::Value>,
}

pub type JidrResult<T> = Result<T, JidrError>;

impl JidrError {
    pub fn new(code: ErrorCode, message: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self {
            code,
            message: message.into(),
            data: None,
        }
    }

    pub fn with_data(mut self, data: serde_json::Value) -> Self {
        self.data = Some(data);
        self
    }

    pub fn unexpected(message: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self::new(ErrorCode::Unexpected, message)
    }

    pub fn usage(message: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self::new(ErrorCode::Usage, message)
    }

    pub fn not_found(message: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self::new(ErrorCode::NotFound, message)
    }

    pub fn busy(message: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self::new(ErrorCode::Busy, message)
    }

    pub fn sdk(message: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self::new(ErrorCode::Sdk, message)
    }

    pub fn root_failed(message: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self::new(ErrorCode::RootFailed, message)
    }

    pub fn boot_timeout(message: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self::new(ErrorCode::BootTimeout, message)
    }
}

/// Adds context to foreign errors: `.ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, "reading config.ini")`.
pub trait ResultExt<T> {
    fn ctx(self, code: ErrorCode, what: impl std::fmt::Display) -> JidrResult<T>;
}

impl<T, E: std::fmt::Display> ResultExt<T> for Result<T, E> {
    fn ctx(self, code: ErrorCode, what: impl std::fmt::Display) -> JidrResult<T> {
        self.map_err(|e| JidrError::new(code, format!("{what}: {e}")))
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn exit_codes_match_the_plan() {
        let codes: Vec<u8> = ErrorCode::ALL.iter().map(|c| c.exit_code()).collect();
        assert_eq!(codes, vec![1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn serializes_snake_case() {
        let e = JidrError::busy("held").with_data(serde_json::json!({"holder": "x"}));
        let v = serde_json::to_value(&e).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(v["code"], "busy");
        assert_eq!(v["data"]["holder"], "x");
        let back: JidrError = serde_json::from_value(v).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(back, e);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rpc_codes_are_distinct() {
        let mut codes: Vec<i64> = ErrorCode::ALL.iter().map(|c| c.rpc_code()).collect();
        codes.sort_unstable();
        codes.dedup();
        assert_eq!(codes.len(), 8);
        assert_eq!(ErrorCode::NotFound.rpc_code(), -32003);
    }
}

//! The Jidr domain model, shared by the daemon, the clients and the providers.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::path::PathBuf;

use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
use schemars::JsonSchema;

/// A hardware profile: what the device looks like (D24: generic names).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
pub struct HardwareProfile {
    /// Stable id, e.g. `phone-6.1-fhd`.
    pub id: String,
    /// Display name, e.g. `Phone 6.1″ FHD+`.
    pub name: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub form_factor: FormFactor,
    pub width: u32,
    pub height: u32,
    pub density: u32,
    pub ram_mb: u32,
    pub cpus: u32,
    /// Data partition size in MB.
    #[serde(default = "default_data_mb")]
    pub data_mb: u32,
    /// Extra `config.ini` keys applied at creation.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub config: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    /// Requested build props (🔎 research: not applied in the MVP).
    #[serde(default)]
    pub build_props: BTreeMap<String, String>,
}

fn default_data_mb() -> u32 {
    6144
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum FormFactor {
    #[default]
    Phone,
    Tablet,
    Foldable,
}

/// Identifies a system image: `system-images;android-35;google_apis;arm64-v8a`.
#[derive(
    Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema,
)]
pub struct ImageRef {
    pub api: u32,
    /// `default`, `google_apis`, `google_apis_playstore`, `aosp_atd`, …
    pub tag: String,
    pub abi: String,
}

impl ImageRef {
    /// The SDK package path.
    pub fn package(&self) -> String {
        format!(
            "system-images;android-{};{};{}",
            self.api, self.tag, self.abi
        )
    }

    /// Directory relative to the SDK root, as `image.sysdir.1` wants it.
    pub fn sysdir(&self) -> String {
        format!(
            "system-images/android-{}/{}/{}/",
            self.api, self.tag, self.abi
        )
    }

    /// Parses `system-images;android-35;google_apis;arm64-v8a`.
    pub fn parse_package(package: &str) -> Option<Self> {
        let mut parts = package.split(';');
        if parts.next()? != "system-images" {
            return None;
        }
        let api = parts.next()?.strip_prefix("android-")?.parse().ok()?;
        let tag = parts.next()?.to_string();
        let abi = parts.next()?.to_string();
        if parts.next().is_some() || tag.is_empty() || abi.is_empty() {
            return None;
        }
        Some(Self { api, tag, abi })
    }

    /// Images where `adb root` works (plan: default, google_apis, atd).
    pub fn allows_adb_root(&self) -> bool {
        !self.tag.contains("playstore")
    }
}

/// How well an API level is supported (D23).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Support {
    Supported,
    BestEffort,
    Unsupported,
}

impl Support {
    pub fn for_api(api: u32) -> Self {
        match api {
            29..=36 => Self::Supported,
            28 => Self::BestEffort,
            _ => Self::Unsupported,
        }
    }
}

    /// SHA-256 of the pristine `ramdisk.img` (filled by the root engine).
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub pristine_ramdisk_sha256: Option<String>,
}

    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub result: Option<serde_json::Value>,
    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,
}

        let ga = ImageRef {
            api: 35,
            tag: "google_apis".into(),
            abi: "arm64-v8a".into(),
        };
        assert!(!ps.allows_adb_root());
        assert!(ga.allows_adb_root());
    }

```rs
//! Where Jidr keeps its files. Everything Jidr writes lives under these
//! directories; the Android Studio SDK and `~/.android/avd` are never written (D3).

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use crate::error::{JidrError, JidrResult};

/// Set to put every Jidr directory under one root (tests, portable installs).
pub const JIDR_HOME_ENV: &str = "JIDR_HOME";

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct JidrPaths {
    /// `~/Library/Application Support/Jidr`
    pub data: PathBuf,
    /// `~/Library/Caches/Jidr`
    pub cache: PathBuf,
    /// `~/Library/Logs/Jidr`
    pub logs: PathBuf,
}

impl JidrPaths {
    /// Platform defaults, or everything under `$JIDR_HOME` when set.
    pub fn discover() -> JidrResult<Self> {
        if let Some(home) = std::env::var_os(JIDR_HOME_ENV).filter(|h| !h.is_empty()) {
            return Ok(Self::under(PathBuf::from(home)));
        }
        let data = dirs::data_dir()
            .ok_or_else(|| JidrError::unexpected("no data directory for this user"))?
            .join("Jidr");
        let cache = dirs::cache_dir()
            .ok_or_else(|| JidrError::unexpected("no cache directory for this user"))?
            .join("Jidr");
        let logs = if cfg!(target_os = "macos") {
            dirs::home_dir()
                .ok_or_else(|| JidrError::unexpected("no home directory"))?
                .join("Library/Logs/Jidr")
        } else {
            data.join("logs")
        };
        Ok(Self { data, cache, logs })
    }

    /// All directories under one root.
    pub fn under(root: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> Self {
        let root = root.into();
        Self {
            data: root.join("data"),
            cache: root.join("cache"),
            logs: root.join("logs"),
        }
    }

    /// Jidr's private Android SDK.
    pub fn sdk(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.data.join("sdk")
    }

    /// Jidr's AVD home (`ANDROID_AVD_HOME` for every emulator we launch).
    pub fn avd_home(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.data.join("avd")
    }

    /// The device registry.
    pub fn devices_file(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.data.join("devices.json")
    }

    /// Daemon-wide settings (gap B4).
    pub fn settings_file(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.data.join("settings.json")
    }

    /// License consent records (D8).
    pub fn consent_file(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.data.join("consent.json")
    }

    /// The daemon's Unix socket.
    pub fn socket(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.data.join("daemon.sock")
    }

    /// Download cache (SDK archives, Magisk APKs by SHA-256).
    pub fn downloads(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.cache.join("downloads")
    }

    /// Per-device log directory.
    pub fn device_logs(&self, device: &str) -> PathBuf {
        self.logs.join("devices").join(device)
    }

    /// True if `path` is inside one of Jidr's own directories.
    pub fn owns(&self, path: &Path) -> bool {
        [&self.data, &self.cache, &self.logs]
            .iter()
            .any(|root| path.starts_with(root))
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn under_root_layout() {
        let p = JidrPaths::under("/tmp/j");
        assert_eq!(p.sdk(), PathBuf::from("/tmp/j/data/sdk"));
        assert_eq!(p.avd_home(), PathBuf::from("/tmp/j/data/avd"));
        assert_eq!(p.socket(), PathBuf::from("/tmp/j/data/daemon.sock"));
        assert!(p.owns(Path::new("/tmp/j/cache/downloads/x")));
        assert!(!p.owns(Path::new("/Users/me/Library/Android/sdk")));
    }
}
