`crates/jidr-core/src/provider.rs`:

```rs
//! The command provider contract. Every action Jidr can take is a command
//! registered by a provider (the daemon core, `jidr-widgets`, `jidr-root`);
//! the GUI, CLI and MCP all call the same commands.

use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::Arc;

use async_trait::async_trait;
use schemars::JsonSchema;
use serde::de::DeserializeOwned;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::Value;
use uuid::Uuid;

use crate::{Cancel, ConnectInfo, Device, JidrError, JidrPaths, JidrResult};

/// One command row, as listed by `commands.list`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct CommandSpec {
    /// Method name, e.g. `device.start`.
    pub id: String,
    /// One-line description for humans and agents.
    pub label: String,
    /// JSON Schema of the params object.
    pub params: Value,
    /// Loses data or can't be undone (MCP policy, D5).
    pub destructive: bool,
    /// Runs as a job: the call returns `{job, pending: true}` (4b).
    pub long_running: bool,
    /// Takes the per-device single-writer lock on `params.device`.
    pub locks_device: bool,
}

impl CommandSpec {
    /// Builds a spec whose params schema comes from `P`.
    pub fn new<P: JsonSchema>(id: &str, label: &str) -> Self {
        let mut params = serde_json::to_value(schemars::schema_for!(P)).unwrap_or(Value::Null);
        // Drop schema noise that agents don't need.
        if let Some(obj) = params.as_object_mut() {
            obj.remove("$schema");
            obj.remove("title");
        }
        Self {
            id: id.to_string(),
            label: label.to_string(),
            params,
            destructive: false,
            long_running: false,
            locks_device: false,
        }
    }

    pub fn destructive(mut self) -> Self {
        self.destructive = true;
        self
    }

    pub fn long_running(mut self) -> Self {
        self.long_running = true;
        self
    }

    pub fn locks_device(mut self) -> Self {
        self.locks_device = true;
        self
    }
}

/// Params of commands that take nothing.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct NoParams {}

/// Deserializes params; unknown keys and type errors become `usage` errors
/// that name the offending key. `null` counts as `{}`.
pub fn parse_params<T: DeserializeOwned>(params: Value) -> JidrResult<T> {
    let params = if params.is_null() {
        Value::Object(Default::default())
    } else {
        params
    };
    serde_json::from_value(params).map_err(|e| JidrError::usage(format!("invalid params: {e}")))
}

/// A change to a stored device (explicit `for<'a>` so async-trait keeps it
/// higher-ranked).
pub type DeviceUpdate = Box<dyn for<'a> FnOnce(&'a mut Device) + Send + 'static>;

/// Reports job progress: fraction (`None` = indeterminate) and a message.
pub type ProgressFn = Arc<dyn Fn(Option<f32>, &str) + Send + Sync>;

/// Reports job progress with the bytes done and expected of a download.
pub type BytesFn = Arc<dyn Fn(Option<f32>, &str, u64, u64) + Send + Sync>;

/// What a provider gets for each call.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct CallCtx {
    pub daemon: Arc<dyn DaemonContext>,
    pub progress: ProgressFn,
    pub bytes: BytesFn,
    pub cancel: Cancel,
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for CallCtx {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("CallCtx")
            .field("cancel", &self.cancel)
            .finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

impl CallCtx {
    pub fn new(daemon: Arc<dyn DaemonContext>) -> Self {
        Self {
            daemon,
            progress: Arc::new(|_, _| {}),
            bytes: Arc::new(|_, _, _, _| {}),
            cancel: Cancel::new(),
        }
    }

    pub fn report(&self, fraction: Option<f32>, message: &str) {
        (self.progress)(fraction, message);
    }

    /// Like [`report`](Self::report), with the bytes of the current download
    /// (`Job.bytes`, gap B5). A plain `report` clears them.
    pub fn report_bytes(&self, fraction: Option<f32>, message: &str, done: u64, total: u64) {
        (self.bytes)(fraction, message, done, total);
    }
}

/// Daemon services available to providers.
#[async_trait]
pub trait DaemonContext: Send + Sync {
    fn paths(&self) -> &JidrPaths;

    /// The `adb` binary of the SDK in use.
    fn adb_path(&self) -> JidrResult<PathBuf>;

    /// A device by name or id.
    async fn device(&self, selector: &str) -> JidrResult<Device>;

    async fn devices(&self) -> Vec<Device>;

    /// Connection details of a running device (`not_found` if stopped).
    async fn connect_info(&self, device: Uuid) -> JidrResult<ConnectInfo>;

    /// Applies `f` to the stored device and saves it.
    async fn update_device(&self, device: Uuid, f: DeviceUpdate) -> JidrResult<Device>;

    /// Starts a device and waits for boot. Callers already hold its lock.
    async fn start_device(
        &self,
        device: Uuid,
        cold_boot: bool,
        cancel: &Cancel,
    ) -> JidrResult<Device>;

    /// Stops a device. Callers already hold its lock.
    async fn stop_device(&self, device: Uuid) -> JidrResult<Device>;

    /// Publishes an event to `events.subscribe` listeners.
    fn emit(&self, topic: &str, data: Value);
}

/// A set of commands.
#[async_trait]
pub trait CommandProvider: Send + Sync {
    /// Short provider name for logs, e.g. `core`, `widgets`, `root`.
    fn name(&self) -> &str;

    fn commands(&self) -> Vec<CommandSpec>;

    /// Runs `method` (one of this provider's ids) with raw params.
    async fn call(&self, ctx: &CallCtx, method: &str, params: Value) -> JidrResult<Value>;

    /// Called after every successful boot of a device, in registration order.
    async fn on_booted(&self, _ctx: &CallCtx, _device: &Device) -> JidrResult<()> {
        Ok(())
    }
}

//! JSON-RPC 2.0 message types (newline-delimited JSON over the socket).

use crate::{ErrorCode, JidrError};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::{Value, json};

pub const PARSE_ERROR: i64 = -32700;
pub const INVALID_REQUEST: i64 = -32600;
pub const METHOD_NOT_FOUND: i64 = -32601;
pub const INVALID_PARAMS: i64 = -32602;

/// Protocol version. Bumped on any breaking change; see docs/control-protocol.md.
pub const PROTOCOL_VERSION: &str = "0.1";

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Request {
    pub jsonrpc: String,
    /// Absent for notifications (which we don't accept from clients).
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub id: Option<Value>,
    pub method: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub params: Value,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct RpcError {
    pub code: i64,
    pub message: String,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub data: Option<Value>,
}

impl RpcError {
    pub fn new(code: i64, message: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self {
            code,
            message: message.into(),
            data: None,
        }
    }

    /// A Jidr error: the JSON-RPC code from its `ErrorCode`, and
    /// `data.code` = the snake_case name (`busy`, `not_found`, …).
    pub fn from_jidr(e: &JidrError) -> Self {
        let mut data = json!({ "code": e.code.as_str(), "exit_code": e.code.exit_code() });
        if let (Some(extra), Some(obj)) = (&e.data, data.as_object_mut()) {
            obj.insert("details".into(), extra.clone());
        }
        Self {
            code: e.code.rpc_code(),
            message: e.message.clone(),
            data: Some(data),
        }
    }

    /// Back to a `JidrError` on the client side.
    pub fn to_jidr(&self) -> JidrError {
        let code = self
            .data
            .as_ref()
            .and_then(|d| d.get("code"))
            .and_then(|c| serde_json::from_value::<ErrorCode>(c.clone()).ok())
            .unwrap_or(match self.code {
                PARSE_ERROR | INVALID_REQUEST | METHOD_NOT_FOUND | INVALID_PARAMS => {
                    ErrorCode::Usage
                }
                _ => ErrorCode::Unexpected,
            });
        let mut err = JidrError::new(code, self.message.clone());
        err.data = self.data.as_ref().and_then(|d| d.get("details")).cloned();
        err
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Response {
    pub jsonrpc: String,
    pub id: Value,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub result: Option<Value>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub error: Option<RpcError>,
}

impl Response {
    pub fn ok(id: Value, result: Value) -> Self {
        Self {
            jsonrpc: "2.0".into(),
            id,
            result: Some(result),
            error: None,
        }
    }

    pub fn err(id: Value, error: RpcError) -> Self {
        Self {
            jsonrpc: "2.0".into(),
            id,
            result: None,
            error: Some(error),
        }
    }
}

/// A server → client notification (events).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Notification {
    pub jsonrpc: String,
    pub method: String,
    pub params: Value,
}

impl Notification {
    pub fn new(method: &str, params: Value) -> Self {
        Self {
            jsonrpc: "2.0".into(),
            method: method.into(),
            params,
        }
    }
}

/// An event published to `events.subscribe` listeners, sent as an `event`
/// notification.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Event {
    /// e.g. `device.status`, `device.boot`, `job.progress`, `logcat`.
    pub topic: String,
    pub data: Value,
}

/// The notification method carrying events.
pub const EVENT_METHOD: &str = "event";

/// `hello` params and result.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct HelloParams {
    /// The client's Jidr version; must equal the daemon's.
    pub version: String,
    /// `cli`, `gui`, `mcp`, …
    #[serde(default)]
    pub client: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct HelloResult {
    pub version: String,
    pub protocol: String,
    pub pid: u32,
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn jidr_errors_round_trip() {
        let e = JidrError::busy("held").with_data(json!({"holder": "device.start", "op": "start"}));
        let r = RpcError::from_jidr(&e);
        assert_eq!(r.code, -32004);
        assert_eq!(r.data.as_ref().unwrap()["code"], "busy");
        assert_eq!(r.data.as_ref().unwrap()["exit_code"], 4);
        let back = r.to_jidr();
        assert_eq!(back, e);
        assert_eq!(
            RpcError::new(PARSE_ERROR, "bad").to_jidr().code,
            ErrorCode::Usage
        );
    }
}

`crates/jidr-cpio/src/compress.rs`:

```rs
//! Compression formats found in ramdisks: gzip (RFC 1952), lz4 legacy frames
//! and xz. Each stream is decoded on its own, so concatenated streams can be
//! split and rebuilt with the same settings.

use std::io::{Read, Write};

use crate::{Error, Result};

/// Upper bound on one decompressed stream; real ramdisks are well under 100 MiB.
pub const MAX_DECOMPRESSED: usize = 1 << 30;

/// The lz4 legacy-frame magic (little-endian `0x184C2102`).
pub const LZ4_LEGACY_MAGIC: [u8; 4] = [0x02, 0x21, 0x4c, 0x18];
/// Uncompressed size of every lz4 legacy block except the last.
pub const LZ4_LEGACY_BLOCK: usize = 8 << 20;
/// AOSP builds ramdisks with `lz4 -l -12`.
pub const LZ4_ANDROID_LEVEL: i32 = 12;

const GZIP_MAGIC: [u8; 2] = [0x1f, 0x8b];
const XZ_MAGIC: [u8; 6] = [0xfd, b'7', b'z', b'X', b'Z', 0x00];
/// Enough for any preset (`-9` needs about 65 MiB to decode).
const XZ_MEMLIMIT: u64 = 512 << 20;
/// What `gzip -n` writes on Unix: deflate, no flags, mtime 0, XFL 0, OS 3.
const GZIP_DEFAULT_HEADER: [u8; 10] = [0x1f, 0x8b, 8, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 3];

/// Integrity check stored in an xz stream header.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum XzCheck {
    None,
    Crc32,
    Crc64,
    Sha256,
}

impl XzCheck {
    fn from_id(id: u8) -> Option<Self> {
        match id {
            0x00 => Some(XzCheck::None),
            0x01 => Some(XzCheck::Crc32),
            0x04 => Some(XzCheck::Crc64),
            0x0a => Some(XzCheck::Sha256),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    fn to_lzma(self) -> liblzma::stream::Check {
        match self {
            XzCheck::None => liblzma::stream::Check::None,
            XzCheck::Crc32 => liblzma::stream::Check::Crc32,
            XzCheck::Crc64 => liblzma::stream::Check::Crc64,
            XzCheck::Sha256 => liblzma::stream::Check::Sha256,
        }
    }
}

/// How one stream is compressed, with the settings needed to reproduce it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Compression {
    /// A raw cpio archive.
    None,
    /// gzip with zlib deflate at `level`; `header` is the original member
    /// header (magic through the optional fields), written back verbatim.
    Gzip { level: u32, header: Vec<u8> },
    /// lz4 legacy frame: 8 MiB blocks, each compressed with liblz4
    /// (HC when `level >= 3`).
    Lz4Legacy { level: i32 },
    /// xz with liblzma's preset `preset` and the given check.
    Xz { preset: u32, check: XzCheck },
}

/// One decoded stream.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Decompressed {
    pub compression: Compression,
    pub data: Vec<u8>,
    /// Input bytes the stream occupied; the next stream starts here.
    pub consumed: usize,
}

impl Compression {
    /// `gzip -n -6`.
    pub fn gzip() -> Self {
        Compression::Gzip {
            level: 6,
            header: GZIP_DEFAULT_HEADER.to_vec(),
        }
    }

    /// `lz4 -l -12`, as AOSP builds emulator ramdisks.
    pub fn lz4_legacy() -> Self {
        Compression::Lz4Legacy {
            level: LZ4_ANDROID_LEVEL,
        }
    }

    /// `xz -9 --check=crc32`: the check the kernel's and other embedded xz
    /// decoders always support.
    pub fn xz() -> Self {
        Compression::Xz {
            preset: 9,
            check: XzCheck::Crc32,
        }
    }

    pub fn name(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Compression::None => "cpio",
            Compression::Gzip { .. } => "gzip",
            Compression::Lz4Legacy { .. } => "lz4-legacy",
            Compression::Xz { .. } => "xz",
        }
    }

    /// Identifies the stream at the start of `bytes` from its magic and
    /// header. Settings that a stream doesn't record (lz4 level, xz preset)
    /// get the Android defaults.
    pub fn detect(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self> {
        if bytes.starts_with(&LZ4_LEGACY_MAGIC) {
            Ok(Compression::lz4_legacy())
        } else if bytes.starts_with(&GZIP_MAGIC) {
            let header_len = gzip_header_len(bytes)?;
            let level = match bytes.get(8) {
                Some(2) => 9,
                Some(4) => 1,
                _ => 6,
            };
            Ok(Compression::Gzip {
                level,
                header: bytes.get(..header_len).unwrap_or_default().to_vec(),
            })
        } else if bytes.starts_with(&XZ_MAGIC) {
            let check = bytes
                .get(7)
                .and_then(|id| XzCheck::from_id(id & 0x0f))
                .ok_or_else(|| corrupt("xz", "unknown integrity check in the stream header"))?;
            Ok(Compression::Xz { preset: 9, check })
        } else if bytes.starts_with(b"070701") || bytes.starts_with(b"070702") {
            Ok(Compression::None)
        } else {
            Err(Error::UnknownFormat { offset: 0 })
        }
    }

    pub fn compress(&self, data: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
        match self {
            Compression::None => Ok(data.to_vec()),
            Compression::Gzip { level, header } => gzip_compress(data, *level, header),
            Compression::Lz4Legacy { level } => lz4_legacy_compress(data, *level),
            Compression::Xz { preset, check } => xz_compress(data, *preset, *check),
        }
    }
}

/// Decodes the single stream at the start of `bytes`.
pub fn decompress(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Decompressed> {
    let compression = Compression::detect(bytes)?;
    let (data, consumed) = match &compression {
        Compression::None => (bytes.to_vec(), bytes.len()),
        Compression::Gzip { header, .. } => gzip_decompress(bytes, header.len())?,
        Compression::Lz4Legacy { .. } => lz4_legacy_decompress(bytes)?,
        Compression::Xz { .. } => xz_decompress(bytes)?,
    };
    Ok(Decompressed {
        compression,
        data,
        consumed,
    })
}

fn corrupt(format: &'static str, message: impl ToString) -> Error {
    Error::Corrupt {
        format,
        message: message.to_string(),
    }
}

/// Reads `reader` to the end, failing past [`MAX_DECOMPRESSED`].
fn read_limited<R: Read>(reader: &mut R, format: &'static str) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    reader
        .take(MAX_DECOMPRESSED as u64 + 1)
        .read_to_end(&mut out)
        .map_err(|e| corrupt(format, e))?;
    if out.len() > MAX_DECOMPRESSED {
        return Err(Error::Limit {
            limit: MAX_DECOMPRESSED,
        });
    }
    Ok(out)
}

// ---- gzip (RFC 1952) -------------------------------------------------------

const FHCRC: u8 = 0x02;
const FEXTRA: u8 = 0x04;
const FNAME: u8 = 0x08;
const FCOMMENT: u8 = 0x10;

fn gzip_header_len(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<usize> {
    let truncated = |offset| Error::Truncated {
        offset,
        what: "a gzip header",
    };
    let fixed = bytes.get(..10).ok_or(truncated(0))?;
    if fixed.get(2) != Some(&8) {
        return Err(corrupt("gzip", "compression method is not deflate"));
    }
    let flags = fixed.get(3).copied().unwrap_or(0);
    let mut off = 10;
    if flags & FEXTRA != 0 {
        let xlen = bytes.get(off..off + 2).ok_or(truncated(off))?;
        off += 2 + usize::from(u16::from_le_bytes([xlen[0], xlen[1]]));
    }
    for flag in [FNAME, FCOMMENT] {
        if flags & flag != 0 {
            let rest = bytes.get(off..).ok_or(truncated(off))?;
            let nul = rest.iter().position(|&b| b == 0).ok_or(truncated(off))?;
            off += nul + 1;
        }
    }
    if flags & FHCRC != 0 {
        off += 2;
    }
    if off > bytes.len() {
        return Err(truncated(off));
    }
    Ok(off)
}

fn gzip_decompress(bytes: &[u8], header_len: usize) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, usize)> {
    let body = bytes.get(header_len..).unwrap_or_default();
    let mut decoder = flate2::bufread::DeflateDecoder::new(body);
    let data = read_limited(&mut decoder, "gzip")?;
    let rest = decoder.into_inner();
    let trailer = rest.get(..8).ok_or(Error::Truncated {
        offset: bytes.len(),
        what: "the gzip CRC32 and size trailer",
    })?;
    let mut crc = flate2::Crc::new();
    crc.update(&data);
    let stored_crc = u32::from_le_bytes([trailer[0], trailer[1], trailer[2], trailer[3]]);
    let stored_len = u32::from_le_bytes([trailer[4], trailer[5], trailer[6], trailer[7]]);
    if crc.sum() != stored_crc || (data.len() as u32) != stored_len {
        return Err(corrupt("gzip", "CRC32 or size trailer mismatch"));
    }
    let consumed = bytes.len() - rest.len() + 8;
    Ok((data, consumed))
}

fn gzip_compress(data: &[u8], level: u32, header: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(data.len() / 2 + header.len() + 8);
    out.extend_from_slice(header);
    let mut encoder = flate2::write::DeflateEncoder::new(out, flate2::Compression::new(level));
    encoder.write_all(data)?;
    let mut out = encoder.finish()?;
    let mut crc = flate2::Crc::new();
    crc.update(data);
    out.extend_from_slice(&crc.sum().to_le_bytes());
    // ISIZE is the input size modulo 2^32 (RFC 1952 §2.3.1).
    out.extend_from_slice(&(data.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
    Ok(out)
}

// ---- lz4 legacy frame ------------------------------------------------------
//
// A legacy frame has no end marker: it runs until the input ends, a block
// size of zero, or the next frame's magic. So an lz4 stream can only be
// followed by another lz4 stream, which is how AOSP concatenates ramdisks.

fn lz4_legacy_decompress(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, usize)> {
    let max_block = lz4::block::compress_bound(LZ4_LEGACY_BLOCK).map_err(|e| corrupt("lz4", e))?;
    let mut data = Vec::new();
    let mut off = LZ4_LEGACY_MAGIC.len();
    while let Some(size) = bytes.get(off..off + 4) {
        let size = u32::from_le_bytes([size[0], size[1], size[2], size[3]]) as usize;
        // The next stream's magic, or zero padding, ends this one.
        if size == 0 || size == u32::from_le_bytes(LZ4_LEGACY_MAGIC) as usize {
            break;
        }
        if size > max_block {
            return Err(corrupt(
                "lz4",
                format!("block at byte {off} is {size} bytes"),
            ));
        }
        let block = bytes.get(off + 4..off + 4 + size).ok_or(Error::Truncated {
            offset: off + 4,
            what: "an lz4 block",
        })?;
        let decoded = lz4::block::decompress(block, Some(LZ4_LEGACY_BLOCK as i32))
            .map_err(|e| corrupt("lz4", format!("block at byte {off}: {e}")))?;
        if data.len() + decoded.len() > MAX_DECOMPRESSED {
            return Err(Error::Limit {
                limit: MAX_DECOMPRESSED,
            });
        }
        data.extend_from_slice(&decoded);
        off += 4 + size;
    }
    // Fewer than 4 bytes left: zero padding ends the stream, anything else is cut off.
    let rest = bytes.get(off..).unwrap_or_default();
    if !rest.is_empty() && rest.len() < 4 && rest.iter().any(|&b| b != 0) {
        return Err(Error::Truncated {
            offset: off,
            what: "an lz4 block size",
        });
    }
    Ok((data, off))
}

fn lz4_legacy_compress(data: &[u8], level: i32) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
    let mode = if level >= 3 {
        lz4::block::CompressionMode::HIGHCOMPRESSION(level)
    } else {
        lz4::block::CompressionMode::DEFAULT
    };
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(data.len() / 2 + 16);
    out.extend_from_slice(&LZ4_LEGACY_MAGIC);
    for chunk in data.chunks(LZ4_LEGACY_BLOCK) {
        let block = lz4::block::compress(chunk, Some(mode), false)?;
        out.extend_from_slice(&(block.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
        out.extend_from_slice(&block);
    }
    Ok(out)
}

// ---- xz ----------------------------------------------------------------------

fn xz_decompress(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, usize)> {
    let stream = liblzma::stream::Stream::new_stream_decoder(XZ_MEMLIMIT, 0)
        .map_err(|e| corrupt("xz", e))?;
    let mut decoder = liblzma::bufread::XzDecoder::new_stream(bytes, stream);
    let data = read_limited(&mut decoder, "xz")?;
    let consumed = bytes.len() - decoder.into_inner().len();
    Ok((data, consumed))
}

fn xz_compress(data: &[u8], preset: u32, check: XzCheck) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
    let stream = liblzma::stream::Stream::new_easy_encoder(preset, check.to_lzma())
        .map_err(|e| corrupt("xz", e))?;
    let mut encoder = liblzma::write::XzEncoder::new_stream(Vec::new(), stream);
    encoder.write_all(data)?;
    Ok(encoder.finish()?)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn sample() -> Vec<u8> {
        (0..100_000u32)
            .flat_map(|i| (i % 251).to_le_bytes())
            .collect()
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_format_round_trips_and_reports_its_length() {
        let data = sample();
        for c in [
            Compression::gzip(),
            Compression::lz4_legacy(),
            Compression::Lz4Legacy { level: 1 },
            Compression::xz(),
        ] {
            let packed = c.compress(&data).unwrap();
            let mut followed = packed.clone();
            followed.extend_from_slice(&LZ4_LEGACY_MAGIC);
            let out = decompress(&followed).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(out.data, data, "{}", c.name());
            assert_eq!(out.consumed, packed.len(), "{}", c.name());
            assert_eq!(Compression::detect(&packed).unwrap().name(), c.name());
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn lz4_legacy_splits_into_8_mib_blocks() {
        let data = vec![7u8; LZ4_LEGACY_BLOCK + 10];
        let packed = Compression::lz4_legacy().compress(&data).unwrap();
        let first = u32::from_le_bytes(packed[4..8].try_into().unwrap()) as usize;
        let second_at = 8 + first;
        assert!(packed.len() > second_at + 4);
        assert_eq!(decompress(&packed).unwrap().data.len(), data.len());
    }

    #[test]
    fn gzip_header_fields_are_kept() {
        // FNAME set: "ramdisk\0" follows the fixed header.
        let mut header = vec![0x1f, 0x8b, 8, FNAME, 1, 2, 3, 4, 2, 3];
        header.extend_from_slice(b"ramdisk\0");
        let c = Compression::Gzip { level: 9, header };
        let packed = c.compress(b"hello hello hello").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(Compression::detect(&packed).unwrap(), c);
        let out = decompress(&packed).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(out.data, b"hello hello hello");
        assert_eq!(out.consumed, packed.len());
    }

    #[test]
    fn xz_check_comes_from_the_stream_header() {
        let c = Compression::Xz {
            preset: 9,
            check: XzCheck::Crc64,
        };
        let packed = c.compress(b"data").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(Compression::detect(&packed).unwrap(), c);
    }

    #[test]
    fn corrupt_input_is_an_error_not_a_panic() {
        let data = sample();
        for c in [
            Compression::gzip(),
            Compression::lz4_legacy(),
            Compression::xz(),
        ] {
            let packed = c.compress(&data).unwrap();
            let truncated = &packed[..packed.len() / 2];
            assert!(decompress(truncated).is_err(), "{}", c.name());
            let mut flipped = packed.clone();
            let mid = flipped.len() / 2;
            flipped[mid] ^= 0xff;
            flipped[mid + 1] ^= 0xff;
            let _ = decompress(&flipped);
        }
        assert!(matches!(
            decompress(b"PK\x03\x04"),
            Err(Error::UnknownFormat { offset: 0 })
        ));
        assert!(decompress(&[0x1f, 0x8b, 8]).is_err());
        assert!(decompress(&[0x02, 0x21, 0x4c, 0x18, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0x7f]).is_err());
    }
}

`crates/jidr-cpio/src/cpio.rs`:

```rs
//! newc cpio archives (`070701`, and `070702` with checksums).
//!
//! Layout, per entry: a 110-byte ASCII header (6-byte magic + 13 fields of 8
//! hex digits), the NUL-terminated name, padding to a 4-byte boundary, the
//! data, padding to a 4-byte boundary. The archive ends with an entry named
//! `TRAILER!!!`; anything after it (usually zero padding) is kept as-is.

use std::io::Write;

use crate::{Error, Result};

pub const S_IFMT: u32 = 0o170_000;
pub const S_IFDIR: u32 = 0o040_000;
pub const S_IFREG: u32 = 0o100_000;
pub const S_IFLNK: u32 = 0o120_000;

const TRAILER: &str = "TRAILER!!!";
const HEADER_LEN: usize = 110;
const FIELDS: [&str; 13] = [
    "ino",
    "mode",
    "uid",
    "gid",
    "nlink",
    "mtime",
    "filesize",
    "devmajor",
    "devminor",
    "rdevmajor",
    "rdevminor",
    "namesize",
    "check",
];

/// Which newc variant the archive uses.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub enum Format {
    /// `070701`: the `check` field is unused (Android's mkbootfs writes this).
    #[default]
    Newc,
    /// `070702`: `check` is the 32-bit sum of the data bytes.
    NewcCrc,
}

impl Format {
    fn magic(self) -> &'static [u8; 6] {
        match self {
            Format::Newc => b"070701",
            Format::NewcCrc => b"070702",
        }
    }
}

/// One cpio entry. Every header field is kept so an unmodified archive
/// writes back byte-identical.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Entry {
    pub name: String,
    pub ino: u32,
    pub mode: u32,
    pub uid: u32,
    pub gid: u32,
    pub nlink: u32,
    pub mtime: u32,
    pub dev_major: u32,
    pub dev_minor: u32,
    pub rdev_major: u32,
    pub rdev_minor: u32,
    /// The raw `check` field of a `070701` entry, kept for byte-identical
    /// output. In `070702` archives the checksum is verified on parse and
    /// recomputed on write, and this stays 0.
    pub check: u32,
    pub data: Vec<u8>,
}

impl Entry {
    fn new(name: impl Into<String>, mode: u32, data: Vec<u8>) -> Self {
        Entry {
            name: name.into(),
            ino: 0,
            mode,
            uid: 0,
            gid: 0,
            nlink: 1,
            mtime: 0,
            dev_major: 0,
            dev_minor: 0,
            rdev_major: 0,
            rdev_minor: 0,
            check: 0,
            data,
        }
    }

    /// A regular file owned by root, with permission bits `perm` (e.g. `0o750`).
    pub fn file(name: impl Into<String>, perm: u32, data: impl Into<Vec<u8>>) -> Self {
        Entry::new(name, S_IFREG | (perm & 0o7777), data.into())
    }

    /// A directory owned by root.
    pub fn dir(name: impl Into<String>, perm: u32) -> Self {
        Entry::new(name, S_IFDIR | (perm & 0o7777), Vec::new())
    }

    /// A symlink; its data is the link target.
    pub fn symlink(name: impl Into<String>, target: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Entry::new(name, S_IFLNK | 0o777, target.into().into_bytes())
    }

    pub fn file_type(&self) -> u32 {
        self.mode & S_IFMT
    }

    pub fn is_file(&self) -> bool {
        self.file_type() == S_IFREG
    }

    pub fn is_dir(&self) -> bool {
        self.file_type() == S_IFDIR
    }

    pub fn is_symlink(&self) -> bool {
        self.file_type() == S_IFLNK
    }

    /// Permission bits, including setuid/setgid/sticky.
    pub fn permissions(&self) -> u32 {
        self.mode & 0o7777
    }

    fn fields(&self, namesize: u32, check: u32) -> Result<[u32; 13]> {
        let filesize = u32::try_from(self.data.len()).map_err(|_| Error::TooLarge {
            name: self.name.clone(),
        })?;
        Ok([
            self.ino,
            self.mode,
            self.uid,
            self.gid,
            self.nlink,
            self.mtime,
            filesize,
            self.dev_major,
            self.dev_minor,
            self.rdev_major,
            self.rdev_minor,
            namesize,
            check,
        ])
    }
}

/// A parsed newc archive: entries in archive order, the trailer entry and the
/// bytes that follow it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Archive {
    pub format: Format,
    entries: Vec<Entry>,
    trailer: Entry,
    tail: Vec<u8>,
}

impl Default for Archive {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Archive::new()
    }
}

impl Archive {
    /// An empty `070701` archive with a standard trailer and no padding.
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Archive {
            format: Format::Newc,
            entries: Vec::new(),
            trailer: Entry::new(TRAILER, 0, Vec::new()),
            tail: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Parses a whole archive. Bytes after the trailer are kept as the tail.
    pub fn parse(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self> {
        let mut format = None;
        let mut entries = Vec::new();
        let mut off = 0;
        loop {
            if off >= bytes.len() {
                return Err(Error::MissingTrailer);
            }
            let (entry, entry_format, next) = parse_entry(bytes, off)?;
            if *format.get_or_insert(entry_format) != entry_format {
                return Err(Error::BadMagic { offset: off });
            }
            off = next;
            if entry.name == TRAILER {
                let tail = bytes.get(off..).unwrap_or_default().to_vec();
                return Ok(Archive {
                    format: entry_format,
                    entries,
                    trailer: entry,
                    tail,
                });
            }
            entries.push(entry);
        }
    }

    /// Serializes the archive, recomputing `check` for [`Format::NewcCrc`].
    pub fn to_bytes(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
        let size = self
            .entries
            .iter()
            .map(|e| HEADER_LEN + e.name.len() + e.data.len() + 8)
            .sum::<usize>()
            + HEADER_LEN
            + 16
            + self.tail.len();
        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(size);
        self.write_to(&mut out)?;
        Ok(out)
    }

    pub fn write_to<W: Write>(&self, out: &mut W) -> Result<()> {
        let mut written = 0;
        for entry in self.entries.iter().chain(std::iter::once(&self.trailer)) {
            written += write_entry(out, self.format, entry, written)?;
        }
        out.write_all(&self.tail)?;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.entries.len()
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.entries.is_empty()
    }

    /// Entries in archive order, without the trailer.
    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &Entry> {
        self.entries.iter()
    }

    /// The entry the kernel ends up with for `name`. Names can repeat
    /// (mkbootfs writes `dev` twice) and the last one wins on unpack, so this
    /// returns the last match.
    pub fn get(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&Entry> {
        self.entries.iter().rev().find(|e| e.name == name)
    }

    pub fn get_mut(&mut self, name: &str) -> Option<&mut Entry> {
        self.entries.iter_mut().rev().find(|e| e.name == name)
    }

    pub fn contains(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        self.get(name).is_some()
    }

    /// Adds `entry`, or replaces the effective entry of the same name in
    /// place. A new entry with `ino == 0` gets the next free inode; a
    /// replacement keeps the inode of the entry it replaces. Returns the
    /// replaced entry.
    pub fn insert(&mut self, mut entry: Entry) -> Option<Entry> {
        if let Some(existing) = self.get_mut(&entry.name) {
            if entry.ino == 0 {
                entry.ino = existing.ino;
            }
            return Some(std::mem::replace(existing, entry));
        }
        if entry.ino == 0 {
            entry.ino = self.next_ino();
        }
        self.entries.push(entry);
        None
    }

    /// Removes every entry named `name`; returns the effective (last) one.
    pub fn remove(&mut self, name: &str) -> Option<Entry> {
        let last = self.entries.iter().rposition(|e| e.name == name)?;
        let removed = self.entries.remove(last);
        self.entries.retain(|e| e.name != name);
        Some(removed)
    }

    /// Renames the entry `from` to `to`, keeping its position and header.
    pub fn rename(&mut self, from: &str, to: &str) -> Result<()> {
        if from != to && self.contains(to) {
            return Err(Error::Exists(to.to_owned()));
        }
        let entry = self
            .get_mut(from)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::NotFound(from.to_owned()))?;
        entry.name = to.to_owned();
        Ok(())
    }

    /// One more than the largest inode in use (trailer included).
    pub fn next_ino(&self) -> u32 {
        self.entries
            .iter()
            .chain(std::iter::once(&self.trailer))
            .map(|e| e.ino)
            .max()
            .unwrap_or(0)
            .saturating_add(1)
    }

    /// The bytes after the trailer entry (usually zero padding).
    pub fn tail(&self) -> &[u8] {
        &self.tail
    }

    pub fn set_tail(&mut self, tail: Vec<u8>) {
        self.tail = tail;
    }
}

fn pad4(n: usize) -> usize {
    (4 - n % 4) % 4
}

fn slice<'a>(bytes: &'a [u8], start: usize, len: usize, what: &'static str) -> Result<&'a [u8]> {
    start
        .checked_add(len)
        .and_then(|end| bytes.get(start..end))
        .ok_or(Error::Truncated {
            offset: start,
            what,
        })
}

fn parse_hex(field: &[u8], offset: usize, name: &'static str) -> Result<u32> {
    let bad = || Error::BadHeader {
        offset,
        field: name,
    };
    let text = std::str::from_utf8(field).map_err(|_| bad())?;
    u32::from_str_radix(text, 16).map_err(|_| bad())
}

/// Parses the entry at `off`; returns it, its format and the offset of the next one.
fn parse_entry(bytes: &[u8], off: usize) -> Result<(Entry, Format, usize)> {
    let header = slice(bytes, off, HEADER_LEN, "a 110-byte cpio header")?;
    let format = match header.get(..6) {
        Some(b"070701") => Format::Newc,
        Some(b"070702") => Format::NewcCrc,
        _ => return Err(Error::BadMagic { offset: off }),
    };
    let mut f = [0u32; 13];
    for (i, (value, name)) in f.iter_mut().zip(FIELDS).enumerate() {
        let start = 6 + 8 * i;
        let digits = header.get(start..start + 8).ok_or(Error::Truncated {
            offset: off + start,
            what: "a cpio header field",
        })?;
        *value = parse_hex(digits, off + start, name)?;
    }
    let [
        ino,
        mode,
        uid,
        gid,
        nlink,
        mtime,
        filesize,
        dev_major,
        dev_minor,
        rdev_major,
        rdev_minor,
        namesize,
        check,
    ] = f;

    let name_off = off + HEADER_LEN;
    let raw_name = slice(bytes, name_off, namesize as usize, "a cpio entry name")?;
    let name = match raw_name.split_last() {
        Some((0, name)) => std::str::from_utf8(name)
            .map_err(|_| Error::BadName { offset: name_off })?
            .to_owned(),
        _ => return Err(Error::BadName { offset: name_off }),
    };
    let data_off = name_off + namesize as usize;
    let data_off = data_off + pad4(data_off);
    let data = slice(bytes, data_off, filesize as usize, "cpio entry data")?.to_vec();
    let next = data_off + data.len();
    let next = next + pad4(next);

    let check = match format {
        Format::Newc => check,
        Format::NewcCrc if checksum(&data) == check => 0,
        Format::NewcCrc => return Err(Error::Checksum { name }),
    };
    let entry = Entry {
        name,
        ino,
        mode,
        uid,
        gid,
        nlink,
        mtime,
        dev_major,
        dev_minor,
        rdev_major,
        rdev_minor,
        check,
        data,
    };
    // A short final padding run is tolerated: some writers stop at the data.
    Ok((entry, format, next.min(bytes.len())))
}

fn checksum(data: &[u8]) -> u32 {
    data.iter()
        .fold(0u32, |sum, &b| sum.wrapping_add(u32::from(b)))
}

/// Writes one entry starting at archive offset `at`; returns the bytes written.
fn write_entry<W: Write>(out: &mut W, format: Format, entry: &Entry, at: usize) -> Result<usize> {
    let namesize = u32::try_from(entry.name.len() + 1).map_err(|_| Error::TooLarge {
        name: entry.name.clone(),
    })?;
    let check = match format {
        Format::Newc => entry.check,
        Format::NewcCrc => checksum(&entry.data),
    };
    let mut header = Vec::with_capacity(HEADER_LEN + entry.name.len() + 4);
    header.extend_from_slice(format.magic());
    for value in entry.fields(namesize, check)? {
        header.extend_from_slice(format!("{value:08x}").as_bytes());
    }
    header.extend_from_slice(entry.name.as_bytes());
    header.push(0);
    header.resize(header.len() + pad4(at + header.len()), 0);
    out.write_all(&header)?;
    out.write_all(&entry.data)?;
    let end = at + header.len() + entry.data.len();
    let padding = pad4(end);
    out.write_all(&[0; 3][..padding])?;
    Ok(header.len() + entry.data.len() + padding)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn sample() -> Archive {
        let mut a = Archive::new();
        a.insert(Entry::dir("dev", 0o755));
        a.insert(Entry::file("init", 0o750, b"#!init".to_vec()));
        a.insert(Entry::symlink("bin", "system/bin"));
        a
    }

    #[test]
    fn round_trips_and_pads_to_four_bytes() {
        let a = sample();
        let bytes = a.to_bytes().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(bytes.len() % 4, 0);
        assert_eq!(Archive::parse(&bytes).unwrap(), a);
    }

    #[test]
    fn header_matches_the_newc_layout() {
        let mut a = Archive::new();
        a.insert(Entry::file("a", 0o644, b"xyz".to_vec()));
        let bytes = a.to_bytes().unwrap();
        let expected_header = b"070701\
            00000001000081a4000000000000000000000001000000000000000300000000\
            0000000000000000000000000000000200000000a\0";
        assert_eq!(&bytes[..112], &expected_header[..]);
        // 110 + 2 = 112 is aligned, so the data follows directly, then one byte of padding.
        assert_eq!(&bytes[112..116], b"xyz\0");
        assert_eq!(&bytes[116..122], b"070701");
    }

    #[test]
    fn keeps_trailer_fields_and_tail() {
        let mut a = sample();
        a.trailer.mode = 0o755;
        a.trailer.ino = 300_012;
        a.set_tail(vec![0; 208]);
        let bytes = a.to_bytes().unwrap();
        let parsed = Archive::parse(&bytes).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(parsed.trailer.ino, 300_012);
        assert_eq!(parsed.tail().len(), 208);
        assert_eq!(parsed.to_bytes().unwrap(), bytes);
    }

    #[test]
    fn duplicate_names_resolve_to_the_last_entry() {
        let mut a = Archive::new();
        a.insert(Entry::dir("dev", 0o755));
        a.entries.push(Entry::dir("dev", 0o700));
        assert_eq!(a.get("dev").unwrap().permissions(), 0o700);
        assert_eq!(a.remove("dev").unwrap().permissions(), 0o700);
        assert!(a.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn insert_replaces_in_place_and_keeps_the_inode() {
        let mut a = sample();
        let ino = a.get("init").unwrap().ino;
        let old = a.insert(Entry::file("init", 0o750, b"magiskinit".to_vec()));
        assert_eq!(old.unwrap().data, b"#!init");
        let names: Vec<_> = a.iter().map(|e| e.name.as_str()).collect();
        assert_eq!(names, ["dev", "init", "bin"]);
        assert_eq!(a.get("init").unwrap().ino, ino);
    }

    #[test]
    fn new_entries_get_fresh_inodes() {
        let mut a = sample();
        let inos: Vec<_> = a.iter().map(|e| e.ino).collect();
        assert_eq!(inos, [1, 2, 3]);
        a.trailer.ino = 50;
        a.insert(Entry::dir("overlay.d", 0o750));
        assert_eq!(a.get("overlay.d").unwrap().ino, 51);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rename_moves_an_entry_and_refuses_to_clobber() {
        let mut a = sample();
        a.rename("init", ".backup/init").unwrap();
        assert!(!a.contains("init"));
        assert!(a.contains(".backup/init"));
        assert!(matches!(a.rename("dev", "bin"), Err(Error::Exists(_))));
        assert!(matches!(a.rename("nope", "x"), Err(Error::NotFound(_))));
    }

    #[test]
    fn crc_format_checks_data() {
        let mut a = sample();
        a.format = Format::NewcCrc;
        let mut bytes = a.to_bytes().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(Archive::parse(&bytes).unwrap().format, Format::NewcCrc);
        let pos = bytes.windows(6).position(|w| w == b"#!init").unwrap();
        bytes[pos] = b'?';
        assert!(matches!(
            Archive::parse(&bytes),
            Err(Error::Checksum { .. })
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_garbage_without_panicking() {
        assert!(matches!(Archive::parse(b""), Err(Error::MissingTrailer)));
        assert!(matches!(
            Archive::parse(&[b'x'; 200]),
            Err(Error::BadMagic { offset: 0 })
        ));
        let mut bytes = sample().to_bytes().unwrap();
        bytes[8] = b'z';
        assert!(matches!(
            Archive::parse(&bytes),
            Err(Error::BadHeader { field: "ino", .. })
        ));
        let bytes = sample().to_bytes().unwrap();
        let cut = bytes.len() - 120;
        assert!(Archive::parse(&bytes[..cut]).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn missing_nul_in_name_is_an_error() {
        let mut bytes = sample().to_bytes().unwrap();
        // "dev\0" -> "devX"
        bytes[113] = b'X';
        assert!(matches!(
            Archive::parse(&bytes),
            Err(Error::BadName { offset: 110 })
        ));
    }
}

`crates/jidr-cpio/src/error.rs`:

```rs
/// Everything that can go wrong while reading, editing or writing a ramdisk.
#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum Error {
    #[error("truncated input at byte {offset}: expected {what}")]
    Truncated { offset: usize, what: &'static str },

    #[error("bad cpio magic at byte {offset} (expected 070701 or 070702)")]
    BadMagic { offset: usize },

    #[error("invalid hex in cpio header field `{field}` at byte {offset}")]
    BadHeader { offset: usize, field: &'static str },

    #[error("cpio entry name at byte {offset} is not NUL-terminated UTF-8")]
    BadName { offset: usize },

    #[error("cpio archive ends without a TRAILER!!! entry")]
    MissingTrailer,

    #[error("checksum mismatch for cpio entry `{name}`")]
    Checksum { name: String },

    #[error("`{name}` is too large for a cpio entry (limit 4 GiB)")]
    TooLarge { name: String },

    #[error("cpio entry `{0}` not found")]
    NotFound(String),

    #[error("cpio entry `{0}` already exists")]
    Exists(String),

    #[error("unknown compression format at byte {offset}")]
    UnknownFormat { offset: usize },

    #[error("{format} data is corrupt: {message}")]
    Corrupt {
        format: &'static str,
        message: String,
    },

    #[error("decompressed data exceeds the {limit}-byte limit")]
    Limit { limit: usize },

    #[error(transparent)]
    Io(#[from] std::io::Error),
}

pub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, Error>;

```

`crates/jidr-cpio/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! Ramdisk cpio (newc) reader/writer with gzip, lz4-legacy and xz support.
//!
//! Written clean-room from the public format descriptions: the newc cpio
//! header (`man 5 cpio`, the Linux `initramfs` buffer format), RFC 1952 for
//! gzip, the lz4 "legacy frame" in the lz4 frame-format document and the
//! `.xz` file format specification.
//!
//! An Android emulator `ramdisk.img` is several compressed streams
//! concatenated (a generic ramdisk, then vendor fragments), each holding one
//! cpio archive. [`Ramdisk`] splits and rebuilds that; [`Archive`] edits one
//! archive. An unmodified image writes back byte-identical, because every
//! header field, the trailer entry and the padding after it are kept, and
//! compression uses the reference implementations (liblz4 HC, zlib).
//!
//! ```no_run
//! # fn main() -> Result<(), jidr_cpio::Error> {
//! use jidr_cpio::{Entry, Ramdisk};
//!
//! let pristine = std::fs::read("ramdisk.img")?;
//! let mut ramdisk = Ramdisk::parse(&pristine)?;

`crates/jidr-cpio/src/ramdisk.rs`:

```rs
use crate::compress::{self, Compression};
use crate::{Archive, Entry, Error, Result};

/// One compressed stream of a ramdisk image and the cpio archive inside it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Segment {
    pub compression: Compression,
    pub archive: Archive,
}

impl Segment {
    pub fn to_bytes(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
        self.compression.compress(&self.archive.to_bytes()?)
    }
}

/// A ramdisk image: concatenated compressed cpio streams, as the emulator
/// ships them (generic ramdisk first, then vendor fragments). The kernel
/// unpacks them in order into one rootfs, so later segments override
/// earlier ones.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Ramdisk {
    pub segments: Vec<Segment>,
    /// Zero padding after the last stream, kept verbatim.
    pub trailing: Vec<u8>,
}

impl Ramdisk {
    pub fn parse(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self> {
        let mut segments = Vec::new();
        let mut off = 0;
        while let Some(rest) = bytes.get(off..).filter(|r| !r.is_empty()) {
            if !segments.is_empty() && rest.iter().all(|&b| b == 0) {
                return Ok(Ramdisk {
                    segments,
                    trailing: rest.to_vec(),
                });
            }
            let decoded = compress::decompress(rest).map_err(|e| at_offset(e, off))?;
            if decoded.consumed == 0 {
                return Err(Error::UnknownFormat { offset: off });
            }
            segments.push(Segment {
                compression: decoded.compression,
                archive: Archive::parse(&decoded.data)?,
            });
            off += decoded.consumed;
        }
        if segments.is_empty() {
            return Err(Error::Truncated {
                offset: 0,
                what: "a ramdisk stream",
            });
        }
        Ok(Ramdisk {
            segments,
            trailing: Vec::new(),
        })
    }

    pub fn to_bytes(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        for segment in &self.segments {
            out.extend_from_slice(&segment.to_bytes()?);
        }
        out.extend_from_slice(&self.trailing);
        Ok(out)
    }

    /// The entry the kernel ends up with for `name` (the last segment that
    /// has it wins), with the index of its segment.
    pub fn get(&self, name: &str) -> Option<(usize, &Entry)> {
        self.segments
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .rev()
            .find_map(|(i, s)| s.archive.get(name).map(|e| (i, e)))
    }
}

/// Makes stream-relative offsets in format errors absolute.
fn at_offset(error: Error, base: usize) -> Error {
    match error {
        Error::UnknownFormat { offset } => Error::UnknownFormat {
            offset: base + offset,
        },
        Error::Truncated { offset, what } => Error::Truncated {
            offset: base + offset,
            what,
        },
        other => other,
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn archive(names: &[&str]) -> Archive {
        let mut a = Archive::new();
        for name in names {
            a.insert(Entry::file(*name, 0o644, name.as_bytes().to_vec()));
        }
        a
    }

    #[test]
    fn concatenated_streams_split_and_rebuild() {
        let ramdisk = Ramdisk {
            segments: vec![
                Segment {
                    compression: Compression::gzip(),
                    archive: archive(&["extra"]),
                },
                Segment {
                    compression: Compression::lz4_legacy(),
                    archive: archive(&["init", "fstab"]),
                },
                Segment {
                    compression: Compression::lz4_legacy(),
                    archive: archive(&["fstab", "lib/modules"]),
                },
            ],
            trailing: vec![0; 12],
        };
        let bytes = ramdisk.to_bytes().unwrap();
        let parsed = Ramdisk::parse(&bytes).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(parsed, ramdisk);
        assert_eq!(parsed.get("fstab").unwrap().0, 2);
        assert_eq!(parsed.get("init").unwrap().0, 1);
        assert!(parsed.get("missing").is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn short_zero_padding_after_lz4_is_trailing_not_truncation() {
        // Regression: 1-3 zero bytes after an lz4 legacy stream were reported
        // as a truncated block size.
        for pad in 1..8 {
            let ramdisk = Ramdisk {
                segments: vec![Segment {
                    compression: Compression::lz4_legacy(),
                    archive: archive(&["init"]),
                }],
                trailing: vec![0; pad],
            };
            let bytes = ramdisk.to_bytes().unwrap();
            assert_eq!(Ramdisk::parse(&bytes).unwrap(), ramdisk, "pad {pad}");
        }
        let mut cut = Segment {
            compression: Compression::lz4_legacy(),
            archive: archive(&["init"]),
        }
        .to_bytes()
        .unwrap();
        cut.extend_from_slice(&[1, 0]);
        assert!(matches!(Ramdisk::parse(&cut), Err(Error::Truncated { .. })));
    }

    #[test]
    fn garbage_after_a_stream_is_an_error_with_its_offset() {
        // gzip members have an explicit end; lz4 legacy frames run to the next magic.
        let segment = Segment {
            compression: Compression::gzip(),
            archive: archive(&["init"]),
        };
        let mut bytes = segment.to_bytes().unwrap();
        let len = bytes.len();
        bytes.extend_from_slice(b"junkjunk");
        assert!(matches!(
            Ramdisk::parse(&bytes),
            Err(Error::UnknownFormat { offset }) if offset == len
        ));
        assert!(Ramdisk::parse(&[]).is_err());
        assert!(Ramdisk::parse(&[0; 16]).is_err());
    }
}

#!/bin/sh
# Regenerates the synthetic ramdisk fixtures with the reference tools, so the
# round-trip tests check jidr-cpio against them byte for byte. The content is
# our own (no Google files); output depends on the tool versions, so commit
# the results instead of regenerating in CI.
#
# Tools used for the committed files: bsdcpio 3.5.3 (libarchive 3.7.4, macOS),
# lz4 1.10.0, GNU-compatible gzip (macOS /usr/bin/gzip), xz 5.8.4.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

make_tree() {
    root=$1
    mkdir -p "$root/dev" "$root/proc" "$root/first_stage_ramdisk" "$root/system/bin"
    printf '#!/system/bin/sh\necho jidr fixture\n' > "$root/init"
    chmod 750 "$root/init"
    printf 'system /system ext4 ro wait\n' > "$root/first_stage_ramdisk/fstab.ranchu"
    chmod 640 "$root/first_stage_ramdisk/fstab.ranchu"
    ln -s /system/bin/sh "$root/system/bin/sh"
}

archive() {
    # Sorted names, fixed mtime: stable entry order and headers.
    (cd "$1" && find . -mindepth 1 | sed 's|^\./||' | LC_ALL=C sort | cpio -o -H newc --quiet)
}

make_tree "$tmp/a"
# 9 MiB of repetitive text: the lz4 legacy stream needs two 8 MiB blocks.
yes 'jidr ramdisk fixture line' | head -c 9437184 > "$tmp/a/system/big.txt"
find "$tmp/a" -exec touch -h -t 202610130000 {} +
archive "$tmp/a" > "$tmp/a.cpio"

lz4 -l -12 -f -q "$tmp/a.cpio" newc.cpio.lz4
gzip -n -6 -c "$tmp/a.cpio" > newc.cpio.gz
xz -9 --check=crc32 -T1 -c "$tmp/a.cpio" > newc.cpio.xz

# Emulator layout: two lz4 legacy streams back to back.
mkdir -p "$tmp/b/lib/modules"
printf 'module\n' > "$tmp/b/lib/modules/virtio.ko"
find "$tmp/b" -exec touch -h -t 202610130000 {} +
archive "$tmp/b" > "$tmp/b.cpio"
rm "$tmp/a/system/big.txt"
archive "$tmp/a" > "$tmp/a-small.cpio"
lz4 -l -12 -f -q "$tmp/a-small.cpio" "$tmp/1.lz4"
lz4 -l -12 -f -q "$tmp/b.cpio" "$tmp/2.lz4"
cat "$tmp/1.lz4" "$tmp/2.lz4" > two-streams.img

`crates/jidr-cpio/tests/properties.rs`:

```rs
// Test helpers outside #[test] fns aren't covered by clippy.toml's allow-*-in-tests.
#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]

use jidr_cpio::compress::{self, XzCheck};
use jidr_cpio::{Archive, Compression, Entry, Format, Ramdisk, Segment};
use proptest::prelude::*;

fn entry() -> impl Strategy<Value = Entry> {
    let name = "[a-z0-9_.]{1,12}(/[a-z0-9_.-]{1,12}){0,3}";
    let data = prop::collection::vec(any::<u8>(), 0..300);
    (name, 0u8..3, 0u32..0o7777, data, any::<u32>(), any::<u32>()).prop_map(
        |(name, kind, perm, data, uid, mtime)| {
            let mut e = match kind {
                0 => Entry::file(name, perm, data),
                1 => Entry::dir(name, perm),
                _ => Entry::symlink(name, String::from_utf8_lossy(&data).into_owned()),
            };
            e.uid = uid;
            e.mtime = mtime;
            e
        },
    )
}

fn archive() -> impl Strategy<Value = Archive> {
    (
        prop::collection::vec(entry(), 0..20),
        any::<bool>(),
        0usize..600,
    )
        .prop_map(|(entries, crc, tail)| {
            let mut a = Archive::new();
            if crc {
                a.format = Format::NewcCrc;
            }
            for e in entries {
                a.insert(e);
            }
            a.set_tail(vec![0; tail]);
            a
        })
}

fn compression() -> impl Strategy<Value = Compression> {
    prop_oneof![
        Just(Compression::None),
        (1u32..=9).prop_map(|level| Compression::Gzip {
            level,
            header: vec![0x1f, 0x8b, 8, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 3],
        }),
        prop_oneof![Just(1), Just(9), Just(12)].prop_map(|level| Compression::Lz4Legacy { level }),
        // Low presets keep the encoder's memory small; the default is tested elsewhere.
        (
            0u32..=2,
            prop_oneof![Just(XzCheck::Crc32), Just(XzCheck::Crc64)]
        )
            .prop_map(|(preset, check)| Compression::Xz { preset, check }),
    ]
}

proptest! {
    #![proptest_config(ProptestConfig::with_cases(128))]

    #[test]
    fn archives_round_trip(a in archive()) {
        let bytes = a.to_bytes().unwrap();
        prop_assert_eq!((bytes.len() - a.tail().len()) % 4, 0);
        let parsed = Archive::parse(&bytes).unwrap();
        prop_assert_eq!(&parsed, &a);
        prop_assert_eq!(parsed.to_bytes().unwrap(), bytes);
    }

    #[test]
    fn edits_keep_the_archive_valid(a in archive(), extra in entry(), victim in 0usize..20) {
        let mut a = a;
        let names: Vec<String> = a.iter().map(|e| e.name.clone()).collect();
        if let Some(name) = names.get(victim % names.len().max(1)) {
            a.remove(name);
            prop_assert!(!a.contains(name));
        }
        let name = extra.name.clone();
        a.insert(extra);
        let parsed = Archive::parse(&a.to_bytes().unwrap()).unwrap();
        prop_assert!(parsed.contains(&name));
        prop_assert_eq!(parsed, a);
    }

    #[test]
    fn compression_round_trips(data in prop::collection::vec(any::<u8>(), 0..20_000), c in compression()) {
        // Raw cpio has to look like cpio to be detected.
        let data = if c == Compression::None {
            Archive::new().to_bytes().unwrap()
        } else {
            data
        };
        let packed = c.compress(&data).unwrap();
        let out = compress::decompress(&packed).unwrap();
        prop_assert_eq!(out.data, data);
        prop_assert_eq!(out.consumed, packed.len());
        prop_assert_eq!(out.compression.name(), c.name());
    }

    #[test]
    fn ramdisks_of_lz4_segments_round_trip(archives in prop::collection::vec(archive(), 1..4), pad in 0usize..64) {
        let ramdisk = Ramdisk {
            segments: archives
                .into_iter()
                .map(|archive| Segment { compression: Compression::lz4_legacy(), archive })
                .collect(),
            trailing: vec![0; pad],
        };
        let bytes = ramdisk.to_bytes().unwrap();
        let parsed = Ramdisk::parse(&bytes).unwrap();
        prop_assert_eq!(parsed.to_bytes().unwrap(), bytes);
    }

    #[test]
    fn arbitrary_bytes_never_panic(bytes in prop::collection::vec(any::<u8>(), 0..2_000)) {
        let _ = Archive::parse(&bytes);
        let _ = Ramdisk::parse(&bytes);
        let _ = compress::decompress(&bytes);
    }

    #[test]
    fn corrupted_archives_never_panic(a in archive(), at in any::<prop::sample::Index>(), byte in any::<u8>()) {
        let mut bytes = a.to_bytes().unwrap();
        if !bytes.is_empty() {
            let i = at.index(bytes.len());
            bytes[i] = byte;
        }
        let _ = Archive::parse(&bytes);
    }
}

`crates/jidr-cpio/tests/roundtrip.rs`:

```rs
//! Byte-identical round-trips: decompress → parse → write → compress must
//! reproduce the input exactly, for fixtures made by the reference tools
//! (tests/fixtures/make.sh) and for every ramdisk in the local SDK.

// Test helpers outside #[test] fns aren't covered by clippy.toml's allow-*-in-tests.
#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use jidr_cpio::{Compression, Entry, Ramdisk};

fn fixture(name: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
    let path = Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))
        .join("tests/fixtures")
        .join(name);
    std::fs::read(&path).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("reading {}: {e}", path.display()))
}

fn assert_round_trip(bytes: &[u8]) -> Ramdisk {
    let ramdisk = Ramdisk::parse(bytes).unwrap();
    let written = ramdisk.to_bytes().unwrap();
    assert!(
        written == bytes,
        "round-trip differs ({} vs {} bytes)",
        written.len(),
        bytes.len()
    );
    ramdisk
}

#[test]
fn reference_lz4_legacy_with_two_blocks() {
    let bytes = fixture("newc.cpio.lz4");
    let ramdisk = assert_round_trip(&bytes);
    assert_eq!(ramdisk.segments.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(ramdisk.segments[0].compression, Compression::lz4_legacy());
    let big = ramdisk.segments[0].archive.get("system/big.txt").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(big.data.len(), 9 << 20);
}

#[test]
fn reference_gzip() {
    let ramdisk = assert_round_trip(&fixture("newc.cpio.gz"));
    assert!(matches!(
        ramdisk.segments[0].compression,
        Compression::Gzip { level: 6, .. }
    ));
}

#[test]
fn reference_xz() {
    let ramdisk = assert_round_trip(&fixture("newc.cpio.xz"));
    assert_eq!(ramdisk.segments[0].compression, Compression::xz());
}

#[test]
fn reference_archive_contents() {
    let ramdisk = assert_round_trip(&fixture("newc.cpio.lz4"));
    let archive = &ramdisk.segments[0].archive;
    let init = archive.get("init").unwrap();
    assert!(init.is_file());
    assert_eq!(init.permissions(), 0o750);
    assert_eq!(init.data, b"#!/system/bin/sh\necho jidr fixture\n");
    let sh = archive.get("system/bin/sh").unwrap();
    assert!(sh.is_symlink());
    assert_eq!(sh.data, b"/system/bin/sh");
    assert!(archive.get("dev").unwrap().is_dir());
}

#[test]
fn emulator_layout_of_concatenated_streams() {
    let ramdisk = assert_round_trip(&fixture("two-streams.img"));
    assert_eq!(ramdisk.segments.len(), 2);
    assert_eq!(ramdisk.get("init").unwrap().0, 0);
    assert_eq!(ramdisk.get("lib/modules/virtio.ko").unwrap().0, 1);
}

#[test]
fn magisk_style_edit_keeps_the_rest_byte_identical() {
    let bytes = fixture("two-streams.img");
    let mut ramdisk = Ramdisk::parse(&bytes).unwrap();
    let vendor_before = ramdisk.segments[1].to_bytes().unwrap();

    let first = &mut ramdisk.segments[0].archive;
    let original_init = first.get("init").unwrap().data.clone();
    first.insert(Entry::dir(".backup", 0o000));
    first.rename("init", ".backup/init").unwrap();
    first.insert(Entry::file("init", 0o750, b"new init".to_vec()));
    first.insert(Entry::dir("overlay.d", 0o750));
    first.insert(Entry::file("overlay.d/sbin/x.xz", 0o644, vec![1, 2, 3]));

    let patched = Ramdisk::parse(&ramdisk.to_bytes().unwrap()).unwrap();
    let first = &patched.segments[0].archive;
    assert_eq!(first.get(".backup/init").unwrap().data, original_init);
    assert_eq!(first.get("init").unwrap().data, b"new init");
    assert!(first.get("overlay.d").unwrap().is_dir());
    assert_eq!(patched.segments[1].to_bytes().unwrap(), vendor_before);
}

/// Every `ramdisk.img` under `$JIDR_TEST_SDK/system-images` (default: Android
/// Studio's SDK, opened read-only). Passes with a note when no SDK exists, so
/// the fixtures above carry the guarantee on CI.
#[test]
fn every_sdk_ramdisk_round_trips_byte_identically() {
    let sdk = std::env::var_os("JIDR_TEST_SDK")
        .map(PathBuf::from)
        .or_else(|| std::env::var_os("HOME").map(|h| PathBuf::from(h).join("Library/Android/sdk")));
    let Some(images) = sdk.map(|s| s.join("system-images")).filter(|p| p.is_dir()) else {
        println!("no SDK system-images found; skipping real-image round-trips");
        return;
    };
    let mut checked = Vec::new();
    for api in read_dirs(&images) {
        for tag in read_dirs(&api) {
            for abi in read_dirs(&tag) {
                let path = abi.join("ramdisk.img");
                if !path.is_file() {
                    continue;
                }
                let bytes = std::fs::read(&path).unwrap();
                let ramdisk = assert_round_trip(&bytes);
                println!(
                    "{}: {} segment(s), {}",
                    path.display(),
                    ramdisk.segments.len(),
                    ramdisk.segments[0].compression.name()
                );
                checked.push(path);
            }
        }
    }
    println!(
        "{} SDK ramdisk(s) round-tripped byte-identically",
        checked.len()
    );
}

fn read_dirs(dir: &Path) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
    let mut dirs: Vec<_> = std::fs::read_dir(dir)
        .map(|entries| {
            entries
                .filter_map(|e| e.ok().map(|e| e.path()))
                .filter(|p| p.is_dir())
                .collect()
        })
        .unwrap_or_default();
    dirs.sort();
    dirs
}

`crates/jidr-daemon/src/bundle.rs`:

```rs
//! `device.logs`: one zip with everything needed to debug a device.

use std::io::Write;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use jidr_core::{Device, ErrorCode, JidrResult, ResultExt};
use zip::write::SimpleFileOptions;

/// Writes `out` with the device record, its config, emulator and crash logs
/// and (when running) a logcat dump. Returns the number of files added.
pub fn write_bundle(
    out: &Path,
    device: &Device,
    avd_dir: &Path,
    log_dir: &Path,
    logcat: Option<&str>,
) -> JidrResult<usize> {
    if let Some(dir) = out.parent() {
        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir)
            .ctx(ErrorCode::Usage, format!("creating {}", dir.display()))?;
    }
    let file =
        std::fs::File::create(out).ctx(ErrorCode::Usage, format!("creating {}", out.display()))?;
    let mut zip = zip::ZipWriter::new(file);
    let opts = SimpleFileOptions::default().compression_method(zip::CompressionMethod::Deflated);
    let mut n = 0;
    let mut add =
        |zip: &mut zip::ZipWriter<std::fs::File>, name: &str, bytes: &[u8]| -> JidrResult<()> {
            zip.start_file(name, opts)
                .ctx(ErrorCode::Unexpected, "writing zip")?;
            zip.write_all(bytes)
                .ctx(ErrorCode::Unexpected, "writing zip")?;
            n += 1;
            Ok(())
        };
    let record = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(device).ctx(ErrorCode::Unexpected, "encoding device")?;
    add(&mut zip, "device.json", &record)?;
    for name in ["config.ini", "hardware-qemu.ini", "emu-launch-params.txt"] {
        if let Ok(bytes) = std::fs::read(avd_dir.join(name)) {
            add(&mut zip, &format!("avd/{name}"), &bytes)?;
        }
    }
    let mut logs: Vec<PathBuf> = std::fs::read_dir(log_dir)
        .map(|rd| {
            rd.flatten()
                .map(|e| e.path())
                .filter(|p| p.is_file())
                .collect()
        })
        .unwrap_or_default();
    logs.sort();
    for p in logs {
        if let (Some(name), Ok(bytes)) = (p.file_name().and_then(|n| n.to_str()), std::fs::read(&p))
        {
            add(&mut zip, &format!("logs/{name}"), &bytes)?;
        }
    }
    if let Some(text) = logcat {
        add(&mut zip, "logcat.txt", text.as_bytes())?;
    }
    let about = format!(
        "jidr {}\nos {} {}\ncreated {}\n",
        env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"),
        std::env::consts::OS,
        std::env::consts::ARCH,
        chrono::Utc::now()
    );
    add(&mut zip, "about.txt", about.as_bytes())?;
    zip.finish().ctx(ErrorCode::Unexpected, "finishing zip")?;
    Ok(n)
}

```
