```rs
//! Typed device tools: screenshot, touch, keys, UI dump. They reach the
//! emulator directly (gRPC + adb) using `device.connect_info`, like the player.

use std::time::Duration;

use jidr_adb::Adb;
use jidr_core::{ConnectInfo, ErrorCode, JidrError, JidrResult};
use jidr_proto::Controller;
use jidr_proto::control::{
    ImageFormat, KeyboardEvent, image_format::ImgFormat, keyboard_event::KeyEventType,
};

/// Screenshots are fitted in a box of this size (plan: PNG ≤ 1024 px).
pub const SHOT_BOX: u32 = 1024;

pub struct DeviceIo {
    pub info: ConnectInfo,
    pub adb: Adb,
}

impl DeviceIo {
    pub fn new(info: ConnectInfo) -> Self {
        let adb = Adb::new(&info.adb_path)
            .device(&info.adb_serial)
            .with_timeout(Duration::from_secs(60));
        Self { info, adb }
    }

    async fn grpc(&self) -> JidrResult<Controller> {
        Ok(
            jidr_backend::grpc::connect_port(self.info.grpc_port, &self.info.grpc_token)
                .await?
                .0,
        )
    }

    /// The current screen size in device pixels, rotation applied.
    pub async fn screen_size(&self) -> JidrResult<(u32, u32)> {
        let wm = self.adb.shell("wm size").await?;
        let (w, h) = parse_wm_size(&wm).ok_or_else(|| {
            JidrError::unexpected(format!("can't read the screen size from {wm:?}"))
        })?;
        let input = self
            .adb
            .shell("dumpsys input | grep -m1 SurfaceOrientation")
            .await
            .unwrap_or_default();
        let rotated = input
            .split(':')
            .nth(1)
            .and_then(|o| o.trim().parse::<u32>().ok())
            .is_some_and(|o| o % 2 == 1);
        Ok(if rotated { (h, w) } else { (w, h) })
    }

    /// PNG fitted in `SHOT_BOX`; returns (png, width, height).
    pub async fn screenshot(&self) -> JidrResult<(Vec<u8>, u32, u32)> {
        let mut c = self.grpc().await?;
        // ADR-0001: ask for width *and* height, or the emulator ignores the size.
        let fmt = ImageFormat {
            format: ImgFormat::Png as i32,
            width: SHOT_BOX,
            height: SHOT_BOX,
            ..Default::default()
        };
        let img = c
            .get_screenshot(fmt)
            .await
            .map_err(|s| jidr_backend::grpc::status_error("screenshot", s))?
            .into_inner();
        if img.image.is_empty() {
            return Err(JidrError::unexpected(
                "the display is off (empty screenshot); press_key Power to wake it",
            ));
        }
        let (w, h) = png_size(&img.image).unwrap_or((0, 0));
        Ok((img.image, w, h))
    }

    pub async fn tap(&self, x: u32, y: u32) -> JidrResult<()> {
        self.adb
            .shell(&format!("input tap {x} {y}"))
            .await
            .map(|_| ())
    }

    pub async fn swipe(&self, from: (u32, u32), to: (u32, u32), ms: u32) -> JidrResult<()> {
        self.adb
            .shell(&format!(
                "input swipe {} {} {} {} {ms}",
                from.0, from.1, to.0, to.1
            ))
            .await
            .map(|_| ())
    }

    /// Types into the focused field with `input text`. (gRPC `sendKey` text
    /// was flaky here: in the agent tests it sometimes dismissed the Settings
    /// search screen it was typing into; `input text` never did.)
    pub async fn type_text(&self, text: &str) -> JidrResult<()> {
        if text.is_empty() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        if !text.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii() && !c.is_ascii_control()) {
            return Err(JidrError::usage(
                "type_text supports printable ASCII; paste other text with command_run clipboard commands",
            ));
        }
        self.adb.shell(&input_text_command(text)).await.map(|_| ())
    }

    /// A key by its web name (`GoHome`, `GoBack`, `AppSwitch`, `Enter`, `Power`, …).
    pub async fn press_key(&self, key: &str) -> JidrResult<()> {
        let mut c = self.grpc().await?;
        let ev = KeyboardEvent {
            key: key.to_string(),
            event_type: KeyEventType::Keypress as i32,
            ..Default::default()
        };
        c.send_key(ev)
            .await
            .map_err(|s| jidr_backend::grpc::status_error("press_key", s))?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// The UI hierarchy as uiautomator XML.
    pub async fn ui_dump(&self) -> JidrResult<String> {
        let out = self
            .adb
            .shell("uiautomator dump /sdcard/jidr_ui.xml >/dev/null && cat /sdcard/jidr_ui.xml")
            .await?;
        let start = out.find("<?xml").or_else(|| out.find("<hierarchy"));
        match start {
            Some(i) => Ok(out[i..].trim().to_string()),
            None => Err(JidrError::new(
                ErrorCode::Unexpected,
                format!("uiautomator gave no hierarchy: {}", out.trim()),
            )),
        }
    }
}

/// `input text '<text>'` for the device shell: spaces become `%s` (how
/// `input text` spells them) and the argument is single-quoted.
pub fn input_text_command(text: &str) -> String {
    let arg = text.replace(' ', "%s").replace('\'', "'\\''");
    format!("input text '{arg}'")
}

/// `Physical size: 1080x2400` / `Override size: 720x1600` (override wins).
pub fn parse_wm_size(text: &str) -> Option<(u32, u32)> {
    let pick = |label: &str| {
        text.lines().find_map(|l| {
            let rest = l.trim().strip_prefix(label)?.trim();
            let (w, h) = rest.split_once('x')?;
            Some((w.trim().parse().ok()?, h.trim().parse().ok()?))
        })
    };
    pick("Override size:").or_else(|| pick("Physical size:"))
}

/// Width and height from a PNG's IHDR chunk.
pub fn png_size(png: &[u8]) -> Option<(u32, u32)> {
    if png.get(..8)? != b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n" || png.get(12..16)? != b"IHDR" {
        return None;
    }
    let w = u32::from_be_bytes(png.get(16..20)?.try_into().ok()?);
    let h = u32::from_be_bytes(png.get(20..24)?.try_into().ok()?);
    Some((w, h))
}

/// Scale from screenshot space to device pixels for a screen of `w`×`h`
/// fitted in `SHOT_BOX`.
pub fn shot_scale(w: u32, h: u32) -> f64 {
    let fit = (f64::from(SHOT_BOX) / f64::from(w.max(1)))
        .min(f64::from(SHOT_BOX) / f64::from(h.max(1)))
        .min(1.0);
    1.0 / fit
}

/// Maps a point given in screenshot space to device pixels, clamped.
pub fn to_device(p: (f64, f64), screen: (u32, u32)) -> (u32, u32) {
    let s = shot_scale(screen.0, screen.1);
    let clamp =
        |v: f64, max: u32| (v * s).round().clamp(0.0, f64::from(max.saturating_sub(1))) as u32;
    (clamp(p.0, screen.0), clamp(p.1, screen.1))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn input_text_is_shell_safe() {
        assert_eq!(input_text_command("battery"), "input text 'battery'");
        assert_eq!(input_text_command("hi there"), "input text 'hi%sthere'");
        assert_eq!(
            input_text_command("it's; rm -rf / & $(x)"),
            "input text 'it'\\''s;%srm%s-rf%s/%s&%s$(x)'"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn wm_size() {
        assert_eq!(
            parse_wm_size("Physical size: 1080x2400\n"),
            Some((1080, 2400))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            parse_wm_size("Physical size: 1080x2400\nOverride size: 720x1600"),
            Some((720, 1600))
        );
        assert_eq!(parse_wm_size("nope"), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn png_header() {
        let mut png = b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n\0\0\0\rIHDR".to_vec();
        png.extend(461u32.to_be_bytes());
        png.extend(1024u32.to_be_bytes());
        assert_eq!(png_size(&png), Some((461, 1024)));
        assert_eq!(png_size(b"GIF89a"), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn screenshot_space_maps_to_device_pixels() {
        // 1080×2400 fits 1024 tall: 460.8 wide, scale 2.34375.
        assert!((shot_scale(1080, 2400) - 2.34375).abs() < 1e-9);
        assert_eq!(to_device((230.0, 512.0), (1080, 2400)), (539, 1200));
        assert_eq!(
            to_device((5000.0, -3.0), (1080, 2400)),
            (1079, 0),
            "clamped"
        );
        // Small screens aren't upscaled.
        assert_eq!(shot_scale(720, 1000), 1.0);
    }
}
```

`crates/jidr-mcp/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! MCP server exposing Jidr to AI agents (`jidr mcp`, stdio).
//!
//! Generic tools cover every protocol command (`command_list`,
//! `command_run`, `jobs_*`); typed tools cover the hot paths of driving a
//! device (`screenshot`, `tap`, `swipe`, `type_text`, `press_key`, `ui_dump`,
//! `logcat_tail`) and of a proxy for security testing (`proxy_set`,
//! `proxy_clear`). Destructive commands follow D5.

pub mod device;

use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use base64::Engine;
use jidr_client::Client;
use jidr_core::provider::CommandSpec;
use jidr_core::{ConnectInfo, Device, JidrError, JidrResult};
use rmcp::model::{
    CallToolRequestParams, CallToolResponse, CallToolResult, ContentBlock, Implementation,
    JsonObject, ListToolsResult, PaginatedRequestParams, ServerCapabilities, ServerConfig, Tool,
    ToolAnnotations,
};
use rmcp::service::RequestContext;
use rmcp::{ErrorData as McpError, RoleServer, ServerHandler, ServiceExt};
use schemars::JsonSchema;
use serde::Deserialize;
use serde_json::{Value, json};

use crate::device::DeviceIo;

/// Methods that only make sense on a raw protocol connection.
const NOT_CALLABLE: &[&str] = &[
    "hello",
    "events.subscribe",
    "logcat.follow",
    "daemon.shutdown",
];
const DEFAULT_RUN_TIMEOUT_S: u64 = 900;
const UI_DUMP_LIMIT: usize = 400_000;
/// The Mac as the emulator sees it: where Burp or mitmproxy listens.
const PROXY_HOST: &str = "10.0.2.2";

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct McpOptions {
    /// Allow destructive commands on devices the agent doesn't own (D5).
    pub allow_destructive: bool,
}

pub struct JidrMcp {
    client: Arc<Client>,
    opts: McpOptions,
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for JidrMcp {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("JidrMcp")
            .field("opts", &self.opts)
            .finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

/// Serves MCP on stdin/stdout until the client disconnects.
pub async fn serve_stdio(client: Client, opts: McpOptions) -> JidrResult<()> {
    let service = JidrMcp::new(client, opts)
        .serve(rmcp::transport::stdio())
        .await
        .map_err(|e| JidrError::unexpected(format!("MCP initialize failed: {e}")))?;
    service
        .waiting()
        .await
        .map_err(|e| JidrError::unexpected(format!("MCP server: {e}")))?;
    Ok(())
}

// ---- tool params --------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct CommandListArgs {
    /// Only commands whose id starts with this, e.g. `device.`.
    #[serde(default)]
    prefix: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct CommandRunArgs {
    /// Command id from command_list, e.g. `device.start`.
    command: String,
    /// Params object matching the command's schema.
    #[serde(default)]
    params: Option<Value>,
    /// For long-running commands: wait at most this long (default 900 s),
    /// then return the job so it can be checked with jobs_list.
    #[serde(default)]
    timeout_s: Option<u64>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct JobsListArgs {
    /// Include finished jobs.
    #[serde(default)]
    all: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct JobArgs {
    /// Job id.
    job: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct DeviceArgs {
    /// Device name or id.
    device: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, Deserialize, JsonSchema, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
enum Coords {
    /// Pixels of the screenshot tool's image (default).
    #[default]
    Screenshot,
    /// Raw device pixels.
    Device,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct TapArgs {
    device: String,
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
    /// Coordinate space of x/y (default: the screenshot image).
    #[serde(default)]
    coords: Coords,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct SwipeArgs {
    device: String,
    x1: f64,
    y1: f64,
    x2: f64,
    y2: f64,
    /// Gesture duration in ms (default 300).
    #[serde(default)]
    duration_ms: Option<u32>,
    #[serde(default)]
    coords: Coords,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct TypeArgs {
    device: String,
    /// Text to type into the focused field (ASCII is reliable).
    text: String,
    /// Press Enter afterwards.
    #[serde(default)]
    enter: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct KeyArgs {
    device: String,
    /// `GoHome`, `GoBack`, `AppSwitch`, `Enter`, `Power`, `AudioVolumeUp`,
    /// `AudioVolumeDown`, `Tab`, `Backspace`, `ArrowUp`/`Down`/`Left`/`Right`.
    key: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct LogcatArgs {
    device: String,
    /// Number of recent lines (default 200).
    #[serde(default)]
    lines: Option<u32>,
    /// logcat filter specs, e.g. `["ActivityManager:I", "*:S"]`.
    #[serde(default)]
    filter: Vec<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct ProxyArgs {
    device: String,
    /// Proxy host as the device sees it (default `10.0.2.2`, this Mac).
    #[serde(default)]
    host: Option<String>,
    /// Proxy port, e.g. 8080 for Burp.
    port: u16,
}

fn schema<T: JsonSchema>() -> JsonObject {
    let mut v = serde_json::to_value(schemars::schema_for!(T))
        .unwrap_or_else(|_| json!({ "type": "object" }));
    if let Some(o) = v.as_object_mut() {
        o.remove("$schema");
        o.remove("title");
    }
    match v {
        Value::Object(o) => o,
        _ => JsonObject::new(),
    }
}

fn tool<T: JsonSchema>(name: &'static str, desc: &'static str, ann: ToolAnnotations) -> Tool {
    Tool::new(name, desc, Arc::new(schema::<T>())).with_annotations(ann)
}

fn read_only() -> ToolAnnotations {
    ToolAnnotations::new()
        .read_only(true)
        .destructive(false)
        .idempotent(true)
        .open_world(false)
}

fn interacts() -> ToolAnnotations {
    ToolAnnotations::new()
        .read_only(false)
        .destructive(false)
        .idempotent(false)
        .open_world(false)
}

fn idempotent() -> ToolAnnotations {
    ToolAnnotations::new()
        .read_only(false)
        .destructive(false)
        .idempotent(true)
        .open_world(false)
}

fn parse<T: serde::de::DeserializeOwned>(args: Option<JsonObject>) -> JidrResult<T> {
    jidr_core::provider::parse_params(Value::Object(args.unwrap_or_default()))
}

/// A Jidr error as a tool result the agent can read and act on.
fn tool_error(e: &JidrError) -> CallToolResult {
    let mut r = CallToolResult::error(vec![ContentBlock::text(format!(
        "{}: {}",
        e.code, e.message
    ))]);
    r.structured_content = Some(json!({ "code": e.code, "message": e.message, "data": e.data }));
    r
}

fn ok_json(v: Value) -> CallToolResult {
    let text = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&v).unwrap_or_default();
    let mut r = CallToolResult::success(vec![ContentBlock::text(text)]);
    r.structured_content = Some(if v.is_object() {
        v
    } else {
        json!({ "result": v })
    });
    r
}

impl JidrMcp {
    pub fn new(client: Client, opts: McpOptions) -> Self {
        Self {
            client: Arc::new(client),
            opts,
        }
    }

    pub fn tools() -> Vec<Tool> {

                ToolAnnotations::new()
                    .read_only(false)
                    .destructive(true)
                    .idempotent(false)
                    .open_world(false),
            ),
            tool::<JobsListArgs>(
                "jobs_list",

            ),

                    .read_only(false)
                    .destructive(false)
                    .idempotent(true)
                    .open_world(false),
            ),

                "Remove a running device's HTTP proxy.",
                idempotent(),

    }

    async fn specs(&self) -> JidrResult<Vec<CommandSpec>> {
        self.client.call_as("commands.list", json!({})).await
    }

    async fn device(&self, selector: &str) -> JidrResult<Device> {
        let d: Value = self
            .client
            .call("device.details", json!({ "device": selector }))
            .await?;
        serde_json::from_value(d["device"].clone())
            .map_err(|e| JidrError::unexpected(e.to_string()))
    }

    async fn io(&self, selector: &str) -> JidrResult<DeviceIo> {
        let info: ConnectInfo = self
            .client
            .call_as("device.connect_info", json!({ "device": selector }))
            .await?;
        Ok(DeviceIo::new(info))
    }

    /// D5: destructive commands need `--allow-destructive` or an agent-owned device.
    async fn check_policy(&self, spec: &CommandSpec, params: &Value) -> JidrResult<()> {
        if !spec.destructive || self.opts.allow_destructive {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let selector = params.get("device").and_then(Value::as_str);
        if let Some(sel) = selector
            && self.device(sel).await?.agent_owned
        {
            return Ok(());
        }
        Err(JidrError::usage(format!(
            "{} is destructive and {} isn't agent-owned; ask the user to run it, to start `jidr mcp --allow-destructive`, or to mark the device agent-owned (`jidr device edit <name> --agent-owned true`)",
            spec.id,
            selector.unwrap_or("the target")
        ))
        .with_data(json!({ "policy": "D5", "command": spec.id })))
    }

    async fn command_run(&self, args: CommandRunArgs) -> JidrResult<Value> {
        if NOT_CALLABLE.contains(&args.command.as_str()) {
            return Err(JidrError::usage(format!(
                "{} can't be called through MCP",
                args.command
            )));
        }
        let specs = self.specs().await?;
        let spec = specs.iter().find(|s| s.id == args.command).ok_or_else(|| {
            JidrError::usage(format!(
                "unknown command {}; see command_list",
                args.command
            ))
        })?;
        let mut params = args.params.unwrap_or_else(|| json!({}));
        // Devices an agent creates are its own (D5), unless it says otherwise.
        if spec.id == "device.create"
            && let Some(o) = params.as_object_mut()
        {
            o.entry("agent_owned").or_insert(json!(true));
        }
        self.check_policy(spec, &params).await?;
        let v = self.client.call(&spec.id, params).await?;
        let Some(job) = jidr_client::pending_job(&v) else {
            return Ok(v);
        };
        let deadline =
            Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(args.timeout_s.unwrap_or(DEFAULT_RUN_TIMEOUT_S));
        loop {
            let j = self
                .client
                .wait_job(job, Some(Duration::from_secs(5)))
                .await?;
            match j.state {
                jidr_core::JobState::Succeeded => return Ok(j.result.unwrap_or(Value::Null)),
                jidr_core::JobState::Failed => {
                    return Err(j
                        .error
                        .unwrap_or_else(|| JidrError::unexpected(format!("{} failed", spec.id))));
                }
                jidr_core::JobState::Cancelled => return Err(jidr_core::cancel::cancelled()),
                _ if Instant::now() >= deadline => {
                    return Ok(
                        json!({ "job": j, "pending": true, "note": "still running; check jobs_list or cancel with jobs_cancel" }),
                    );
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
    }

    async fn point(&self, io: &DeviceIo, x: f64, y: f64, coords: Coords) -> JidrResult<(u32, u32)> {
        match coords {
            Coords::Device => Ok((x.max(0.0).round() as u32, y.max(0.0).round() as u32)),
            Coords::Screenshot => Ok(device::to_device((x, y), io.screen_size().await?)),
        }
    }

    async fn dispatch(&self, name: &str, args: Option<JsonObject>) -> JidrResult<CallToolResult> {
        match name {
            "command_list" => {
                let a: CommandListArgs = parse(args)?;
                let specs: Vec<CommandSpec> = self
                    .specs()
                    .await?
                    .into_iter()
                    .filter(|s| a.prefix.as_deref().is_none_or(|p| s.id.starts_with(p)))
                    .collect();
                Ok(ok_json(json!({ "commands": specs })))
            }
            "command_run" => Ok(ok_json(self.command_run(parse(args)?).await?)),
            "jobs_list" => {
                let a: JobsListArgs = parse(args)?;
                Ok(ok_json(
                    json!({ "jobs": self.client.call("jobs.list", json!({ "all": a.all })).await? }),
                ))
            }
            "jobs_cancel" => {
                let a: JobArgs = parse(args)?;
                Ok(ok_json(
                    self.client
                        .call("jobs.cancel", json!({ "job": a.job }))
                        .await?,
                ))
            }
            "screenshot" => {
                let a: DeviceArgs = parse(args)?;
                let io = self.io(&a.device).await?;
                let (png, w, h) = io.screenshot().await?;
                let screen = io.screen_size().await.unwrap_or((w, h));
                let b64 = base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD.encode(&png);
                let note = format!(
                    "Screenshot {w}×{h} of a {}×{} screen (×{:.3} to device pixels). tap/swipe use this image's coordinates by default.",
                    screen.0,
                    screen.1,
                    device::shot_scale(screen.0, screen.1)
                );
                let mut r = CallToolResult::success(vec![
                    ContentBlock::image(b64, "image/png"),
                    ContentBlock::text(note),
                ]);
                r.structured_content = Some(
                    json!({ "width": w, "height": h, "screen": { "width": screen.0, "height": screen.1 } }),
                );
                Ok(r)
            }
            "tap" => {
                let a: TapArgs = parse(args)?;
                let io = self.io(&a.device).await?;
                let (x, y) = self.point(&io, a.x, a.y, a.coords).await?;
                io.tap(x, y).await?;
                Ok(ok_json(json!({ "tapped": { "x": x, "y": y } })))
            }
            "swipe" => {
                let a: SwipeArgs = parse(args)?;
                let io = self.io(&a.device).await?;
                let from = self.point(&io, a.x1, a.y1, a.coords).await?;
                let to = self.point(&io, a.x2, a.y2, a.coords).await?;
                io.swipe(from, to, a.duration_ms.unwrap_or(300).clamp(10, 10_000))
                    .await?;
                Ok(ok_json(
                    json!({ "swiped": { "from": [from.0, from.1], "to": [to.0, to.1] } }),
                ))
            }
            "type_text" => {
                let a: TypeArgs = parse(args)?;
                let io = self.io(&a.device).await?;
                io.type_text(&a.text).await?;
                if a.enter {
                    io.press_key("Enter").await?;
                }
                Ok(ok_json(json!({ "typed": a.text.chars().count() })))
            }
            "press_key" => {
                let a: KeyArgs = parse(args)?;
                self.io(&a.device).await?.press_key(&a.key).await?;
                Ok(ok_json(json!({ "pressed": a.key })))
            }
            "ui_dump" => {
                let a: DeviceArgs = parse(args)?;
                let mut xml = self.io(&a.device).await?.ui_dump().await?;
                if xml.len() > UI_DUMP_LIMIT {
                    let cut = (0..=UI_DUMP_LIMIT)
                        .rev()
                        .find(|i| xml.is_char_boundary(*i))
                        .unwrap_or(0);
                    xml.truncate(cut);
                    xml.push_str("\n<!-- truncated -->");
                }
                Ok(CallToolResult::success(vec![ContentBlock::text(xml)]))
            }
            "logcat_tail" => {
                let a: LogcatArgs = parse(args)?;
                let v = self
                    .client
                    .call("logcat.dump", json!({ "device": a.device, "lines": a.lines.unwrap_or(200), "filter": a.filter }))
                    .await?;
                Ok(CallToolResult::success(vec![ContentBlock::text(
                    v["text"].as_str().unwrap_or_default(),
                )]))
            }
            "proxy_set" => {
                let a: ProxyArgs = parse(args)?;
                let host = a.host.as_deref().unwrap_or(PROXY_HOST);
                Ok(ok_json(
                    self.client
                        .call(
                            "network.proxy.set",
                            json!({ "device": a.device, "host": host, "port": a.port }),
                        )
                        .await?,
                ))
            }
            "proxy_clear" => {
                let a: DeviceArgs = parse(args)?;
                Ok(ok_json(
                    self.client
                        .call("network.proxy.clear", json!({ "device": a.device }))
                        .await?,
                ))
            }
            other => Err(JidrError::usage(format!("unknown tool {other}"))),
        }
    }
}

impl ServerHandler for JidrMcp {
    fn get_info(&self) -> ServerConfig {
        ServerConfig::new(ServerCapabilities::builder().enable_tools().build())
            .with_server_info(Implementation::new("jidr", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")))
            .with_instructions(
                "Jidr runs Android emulators (optionally rooted). Typical loop: command_run device.list / \
                 device.create {name, image: \"35\"} / device.start, then screenshot → tap/swipe/type_text → \
                 ui_dump to find elements. command_list shows every command. Devices you create are yours to delete.",
            )
    }

    fn list_tools(
        &self,
        _request: Option<PaginatedRequestParams>,
        _context: RequestContext<RoleServer>,
    ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<ListToolsResult, McpError>> + Send + '_ {
        std::future::ready(Ok(ListToolsResult::with_all_items(Self::tools())))
    }

    async fn call_tool(
        &self,
        request: CallToolRequestParams,
        _context: RequestContext<RoleServer>,
    ) -> Result<CallToolResponse, McpError> {
        let name = request.name.to_string();
        if !Self::tools().iter().any(|t| t.name == name) {
            return Err(McpError::invalid_params(
                format!("unknown tool {name}"),
                None,
            ));
        }
        let started = Instant::now();
        let result = match self.dispatch(&name, request.arguments).await {
            Ok(r) => r,
            Err(e) => tool_error(&e),
        };
        tracing::debug!(tool = %name, ms = started.elapsed().as_millis() as u64, "tool call");
        Ok(CallToolResponse::Complete(result))
    }
}
```

`crates/jidr-mcp/tests/agent_tasks.rs`:

```rs
//! Five scripted agent tasks over MCP on a real emulator (in-process daemon
//! with the AOSP backend). Latency per tool is printed, not gated.
#![cfg(feature = "emulator")]
#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]

mod common;

use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use common::Mcp;
use jidr_core::{ImageRef, JidrPaths};
use jidr_daemon::{Daemon, DaemonConfig};
use jidr_mcp::McpOptions;
use rmcp::model::ContentBlock;
use serde_json::{Value, json};

fn test_sdk() -> PathBuf {
    std::env::var_os("JIDR_TEST_SDK")
        .map(PathBuf::from)
        .unwrap_or_else(|| {
            PathBuf::from(std::env::var("HOME").unwrap()).join("Library/Android/sdk")
        })
}

fn test_image() -> String {
    let abi = if cfg!(target_arch = "aarch64") {
        "arm64-v8a"
    } else {
        "x86_64"
    };
    let pkg = std::env::var("JIDR_TEST_IMAGE")
        .unwrap_or_else(|_| format!("system-images;android-31;google_apis;{abi}"));
    ImageRef::parse_package(&pkg).unwrap().package()
}

/// Reads attribute `name` of one `<node ...` fragment of a ui_dump.
fn attr(node: &str, name: &str) -> Option<String> {
    // The split leaves the first attribute without its leading space.
    let node = format!(" {node}");
    let start = node.find(&format!(" {name}=\""))? + name.len() + 3;
    let end = node[start..].find('"')? + start;
    Some(node[start..end].to_string())
}

/// Center (device px) of the first node matching `pred`.
fn find_node(xml: &str, pred: impl Fn(&str) -> bool) -> Option<(u32, u32)> {
    xml.split("<node ").skip(1).find_map(|node| {
        if !pred(node) {
            return None;
        }
        let b = attr(node, "bounds")?;
        let nums: Vec<u32> = b
            .split(|c: char| !c.is_ascii_digit())
            .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
            .filter_map(|s| s.parse().ok())
            .collect();
        match nums.as_slice() {
            [x1, y1, x2, y2] => Some(((x1 + x2) / 2, (y1 + y2) / 2)),
            _ => None,
        }
    })
}

/// Center (device px) of the first node whose text or content-desc equals `label`.
fn find(xml: &str, label: &str) -> Option<(u32, u32)> {
    find_node(xml, |node| {
        [attr(node, "text"), attr(node, "content-desc")]
            .iter()
            .flatten()
            .any(|v| v.eq_ignore_ascii_case(label))
    })
}

/// The app drawer's search field. Its label differs by image (Pixel
/// launcher on arm64, Launcher3 on the x86_64 CI images), so an agent
/// would fall back to "the text field" or "the thing with search in its id".
fn find_search_field(xml: &str) -> Option<(u32, u32)> {
    find(xml, "Search your phone and more")
        .or_else(|| find(xml, "Search apps"))
        .or_else(|| {
            find_node(xml, |node| {
                attr(node, "class").is_some_and(|c| c.ends_with("EditText"))
            })
        })
        .or_else(|| {
            find_node(xml, |node| {
                attr(node, "resource-id").is_some_and(|id| id.contains("search"))
            })
        })
}

/// Whether a text field has keyboard focus (the tap on the search field took).
fn text_field_focused(xml: &str) -> bool {
    xml.split("<node ").skip(1).any(|node| {
        attr(node, "class").is_some_and(|c| c.ends_with("EditText"))
            && attr(node, "focused").as_deref() == Some("true")
    })
}

/// The "Wait" button of an "… isn't responding" dialog, if one is up. On a
/// slow first boot the launcher can hang for a while (API 30 CI); an agent
/// taps Wait and carries on.
fn anr_wait(xml: &str) -> Option<(u32, u32)> {
    if xml.contains("isn't responding") {
        find(xml, "Wait")
    } else {
        None
    }
}

/// Taps Wait on an "isn't responding" dialog. True if there was one.
async fn dismiss_anr(mcp: &Mcp, dev: &str, xml: &str) -> bool {
    let Some((x, y)) = anr_wait(xml) else {
        return false;
    };
    mcp.ok(
        "tap",
        json!({ "device": dev, "x": x, "y": y, "coords": "device" }),
    )
    .await;
    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(2)).await;
    true
}

/// The start of a ui_dump, for a failure message.
fn excerpt(xml: &str) -> String {
    xml.chars().take(4000).collect()
}

/// Polls ui_dump for up to `secs` until `pred` holds, answering any "isn't
/// responding" dialog on the way. Err carries the last dump.
async fn poll_ui(
    mcp: &Mcp,
    dev: &str,
    secs: u64,
    pred: impl Fn(&str) -> bool,
) -> Result<String, String> {
    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(secs);
    loop {
        let r = mcp.call("ui_dump", json!({ "device": dev })).await;
        let xml = common::text(&r);
        if r.is_error != Some(true) && pred(&xml) {
            return Ok(xml);
        }
        if Instant::now() > deadline {
            return Err(xml);
        }
        dismiss_anr(mcp, dev, &xml).await;
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(800)).await;
    }
}

/// Goes home and swipes up until the app drawer shows `label` (one swipe
/// doesn't always open it). Returns the last dump.
async fn open_drawer(mcp: &Mcp, dev: &str, (w, h): (f64, f64), label: &str) -> String {
    mcp.ok("press_key", json!({ "device": dev, "key": "GoHome" }))
        .await;
    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(2)).await;
    let mut drawer = String::new();
    for _ in 0..4 {
        mcp.ok("swipe", json!({ "device": dev, "x1": w / 2.0, "y1": h * 0.85, "x2": w / 2.0, "y2": h * 0.2, "duration_ms": 400 })).await;
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(2)).await;
        drawer = common::text(&mcp.call("ui_dump", json!({ "device": dev })).await);
        if find(&drawer, label).is_some() {
            break;
        }
        dismiss_anr(mcp, dev, &drawer).await;
    }
    drawer
}

#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
async fn five_agent_tasks() {
    let tmp = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let paths = JidrPaths::under(tmp.path().join("j"));
    let daemon = Daemon::builder(
        DaemonConfig {
            paths: paths.clone(),
            studio_sdk: Some(test_sdk()),
            idle_timeout: None,
            sdk_repo: None,
        },
        Arc::new(jidr_backend::AospBackend::new()),
    )
    .build()
    .unwrap();
    let (stop_tx, stop_rx) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel::<()>();
    let serving = tokio::spawn(daemon.serve(async {
        let _ = stop_rx.await;
    }));
    while !paths.socket().exists() {
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20)).await;
    }
    let human = jidr_client::Client::connect(&paths.socket(), "test")
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let mcp = Mcp::connect(
        jidr_client::Client::connect(&paths.socket(), "mcp")
            .await
            .unwrap(),
        McpOptions::default(),
    )
    .await;
    // A per-process device name, a guard that kills its emulator however
    // the test ends, and cleanup of orphans from earlier killed runs.
    jidr_backend::testing::kill_orphans("agent-phone-");
    let dev_name = jidr_backend::testing::unique_avd("agent-phone");
    let dev = dev_name.as_str();
    let _guard = jidr_backend::testing::AvdGuard::new(dev);

    // Task 1: create and boot a device, then look at it.
    let t = Instant::now();
    let created = mcp
        // The default 4 GB profile: on 2 GB, API 31's first-boot background work
        // gets Settings' search process killed ("app died") mid-task.
        .ok(
            "command_run",
            json!({ "command": "device.create", "params": { "name": dev, "image": test_image() } }),
        )
        .await;
    assert_eq!(created["agent_owned"], true);
    let booted = mcp
        .ok(
            "command_run",
            json!({ "command": "device.start", "params": { "device": dev } }),
        )
        .await;
    assert_eq!(booted["status"]["state"], "running");
    let shot = mcp.call("screenshot", json!({ "device": dev })).await;
    let png = shot
        .content
        .iter()
        .find_map(|c| match c {
            ContentBlock::Image(i) => Some(i.data.clone()),
            _ => None,
        })
        .expect("an image");
    let sc = shot.structured_content.clone().unwrap();
    assert!(
        sc["width"].as_u64().unwrap() <= 1024 && sc["height"].as_u64().unwrap() <= 1024,
        "{sc}"
    );
    assert!(png.len() > 1000);
    println!(
        "task 1 (create, boot, screenshot): {:.1} s",
        t.elapsed().as_secs_f64()
    );

    // Task 2: open Settings from the app drawer, the way an agent would:
    // tap the icon, check that Settings came up, and try again if it didn't
    // (API 33 CI: one tap left Settings unopened for 30 s).
    let t = Instant::now();
    let size = (
        sc["width"].as_f64().unwrap(),
        sc["height"].as_f64().unwrap(),
    );
    let (w, h) = size;
    let mut settings = None;
    for attempt in 1..=3 {
        let drawer = open_drawer(&mcp, dev, size, "Settings").await;
        let (x, y) = find(&drawer, "Settings")
            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("no Settings icon:\n{}", excerpt(&drawer)));
        mcp.ok(
            "tap",
            json!({ "device": dev, "x": x, "y": y, "coords": "device" }),
        )
        .await;
        match poll_ui(&mcp, dev, 20, |xml| xml.contains("com.android.settings")).await {
            Ok(xml) => {
                settings = Some(xml);
                break;
            }
            Err(xml) => println!(
                "  task 2 attempt {attempt}: Settings didn't open; the screen:\n{}",
                excerpt(&xml)
            ),
        }
    }
    let settings = settings.expect("Settings never opened (screens above)");
    println!("task 2 (open Settings): {:.1} s", t.elapsed().as_secs_f64());

    // Task 3: type into a search field: the launcher's app search. (Settings'
    // own search lives in Settings Intelligence, which a freshly booted device
    // restarts during first-boot updates: "app died" mid-task. The launcher
    // stays up.) Like an agent: look, act, check, retry.
    let _ = settings;
    let t = Instant::now();
    let mut typed = None;
    for attempt in 1..=3 {
        mcp.ok("press_key", json!({ "device": dev, "key": "GoHome" }))
            .await;
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(1500)).await;
        // As in task 2, one swipe doesn't always open the drawer.
        let mut xml = String::new();
        let mut field = None;
        let mut last = String::new();
        for _ in 0..3 {
            mcp.ok("swipe", json!({ "device": dev, "x1": w / 2.0, "y1": h * 0.85, "x2": w / 2.0, "y2": h * 0.2, "duration_ms": 400 })).await;
            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(1500)).await;
            xml = common::text(&mcp.call("ui_dump", json!({ "device": dev })).await);
            field = find_search_field(&xml);
            if field.is_some() {
                break;
            }
            dismiss_anr(&mcp, dev, &xml).await;
        }
        if let Some((fx, fy)) = field {
            // Tap the field and wait for it to take focus before typing; a
            // tap on a busy first-boot launcher can be dropped (API 33 CI),
            // so an agent taps again.
            for _ in 0..2 {
                mcp.ok(
                    "tap",
                    json!({ "device": dev, "x": fx, "y": fy, "coords": "device" }),
                )
                .await;
                let focused = poll_ui(&mcp, dev, 6, text_field_focused).await;
                if let Err(x) = &focused {
                    last = x.clone();
                } else {
                    break;
                }
            }
            mcp.ok("type_text", json!({ "device": dev, "text": "clock" }))
                .await;
            for _ in 0..10 {
                let xml = common::text(&mcp.call("ui_dump", json!({ "device": dev })).await);
                last = xml.clone();
                // The field now holds the typed text (lowercase, unlike the "Clock" app label).
                if xml.contains("text=\"clock\"") {
                    typed = Some(xml);
                    break;
                }
                // First use of the launcher search asks "Always show keyboard
                // here?": answer it like an agent would, then type again.
                if xml.contains("Always show keyboard here?")
                    && let Some((bx, by)) = find(&xml, "Yes")
                {
                    mcp.ok(
                        "tap",
                        json!({ "device": dev, "x": bx, "y": by, "coords": "device" }),
                    )
                    .await;
                    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(1000)).await;
                    mcp.ok("type_text", json!({ "device": dev, "text": "clock" }))
                        .await;
                }
                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(700)).await;
            }
        }
        if typed.is_some() {
            break;
        }
        println!(
            "  task 3 attempt {attempt} didn't land (field found: {})",
            field.is_some()
        );
        if field.is_none() {
            println!("  drawer dump:\n{}", excerpt(&xml));
        } else {
            println!("  screen after typing:\n{}", excerpt(&last));
        }
    }
    let results = typed.expect("typing into the launcher search never showed the text");
    assert!(results.contains("Clock"), "the search lists the Clock app");
    println!(
        "task 3 (type into search): {:.1} s",
        t.elapsed().as_secs_f64()
    );

    // Task 4: read the device log.
    let t = Instant::now();
    let log = mcp.call("logcat_tail", json!({ "device": dev, "lines": 500, "filter": ["ActivityTaskManager:I", "ActivityManager:I", "*:S"] })).await;
    let log = common::text(&log);
    assert!(
        log.contains("ActivityTaskManager") || log.contains("ActivityManager"),
        "{}",
        &log[..log.len().min(2000)]
    );
    println!("task 4 (logcat): {:.1} s", t.elapsed().as_secs_f64());

    // Task 5: clean up under the D5 policy.
    let t = Instant::now();
    human
        .call(
            "device.create",
            json!({ "name": "humans", "image": test_image() }),
        )
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let e = mcp
        .err(
            "command_run",
            json!({ "command": "device.delete", "params": { "device": "humans" } }),
        )
        .await;
    assert_eq!(e["data"]["policy"], "D5");
    mcp.ok(
        "command_run",
        json!({ "command": "device.stop", "params": { "device": dev } }),
    )
    .await;
    mcp.ok(
        "command_run",
        json!({ "command": "device.delete", "params": { "device": dev } }),
    )
    .await;
    let jobs = mcp.ok("jobs_list", json!({ "all": true })).await;
    assert!(
        jobs["jobs"]
            .as_array()
            .unwrap()
            .iter()
            .all(|j| j["state"] == "succeeded")
    );
    let left: Value = human.call("device.list", json!({})).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        left.as_array().unwrap().len(),
        1,
        "only the human's device remains"
    );
    println!(
        "task 5 (stop, delete, policy): {:.1} s",
        t.elapsed().as_secs_f64()
    );

    mcp.report();
    let _ = stop_tx.send(());
    let _ = serving.await;
}
```

`crates/jidr-mcp/tests/common/mod.rs`:

```rs
//! An rmcp client talking to an in-process `JidrMcp` over a duplex pipe.
#![allow(dead_code)]

use std::time::Instant;

use jidr_mcp::{JidrMcp, McpOptions};
use rmcp::model::{CallToolRequestParams, CallToolResult, ContentBlock, Tool};
use rmcp::service::RunningService;
use rmcp::{RoleClient, ServiceExt};
use serde_json::Value;

pub struct Mcp {
    client: RunningService<RoleClient, ()>,
    _server: tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>,
    /// (tool, milliseconds) of every call, for the latency report.
    pub timings: std::sync::Mutex<Vec<(String, u128)>>,
}

impl Mcp {
    pub async fn connect(jidr: jidr_client::Client, opts: McpOptions) -> Self {
        let (server_io, client_io) = tokio::io::duplex(8 << 20);
        let server = tokio::spawn(async move {
            if let Ok(running) = JidrMcp::new(jidr, opts).serve(server_io).await {
                let _ = running.waiting().await;
            }
        });
        let client = ().serve(client_io).await.unwrap();
        Self {
            client,
            _server: server,
            timings: Default::default(),
        }
    }

    pub async fn tools(&self) -> Vec<Tool> {
        self.client.list_all_tools().await.unwrap()
    }

    /// Calls a tool; returns the result (errors are results with is_error).
    pub async fn call(&self, name: &str, args: Value) -> CallToolResult {
        let params = CallToolRequestParams::new(name.to_string())
            .with_arguments(args.as_object().cloned().unwrap_or_default());
        let t = Instant::now();
        let r = self.client.call_tool(params).await.unwrap();
        self.timings
            .lock()
            .unwrap()
            .push((name.to_string(), t.elapsed().as_millis()));
        r
    }

    /// A successful call's structured content.
    pub async fn ok(&self, name: &str, args: Value) -> Value {
        let r = self.call(name, args.clone()).await;
        assert_ne!(r.is_error, Some(true), "{name} {args} failed: {}", text(&r));
        r.structured_content.clone().unwrap_or(Value::Null)
    }

    /// A failed call's structured error `{code, message, data}`.
    pub async fn err(&self, name: &str, args: Value) -> Value {
        let r = self.call(name, args.clone()).await;
        assert_eq!(
            r.is_error,
            Some(true),
            "{name} {args} unexpectedly succeeded: {}",
            text(&r)
        );
        r.structured_content.clone().unwrap_or(Value::Null)
    }

    pub fn report(&self) {
        let t = self.timings.lock().unwrap();
        let mut by: std::collections::BTreeMap<&str, Vec<u128>> = Default::default();
        for (n, ms) in t.iter() {
            by.entry(n).or_default().push(*ms);
        }
        println!("MCP tool latency (ms), not gated:");
        for (n, mut v) in by {
            v.sort_unstable();
            println!(
                "  {n:<14} calls {:>3}  median {:>6}  max {:>6}",
                v.len(),
                v[v.len() / 2],
                v[v.len() - 1]
            );
        }
    }
}

/// All text content of a result.
pub fn text(r: &CallToolResult) -> String {
    r.content
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|c| match c {
            ContentBlock::Text(t) => Some(t.text.clone()),
            _ => None,
        })
        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        .join("\n")
}
```

```rs
//! MCP tools against the fake daemon: tool list, generic commands, D5 policy.
#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]

mod common;

use common::Mcp;
use jidr_daemon::testing::TestDaemon;
use jidr_mcp::McpOptions;
use serde_json::json;

async fn setup(opts: McpOptions) -> (tempfile::TempDir, TestDaemon, jidr_client::Client, Mcp) {
    let tmp = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let d = TestDaemon::start(tmp.path()).await.unwrap();
    let human = jidr_client::Client::connect(&d.paths.socket(), "test")
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let agent = jidr_client::Client::connect(&d.paths.socket(), "mcp")
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let mcp = Mcp::connect(agent, opts).await;
    (tmp, d, human, mcp)
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn tools_are_listed_with_annotations() {
    let (_t, d, _h, mcp) = setup(McpOptions::default()).await;
    let tools = mcp.tools().await;
    let names: Vec<&str> = tools.iter().map(|t| t.name.as_ref()).collect();
    for want in [
        "command_list",
        "command_run",
        "jobs_list",
        "jobs_cancel",
        "screenshot",
        "tap",
        "swipe",
        "type_text",
        "press_key",
        "ui_dump",
        "logcat_tail",
        "proxy_set",
        "proxy_clear",
    ] {
        assert!(names.contains(&want), "{want} missing from {names:?}");
    }
    for t in &tools {
        let a = t
            .annotations
            .as_ref()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{} has no annotations", t.name));
        assert!(
            a.read_only_hint.is_some()
                && a.destructive_hint.is_some()
                && a.open_world_hint.is_some(),
            "{}",
            t.name
        );
        assert_eq!(
            t.input_schema.get("type"),
            Some(&json!("object")),
            "{}",
            t.name
        );
        assert!(t.description.as_ref().is_some_and(|d| d.len() > 10));
    }
    let shot = tools.iter().find(|t| t.name == "screenshot").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        shot.annotations.as_ref().unwrap().read_only_hint,
        Some(true)
    );
    d.stop().await;
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn generic_commands_and_jobs() {
    let (_t, d, _h, mcp) = setup(McpOptions::default()).await;
    let list = mcp.ok("command_list", json!({ "prefix": "device." })).await;
    let cmds = list["commands"].as_array().unwrap();
    assert!(
        cmds.iter()
            .all(|c| c["id"].as_str().unwrap().starts_with("device."))
    );
    assert!(
        cmds.iter()
            .any(|c| c["id"] == "device.start" && c["longRunning"] == true)
    );

    let created = mcp
        .ok(
            "command_run",
            json!({ "command": "device.create", "params": { "name": "Bot", "image": "35" } }),
        )
        .await;
    assert_eq!(
        created["agent_owned"], true,
        "devices an agent creates are its own (D5)"
    );
    let started = mcp
        .ok(
            "command_run",
            json!({ "command": "device.start", "params": { "device": "Bot" } }),
        )
        .await;
    assert_eq!(started["status"]["state"], "running", "jobs are waited for");
    let logs = mcp
        .call("logcat_tail", json!({ "device": "Bot", "lines": 5 }))
        .await;
    assert!(common::text(&logs).contains("hello"));

    // A job still running at the timeout comes back as a job.
    let _gate = d.backend.gate_starts();
    mcp.ok(
        "command_run",
        json!({ "command": "device.stop", "params": { "device": "Bot" } }),
    )
    .await;
    let pending = mcp
        .ok(
            "command_run",
            json!({ "command": "device.start", "params": { "device": "Bot" }, "timeout_s": 1 }),
        )
        .await;
    assert_eq!(pending["pending"], true);
    let jobs = mcp.ok("jobs_list", json!({})).await;
    let job = jobs["jobs"][0]["id"].as_str().unwrap().to_string();
    mcp.ok("jobs_cancel", json!({ "job": job })).await;

    // Errors are tool results with a code the agent can act on.
    let e = mcp
        .err(
            "command_run",
            json!({ "command": "device.start", "params": { "device": "nope" } }),
        )
        .await;
    assert_eq!(e["code"], "not_found");
    let e = mcp
        .err(
            "command_run",
            json!({ "command": "device.start", "params": { "devise": "Bot" } }),
        )
        .await;
    assert_eq!(e["code"], "usage");
    let e = mcp
        .err("command_run", json!({ "command": "nope.nope" }))
        .await;
    assert!(e["message"].as_str().unwrap().contains("command_list"));
    for blocked in [
        "daemon.shutdown",
        "events.subscribe",
        "logcat.follow",
        "hello",
    ] {
        let e = mcp.err("command_run", json!({ "command": blocked })).await;
        assert!(
            e["message"].as_str().unwrap().contains("can't be called"),
            "{blocked}"
        );
    }
    let e = mcp.err("tap", json!({ "device": "Bot", "x": 1 })).await;
    assert_eq!(e["code"], "usage", "missing y");
    let e = mcp.err("proxy_set", json!({ "device": "Bot" })).await;
    assert_eq!(e["code"], "usage", "missing port");
    d.stop().await;
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn destructive_policy_d5() {
    let (_t, d, human, mcp) = setup(McpOptions::default()).await;
    // A device the user made: the agent may use it but not destroy it.
    human
        .call("device.create", json!({ "name": "Users", "image": "35" }))
        .await
        .unwrap();
    mcp.ok(
        "command_run",
        json!({ "command": "device.start", "params": { "device": "Users" } }),
    )
    .await;
    mcp.ok(
        "command_run",
        json!({ "command": "device.stop", "params": { "device": "Users" } }),
    )
    .await;
    for cmd in ["device.delete", "device.reset"] {
        let e = mcp
            .err(
                "command_run",
                json!({ "command": cmd, "params": { "device": "Users" } }),
            )
            .await;
        assert_eq!(e["data"]["policy"], "D5", "{cmd}: {e}");
    }
    // Its own device: allowed.
    mcp.ok(
        "command_run",
        json!({ "command": "device.create", "params": { "name": "Mine", "image": "35" } }),
    )
    .await;
    mcp.ok(
        "command_run",
        json!({ "command": "device.delete", "params": { "device": "Mine" } }),
    )
    .await;
    // Explicitly not agent-owned → refused even though the agent made it.
    mcp.ok("command_run", json!({ "command": "device.create", "params": { "name": "Shared", "image": "35", "agent_owned": false } })).await;
    mcp.err(
        "command_run",
        json!({ "command": "device.delete", "params": { "device": "Shared" } }),
    )
    .await;
    d.stop().await;

    // With --allow-destructive, anything goes.
    let (_t, d, human, mcp) = setup(McpOptions {
        allow_destructive: true,
    })
    .await;
    human
        .call("device.create", json!({ "name": "Users", "image": "35" }))
        .await
        .unwrap();
    mcp.ok(
        "command_run",
        json!({ "command": "device.delete", "params": { "device": "Users" } }),
    )
    .await;
    d.stop().await;
}

/// The MCPB bundle's manifest (packaging/mcp/manifest.json) lists the tools
/// for Claude Desktop and the registries; it must match what the server serves.
#[test]
fn mcpb_manifest_lists_every_tool() {
    let path = concat!(
        env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"),
        "/../../packaging/mcp/manifest.json"
    );
    let manifest: serde_json::Value =
        serde_json::from_str(&std::fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap()).unwrap();
    let mut listed: Vec<&str> = manifest["tools"]
        .as_array()
        .unwrap()
        .iter()
        .map(|t| t["name"].as_str().unwrap())
        .collect();
    let served = jidr_mcp::JidrMcp::tools();
    let mut served: Vec<&str> = served.iter().map(|t| t.name.as_ref()).collect();
    listed.sort_unstable();
    served.sort_unstable();
    assert_eq!(listed, served);
}
```

`crates/jidr-proto/build.rs`:

```rs
//! Generates the gRPC client/server code from the installed SDK emulator's
//! protos, falling back to the vendored copies in `proto/`.

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

const FILES: &[&str] = &["emulator_controller.proto", "snapshot_service.proto"];

fn sdk_proto_dir() -> Option<PathBuf> {
    if std::env::var_os("JIDR_PROTO_VENDORED").is_some_and(|v| v == "1") {
        return None;
    }
    let roots = ["ANDROID_SDK_ROOT", "ANDROID_HOME"]
        .iter()
        .filter_map(std::env::var_os)
        .map(PathBuf::from)
        .chain(std::env::var_os("HOME").map(|h| PathBuf::from(h).join("Library/Android/sdk")));
    roots.map(|r| r.join("emulator/lib")).find(|d| {
        FILES
            .iter()
            .chain(["snapshot.proto"].iter())
            .all(|f| d.join(f).is_file())
    })
}

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=JIDR_PROTO_VENDORED");
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=ANDROID_SDK_ROOT");
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=ANDROID_HOME");
    let vendored = Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("proto");
    let (dir, source) = match sdk_proto_dir() {
        Some(d) => (d, "sdk"),
        None => (vendored, "vendored"),
    };
    for f in FILES.iter().chain(["snapshot.proto"].iter()) {
        println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", dir.join(f).display());
    }
    println!("cargo:rustc-env=JIDR_PROTO_SOURCE={source}");
    println!("cargo:rustc-env=JIDR_PROTO_DIR={}", dir.display());
    let files: Vec<PathBuf> = FILES.iter().map(|f| dir.join(f)).collect();
    tonic_prost_build::configure()
        .build_server(true)
        .compile_protos(&files, &[dir])?;
    Ok(())
}
```

`crates/jidr-proto/proto/README.md`:

```md
# Vendored emulator protos

Fallback copies of the AOSP emulator's public gRPC definitions (Apache-2.0, © The Android Open Source Project), taken from Android Emulator 35.6.11 (`$ANDROID_SDK_ROOT/emulator/lib/`):

- `emulator_controller.proto`
- `snapshot_service.proto`
- `snapshot.proto`

`build.rs` prefers the protos shipped with the installed SDK emulator. It uses these copies when no SDK is found, or when `JIDR_PROTO_VENDORED=1` is set. Refresh them when the minimum supported emulator version changes.
```
