`crates/jidr-sdk/src/avd.rs`:

```rs
//! AVD lifecycle in Jidr's own AVD home (never `~/.android/avd`): create from a
//! profile + image, edit `config.ini`, clone, delete, factory reset.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use jidr_core::{ErrorCode, HardwareProfile, ImageRef, JidrError, JidrResult, ResultExt};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

/// `config.ini` with order, comments and `key=value` / `key = value`
/// formatting preserved, so a read → write round trip is byte-identical.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ConfigIni {
    lines: Vec<Line>,
    trailing_newline: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Line {
    Entry {
        key: String,
        sep: String,
        value: String,
    },
    Other(String),
}

impl ConfigIni {
    pub fn parse(text: &str) -> Self {
        let lines = text
            .lines()
            .map(|l| match l.split_once('=') {
                Some((k, v)) if !l.trim_start().starts_with('#') && !k.trim().is_empty() => {
                    let key = k.trim_end();
                    let ws_before = &k[key.len()..];
                    let value = v.trim_start();
                    let ws_after = &v[..v.len() - value.len()];
                    Line::Entry {
                        key: key.to_string(),
                        sep: format!("{ws_before}={ws_after}"),
                        value: value.to_string(),
                    }
                }
                _ => Line::Other(l.to_string()),
            })
            .collect();
        Self {
            lines,
            trailing_newline: text.ends_with('\n') || text.is_empty(),
        }
    }

    pub fn read(path: &Path) -> JidrResult<Self> {
        let text = std::fs::read_to_string(path)
            .ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, format!("reading {}", path.display()))?;
        Ok(Self::parse(&text))
    }

    pub fn write(&self, path: &Path) -> JidrResult<()> {
        let tmp = path.with_extension("ini.tmp");
        std::fs::write(&tmp, self.to_string())
            .ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, format!("writing {}", tmp.display()))?;
        std::fs::rename(&tmp, path).ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, format!("writing {}", path.display()))
    }

    pub fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&str> {
        self.lines.iter().rev().find_map(|l| match l {
            Line::Entry { key: k, value, .. } if k == key => Some(value.as_str()),
            _ => None,
        })
    }

    /// Updates the last occurrence of `key`, or appends it.
    pub fn set(&mut self, key: &str, value: impl Into<String>) {
        let value = value.into();
        for l in self.lines.iter_mut().rev() {
            if let Line::Entry {
                key: k, value: v, ..
            } = l
                && k == key
            {
                *v = value;
                return;
            }
        }
        let sep = self
            .lines
            .iter()
            .find_map(|l| match l {
                Line::Entry { sep, .. } => Some(sep.clone()),
                Line::Other(_) => None,
            })
            .unwrap_or_else(|| "=".into());
        self.lines.push(Line::Entry {
            key: key.to_string(),
            sep,
            value,
        });
    }

    pub fn remove(&mut self, key: &str) {
        self.lines
            .retain(|l| !matches!(l, Line::Entry { key: k, .. } if k == key));
    }

    pub fn entries(&self) -> BTreeMap<String, String> {
        self.lines
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|l| match l {
                Line::Entry { key, value, .. } => Some((key.clone(), value.clone())),
                Line::Other(_) => None,
            })
            .collect()
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Display for ConfigIni {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        for (i, l) in self.lines.iter().enumerate() {
            if i > 0 {
                f.write_str("\n")?;
            }
            match l {
                Line::Entry { key, sep, value } => write!(f, "{key}{sep}{value}")?,
                Line::Other(s) => f.write_str(s)?,
            }
        }
        if self.trailing_newline && !self.lines.is_empty() {
            f.write_str("\n")?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// What to create.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct AvdSpec {
    /// AVD id: `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, ≤ 64 chars.
    pub name: String,
    pub display_name: String,
    pub profile: HardwareProfile,
    pub image: ImageRef,
    /// Extra or overriding `config.ini` keys.
    pub overrides: BTreeMap<String, String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct AvdInfo {
    pub name: String,
    pub dir: PathBuf,
    pub display_name: Option<String>,
    pub image: Option<ImageRef>,
}

/// Files and directories that belong to a running or previous emulator
/// session and must not be cloned.
const RUNTIME_ENTRIES: &[&str] = &[
    "hardware-qemu.ini",
    "hardware-qemu.ini.lock",
    "multiinstance.lock",
    "bootcompleted.ini",
    "emu-launch-params.txt",
    "read-snapshot.txt",
    "snapshots",
    "tmpAdbCmds",
    "emulator-user.ini",
    "AVD.conf",
];

/// Files removed by a factory reset; the emulator recreates them from the
/// image on the next boot (same effect as `-wipe-data`).
const USER_DATA_ENTRIES: &[&str] = &[
    "userdata-qemu.img",
    "userdata-qemu.img.qcow2",
    "cache.img",
    "cache.img.qcow2",
    "encryptionkey.img",
    "encryptionkey.img.qcow2",
    "snapshots",
    "data",
    "modem_simulator",
    "bootcompleted.ini",
];

pub fn validate_name(name: &str) -> JidrResult<()> {
    let ok = !name.is_empty()
        && name.len() <= 64
        && !name.starts_with('.')
        && name
            .chars()
            .all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(c, '.' | '_' | '-'));
    if ok {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(JidrError::usage(format!(
            "invalid AVD name {name:?}: use 1–64 of A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ -, not starting with a dot"
        )))
    }
}

/// Manages AVDs under one AVD home.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct AvdManager {
    home: PathBuf,
}

impl AvdManager {
    pub fn new(home: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> Self {
        Self { home: home.into() }
    }

    pub fn home(&self) -> &Path {
        &self.home
    }

    pub fn dir(&self, name: &str) -> PathBuf {
        self.home.join(format!("{name}.avd"))
    }

    fn ini(&self, name: &str) -> PathBuf {
        self.home.join(format!("{name}.ini"))
    }

    pub fn exists(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        self.dir(name).join("config.ini").is_file()
    }

    fn require(&self, name: &str) -> JidrResult<PathBuf> {
        validate_name(name)?;
        if self.exists(name) {
            Ok(self.dir(name))
        } else {
            Err(JidrError::not_found(format!("AVD {name} does not exist")))
        }
    }

    /// The `config.ini` Jidr writes for a profile + image.
    pub fn config_for(spec: &AvdSpec) -> ConfigIni {
        let p = &spec.profile;
        let i = &spec.image;
        let cpu_arch = if i.abi.starts_with("arm64") {
            "arm64"
        } else {
            "x86_64"
        };
        let heap = if p.ram_mb >= 4096 { 512 } else { 256 };
        let mut c = ConfigIni::default();
        let entries: [(&str, String); 26] = [
            ("AvdId", spec.name.clone()),
            ("avd.ini.displayname", spec.display_name.clone()),
            ("avd.ini.encoding", "UTF-8".into()),
            ("abi.type", i.abi.clone()),
            ("hw.cpu.arch", cpu_arch.into()),
            ("hw.cpu.ncore", p.cpus.to_string()),
            ("hw.ramSize", p.ram_mb.to_string()),
            ("vm.heapSize", heap.to_string()),
            ("hw.lcd.width", p.width.to_string()),
            ("hw.lcd.height", p.height.to_string()),
            ("hw.lcd.density", p.density.to_string()),
            ("hw.gpu.enabled", "yes".into()),
            ("hw.gpu.mode", "auto".into()),
            ("hw.keyboard", "yes".into()),
            ("hw.mainKeys", "no".into()),
            ("hw.initialOrientation", "portrait".into()),
            ("hw.sdCard", "no".into()),
            ("image.sysdir.1", i.sysdir()),
            ("tag.id", i.tag.clone()),
            ("target", format!("android-{}", i.api)),
            ("PlayStore.enabled", i.tag.contains("playstore").to_string()),
            ("disk.dataPartition.size", format!("{}M", p.data_mb)),
            ("fastboot.forceColdBoot", "no".into()),
            ("showDeviceFrame", "no".into()),
            ("runtime.network.latency", "none".into()),
            ("runtime.network.speed", "full".into()),
        ];
        for (k, v) in entries {
            c.set(k, v);
        }
        for (k, v) in p.config.iter().chain(&spec.overrides) {
            c.set(k, v.clone());
        }
        c
    }

    pub fn create(&self, spec: &AvdSpec) -> JidrResult<AvdInfo> {
        validate_name(&spec.name)?;
        if self.exists(&spec.name) {
            return Err(JidrError::usage(format!(
                "AVD {} already exists",
                spec.name
            )));
        }
        let dir = self.dir(&spec.name);
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, format!("creating {}", dir.display()))?;
        Self::config_for(spec).write(&dir.join("config.ini"))?;
        self.write_pointer(&spec.name, spec.image.api)?;
        self.info(&spec.name)
    }

    /// `<home>/<name>.ini`, which the emulator uses to find the AVD dir.
    fn write_pointer(&self, name: &str, api: u32) -> JidrResult<()> {
        let mut ini = ConfigIni::default();
        ini.set("avd.ini.encoding", "UTF-8");
        ini.set("path", self.dir(name).to_string_lossy());
        ini.set("path.rel", format!("avd/{name}.avd"));
        ini.set("target", format!("android-{api}"));
        ini.write(&self.ini(name))
    }

    pub fn config(&self, name: &str) -> JidrResult<ConfigIni> {
        ConfigIni::read(&self.require(name)?.join("config.ini"))
    }

    /// Applies `changes` (value `None` removes the key).
    pub fn edit(
        &self,
        name: &str,
        changes: &BTreeMap<String, Option<String>>,
    ) -> JidrResult<ConfigIni> {
        self.ensure_stopped(name)?;
        let path = self.require(name)?.join("config.ini");
        let mut c = ConfigIni::read(&path)?;
        for (k, v) in changes {
            match v {
                Some(v) => c.set(k, v.clone()),
                None => c.remove(k),
            }
        }
        c.write(&path)?;
        Ok(c)
    }

    pub fn info(&self, name: &str) -> JidrResult<AvdInfo> {
        let dir = self.require(name)?;
        let c = ConfigIni::read(&dir.join("config.ini"))?;
        let image = c.get("image.sysdir.1").and_then(|s| {
            let parts: Vec<&str> = s.trim_end_matches('/').split('/').collect();
            match parts.as_slice() {
                ["system-images", api, tag, abi] => Some(ImageRef {
                    api: api.strip_prefix("android-")?.parse().ok()?,
                    tag: tag.to_string(),
                    abi: abi.to_string(),
                }),
                _ => None,
            }
        });
        Ok(AvdInfo {
            name: name.to_string(),
            display_name: c.get("avd.ini.displayname").map(str::to_string),
            image,
            dir,
        })
    }

    pub fn list(&self) -> JidrResult<Vec<AvdInfo>> {
        let Ok(rd) = std::fs::read_dir(&self.home) else {
            return Ok(Vec::new());
        };
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        for e in rd.flatten() {
            let file = e.file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
            if let Some(name) = file.strip_suffix(".avd")
                && validate_name(name).is_ok()
                && self.exists(name)
            {
                out.push(self.info(name)?);
            }
        }
        out.sort_by(|a, b| a.name.cmp(&b.name));
        Ok(out)
    }

    /// True if an emulator process currently holds this AVD.
    pub fn is_running(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        is_locked(&self.dir(name))
    }

    fn ensure_stopped(&self, name: &str) -> JidrResult<()> {
        if self.is_running(name) {
            return Err(JidrError::busy(format!(
                "AVD {name} is running; stop it first"
            )));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Copies an AVD, minus runtime state and snapshots (the clone cold-boots).
    /// The qcow2 overlays reference their backing files by relative name, so
    /// they stay valid in the new directory.
    pub fn clone_avd(&self, src: &str, dst: &str, display_name: &str) -> JidrResult<AvdInfo> {
        let from = self.require(src)?;
        validate_name(dst)?;
        self.ensure_stopped(src)?;
        if self.exists(dst) {
            return Err(JidrError::usage(format!("AVD {dst} already exists")));
        }
        let to = self.dir(dst);
        let result = copy_tree(&from, &to, RUNTIME_ENTRIES).and_then(|()| {
            let mut c = ConfigIni::read(&to.join("config.ini"))?;
            c.set("AvdId", dst);
            c.set("avd.ini.displayname", display_name);
            c.write(&to.join("config.ini"))?;
            let api = c
                .get("target")
                .and_then(|t| t.strip_prefix("android-"))
                .and_then(|a| a.parse().ok())
                .unwrap_or(0);
            self.write_pointer(dst, api)?;
            self.info(dst)
        });
        if result.is_err() {
            let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&to);
            let _ = std::fs::remove_file(self.ini(dst));
        }
        result
    }

    pub fn delete(&self, name: &str) -> JidrResult<()> {
        let dir = self.require(name)?;
        self.ensure_stopped(name)?;
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, format!("deleting {}", dir.display()))?;
        match std::fs::remove_file(self.ini(name)) {
            Err(e) if e.kind() != std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
                Err(JidrError::sdk(format!("deleting {}.ini: {e}", name)))
            }
            _ => Ok(()),
        }
    }

    /// Wipes user data; the next boot is a fresh first boot.
    pub fn factory_reset(&self, name: &str) -> JidrResult<()> {
        let dir = self.require(name)?;
        self.ensure_stopped(name)?;
        for entry in USER_DATA_ENTRIES {
            let p = dir.join(entry);
            let res = if p.is_dir() {
                std::fs::remove_dir_all(&p)
            } else {
                std::fs::remove_file(&p)
            };
            match res {
                Err(e) if e.kind() != std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
                    return Err(JidrError::sdk(format!("removing {}: {e}", p.display())));
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Bytes on disk used by the AVD (allocated blocks; images are sparse).
    pub fn disk_usage(&self, name: &str) -> JidrResult<u64> {
        Ok(disk_usage(&self.require(name)?))
    }
}

/// The emulator holds `hardware-qemu.ini.lock` (containing its pid) while
/// running. The file stays behind after exit, so the pid must be alive.
fn is_locked(dir: &Path) -> bool {
    let Ok(bytes) = std::fs::read(dir.join("hardware-qemu.ini.lock")) else {
        return false;
    };
    match lock_pid(&bytes) {
        Some(pid) => process_alive(pid),
        // An empty or garbled lock can't name a live process.
        None => false,
    }
}

/// The pid in a lock file: leading ASCII digits (the emulator pads the file
/// with NUL bytes).
fn lock_pid(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<u32> {
    let digits: String = bytes
        .iter()
        .skip_while(|b| b.is_ascii_whitespace())
        .take_while(|b| b.is_ascii_digit())
        .map(|b| *b as char)
        .collect();
    digits.parse().ok()
}

pub fn process_alive(pid: u32) -> bool {
    std::process::Command::new("kill")
        .args(["-0", &pid.to_string()])
        .stderr(std::process::Stdio::null())
        .status()
        .map(|s| s.success())
        .unwrap_or(false)
}

fn copy_tree(from: &Path, to: &Path, skip: &[&str]) -> JidrResult<()> {
    std::fs::create_dir_all(to).ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, format!("creating {}", to.display()))?;
    for e in std::fs::read_dir(from).ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, format!("reading {}", from.display()))? {
        let e = e.ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, "reading directory entry")?;
        let name = e.file_name();
        if skip.iter().any(|s| name == *s) || name.to_string_lossy().ends_with(".lock") {
            continue;
        }
        let (src, dst) = (e.path(), to.join(&name));
        let ty = e.file_type().ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, "reading file type")?;
        if ty.is_dir() {
            copy_tree(&src, &dst, &[])?;
        } else if ty.is_file() {
            // On APFS, std::fs::copy uses clonefile: instant and space-free.
            std::fs::copy(&src, &dst).ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, format!("copying {}", src.display()))?;
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub fn disk_usage(path: &Path) -> u64 {
    let Ok(meta) = std::fs::symlink_metadata(path) else {
        return 0;
    };
    let own = allocated(&meta);
    if !meta.is_dir() {
        return own;
    }
    std::fs::read_dir(path)
        .map(|rd| rd.flatten().map(|e| disk_usage(&e.path())).sum::<u64>())
        .unwrap_or(0)
        + own
}

#[cfg(unix)]
fn allocated(meta: &std::fs::Metadata) -> u64 {
    use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;
    meta.blocks() * 512
}

#[cfg(not(unix))]
fn allocated(meta: &std::fs::Metadata) -> u64 {
    meta.len()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    const STUDIO_STYLE: &str = "\
AvdId = Pixel_5_API_31
PlayStore.enabled = false
# a comment
abi.type = arm64-v8a
hw.lcd.width = 1080
image.sysdir.1 = system-images/android-31/google_apis/arm64-v8a/
odd=no-spaces
";

    #[test]
    fn config_ini_round_trips_byte_identical() {
        for text in [STUDIO_STYLE, "a=1\nb=2", "", "x = y\n\n\nz=w\n"] {
            assert_eq!(ConfigIni::parse(text).to_string(), text, "{text:?}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn config_ini_edits_preserve_style() {
        let mut c = ConfigIni::parse(STUDIO_STYLE);
        assert_eq!(c.get("hw.lcd.width"), Some("1080"));
        c.set("hw.lcd.width", "1440");
        c.set("hw.ramSize", "4096");
        c.remove("odd");
        let out = c.to_string();
        assert!(out.contains("hw.lcd.width = 1440\n"));
        assert!(out.ends_with("hw.ramSize = 4096\n"), "{out}");
        assert!(out.contains("# a comment\n"));
        assert!(!out.contains("odd"));
        assert_eq!(ConfigIni::parse(&out).get("hw.ramSize"), Some("4096"));
    }

    fn profile() -> HardwareProfile {
        crate::profiles::builtin().into_iter().next().unwrap()
    }

    fn spec(name: &str) -> AvdSpec {
        AvdSpec {
            name: name.into(),
            display_name: format!("{name} display"),
            profile: profile(),
            image: ImageRef {
                api: 31,
                tag: "google_apis".into(),
                abi: "arm64-v8a".into(),
            },
            overrides: BTreeMap::from([("hw.keyboard".to_string(), "no".to_string())]),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn create_edit_clone_reset_delete() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let m = AvdManager::new(dir.path());
        let info = m.create(&spec("a1")).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(info.image.as_ref().unwrap().api, 31);
        assert_eq!(m.create(&spec("a1")).unwrap_err().code, ErrorCode::Usage);
        let c = m.config("a1").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(c.get("hw.keyboard"), Some("no"), "overrides win");
        assert_eq!(c.get("hw.cpu.arch"), Some("arm64"));
        assert!(
            std::fs::read_to_string(dir.path().join("a1.ini"))
                .unwrap()
                .contains("a1.avd")
        );

        m.edit(
            "a1",
            &BTreeMap::from([
                ("hw.ramSize".into(), Some("3072".into())),
                ("hw.sdCard".into(), None),
            ]),
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(m.config("a1").unwrap().get("hw.ramSize"), Some("3072"));
        assert_eq!(m.config("a1").unwrap().get("hw.sdCard"), None);

        // Simulate a used AVD: user data, a stale lock from a dead process, snapshots.
        let d = m.dir("a1");
        std::fs::write(d.join("userdata-qemu.img"), b"data").unwrap();
        std::fs::write(d.join("hardware-qemu.ini.lock"), b"999999").unwrap();
        std::fs::create_dir_all(d.join("snapshots/default_boot")).unwrap();
        assert!(!m.is_running("a1"), "stale lock from a dead pid");

        let cl = m.clone_avd("a1", "a2", "Copy").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(cl.display_name.as_deref(), Some("Copy"));
        assert_eq!(m.config("a2").unwrap().get("AvdId"), Some("a2"));
        assert!(m.dir("a2").join("userdata-qemu.img").is_file());
        assert!(!m.dir("a2").join("snapshots").exists());
        assert!(!m.dir("a2").join("hardware-qemu.ini.lock").exists());
        assert_eq!(
            m.list()
                .unwrap()
                .iter()
                .map(|a| a.name.as_str())
                .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            ["a1", "a2"]
        );

        m.factory_reset("a1").unwrap();
        assert!(!d.join("userdata-qemu.img").exists());
        assert!(d.join("config.ini").exists());

        m.delete("a1").unwrap();
        m.delete("a2").unwrap();
        assert!(m.list().unwrap().is_empty());
        assert!(!dir.path().join("a1.ini").exists());
        assert_eq!(m.delete("a1").unwrap_err().code, ErrorCode::NotFound);
    }

    #[test]
    fn running_avd_is_protected() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let m = AvdManager::new(dir.path());
        m.create(&spec("busy")).unwrap();
        // Our own pid is alive.
        std::fs::write(
            m.dir("busy").join("hardware-qemu.ini.lock"),
            std::process::id().to_string(),
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert!(m.is_running("busy"));
        assert_eq!(m.delete("busy").unwrap_err().code, ErrorCode::Busy);
        assert_eq!(m.factory_reset("busy").unwrap_err().code, ErrorCode::Busy);
        assert_eq!(
            m.clone_avd("busy", "b2", "x").unwrap_err().code,
            ErrorCode::Busy
        );
    }

    /// Regression: real emulator lock files are NUL-padded after the pid;
    /// parsing failed and every stopped AVD looked busy.
    #[test]
    fn nul_padded_lock_files() {
        assert_eq!(lock_pid(b"12345\0\0\0\0"), Some(12345));
        assert_eq!(lock_pid(b" 42\n"), Some(42));
        assert_eq!(lock_pid(b"\0\0"), None);
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let m = AvdManager::new(dir.path());
        m.create(&spec("pad")).unwrap();
        let lock = m.dir("pad").join("hardware-qemu.ini.lock");
        std::fs::write(&lock, b"999999\0\0\0").unwrap();
        assert!(!m.is_running("pad"), "dead pid");
        let mut own = std::process::id().to_string().into_bytes();
        own.extend([0, 0, 0]);
        std::fs::write(&lock, own).unwrap();
        assert!(m.is_running("pad"), "live pid");
    }

    #[test]
    fn names_are_validated() {
        for bad in ["", ".hidden", "a b", "a/b", "x".repeat(65).as_str()] {
            assert_eq!(
                validate_name(bad).unwrap_err().code,
                ErrorCode::Usage,
                "{bad:?}"
            );
        }
        validate_name("Pixel_6.1-fhd").unwrap();
    }
}
```

`crates/jidr-sdk/src/cache.rs`:

```rs
//! Content-addressed download cache (D30): files are stored and looked up by
//! SHA-256, so a pinned Magisk APK is downloaded once, verified every time
//! and usable offline (`--magisk <path>` imports a local copy).

use std::io::Read;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::time::{Duration, SystemTime};

use jidr_core::{Cancel, ErrorCode, JidrError, JidrResult, ResultExt};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};

use crate::install::Fetcher;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct CacheEntry {
    pub sha256: String,
    pub path: PathBuf,
    pub size: u64,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct PruneReport {
    pub removed: usize,
    pub bytes: u64,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct DownloadCache {
    dir: PathBuf,
}

fn valid_hex(sha256: &str) -> JidrResult<String> {
    let h = sha256.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
    if h.len() == 64 && h.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_hexdigit()) {
        Ok(h)
    } else {
        Err(JidrError::usage(format!(
            "{sha256:?} is not a SHA-256 hex digest"
        )))
    }
}

/// SHA-256 of a file, streamed.
pub fn sha256_file(path: &Path) -> JidrResult<String> {
    let mut f =
        std::fs::File::open(path).ctx(ErrorCode::Usage, format!("opening {}", path.display()))?;
    let mut h = Sha256::new();
    let mut buf = vec![0u8; 1 << 20];
    loop {
        let n = f
            .read(&mut buf)
            .ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, format!("reading {}", path.display()))?;
        if n == 0 {
            break;
        }
        h.update(&buf[..n]);
    }
    Ok(hex::encode(h.finalize()))
}

impl DownloadCache {
    /// The cache under `paths.downloads()`.
    pub fn new(dir: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> Self {
        Self { dir: dir.into() }
    }

    fn root(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.dir.join("sha256")
    }

    /// Where a file with this hash lives (the extension is cosmetic).
    pub fn path_for(&self, sha256: &str, ext: Option<&str>) -> JidrResult<PathBuf> {
        let h = valid_hex(sha256)?;
        let name =
            match ext.filter(|e| !e.is_empty() && e.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric())) {
                Some(e) => format!("{h}.{e}"),
                None => h,
            };
        Ok(self.root().join(name))
    }

    /// A cached file with this hash, if present.
    pub fn get(&self, sha256: &str) -> JidrResult<Option<PathBuf>> {
        let h = valid_hex(sha256)?;
        let Ok(rd) = std::fs::read_dir(self.root()) else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        Ok(rd.flatten().map(|e| e.path()).find(|p| {
            p.file_name()
                .and_then(|n| n.to_str())
                .is_some_and(|n| n == h || n.split('.').next() == Some(h.as_str()))
        }))
    }

    /// A cached file with this hash whose content still matches it.
    pub fn get_verified(&self, sha256: &str) -> JidrResult<Option<PathBuf>> {
        let Some(p) = self.get(sha256)? else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        if sha256_file(&p)? == valid_hex(sha256)? {
            Ok(Some(p))
        } else {
            tracing::warn!(path = %p.display(), "corrupt cache entry removed");
            let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&p);
            Ok(None)
        }
    }

    /// Downloads `url` unless a verified copy is cached; the content must hash
    /// to `sha256` or nothing is stored.
    pub async fn fetch(
        &self,
        fetcher: &Fetcher,
        url: &str,
        sha256: &str,
        on_bytes: &(dyn Fn(u64, u64) + Send + Sync),
        cancel: &Cancel,
    ) -> JidrResult<PathBuf> {
        let want = valid_hex(sha256)?;
        if let Some(p) = self.get_verified(&want)? {
            return Ok(p);
        }
        std::fs::create_dir_all(self.root()).ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, "creating download cache")?;
        let ext = Path::new(url.split(['?', '#']).next().unwrap_or(url))
            .extension()
            .and_then(|e| e.to_str())
            .map(str::to_string);
        let tmp = self.root().join(format!(".{}.part", uuid::Uuid::new_v4()));
        let result = fetcher.download(url, &tmp, on_bytes, cancel).await;
        let digests = match result {
            Ok(d) => d,
            Err(e) => {
                let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&tmp);
                return Err(e);
            }
        };
        if digests.sha256 != want {
            let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&tmp);
            return Err(JidrError::sdk(format!(
                "checksum mismatch for {url}: expected sha256 {want}, got {}",
                digests.sha256
            )));
        }
        let dest = self.path_for(&want, ext.as_deref())?;
        std::fs::rename(&tmp, &dest).ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, "storing download")?;
        Ok(dest)
    }

    /// Copies a local file into the cache (offline installs). If `expected`
    /// is given, the file must hash to it.
    pub fn import(&self, path: &Path, expected: Option<&str>) -> JidrResult<CacheEntry> {
        let actual = sha256_file(path)?;
        if let Some(e) = expected {
            let e = valid_hex(e)?;
            if e != actual {
                return Err(JidrError::usage(format!(
                    "{} has sha256 {actual}, expected {e}",
                    path.display()
                )));
            }
        }
        std::fs::create_dir_all(self.root()).ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, "creating download cache")?;
        let ext = path.extension().and_then(|e| e.to_str());
        let dest = match self.get(&actual)? {
            Some(p) => p,
            None => {
                let dest = self.path_for(&actual, ext)?;
                let tmp = self.root().join(format!(".{}.part", uuid::Uuid::new_v4()));
                std::fs::copy(path, &tmp)
                    .ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, format!("copying {}", path.display()))?;
                std::fs::rename(&tmp, &dest).ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, "storing import")?;
                dest
            }
        };
        let size = std::fs::metadata(&dest).map(|m| m.len()).unwrap_or(0);
        Ok(CacheEntry {
            sha256: actual,
            path: dest,
            size,
        })
    }

    pub fn list(&self) -> Vec<CacheEntry> {
        let Ok(rd) = std::fs::read_dir(self.root()) else {
            return Vec::new();
        };
        let mut out: Vec<CacheEntry> = rd
            .flatten()
            .filter_map(|e| {
                let path = e.path();
                let name = path.file_name()?.to_str()?.to_string();
                let sha256 = name.split('.').next()?.to_string();
                valid_hex(&sha256).ok()?;
                Some(CacheEntry {
                    size: e.metadata().map(|m| m.len()).unwrap_or(0),
                    sha256,
                    path,
                })
            })
            .collect();
        out.sort_by(|a, b| a.sha256.cmp(&b.sha256));
        out
    }

    /// Removes entries (and stale partial downloads) not modified within
    /// `older_than`; `None` removes everything.
    pub fn prune(&self, older_than: Option<Duration>) -> PruneReport {
        let mut report = PruneReport::default();
        let Ok(rd) = std::fs::read_dir(self.root()) else {
            return report;
        };
        let now = SystemTime::now();
        for e in rd.flatten() {
            let Ok(meta) = e.metadata() else { continue };
            let old_enough = match older_than {
                None => true,
                Some(age) => meta
                    .modified()
                    .ok()
                    .and_then(|m| now.duration_since(m).ok())
                    .is_some_and(|d| d >= age),
            };
            if old_enough && meta.is_file() && std::fs::remove_file(e.path()).is_ok() {
                report.removed += 1;
                report.bytes += meta.len();
            }
        }
        report
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn sha(b: &[u8]) -> String {
        hex::encode(Sha256::digest(b))
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn fetch_verifies_and_reuses() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let src = dir.path().join("Magisk-v27.0.apk");
        std::fs::write(&src, b"magisk bytes").unwrap();
        let url = format!("file://{}", src.display());
        let cache = DownloadCache::new(dir.path().join("cache"));
        let f = Fetcher::new().unwrap();
        let p = cache
            .fetch(&f, &url, &sha(b"magisk bytes"), &|_, _| {}, &Cancel::new())
            .await
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&p).unwrap(), b"magisk bytes");
        assert_eq!(p.extension().unwrap(), "apk");
        // Second fetch is served from the cache even if the source is gone.
        std::fs::remove_file(&src).unwrap();
        let again = cache
            .fetch(&f, &url, &sha(b"magisk bytes"), &|_, _| {}, &Cancel::new())
            .await
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(again, p);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn wrong_hash_stores_nothing() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let src = dir.path().join("x.apk");
        std::fs::write(&src, b"tampered").unwrap();
        let cache = DownloadCache::new(dir.path().join("cache"));
        let err = cache
            .fetch(
                &Fetcher::new().unwrap(),
                &format!("file://{}", src.display()),
                &sha(b"original"),
                &|_, _| {},
                &Cancel::new(),
            )
            .await
            .unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.message.contains("checksum mismatch"), "{err}");
        assert!(cache.list().is_empty());
        assert_eq!(cache.prune(None).removed, 0, "no partial file left");
    }

    #[test]
    fn import_get_list_prune() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let src = dir.path().join("local.apk");
        std::fs::write(&src, b"offline").unwrap();
        let cache = DownloadCache::new(dir.path().join("cache"));
        assert_eq!(
            cache.import(&src, Some(&sha(b"other"))).unwrap_err().code,
            ErrorCode::Usage
        );
        let e = cache.import(&src, Some(&sha(b"offline"))).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(e.sha256, sha(b"offline"));
        assert_eq!(cache.import(&src, None).unwrap().path, e.path, "idempotent");
        assert_eq!(cache.get(&e.sha256).unwrap(), Some(e.path.clone()));
        assert_eq!(cache.list().len(), 1);

        // A corrupted entry is detected and dropped.
        std::fs::write(&e.path, b"bitrot").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(cache.get_verified(&e.sha256).unwrap(), None);
        assert!(cache.list().is_empty());

        cache.import(&src, None).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            cache.prune(Some(Duration::from_secs(3600))).removed,
            0,
            "too new"
        );
        let r = cache.prune(None);
        assert_eq!((r.removed, r.bytes), (1, 7));
        assert!(cache.get("nothex").is_err());
    }
}
```

```rs
//! The system-image catalog shown to users: remote listings merged with what
//! is installed, filtered to the host ABI and the supported API range (D23).

use std::collections::BTreeMap;

use jidr_core::{ImageRef, Support, SystemImage};

use crate::repo::Repository;
use crate::sdk::{Sdk, SdkSet};

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct CatalogFilter {
    /// Only images with this ABI (the host ABI by default).
    pub abi: String,
    /// Include API 28 (best effort).
    pub include_best_effort: bool,
    /// Highest channel to include (0 = stable).
    pub max_channel: u32,
}

impl Default for CatalogFilter {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            abi: crate::host::host_abi().to_string(),
            include_best_effort: true,
            max_channel: 0,
        }
    }
}

impl CatalogFilter {
    fn accepts(&self, image: &ImageRef) -> bool {
        image.abi == self.abi
            && match Support::for_api(image.api) {
                Support::Supported => true,
                Support::BestEffort => self.include_best_effort,
                Support::Unsupported => false,
            }
    }
}

/// Builds the catalog. `repo` may be empty (offline): installed images still show.
pub fn image_catalog(repo: &Repository, sdks: &SdkSet, filter: &CatalogFilter) -> Vec<SystemImage> {
    let mut by_ref: BTreeMap<ImageRef, SystemImage> = BTreeMap::new();
    for pkg in repo
        .packages
        .iter()
        .filter(|p| p.channel <= filter.max_channel)
    {
        let Some(image) = &pkg.image else { continue };
        if !filter.accepts(image) {
            continue;
        }
        let newer = by_ref.get(image).is_none_or(|cur| {
            crate::repo::Revision::parse(&cur.revision).is_none_or(|r| pkg.revision > r)
        });
        if newer {
            by_ref.insert(
                image.clone(),
                SystemImage {
                    image: image.clone(),
                    display: pkg.display.clone(),
                    revision: pkg.revision.to_string(),
                    support: Support::for_api(image.api),
                    size: pkg.archive_for_host().map(|a| a.size).unwrap_or(0),
                    license: pkg.license.clone(),
                    installed_in: None,
                    pristine_ramdisk_sha256: None,
                },
            );
        }
    }
    // Installed images, including ones no longer listed remotely.
    for sdk in std::iter::once(&sdks.private).chain(sdks.studio.as_ref()) {
        for image in sdk
            .installed_images()
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|i| filter.accepts(i))
        {
            let entry = by_ref.entry(image.clone()).or_insert_with(|| SystemImage {
                display: format!("Android API {} ({})", image.api, image.tag),
                revision: String::new(),
                support: Support::for_api(image.api),
                size: 0,
                license: None,
                installed_in: None,
                pristine_ramdisk_sha256: None,
                image,
            });
            if entry.installed_in.is_none() {
                entry.installed_in = Some(sdk.root.clone());
                // G14: the SDK's ramdisk is never modified (the root engine
                // patches a per-device copy), so this is the pristine hash.
                entry.pristine_ramdisk_sha256 = ramdisk_sha256(sdk, &entry.image);
            }
        }
    }
    by_ref.into_values().rev().collect()
}

/// SHA-256 of `ramdisk.img` in `sdk`'s copy of `image`.
fn ramdisk_sha256(sdk: &Sdk, image: &ImageRef) -> Option<String> {
    crate::cache::sha256_file(&sdk.image_dir(image).join("ramdisk.img")).ok()
}

/// SHA-256 of the unmodified `ramdisk.img` of `image`, from the SDK that
/// holds it (private first, like a launch), or `None` when it isn't
/// installed (gap G14).
pub fn pristine_ramdisk_sha256(sdks: &SdkSet, image: &ImageRef) -> Option<String> {
    sdks.find_image(image)
        .and_then(|sdk| ramdisk_sha256(sdk, image))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::sdk::Sdk;
    use jidr_core::JidrPaths;

    const XML: &str = r#"<r>
      <remotePackage path="system-images;android-35;google_apis;arm64-v8a"><revision><major>3</major></revision><archives/></remotePackage>
      <remotePackage path="system-images;android-35;google_apis;arm64-v8a"><revision><major>5</major></revision><archives/></remotePackage>
      <remotePackage path="system-images;android-35;google_apis;x86_64"><revision><major>5</major></revision><archives/></remotePackage>
      <remotePackage path="system-images;android-27;google_apis;arm64-v8a"><revision><major>1</major></revision><archives/></remotePackage>
      <remotePackage path="system-images;android-28;default;arm64-v8a"><revision><major>1</major></revision><archives/></remotePackage>
      <remotePackage path="system-images;android-36;google_apis;arm64-v8a"><revision><major>1</major></revision><channelRef ref="channel-2"/><archives/></remotePackage>
    </r>"#;

    #[test]
    fn filters_abi_api_channel_and_keeps_latest() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let repo = Repository::parse(XML, "file:///x.xml").unwrap();
        let sdks = SdkSet {
            private: Sdk::private(&JidrPaths::under(dir.path())),
            studio: None,
        };
        let filter = CatalogFilter {
            abi: "arm64-v8a".into(),
            include_best_effort: true,
            max_channel: 0,
        };
        let cat = image_catalog(&repo, &sdks, &filter);
        let ids: Vec<(u32, &str)> = cat
            .iter()
            .map(|i| (i.image.api, i.revision.as_str()))
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(ids, vec![(35, "5.0.0"), (28, "1.0.0")]);

        let strict = CatalogFilter {
            include_best_effort: false,
            ..filter
        };
        assert_eq!(image_catalog(&repo, &sdks, &strict).len(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn installed_images_show_offline() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let studio = dir.path().join("studio");
        let img = ImageRef {
            api: 31,
            tag: "google_apis".into(),
            abi: "arm64-v8a".into(),
        };
        let d = studio.join(img.sysdir());
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&d).unwrap();
        for f in ["source.properties", "system.img", "ramdisk.img"] {
            std::fs::write(d.join(f), b"x").unwrap();
        }
        let sdks = SdkSet {
            private: Sdk::private(&JidrPaths::under(dir.path().join("j"))),
            studio: Some(Sdk::read_only(&studio)),
        };
        let filter = CatalogFilter {
            abi: "arm64-v8a".into(),
            ..Default::default()
        };
        let cat = image_catalog(&Repository::default(), &sdks, &filter);
        assert_eq!(cat.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(cat[0].installed_in.as_deref(), Some(studio.as_path()));
        // G14: the SDK's unmodified ramdisk.img ("x").
        assert_eq!(
            cat[0].pristine_ramdisk_sha256.as_deref(),
            Some("2d711642b726b04401627ca9fbac32f5c8530fb1903cc4db02258717921a4881")
        );
        assert_eq!(
            pristine_ramdisk_sha256(&sdks, &img).as_deref(),
            Some("2d711642b726b04401627ca9fbac32f5c8530fb1903cc4db02258717921a4881")
        );
        let missing = ImageRef { api: 30, ..img };
        assert_eq!(pristine_ramdisk_sha256(&sdks, &missing), None);
    }
}
```

`crates/jidr-sdk/src/host.rs`:

```rs
//! Facts about the host machine: ABI, hypervisor, free disk space.

use std::path::Path;
use std::process::Command;

use jidr_core::{ErrorCode, JidrError, JidrResult, ResultExt};

/// The system-image ABI that runs natively on this host.
pub fn host_abi() -> &'static str {
    if cfg!(target_arch = "aarch64") {
        "arm64-v8a"
    } else {
        "x86_64"
    }
}

/// `host-os` as used in the SDK repository XML.
pub fn host_os() -> &'static str {
    if cfg!(target_os = "macos") {
        "macosx"
    } else if cfg!(target_os = "windows") {
        "windows"
    } else {
        "linux"
    }
}

/// `host-arch` as used in the SDK repository XML.
pub fn host_arch() -> &'static str {
    if cfg!(target_arch = "aarch64") {
        "aarch64"
    } else {
        "x64"
    }
}

/// True if hardware virtualization is usable (HVF on macOS, KVM on Linux).
pub fn hypervisor_available() -> bool {
    if cfg!(target_os = "macos") {
        Command::new("sysctl")
            .args(["-n", "kern.hv_support"])
            .output()
            .map(|o| String::from_utf8_lossy(&o.stdout).trim() == "1")
            .unwrap_or(false)
    } else if cfg!(target_os = "linux") {
        std::fs::OpenOptions::new()
            .read(true)
            .write(true)
            .open("/dev/kvm")
            .is_ok()
    } else {
        false
    }
}

/// Bytes available to this user on the volume holding `path` (or its nearest
/// existing ancestor).
pub fn free_space(path: &Path) -> JidrResult<u64> {
    let existing = path.ancestors().find(|p| p.exists()).ok_or_else(|| {
        JidrError::unexpected(format!("no existing ancestor of {}", path.display()))
    })?;
    fs4::available_space(existing).ctx(
        ErrorCode::Sdk,
        format!("free space of {}", existing.display()),
    )
}

/// Fails with `sdk` if fewer than `needed` bytes are free at `path`.
pub fn ensure_free_space(path: &Path, needed: u64) -> JidrResult<()> {
    let free = free_space(path)?;
    if free < needed {
        return Err(JidrError::sdk(format!(
            "not enough disk space at {}: need {:.1} GB, {:.1} GB free",
            path.display(),
            needed as f64 / 1e9,
            free as f64 / 1e9
        ))
        .with_data(serde_json::json!({"needed": needed, "free": free})));
    }
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn abi_matches_arch() {
        #[cfg(target_arch = "aarch64")]
        assert_eq!((host_abi(), host_arch()), ("arm64-v8a", "aarch64"));
        #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
        assert_eq!((host_abi(), host_arch()), ("x86_64", "x64"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn free_space_uses_existing_ancestor() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let missing = dir.path().join("a/b/c");
        assert!(free_space(&missing).unwrap() > 0);
        let err = ensure_free_space(&missing, u64::MAX).unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(err.code, ErrorCode::Sdk);
    }
}
```

`crates/jidr-sdk/src/install.rs`:

```rs
//! Native SDK package installer: download → SHA-1 check → unzip into a staging
//! directory → atomic move into the private SDK. No Java, no sdkmanager.
//! Only runs after the package's license has been accepted (D8).

use jidr_core::{Cancel, ErrorCode, JidrError, JidrResult, ResultExt};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use sha1::{Digest, Sha1};
use std::io::Write;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use crate::license::ConsentStore;
use crate::repo::{RemotePackage, Repository};
use crate::sdk::Sdk;

/// Extracted size is roughly this many times the archive size.
const EXTRACT_FACTOR: f64 = 2.5;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Phase {
    Downloading,
    Verifying,
    Extracting,
    Done,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct Progress {
    pub package: String,
    pub phase: Phase,
    pub done: u64,
    pub total: u64,
}

fn check_cancel(cancel: &Cancel) -> JidrResult<()> {
    cancel.check()
}

/// Lowercase hex digests of a download.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Digests {
    pub sha1: String,
    pub sha256: String,
}

/// Fetches small documents (repository XML) over https or `file://`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Fetcher {
    http: reqwest::Client,
}

impl Fetcher {
    pub fn new() -> JidrResult<Self> {
        let http = reqwest::Client::builder()
            .user_agent(concat!("jidr/", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")))
            // A stalled network fails instead of hanging a command forever.
            .connect_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(15))
            .read_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(60))
            .build()
            .ctx(ErrorCode::Unexpected, "building HTTP client")?;
        Ok(Self { http })
    }

    pub async fn text(&self, url: &str) -> JidrResult<String> {
        if let Some(path) = url.strip_prefix("file://") {
            return tokio::fs::read_to_string(path)
                .await
                .ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, format!("reading {url}"));
        }
        self.http
            .get(url)
            .timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(60))
            .send()
            .await
            .and_then(|r| r.error_for_status())
            .ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, format!("fetching {url}"))?
            .text()
            .await
            .ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, format!("reading {url}"))
    }

    /// Downloads `url` to `dest`, hashing as it goes.
    pub async fn download(
        &self,
        url: &str,
        dest: &Path,
        on_bytes: &(dyn Fn(u64, u64) + Send + Sync),
        cancel: &Cancel,
    ) -> JidrResult<Digests> {
        let mut hasher = Sha1::new();
        let mut hasher256 = sha2::Sha256::new();
        let file = std::fs::File::create(dest)
            .ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, format!("creating {}", dest.display()))?;
        let mut out = std::io::BufWriter::new(file);
        if let Some(path) = url.strip_prefix("file://") {
            let bytes = tokio::fs::read(path)
                .await
                .ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, format!("reading {url}"))?;
            check_cancel(cancel)?;
            hasher.update(&bytes);
            hasher256.update(&bytes);
            out.write_all(&bytes)
                .ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, "writing download")?;
            on_bytes(bytes.len() as u64, bytes.len() as u64);
        } else {
            let mut resp = self
                .http
                .get(url)
                .send()
                .await
                .and_then(|r| r.error_for_status())
                .ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, format!("downloading {url}"))?;
            let total = resp.content_length().unwrap_or(0);
            let mut done = 0u64;
            while let Some(chunk) = resp
                .chunk()
                .await
                .ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, format!("downloading {url}"))?
            {
                check_cancel(cancel)?;
                hasher.update(&chunk);
                hasher256.update(&chunk);
                out.write_all(&chunk)
                    .ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, "writing download")?;
                done += chunk.len() as u64;
                on_bytes(done, total);
            }
        }
        out.flush().ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, "writing download")?;
        Ok(Digests {
            sha1: hex::encode(hasher.finalize()),
            sha256: hex::encode(hasher256.finalize()),
        })
    }

    /// Fetches and merges every listing Jidr uses.
    pub async fn repository(&self, base: &str) -> JidrResult<Repository> {
        let mut repo = Repository::default();
        for url in crate::repo::listing_urls(base) {
            match self.text(&url).await {
                Ok(xml) => repo.merge(Repository::parse(&xml, &url)?),
                // The main listing is required; a missing image listing isn't fatal.
                Err(e) if url.contains("/sys-img/") => tracing::warn!("skipping {url}: {e}"),
                Err(e) => return Err(e),
            }
        }
        Ok(repo)
    }
}

/// Where a package lands inside the SDK: `a;b;c` → `a/b/c`.
pub fn install_dir(sdk: &Sdk, package: &str) -> PathBuf {
    package
        .split(';')
        .fold(sdk.root.clone(), |p, part| p.join(part))
}

/// Marker written into every package Jidr installs.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct InstalledMarker {
    pub path: String,
    pub revision: String,
    pub sha1: String,
}

pub const MARKER_FILE: &str = ".jidr-package.json";

/// Installs one package into the private SDK.
pub async fn install(
    fetcher: &Fetcher,
    sdk: &Sdk,
    repo: &Repository,
    consent: &ConsentStore,
    pkg: &RemotePackage,
    progress: &(dyn Fn(Progress) + Send + Sync),
    cancel: &Cancel,
) -> JidrResult<PathBuf> {
    sdk.ensure_writable()?;
    if let Some(id) = &pkg.license
        && !consent.is_accepted(repo.license(id)?)
    {
        return Err(
            JidrError::sdk(format!("license {id} has not been accepted"))
                .with_data(serde_json::json!({"license": id, "package": pkg.path})),
        );
    }
    let archive = pkg
        .archive_for_host()
        .ok_or_else(|| JidrError::sdk(format!("{} has no archive for this host", pkg.path)))?;
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&sdk.root)
        .ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, format!("creating {}", sdk.root.display()))?;
    crate::host::ensure_free_space(
        &sdk.root,
        archive.size + (archive.size as f64 * EXTRACT_FACTOR) as u64,
    )?;

    let staging_root = sdk.root.join(".jidr-staging");
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&staging_root).ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, "creating staging dir")?;
    let id = uuid::Uuid::new_v4();
    let zip_path = staging_root.join(format!("{id}.zip"));
    let extract_dir = staging_root.join(id.to_string());
    let result = async {
        let report = |phase, done, total| {
            progress(Progress {
                package: pkg.path.clone(),
                phase,
                done,
                total,
            })
        };
        let size = archive.size;
        let sha1 = fetcher
            .download(
                &archive.url,
                &zip_path,
                &|done, total| {
                    report(
                        Phase::Downloading,
                        done,
                        if total > 0 { total } else { size },
                    )
                },
                cancel,
            )
            .await?
            .sha1;
        report(Phase::Verifying, size, size);
        if sha1 != archive.sha1 {
            return Err(JidrError::sdk(format!(
                "checksum mismatch for {}: expected {}, got {sha1}",
                archive.url, archive.sha1
            )));
        }
        check_cancel(cancel)?;
        report(Phase::Extracting, 0, size);
        let (zp, ed) = (zip_path.clone(), extract_dir.clone());
        let top = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || extract_single_root(&zp, &ed))
            .await
            .ctx(ErrorCode::Unexpected, "extract task")??;
        check_cancel(cancel)?;
        let marker = InstalledMarker {
            path: pkg.path.clone(),
            revision: pkg.revision.to_string(),
            sha1,
        };
        let marker_json =
            serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&marker).ctx(ErrorCode::Unexpected, "encoding marker")?;
        std::fs::write(top.join(MARKER_FILE), marker_json)
            .ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, "writing package marker")?;

        let target = install_dir(sdk, &pkg.path);
        if let Some(parent) = target.parent() {
            std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)
                .ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, format!("creating {}", parent.display()))?;
        }
        if target.exists() {
            let old = staging_root.join(format!("{id}.old"));
            std::fs::rename(&target, &old)
                .ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, format!("moving old {}", target.display()))?;
        }
        std::fs::rename(&top, &target)
            .ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, format!("installing {}", target.display()))?;
        report(Phase::Done, size, size);
        Ok(target)
    }
    .await;
    // This install's staging leftovers (zip, extract dir, replaced package) are
    // always removed; the staging root goes too once no other install uses it.
    let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&zip_path);
    let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&extract_dir);
    let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(staging_root.join(format!("{id}.old")));
    let _ = std::fs::remove_dir(&staging_root);
    result
}

/// Extracts `zip` into `dest` and returns its single top-level directory.
fn extract_single_root(zip: &Path, dest: &Path) -> JidrResult<PathBuf> {
    let file =
        std::fs::File::open(zip).ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, format!("opening {}", zip.display()))?;
    let mut archive = zip::ZipArchive::new(file).ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, "reading zip")?;
    archive
        .extract(dest)
        .ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, "extracting zip")?;
    let mut entries: Vec<PathBuf> = std::fs::read_dir(dest)
        .ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, "listing extracted files")?
        .flatten()
        .map(|e| e.path())
        .filter(|p| p.file_name().is_some_and(|n| n != "__MACOSX"))
        .collect();
    match (entries.pop(), entries.is_empty()) {
        (Some(top), true) if top.is_dir() => Ok(top),
        _ => Err(JidrError::sdk(
            "archive must contain exactly one top-level directory",
        )),
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::repo::Repository;
    use jidr_core::JidrPaths;

    /// Builds `emu.zip` with `emulator/emulator` + `emulator/lib/x.txt` and a
    /// listing pointing at it via file://.
    fn fixture(dir: &Path, corrupt: bool) -> (Repository, String) {
        let zip_path = dir.join("emu.zip");
        let mut zw = zip::ZipWriter::new(std::fs::File::create(&zip_path).unwrap());
        let opts = zip::write::SimpleFileOptions::default().unix_permissions(0o755);
        zw.add_directory("emulator/", opts).unwrap();
        zw.start_file("emulator/emulator", opts).unwrap();
        zw.write_all(b"#!/bin/sh\necho emu\n").unwrap();
        zw.start_file("emulator/lib/x.txt", opts).unwrap();
        zw.write_all(b"x").unwrap();
        zw.finish().unwrap();
        let bytes = std::fs::read(&zip_path).unwrap();
        let sha1 = if corrupt {
            "00".repeat(20)
        } else {
            hex::encode(Sha1::digest(&bytes))
        };
        let xml = format!(
            r#"<r><license id="l" type="text">Terms.</license>
            <remotePackage path="emulator"><revision><major>36</major></revision>
            <uses-license ref="l"/><archives><archive><complete><size>{}</size>
            <checksum type="sha1">{sha1}</checksum><url>emu.zip</url></complete></archive></archives>
            </remotePackage></r>"#,
            bytes.len()
        );
        let url = format!("file://{}/repository2-3.xml", dir.display());
        (Repository::parse(&xml, &url).unwrap(), sha1)
    }

    fn rt() -> tokio::runtime::Runtime {
        tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread()
            .enable_all()
            .build()
            .unwrap()
    }

    #[test]
    fn installs_after_consent_only() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let (repo, _) = fixture(dir.path(), false);
        let paths = JidrPaths::under(dir.path().join("jidr"));
        let sdk = Sdk::private(&paths);
        let mut consent = ConsentStore::load(paths.consent_file()).unwrap();
        let pkg = repo.latest("emulator", 0).unwrap();
        let fetcher = Fetcher::new().unwrap();
        let cancel = Cancel::default();
        let phases = std::sync::Mutex::new(Vec::new());
        let progress = |p: Progress| phases.lock().unwrap().push(p.phase);

        let err = rt()
            .block_on(install(
                &fetcher, &sdk, &repo, &consent, pkg, &progress, &cancel,
            ))
            .unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.message.contains("not been accepted"), "{err}");
        assert!(!sdk.root.join("emulator").exists());

        consent.accept(repo.license("l").unwrap()).unwrap();
        let target = rt()
            .block_on(install(
                &fetcher, &sdk, &repo, &consent, pkg, &progress, &cancel,
            ))
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(target, sdk.root.join("emulator"));
        assert!(sdk.emulator().is_file());
        assert!(target.join("lib/x.txt").is_file());
        assert!(target.join(MARKER_FILE).is_file());
        assert!(!sdk.root.join(".jidr-staging").exists());
        #[cfg(unix)]
        {
            use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
            let mode = std::fs::metadata(sdk.emulator())
                .unwrap()
                .permissions()
                .mode();
            assert!(mode & 0o111 != 0, "executable bit kept");
        }
        let seen = phases.lock().unwrap().clone();
        assert_eq!(seen.first(), Some(&Phase::Downloading));
        assert_eq!(seen.last(), Some(&Phase::Done));

        // Reinstall replaces the old directory.
        rt().block_on(install(
            &fetcher, &sdk, &repo, &consent, pkg, &progress, &cancel,
        ))
        .unwrap();
        assert!(sdk.emulator().is_file());
    }

    #[test]
    fn checksum_mismatch_leaves_nothing_behind() {
```

```rs
//! License consent (D8): the user sees the actual license text and accepts
//! it; we record the id and the SHA-256 of that exact text. A changed text has
//! a new hash and needs consent again. Nothing is ever accepted implicitly.

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
use jidr_core::{ErrorCode, JidrError, JidrResult, ResultExt};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};

use crate::repo::{License, RemotePackage, Repository};

pub fn license_sha256(text: &str) -> String {
    hex::encode(Sha256::digest(text.as_bytes()))
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct Consent {
    pub id: String,
    pub sha256: String,
    pub accepted_at: DateTime<Utc>,
}

/// A license the user still has to accept, with the text to show them.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct PendingLicense {
    pub id: String,
    pub sha256: String,
    pub text: String,
    /// Packages that need it.
    pub packages: Vec<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct ConsentStore {
    path: PathBuf,
    records: Vec<Consent>,
}

impl ConsentStore {
    /// Loads the store; a missing file is an empty store.
    pub fn load(path: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> JidrResult<Self> {
        let path = path.into();
        let records = match std::fs::read(&path) {
            Ok(bytes) => serde_json::from_slice(&bytes)
                .ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, format!("reading {}", path.display()))?,
            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Vec::new(),
            Err(e) => return Err(JidrError::sdk(format!("reading {}: {e}", path.display()))),
        };
        Ok(Self { path, records })
    }

    pub fn path(&self) -> &Path {
        &self.path
    }

    pub fn records(&self) -> &[Consent] {
        &self.records
    }

    pub fn is_accepted(&self, license: &License) -> bool {
        let hash = license_sha256(&license.text);
        self.records
            .iter()
            .any(|r| r.id == license.id && r.sha256 == hash)
    }

    /// Records consent for this exact text and saves the store.
    pub fn accept(&mut self, license: &License) -> JidrResult<Consent> {
        let consent = Consent {
            id: license.id.clone(),
            sha256: license_sha256(&license.text),
            accepted_at: Utc::now(),
        };
        if !self.is_accepted(license) {
            self.records.push(consent.clone());
            self.save()?;
        }
        Ok(consent)
    }

    /// Accepts a license by id + hash (the headless `--accept-licenses` path
    /// prints each hash first; the hash must match the current text).
    pub fn accept_hash(
        &mut self,
        repo: &Repository,
        id: &str,
        sha256: &str,
    ) -> JidrResult<Consent> {
        let license = repo.license(id)?;
        let current = license_sha256(&license.text);
        if current != sha256 {
            return Err(JidrError::usage(format!(
                "license {id} text changed: current hash is {current}, you accepted {sha256}"
            )));
        }
        self.accept(license)
    }

    fn save(&self) -> JidrResult<()> {
        if let Some(dir) = self.path.parent() {
            std::fs::create_dir_all(dir)
                .ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, format!("creating {}", dir.display()))?;
        }
        let json = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&self.records)
            .ctx(ErrorCode::Unexpected, "encoding consent")?;
        let tmp = self.path.with_extension("json.tmp");
        std::fs::write(&tmp, json).ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, format!("writing {}", tmp.display()))?;
        std::fs::rename(&tmp, &self.path)
            .ctx(ErrorCode::Sdk, format!("writing {}", self.path.display()))
    }

    /// Licenses still needed before `packages` can be installed.
    pub fn pending(
        &self,
        repo: &Repository,
        packages: &[&RemotePackage],
    ) -> JidrResult<Vec<PendingLicense>> {
        let mut out: Vec<PendingLicense> = Vec::new();
        for pkg in packages {
            let Some(id) = &pkg.license else { continue };
            let license = repo.license(id)?;
            if self.is_accepted(license) {
                continue;
            }
            match out.iter_mut().find(|p| &p.id == id) {
                Some(p) => p.packages.push(pkg.path.clone()),
                None => out.push(PendingLicense {
                    id: id.clone(),
                    sha256: license_sha256(&license.text),
                    text: license.text.clone(),
                    packages: vec![pkg.path.clone()],
                }),
            }
        }
        Ok(out)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::repo::tests::FIXTURE;

    fn repo() -> Repository {
        Repository::parse(FIXTURE, "https://x/repo.xml").unwrap()
    }

    #[test]
    fn consent_round_trip_and_rehash_on_change() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let path = dir.path().join("consent.json");
        let repo = repo();
        let lic = repo.license("test-license").unwrap().clone();

        let mut store = ConsentStore::load(&path).unwrap();
        assert!(!store.is_accepted(&lic));
        store.accept(&lic).unwrap();
        store.accept(&lic).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(store.records().len(), 1, "accepting twice records once");

        let reloaded = ConsentStore::load(&path).unwrap();
        assert!(reloaded.is_accepted(&lic));

        let changed = License {
            id: lic.id.clone(),
            text: format!("{} (amended)", lic.text),
        };
        assert!(
            !reloaded.is_accepted(&changed),
            "a new text needs new consent"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn pending_groups_packages_by_license() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let repo = repo();
        let pkgs: Vec<&RemotePackage> = repo
            .packages
            .iter()
            .filter(|p| p.license.is_some())
            .collect();
        let mut store = ConsentStore::load(dir.path().join("c.json")).unwrap();
        let pending = store.pending(&repo, &pkgs).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(pending.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(pending[0].packages.len(), 2);

        let hash = pending[0].sha256.clone();
        assert_eq!(
            store
                .accept_hash(&repo, "test-license", "bad")
                .unwrap_err()
                .code,
            ErrorCode::Usage
        );
        store.accept_hash(&repo, "test-license", &hash).unwrap();
        assert!(store.pending(&repo, &pkgs).unwrap().is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn corrupt_store_is_an_error_not_a_reset() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let path = dir.path().join("c.json");
        std::fs::write(&path, b"{not json").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(ConsentStore::load(&path).unwrap_err().code, ErrorCode::Sdk);
    }
}
```

```rs
//! Built-in hardware profiles with generic names (D24).

use jidr_core::{HardwareProfile, JidrError, JidrResult};

const BUILTIN: &[&str] = &[
    include_str!("../../../assets/profiles/phone-6.1-fhd.toml"),
    include_str!("../../../assets/profiles/phone-6.7-qhd.toml"),
    include_str!("../../../assets/profiles/small-phone-5.toml"),
    include_str!("../../../assets/profiles/tablet-11.toml"),
];

/// The built-in profiles; the first one is the default.
pub fn builtin() -> Vec<HardwareProfile> {
    BUILTIN
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|t| match toml::from_str(t) {
            Ok(p) => Some(p),
            Err(e) => {
                tracing::error!("bad built-in profile: {e}");
                None
            }
        })
        .collect()
}

pub fn find(id: &str) -> JidrResult<HardwareProfile> {
    builtin()
        .into_iter()
        .find(|p| p.id == id)
        .ok_or_else(|| JidrError::not_found(format!("no hardware profile {id}")))
}

pub fn default_profile() -> JidrResult<HardwareProfile> {
    builtin()
        .into_iter()
        .next()
        .ok_or_else(|| JidrError::unexpected("no built-in profiles"))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn all_builtin_profiles_parse() {
        let all = builtin();
        assert_eq!(all.len(), BUILTIN.len());
        let mut ids: Vec<&str> = all.iter().map(|p| p.id.as_str()).collect();
        ids.dedup();
        assert_eq!(ids.len(), all.len(), "ids are unique");
        assert_eq!(default_profile().unwrap().id, "phone-6.1-fhd");
        assert_eq!(
            find("tablet-11").unwrap().config["hw.initialOrientation"],
            "landscape"
        );
        assert!(find("nope").is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn names_are_generic() {
        for p in builtin() {
            for brand in ["Pixel", "Galaxy", "Nexus", "Samsung", "Google"] {
                assert!(
                    !p.name.contains(brand),
                    "{} uses a brand name (D24)",
                    p.name
                );
            }
        }
    }
}
```
