`crates/jidr-widgets/tests/common/mod.rs`:

```rs
//! Emulator test setup: a real daemon (AOSP backend + the widgets provider)
//! in a temp Jidr home, one device booted from `JIDR_TEST_IMAGE` using the
//! `JIDR_TEST_SDK` SDK read-only (D3). Boots serialise on a file lock so a
//! parallel nextest run doesn't start several emulators at once.
#![allow(dead_code)]

use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use jidr_backend::AospBackend;
use jidr_client::Client;
use jidr_core::{ConnectInfo, JidrPaths};
use jidr_daemon::{Daemon, DaemonConfig};
use serde_json::{Value, json};

pub fn test_sdk() -> PathBuf {
    std::env::var_os("JIDR_TEST_SDK")
        .map(PathBuf::from)
        .unwrap_or_else(|| dirs::home_dir().unwrap().join("Library/Android/sdk"))
}

pub fn test_image() -> String {
    std::env::var("JIDR_TEST_IMAGE").unwrap_or_else(|_| {
        format!(
            "system-images;android-31;google_apis;{}",
            jidr_sdk::host::host_abi()
        )
    })
}

pub struct Env {
    pub tmp: tempfile::TempDir,
    pub paths: JidrPaths,
    pub client: Client,
    pub device: String,
    pub info: ConnectInfo,
    pub daemon: Arc<Daemon>,
    shutdown: Option<tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<()>>,
    task: Option<tokio::task::JoinHandle<jidr_core::JidrResult<()>>>,
    _lock: std::fs::File,
}

impl Env {
    /// Creates and cold boots `name` (720×1280 small phone, no root).
    pub async fn boot(name: &str) -> Env {
        let lock =
            std::fs::File::create(std::env::temp_dir().join("jidr-widgets-emulator.lock")).unwrap();
        lock.lock().unwrap();
        let tmp = tempfile::tempdir_in(std::env::temp_dir()).unwrap();
        // Short root: the daemon socket path must fit in sun_path.
        let paths = JidrPaths::under(tmp.path().join("j"));
        let repo = tmp.path().join("repo");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&repo).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(
            repo.join("repository2-3.xml"),
            "<sdk:sdk-repository xmlns:sdk=\"x\"/>",
        )
        .unwrap();
        let daemon = Daemon::builder(
            DaemonConfig {
                paths: paths.clone(),
                studio_sdk: Some(test_sdk()),
                idle_timeout: None,
                sdk_repo: Some(format!("file://{}/", repo.display())),
            },
            Arc::new(AospBackend::new()),
        )
        .provider(jidr_widgets::provider())
        .build()
        .unwrap();
        let (tx, rx) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel();
        let d = daemon.clone();
        let task = tokio::spawn(async move {
            d.serve(async {
                let _ = rx.await;
            })
            .await
        });
        for _ in 0..500 {
            if paths.socket().exists() {
                break;
            }
            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
        }
        let client = Client::connect(&paths.socket(), "test").await.unwrap();
        client
            .call(
                "device.create",
                json!({ "name": name, "image": test_image(), "profile": "small-phone-5", "root_mode": "none" }),
            )
            .await
            .unwrap();
        let t = Instant::now();
        client
            .run(
                "device.start",
                json!({ "device": name, "cold_boot": true }),
                |_| {},
            )
            .await
            .unwrap();
        println!("{name}: booted in {:.1} s", t.elapsed().as_secs_f64());
        let info: ConnectInfo = client
            .call_as("device.connect_info", json!({ "device": name }))
            .await
            .unwrap();
        Env {
            tmp,
            paths,
            client,
            device: name.into(),
            info,
            daemon,
            shutdown: Some(tx),
            task: Some(task),
            _lock: lock,
        }
    }

    pub async fn call(&self, method: &str, mut params: Value) -> Value {
        params["device"] = json!(self.device);
        match self.client.call(method, params.clone()).await {
            Ok(v) => v,
            Err(e) => panic!("{method} {params}: {e}"),
        }
    }

    /// Calls a long-running command and follows its job.
    pub async fn run(&self, method: &str, mut params: Value) -> Value {
        params["device"] = json!(self.device);
        match self.client.run(method, params.clone(), |_| {}).await {
            Ok(v) => v,
            Err(e) => panic!("{method} {params}: {e}"),
        }
    }

    /// `adb -s <serial> …`: (stdout, stderr). adb reports "device offline"
    /// and closed transports on stderr.
    pub fn adb_out(&self, args: &[&str]) -> (String, String) {
        let out = std::process::Command::new(&self.info.adb_path)
            .arg("-s")
            .arg(&self.info.adb_serial)
            .args(args)
            .output()
            .unwrap();
        (
            String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout).into_owned(),
            String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr).into_owned(),
        )
    }

    pub fn adb(&self, args: &[&str]) -> String {
        self.adb_out(args).0
    }

    pub fn shell(&self, cmd: &str) -> String {
        self.adb(&["shell", cmd])
    }

    /// Polls `f` until it returns true (30 s). The Linux KVM runners use
    /// software rendering, and a snapshot restore or a telephony signal
    /// refresh there can take longer than 10 s.
    pub async fn eventually(&self, what: &str, f: impl Fn(&Env) -> bool) {
        let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(30);
        while Instant::now() < deadline {
            if f(self) {
                return;
            }
            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(300)).await;
        }
        panic!("timed out waiting for: {what}");
    }

    /// Like `eventually`, on the output of a device shell command. On timeout
    /// the panic shows the last output's lines that contain any of `show`, and
    /// `context`, so a CI failure says what the device reported.
    pub async fn eventually_shell(
        &self,
        what: &str,
        cmd: &str,
        show: &[&str],
        context: &str,
        ok: impl Fn(&str) -> bool,
    ) {
        self.eventually_shell_with(what, cmd, show, |_| context.to_string(), ok)
            .await;
    }

    /// Like `eventually_shell`, with context read from the device at the
    /// timeout (e.g. the console's `gsm status`).
    pub async fn eventually_shell_with(
        &self,
        what: &str,
        cmd: &str,
        show: &[&str],
        context: impl Fn(&Env) -> String,
        ok: impl Fn(&str) -> bool,
    ) {
        let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(30);
        let (mut out, mut err) = (String::new(), String::new());
        while Instant::now() < deadline {
            (out, err) = self.adb_out(&["shell", cmd]);
            if ok(&out) {
                return;
            }
            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(300)).await;
        }
        let seen: Vec<&str> = out
            .lines()
            .filter(|l| show.iter().any(|k| l.contains(k)))
            .collect();
        let (state, state_err) = self.adb_out(&["get-state"]);
        panic!(
            "timed out waiting for: {what}\n`{cmd}` showed:\n{}\nstderr: {}\nadb get-state: {} {}\n{}",
            seen.join("\n"),
            err.trim(),
            state.trim(),
            state_err.trim(),
            context(self)
        );
    }

    /// Stops the device and the daemon.
    pub async fn stop(mut self) {
        let _ = self
            .client
            .call("device.stop", json!({ "device": self.device }))
            .await;
        if let Some(tx) = self.shutdown.take() {
            let _ = tx.send(());
        }
        if let Some(t) = self.task.take() {
            let _ = t.await;
        }
    }
}

impl Drop for Env {
    /// Never leak an emulator, even when a test panics.
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if self.shutdown.is_some() {
            let _ = std::process::Command::new(&self.info.adb_path)
                .args(["-s", &self.info.adb_serial, "emu", "kill"])
                .output();
        }
    }
}

`crates/jidr-widgets/tests/gps_emulator.rs`:

```rs
//! Phase 8b: a GPS fix shows in `dumpsys location`, and a 3-point GPX
//! replay moves the reported location through the points in order.
#![cfg(feature = "emulator")]
#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]

mod common;

use std::path::Path;

use serde_json::json;

const POINTS: [(f64, f64); 3] = [(32.8854, 13.1802), (32.8754, 13.1902), (32.8654, 13.2002)];

/// Builds the location probe app (tests/fixtures/build-hello-apk.sh).
fn build_probe(dir: &Path) -> std::path::PathBuf {
    let out = dir.join("locprobe.apk");
    let script = Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("tests/fixtures/build-hello-apk.sh");
    let st = std::process::Command::new("bash")
        .arg(script)
        .arg(&out)
        .arg("locprobe")
        .status()
        .unwrap();
    assert!(st.success(), "building the probe app failed");
    out
}

/// Probe fixes from logcat, oldest first.
fn fixes(env: &common::Env) -> Vec<(f64, f64)> {
    env.adb(&["logcat", "-d", "-s", "JidrLocProbe"])
        .lines()
        .filter_map(|l| {
            let (_, v) = l.split_once("JidrLocProbe: ")?;
            let (a, b) = v.trim().split_once(',')?;
            Some((a.parse().ok()?, b.parse().ok()?))
        })
        .collect()
}

fn near(a: (f64, f64), b: (f64, f64)) -> bool {
    (a.0 - b.0).abs() < 0.0015 && (a.1 - b.1).abs() < 0.0015
}

#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
async fn gps_fix_and_route_replay() {
    let env = common::Env::boot("widgets8b").await;
    let probe = build_probe(env.tmp.path());
    env.call(
        "file.install",
        json!({ "apk": probe, "grant_permissions": true }),
    )
    .await;
    env.adb(&["logcat", "-c"]);
    env.call("app.launch", json!({ "package": "ly.jidr.locprobe" }))
        .await;

    // Martyrs' Square, Tripoli.
    env.call(
        "gps.set",
        json!({ "latitude": 32.8954, "longitude": 13.1802, "altitude": 21 }),
    )
    .await;
    env.eventually("Tripoli in dumpsys location", |e| {
        let d = e.shell("dumpsys location");
        d.contains("32.8954") && d.contains("13.180")
    })
    .await;
    let g = env.call("gps.get", json!({})).await;
    assert!(
        (g["latitude"].as_f64().unwrap() - 32.8954).abs() < 1e-6,
        "{g}"
    );

    // Three-point route: fixes arrive near each point, in order.
    let gpx = env.tmp.path().join("route.gpx");
    let pts: String = POINTS
        .iter()
        .map(|(la, lo)| format!("<trkpt lat=\"{la}\" lon=\"{lo}\"><ele>20</ele></trkpt>"))
        .collect();
    std::fs::write(
        &gpx,
        format!("<gpx version=\"1.1\"><trk><trkseg>{pts}</trkseg></trk></gpx>"),
    )
    .unwrap();
    env.adb(&["logcat", "-c"]);
    let r = env
        .run(
            "gps.route",
            json!({ "path": gpx, "speed": 1.0, "mps": 600.0 }),
        )
        .await;
    assert!(r["total_m"].as_f64().unwrap() > 2500.0, "{r}");
    env.eventually("the last point reported", |e| {
        fixes(e).iter().any(|f| near(*f, POINTS[2]))
    })
    .await;
    let got = fixes(&env);
    let first = |p: (f64, f64), from: usize| {
        got.iter()
            .skip(from)
            .position(|f| near(*f, p))
            .map(|i| i + from)
    };
    let a = first(POINTS[0], 0).unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("point 1 missing in {got:?}"));
    let b = first(POINTS[1], a).unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("point 2 not after point 1 in {got:?}"));
    let c = first(POINTS[2], b).unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("point 3 not after point 2 in {got:?}"));
    assert!(a < b && b < c, "{got:?}");
    // Latitude only falls along this route.
    assert!(
        got[a..=c].windows(2).all(|w| w[1].0 <= w[0].0 + 1e-4),
        "{got:?}"
    );

    env.stop().await;
}

//! Phase 10a: a screenshot is a PNG of the screen, and a 5-minute
//! recording passes ffprobe (h264, 300 ± 2 s, ≥ 30 × 300 × 0.9 frames).
#![cfg(feature = "emulator")]
#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]

mod common;

use serde_json::{Value, json};

#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
async fn media_screenshot_and_five_minute_recording() {
    let env = common::Env::boot("widgets10a").await;

    // Screenshot.
    let png = env.tmp.path().join("shot.png");
    let s = env.call("media.screenshot", json!({ "path": png })).await;
    assert_eq!(s["path"], json!(png));
    let bytes = std::fs::read(&png).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(&bytes[..8], b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n");
    assert_eq!(
        (s["width"].as_u64(), s["height"].as_u64()),
        (Some(720), Some(1280)),
        "{s}"
    );

    // Recording encodes with AVFoundation (VideoToolbox): macOS only.
    if !cfg!(target_os = "macos") {
        env.stop().await;
        return;
    }

    // Recording at a constant 30 fps (the last frame repeats while the screen is still).
    let mp4 = env.tmp.path().join("rec.mp4");
    let started = std::time::Instant::now();
    let rec = env
        .run(
            "media.record",
            json!({ "path": mp4, "max_seconds": 300, "fps": 30 }),
        )
        .await;
    println!(
        "recorded in {:.1} s: {rec}",
        started.elapsed().as_secs_f64()
    );
    assert!(rec["frames"].as_i64().unwrap() >= 8100, "{rec}");

    let probe = std::process::Command::new("ffprobe")
        .args([
            "-v",
            "error",
            "-select_streams",
            "v:0",
            "-count_frames",
            "-show_entries",
            "stream=codec_name,nb_read_frames,duration,width,height",
            "-show_entries",
            "format=duration",
            "-of",
            "json",
        ])
        .arg(&mp4)
        .output()
        .expect("ffprobe on PATH");
    assert!(
        probe.status.success(),
        "{}",
        String::from_utf8_lossy(&probe.stderr)
    );
    let v: Value = serde_json::from_slice(&probe.stdout).unwrap();
    println!("ffprobe: {v}");
    let stream = &v["streams"][0];
    assert_eq!(stream["codec_name"], "h264");
    let duration: f64 = v["format"]["duration"].as_str().unwrap().parse().unwrap();
    assert!((298.0..=302.0).contains(&duration), "duration {duration}");
    let frames: u64 = stream["nb_read_frames"].as_str().unwrap().parse().unwrap();
    assert!(frames >= 8100, "frames {frames}");

    env.stop().await;
}

`crates/jidr-widgets/tests/proxy_emulator.rs`:

```rs
//! The global HTTP proxy on a real emulator: `network.proxy.set` reaches
//! Android's connectivity service (its ProxyTracker broadcasts the new
//! proxy), and `network.proxy.clear` removes it. Run it on an API 34+ image
//! (`JIDR_TEST_IMAGE=system-images;android-35;google_apis;arm64-v8a`).
#![cfg(feature = "emulator")]
#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]

mod common;

use serde_json::json;

/// The proxies ConnectivityService's ProxyTracker announced, oldest first:
/// `sending Proxy Broadcast for [10.0.2.2] 8080 xl=`.
fn broadcasts(log: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    log.lines()
        .filter_map(|l| {
            l.split_once("sending Proxy Broadcast for ")
                .map(|(_, p)| p.trim().to_string())
        })
        .collect()
}

const PROXY_LOG: &str = "logcat -d -s ProxyTracker";

#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
async fn proxy_set_and_clear() {
    let env = common::Env::boot("widgets-proxy").await;
    let none = env.call("network.proxy.get", json!({})).await;
    assert!(none["proxy"].is_null(), "{none}");

    let set = env
        .call(
            "network.proxy.set",
            json!({ "host": "10.0.2.2", "port": 8080 }),
        )
        .await;
    assert_eq!(set["proxy"], "10.0.2.2:8080", "{set}");
    assert_eq!(
        env.shell("settings get global http_proxy").trim(),
        "10.0.2.2:8080"
    );
    env.eventually_shell(
        "the connectivity service applies the proxy",
        PROXY_LOG,
        &["Proxy Broadcast"],
        "",
        |out| {
            broadcasts(out)
                .last()
                .is_some_and(|p| p.starts_with("[10.0.2.2] 8080"))
        },
    )
    .await;
    let got = env.call("network.proxy.get", json!({})).await;
    assert_eq!(
        (got["host"].as_str(), got["port"].as_u64()),
        (Some("10.0.2.2"), Some(8080))
    );

    let cleared = env.call("network.proxy.clear", json!({})).await;
    assert!(cleared["proxy"].is_null(), "{cleared}");
    env.eventually_shell(
        "the connectivity service drops the proxy",
        PROXY_LOG,
        &["Proxy Broadcast"],
        "",
        |out| {
            broadcasts(out)
                .last()
                .is_some_and(|p| !p.contains("10.0.2.2"))
        },
    )
    .await;
    assert_eq!(env.shell("settings get global http_proxy").trim(), ":0");
    let got = env.call("network.proxy.get", json!({})).await;
    assert!(got["proxy"].is_null(), "{got}");
    env.stop().await;
}

#[test]
fn reads_proxy_broadcasts() {
    let log = "11-02 18:25:51.200  1936  2374 D ProxyTracker: sending Proxy Broadcast for [10.0.2.2] 8080 xl=\n\
               11-02 18:26:01.000  1936  2374 D ProxyTracker: sending Proxy Broadcast for null\n";
    assert_eq!(broadcasts(log), ["[10.0.2.2] 8080 xl=", "null"]);
    assert!(broadcasts("nothing").is_empty());
}

`crates/jidr-widgets/tests/snapshot_emulator.rs`:

```rs
//! Phase 10b: save → modify → load restores the state, and a snapshot
//! taken under another root mode is refused (D29).
#![cfg(feature = "emulator")]
#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]

mod common;

use jidr_core::RootMode;
use jidr_core::provider::DaemonContext;
use serde_json::{Value, json};

fn marker(env: &common::Env) -> String {
    env.shell("settings get global jidr_marker")
        .trim()
        .to_string()
}

fn find<'a>(list: &'a Value, name: &str) -> Option<&'a Value> {
    list["snapshots"]
        .as_array()?
        .iter()
        .find(|s| s["name"] == name)
}

#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
async fn snapshot_round_trip_and_cross_root_refusal() {
    let env = common::Env::boot("widgets10b").await;

    env.shell("settings put global jidr_marker before");
    assert_eq!(marker(&env), "before");
    env.run("snapshot.save", json!({ "name": "Clean install" }))
        .await;
    let list = env.call("snapshot.list", json!({})).await;
    let s = find(&list, "Clean install").unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{list}"));
    assert_eq!(s["root_mode"], "none");
    assert_eq!(s["restorable"], true);
    assert!(s["size_bytes"].as_u64().unwrap() > 0, "{s}");

    env.shell("settings put global jidr_marker after");
    assert_eq!(marker(&env), "after");
    env.run("snapshot.load", json!({ "name": "Clean install" }))
        .await;
    // Prints what adb sees on timeout: nothing at all means adb lost the
    // device after the restore.
    env.eventually_shell(
        "the marker back to before",
        "settings get global jidr_marker; echo boot_completed=$(getprop sys.boot_completed)",
        &[""],
        "",
        |out| out.lines().next().is_some_and(|l| l.trim() == "before"),
    )
    .await;

    // What root.set does: the device's root mode changes.
    let id = env.daemon.state().device(&env.device).await.unwrap().id;
    env.daemon
        .state()
        .update_device(id, Box::new(|d| d.root.mode = RootMode::Adb))
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let err = env
        .client
        .run(
            "snapshot.load",
            json!({ "device": env.device, "name": "Clean install" }),
            |_| {},
        )
        .await
        .unwrap_err();
    assert!(
        err.message.contains("Not rooted") && err.message.contains("Shell root"),
        "{err}"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        err.data.as_ref().unwrap()["details"]["refused"]
            .as_str()
            .or(err.data.as_ref().unwrap()["refused"].as_str()),
        Some("root_mode"),
        "{err:?}"
    );
    let list = env.call("snapshot.list", json!({})).await;
    assert_eq!(find(&list, "Clean install").unwrap()["restorable"], false);

    env.call("snapshot.delete", json!({ "name": "Clean install" }))
        .await;
    let list = env.call("snapshot.list", json!({})).await;
    assert!(find(&list, "Clean install").is_none(), "{list}");

    env.stop().await;
}

`crates/jidr-widgets/tests/widgets_emulator.rs`:

```rs
//! Phase 8a: every core widget command has an adb-observable effect on a
//! real emulator.
#![cfg(feature = "emulator")]
#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]

mod common;

use serde_json::json;

/// The display rotation (0–3) in `dumpsys window` output.
fn rotation_in(out: &str) -> Option<u32> {
    out.lines().find_map(|l| {
        l.trim()
            .strip_prefix("mRotation=")
            .and_then(|r| r.split_whitespace().next()?.parse().ok())
    })
}

/// `dumpsys window` plus the auto-rotate setting, for rotation waits.
const ROTATION_STATE: &str =
    "dumpsys window; echo accelerometer_rotation=$(settings get system accelerometer_rotation)";
const ROTATION_LINES: &[&str] = &[
    "mRotation=",
    "mCurrentFocus",
    "mFocusedApp",
    "accelerometer_rotation",
];

/// Rotates the physical model to `angle` and waits for the window manager to
/// report `want`. Sends the rotation once more after 10 s: a sensor sample
/// can be missed while the HAL batches.
async fn rotate_to(env: &common::Env, angle: u32, want: u32) {
    env.call("sensor.rotate", json!({ "angle": angle })).await;
    let deadline = std::time::Instant::now() + std::time::Duration::from_secs(10);
    while std::time::Instant::now() < deadline {
        if rotation_in(&env.shell("dumpsys window")) == Some(want) {
            return;
        }
        tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(300)).await;
    }
    env.call("sensor.rotate", json!({ "angle": angle })).await;
    env.eventually_shell(
        &format!("rotation {angle}°"),
        ROTATION_STATE,
        ROTATION_LINES,
        &format!("sent sensor.rotate {angle} twice"),
        |out| rotation_in(out) == Some(want),
    )
    .await;
}

/// Switches mobile data and waits for telephony to follow (`mDataRegState`).
/// Sends `network.set` once more after 10 s, and on timeout shows the
/// console's `gsm status` (did the emulated radio take it?).
async fn mobile_to(env: &common::Env, on: bool) {
    let registry = "dumpsys telephony.registry";
    let done = |out: &str| service_state(out).contains("mDataRegState=0(") == on;
    let deadline = std::time::Instant::now() + std::time::Duration::from_secs(10);
    while std::time::Instant::now() < deadline {
        if done(&env.shell(registry)) {
            return;
        }
        tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(300)).await;
    }
    let again = env.call("network.set", json!({ "mobile": on })).await;
    env.eventually_shell_with(
        &format!("mobile data {}", if on { "on" } else { "off" }),
        registry,
        &["mServiceState="],
        |e| {
            format!(
                "sent network.set mobile={on} twice (second: {again})\n`adb emu gsm status`:\n{}",
                e.adb(&["emu", "gsm", "status"]).trim()
            )
        },
        done,
    )
    .await;
}

/// Telephony's current service state line (`mServiceState={…}`); the rest of
/// `dumpsys telephony.registry` holds older states.
fn service_state(registry: &str) -> &str {
    registry
        .lines()
        .find(|l| l.trim_start().starts_with("mServiceState="))
        .unwrap_or("")
}

#[test]
fn service_state_is_the_current_line() {
    let reg = "  mServiceState={mVoiceRegState=0(IN_SERVICE), mDataRegState=1(OUT_OF_SERVICE)}\n  2026 - notifyServiceStateForSubscriber: state={mVoiceRegState=3(POWER_OFF), mDataRegState=0(IN_SERVICE)}";
    assert!(service_state(reg).contains("mVoiceRegState=0("));
    assert!(!service_state(reg).contains("mDataRegState=0("));
    assert_eq!(service_state("nothing"), "");
}

/// The signal level (0–4) telephony reports: the highest level of any radio
/// in the `mSignalStrength` line. Images differ in which radio carries the
/// signal (WCDMA on API 31 arm64, LTE on API 30 x86_64), and the others report
/// level 0.
fn signal_level(registry: &str) -> Option<u32> {
    let line = registry.lines().find(|l| l.contains("mSignalStrength="))?;
    line.replace(" = ", "=")
        .split([' ', ',', '{', '}'])
        .filter_map(|t| {
            t.strip_prefix("level=")
                .or_else(|| t.strip_prefix("mLevel="))
        })
        .filter_map(|v| v.parse().ok())
        .max()
}

#[test]
fn signal_level_reads_any_radio() {
    // API 30 x86_64 after `gsm signal-profile 0` (CI run 38592875474): LTE is primary.
    let lte = "  mSignalStrength=SignalStrength:{mCdma=CellSignalStrengthCdma: cdmaDbm=2147483647 level=0,mGsm=CellSignalStrengthGsm: rssi=2147483647 ber=2147483647 mTa=2147483647 mLevel=0,mWcdma=CellSignalStrengthWcdma: ss=2147483647 level=0,mLte=CellSignalStrengthLte: rssi=2147483647 rsrp=-140 rsrq=-3 rssnr=-20 cqi=0 ta=500 level=0 parametersUseForLevel=0,mNr=CellSignalStrengthNr:{ ssRsrp = 2147483647 level = 0 parametersUseForLevel = 0 },primary=CellSignalStrengthLte}";
    assert_eq!(signal_level(lte), Some(0));
    assert_eq!(
        signal_level(&lte.replace(
            "rsrp=-140 rsrq=-3 rssnr=-20 cqi=0 ta=500 level=0",
            "rsrp=-85 level=4"
        )),
        Some(4)
    );
    assert_eq!(signal_level(&lte.replace("mLevel=0", "mLevel=3")), Some(3));
    assert_eq!(
        signal_level(&lte.replace("level = 0", "level = 2")),
        Some(2)
    );
    assert_eq!(signal_level("mServiceState=x"), None);
}

/// Whether `service check <name>` found the AIDL service.
fn service_found(check: &str) -> bool {
    check.trim_end().ends_with(": found")
}

#[test]
fn service_found_reads_service_check() {
    let name = "android.hardware.biometrics.fingerprint.IFingerprint/default";
    assert!(service_found(&format!("Service {name}: found\n")));
    assert!(!service_found(&format!("Service {name}: not found\n")));
    assert!(!service_found(""));
}

#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
async fn widgets_core_commands() {
    let env = common::Env::boot("widgets8a").await;

    // Battery: level and charger reach Android's battery service.
    env.call("battery.set", json!({ "level": 42, "charging": false }))
        .await;
    env.eventually("battery level 42, unplugged", |e| {
        let b = e.shell("dumpsys battery");
        b.contains("level: 42") && b.contains("AC powered: false")
    })
    .await;
    env.call("battery.set", json!({ "charging": true })).await;
    env.eventually("AC powered", |e| {
        e.shell("dumpsys battery").contains("AC powered: true")
    })
    .await;
    assert_eq!(env.call("battery.get", json!({})).await["level"], 42);

    // Rotation: the window manager follows the physical model. Auto-rotate
    // on, and Settings in front (the launcher is portrait-only).
    env.shell("settings put system accelerometer_rotation 1");
    let settings_focused = |out: &str| {
        out.lines().any(|l| {
            (l.contains("mCurrentFocus") || l.contains("mFocusedApp"))
                && l.contains("com.android.settings")
        })
    };
    let launched = env
        .call("app.launch", json!({ "package": "com.android.settings" }))
        .await;
    let deadline = std::time::Instant::now() + std::time::Duration::from_secs(10);
    while std::time::Instant::now() < deadline && !settings_focused(&env.shell("dumpsys window")) {
        tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(300)).await;
    }
    if !settings_focused(&env.shell("dumpsys window")) {
        env.call("app.launch", json!({ "package": "com.android.settings" }))
            .await;
    }
    env.eventually_shell(
        "Settings focused",
        ROTATION_STATE,
        ROTATION_LINES,
        &format!("app.launch com.android.settings (twice if needed) returned {launched}"),
        settings_focused,
    )
    .await;
    rotate_to(&env, 90, 1).await;
    rotate_to(&env, 0, 0).await;

    // Motion/environment sensors read back what was set.
    env.call(
        "sensor.set",
        json!({ "sensor": "light", "values": [123.0] }),
    )
    .await;
    let light = env.call("sensor.get", json!({ "sensor": "light" })).await;
    assert!(
        (light["values"][0].as_f64().unwrap() - 123.0).abs() < 0.5,
        "{light}"
    );

    // Network: Wi-Fi/mobile toggles and a speed/delay profile.
    env.call(
        "network.set",
        json!({ "wifi": false, "mobile": false, "profile": "edge" }),
    )
    .await;
    env.eventually("Wi-Fi off", |e| {
        e.shell("settings get global wifi_on").trim() == "0"
    })
    .await;
    // Mobile data is switched at the emulated radio (console `gsm data`).
    let registry = "dumpsys telephony.registry";
    mobile_to(&env, false).await;
    let net = env.call("network.get", json!({})).await;
    assert_eq!(net["mobile"], false, "{net}");
    let status = env.adb(&["emu", "network", "status"]);
    assert!(status.contains("473600 bits/s"), "edge speed: {status}");
    env.call(
        "network.set",
        json!({ "wifi": true, "mobile": true, "profile": "full" }),
    )
    .await;
    env.eventually("Wi-Fi on", |e| {
        e.shell("settings get global wifi_on").trim() == "1"
    })
    .await;
    mobile_to(&env, true).await;
    let net = env.call("network.get", json!({})).await;
    assert_eq!(net["mobile"], true, "{net}");

    // An incoming call is dropped while the radio isn't in service (on API 30
    // CI it was restarting when the call came), so wait for voice service.
    env.eventually_shell(
        "voice in service",
        registry,
        &["mServiceState="],
        "",
        |out| service_state(out).contains("mVoiceRegState=0("),
    )
    .await;

    // Phone: an incoming call rings, ending it goes idle; SMS lands in the inbox.
    env.call("phone.call", json!({ "number": "+218 91 234 5678" }))
        .await;
    env.eventually_shell(
        "ringing",
        "dumpsys telephony.registry",
        &["mCallState", "mCallIncomingNumber", "mVoiceRegState"],
        "",
        |out| out.contains("mCallState=1"),
    )
    .await;
    env.call(
        "phone.call",
        json!({ "number": "+218912345678", "action": "end" }),
    )
    .await;
    env.eventually("idle", |e| {
        e.shell("dumpsys telephony.registry")
            .contains("mCallState=0")
    })
    .await;
    env.call(
        "phone.sms",
        json!({ "from": "+218911111111", "text": "Courier is 4 min away" }),
    )
    .await;
    env.eventually("SMS in the inbox", |e| {
        e.shell("content query --uri content://sms/inbox --projection address:body")
            .contains("Courier is 4 min away")
    })
    .await;

    // Mobile signal bars (R3): more bars, stronger reported signal.
    env.call("phone.gsm", json!({ "signal": 0 })).await;
    env.eventually_shell("weak signal", registry, &["mSignalStrength"], "", |out| {
        signal_level(out).is_some_and(|l| l <= 1)
    })
    .await;
    env.call("phone.gsm", json!({ "signal": 4 })).await;
    env.eventually_shell("strong signal", registry, &["mSignalStrength"], "", |out| {
        signal_level(out).is_some_and(|l| l >= 3)
    })
    .await;

    // Android controls: Home shows the launcher, volume shows the volume panel.
    env.call("key.press", json!({ "key": "home" })).await;
    env.eventually("launcher focused", |e| {
        let w = e.shell("dumpsys window");
        w.lines()
            .any(|l| l.contains("mCurrentFocus") && l.to_lowercase().contains("launcher"))
    })
    .await;
    // The volume panel shows for a few seconds after a press and then hides,
    // and one `dumpsys window` can take that long on a CI runner. So press,
    // watch for up to 4 s, and press again if it was missed.
    let panel = |e: &common::Env| {
        e.shell("dumpsys window windows")
            .split("Window #")
            .any(|win| win.contains("VolumeDialogImpl") && win.contains("isVisible=true"))
    };
    let mut shown = false;
    'press: for _ in 0..5 {
        env.call("key.press", json!({ "key": "volume_up" })).await;
        let until = std::time::Instant::now() + std::time::Duration::from_secs(4);
        while std::time::Instant::now() < until {
            if panel(&env) {
                shown = true;
                break 'press;
            }
            tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(200)).await;
        }
    }
    assert!(shown, "volume panel never showed after 5 volume_up presses");

    // Developer toggles.
    env.call(
        "dev.set",
        json!({ "show_taps": true, "pointer_location": true, "layout_bounds": true, "animation_scale": 0.5 }),
    )
    .await;
    assert_eq!(env.shell("settings get system show_touches").trim(), "1");
    assert_eq!(
        env.shell("settings get system pointer_location").trim(),
        "1"
    );
    assert_eq!(env.shell("getprop debug.layout").trim(), "true");
    assert_eq!(
        env.shell("settings get global window_animation_scale")
            .trim(),
        "0.5"
    );
    env.call("dev.set", json!({ "show_taps": false, "pointer_location": false, "layout_bounds": false, "animation_scale": 1.0 })).await;
    assert_eq!(env.shell("settings get system show_touches").trim(), "0");

    // Clipboard round trip.
    env.call("clipboard.set", json!({ "text": "hello from jidr" }))
        .await;
    assert_eq!(
        env.call("clipboard.get", json!({})).await["text"],
        "hello from jidr"
    );

    // Fingerprint (R8): the HAL sees the finger land and lift.
    env.adb(&["logcat", "-c"]);
    env.call("fingerprint.touch", json!({ "finger": 1 })).await;
    env.call("fingerprint.remove", json!({})).await;
    // The HIDL HAL (`fingerprint@2.1`, API 31) logs every touch as
    // `FingerprintHal`. The AIDL HAL (`fingerprint-service.ranchu`, API 35)
    // logs only inside an enroll or authenticate session, so there it is
    // enough that the console accepted both commands and the HAL is up.
    let aidl =
        env.shell("service check android.hardware.biometrics.fingerprint.IFingerprint/default");
    if !service_found(&aidl) {
        env.eventually_shell(
            "fingerprint HAL events",
            "logcat -d",
            &["inger"],
            "",
            |log| {
                log.lines()
                    .any(|l| l.contains("FingerprintHal") && l.contains("off"))
            },
        )
        .await;
    }

    // Host webcam (R7): stored in the device's launch args for the next start.
    let cam = env.call("camera.set", json!({ "back": "webcam0" })).await;
    assert_eq!(cam["back"], "webcam0");
    let det = env.call("device.details", json!({})).await;
    let args = det["device"]["launch"]["extra_args"].as_array().unwrap();
    assert!(
        args.windows(2)
            .any(|w| w[0] == "-camera-back" && w[1] == "webcam0"),
        "{args:?}"
    );

    env.stop().await;
}

`docs/clean-room.md`:

```md
# Clean-room policy

Jidr re-creates the *behaviour* of Genymotion Desktop's public feature set. It must never derive from Genymotion's code, or from GPL code we don't want to inherit.

## Allowed sources

| Source | Use |
|---|---|
| Genymotion public docs (docs.genymotion.com, genymotion.com/pricing, /features) | Feature lists, user-visible behaviour, CLI command names, exit-code semantics |
| AOSP emulator public protos (`emulator_controller.proto`, `snapshot_service.proto`, shipped in the SDK) | gRPC API; we generate code from them (Apache-2.0) |
| developer.android.com emulator docs (command line, console, AVD management) | Flags, console commands, config.ini keys |
| Android SDK tools (`sdkmanager`, `avdmanager`, `adb`, `emulator`), run on the user's machine | Observed behaviour, outputs |
| Magisk and rootAVD scripts (GPL-3.0) | **Read only**, to learn the documented ramdisk layout. Never copy or translate code. |
| avdroot (MIT) | Prior art; may be ported with attribution in `NOTICE` |
| Public specs (cpio newc, gzip, lz4 legacy, xz) | Format implementations |

## Forbidden

- Decompiling, disassembling, string-dumping or otherwise inspecting Genymotion binaries, installers, images or network traffic.
- Copying or line-by-line translating GPL code (Magisk, rootAVD) into Apache-2.0 crates.
- Bundling or redistributing the Android SDK, emulator, system images or Magisk.
- Google, Android or Genymotion logos anywhere in the product or site.

## Log

Record any non-obvious source you used, so provenance can be audited later.

| Date | Stream | Source | What it informed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-13 | A | SDK `emulator/lib/emulator_controller.proto`, `snapshot_service.proto` (emulator 35.6.11) | gRPC bindings (`jidr-proto`) |
| 2026-10-13 | C | `man 5 cpio` (newc), the Linux kernel's initramfs buffer-format doc, RFC 1952 (gzip), the lz4 frame-format doc (legacy frame), the `.xz` format spec; the local SDK `ramdisk.img` files, read-only, decompressed with the `lz4`/`gzip` CLIs to observe the layout | `jidr-cpio` (Phase 9b) |
| 2026-10-14 | C | Magisk's `scripts/boot_patch.sh` (read-only, GPL) and avdroot's `internal/{magisk,cpio,adb}` (MIT) — the documented ramdisk entries (`init` → `magiskinit`, `overlay.d/sbin/{magisk,stub,init-ld}.xz`, `.backup/.magisk`), the payload/ABI layout inside the APK, the `/data/adb/magisk` environment, and the su-policy grant (`magisk --sqlite`). avdroot's algorithm is ported with attribution in `NOTICE`; no GPL code was copied. | `jidr-root` Magisk mode (Phase 9d) |
| 2026-10-15 | C | Magisk v30.7 `app/core` `Config.kt`, `SuRequestHandler.kt`, `PreferenceConfig.kt` and `native/src/core/su/db.rs` (read-only, GPL) — learned that the superuser "automatic response" is the SharedPreferences key `su_auto_response` (values `0` prompt / `1` deny / `2` allow), not a `magisk --sqlite` `settings` row; the native `uid_granted_root` only consults per-uid `policies`. No GPL code was copied. | `jidr-root` `root.auto_grant` (G15) |
| 2026-11-02 | B | `emulator_controller.proto` comments on `Touch.x`/`y` ("physical location on the screen") and `ImageFormat.rotation`; a temp tablet AVD with `pointer_location` on and `dumpsys input`, read over `adb` | Player touches are sent in unrotated panel pixels, mapped through the frame's rotation (#51) |

`docs/cli.md`:

```md
# `jidr` command line

`jidr` drives everything the Jidr app can do, from a terminal or a CI script. It talks to the Jidr daemon, which it starts automatically when needed (D4). Run `jidr --help` or `jidr <command> --help` for every flag; `jidr completions zsh|bash|fish` prints shell completions.

## Quick start

```bash
jidr image list                                   # images for this Mac
jidr image install 35 --accept-licenses           # API 35 google_apis
jidr device create Phone --image 35               # rooted with adb by default (D7)
jidr device start Phone                           # waits until booted
jidr install Phone app.apk
jidr logcat Phone -n 100
jidr device stop Phone
```

In CI, add `--json` and check the exit code:

```bash
jidr --json device start Phone --timeout 300 || exit $?
```

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `device create <name> --image <img> [--profile id] [--ram MB] [--cpus N] [--width px] [--height px] [--density dpi] [--data-mb MB] [--root none\|adb\|magisk] [--agent-owned]` | Create a device. `<img>` is `35`, `35:google_apis`, `35:google_apis_playstore`, `35:google_apis:arm64-v8a` or a full `system-images;…` package. |
| `device start <names…> \| --all [--cold-boot] [--no-wait] [--timeout s]` | Start and wait for boot. `--timeout` cancels the boot and exits 5. `--no-wait` returns the boot job id. |
| `device stop <names…> \| --all` | Stop, saving quick-boot state (D29). |
| `device list`, `device details <name>`, `device connect-info <name>` | Status, settings and disk usage; the gRPC endpoint/token and adb serial of a running device. |
| `device clone <name> <new>`, `device edit <name> [--rename n] [--ram …] [--agent-owned bool]` | Copy or change a stopped device. |
| `device reset <name> --yes`, `device delete <names…> \| --all --yes` | Destructive: wipe data, or delete. Without `--yes` they ask on a terminal and refuse otherwise. |
| `install <name> <apk> [--no-replace] [--grant] [--downgrade]` | Install an APK. A signature mismatch fails with `details.signature_mismatch = true`. |
| `push <name> <local> [remote]`, `pull <name> <remote> <local>` | Copy files (push defaults to `/sdcard/Download/`). |
| `logcat <name> [-n N] [--filter spec…] [-f] [--clear]` | Dump, follow (`-f`) or clear the log. |
| `flash <name> <zip>` | Not available yet (open research item). |
| `image list [--installed]`, `image install <img> [--accept-licenses]` | System images. |
| `profile list` | Built-in hardware profiles (D24). |
| `sdk status`, `sdk licenses <pkgs…>`, `sdk install <pkgs…> [--accept-licenses]` | The SDK Jidr uses (its private one; Android Studio's is only read, D3). |
| `root set <name> none\|adb\|magisk`, `root verify <name>`, `root status <name>` | Root modes (provided by the root engine). |
| `snapshot list\|save\|load\|delete <name> [snapshot]` | Snapshots tagged with their root mode (provided by the widgets provider). |
| `proxy set <name> [host:]port`, `proxy clear <name>`, `proxy show <name>` | The device's global HTTP proxy (widgets provider, `network.proxy.*`). The host defaults to `10.0.2.2`, this Mac. |
| `jobs list [--all]`, `jobs wait <job>`, `jobs cancel <job>` | Long-running operations. |
| `commands` | Every protocol command (what the GUI and MCP see). |
| `call <method> [params-json]` | Call any protocol command directly, e.g. `jidr call device.start '{"device":"Phone","cold_boot":true}'`. Follows jobs. |
| `daemon [run]`, `daemon stop`, `daemon status` | Run the daemon in the foreground, stop it (devices keep running), or show it. |
| `completions <shell>` | Shell completions. |

Global flags: `--json`, `-q/--quiet` (no progress), `--restart-stale` (or `JIDR_RESTART_STALE=1`).

## HTTP proxy

Point a running device at Burp, mitmproxy or any HTTP proxy on your Mac:

```bash
jidr proxy set Phone 8080             # 10.0.2.2:8080, the Mac's port 8080
jidr proxy set Phone 192.168.1.5:3128 # a proxy elsewhere on the network
jidr proxy show Phone
jidr proxy clear Phone
```

Inside the emulator `10.0.2.2` is the Mac's `127.0.0.1`, so Burp's default listener (`127.0.0.1:8080`) works as it is; `127.0.0.1` on the device is the device itself. The proxy is Android's global `http_proxy` setting: apps that use the system proxy (most HTTP stacks, WebView, Chrome) send their traffic through it, on Wi-Fi and mobile data. It takes effect at once and stays across restarts and snapshots until you clear it. To read HTTPS, apps must also trust the proxy's CA certificate.

## Licenses (D8)

Images and the emulator are downloaded from Google on your machine, after you accept their license. On a terminal, `jidr image install` shows each license and asks. Headless, `--accept-licenses` prints each license id and the SHA-256 of its text, then records your consent. Read the texts first with `jidr sdk licenses <package>`. When a license text changes, Jidr asks again.

## JSON output (`--json`)

Every command prints exactly one JSON line (`logcat -f` prints one per log line):

```json
{"jidr_json": 1, "ok": true, "result": …}
{"jidr_json": 1, "ok": false, "error": {"code": "not_found", "exit_code": 3, "message": "no device named \"x\"", "data": null}}
```

`jidr_json` is the envelope version; it changes only on breaking changes (see the changelog below). `result` is the protocol result of the underlying command (docs/control-protocol.md). Commands that act on several devices (`device start|stop|delete`) return an array.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | OK |
| 1 | Unexpected error |
| 2 | Usage: bad arguments or params, unknown command, missing `--yes` |
| 3 | Not found (device, image, job…), or the device isn't running |
| 4 | Busy: another operation holds the device (`error.data.holder` is the job) |
| 5 | Boot timeout |
| 6 | SDK, emulator, download or license problem |
| 7 | Root failed |
| 8 | Daemon stale: a daemon of another version is running (use `--restart-stale`) |

## Environment

| Variable | Effect |
|---|---|
| `JIDR_HOME` | Put all Jidr data under this directory (tests, portable setups) |
| `JIDR_LOG` | Daemon log filter, e.g. `debug` |
| `JIDR_DAEMON_BIN` | The `jidr` binary used to auto-start the daemon |
| `JIDR_SDK_REPO` | SDK repository mirror (default Google's) |
| `JIDR_RESTART_STALE` | Same as `--restart-stale` |

## Changelog

| `jidr_json` | Change |
|---|---|
| 1 | Initial format. |

`docs/control-protocol.md`:

```md
# Jidr control protocol (v0.1)

The daemon (`jidr daemon`) owns every device. The GUI, the CLI (`jidr`) and the MCP server (`jidr mcp`) are clients of this protocol and nothing else, so anything one client can do, all can. Reference client: `crates/jidr-client`.

Frozen as **v0.1** at the git tag `protocol-v0.1`. A change after the tag needs an entry in the [changelog](#changelog).

## Transport

- **Socket:** a Unix domain socket at `~/Library/Application Support/Jidr/daemon.sock` (`$JIDR_HOME/data/daemon.sock` when `JIDR_HOME` is set), mode `0600`. One daemon per user; a second one refuses to start.
- **Framing:** [JSON-RPC 2.0](https://www.jsonrpc.org/specification), one JSON object per line (newline-delimited JSON, as in MCP's stdio transport). Lines are at most 4 MB.
- **Concurrency:** requests on one connection run concurrently; match answers by `id`. Notifications from the daemon have no `id`.
- **Lifetime (D4):** clients start the daemon on demand (`jidr daemon`, detached). It exits after 10 minutes with no running device, no connected client and no active job. Emulators that outlive a daemon are re-adopted by the next one.

## Handshake

The first request on a connection must be `hello`. Anything else before it gets `-32600`.

```json
→ {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"hello","params":{"version":"0.1.0","client":"cli"}}
← {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"version":"0.1.0","protocol":"0.1","pid":4242}}
```

Clients ship with the daemon, so versions must be equal; there's no negotiation. A mismatch means a stale daemon from an older install:

```json
← {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"error":{"code":-32008,"message":"the running daemon is 0.1.0 but this client is 0.2.0; restart the daemon","data":{"code":"daemon_stale","exit_code":8,"details":{"daemon_version":"0.1.0","client_version":"0.2.0"}}}}
```

`daemon.shutdown` is the one method allowed before `hello`: it lets a newer client replace a stale daemon. Running emulators keep running and are re-adopted.

## Errors

Protocol errors use the standard JSON-RPC codes. Jidr errors carry one of eight codes, which are also the CLI's exit codes, in `error.data.code`; `error.data.details` holds structured extras.

| `data.code` | JSON-RPC code | CLI exit | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| — | -32700 | 2 | Not valid JSON |
| — | -32600 | 2 | Not a valid request (wrong `jsonrpc`, no `hello` yet) |
| — | -32601 | 2 | Unknown method |
| `usage` | -32602 | 2 | Invalid params; the message names the offending key |
| `unexpected` | -32001 | 1 | A bug, or an error we didn't classify |
| `not_found` | -32003 | 3 | No such device, image, profile, job or snapshot (or the device isn't running) |
| `busy` | -32004 | 4 | Another operation holds the device: `details: {holder, op, device}` |
| `boot_timeout` | -32005 | 5 | The device didn't boot in time |
| `sdk` | -32006 | 6 | SDK, emulator, adb, download or license problem (`details.pending_licenses` lists what to accept) |
| `root_failed` | -32007 | 7 | Rooting, verifying or reverting root failed |
| `daemon_stale` | -32008 | 8 | Client and daemon versions differ |

Params are checked against the command's JSON Schema before anything runs: unknown keys, missing required keys and wrong primitive types are all `-32602`.

## Devices and locks

Commands take a device as `"device": "<name or id>"`; names are unique, case-insensitive. Commands marked *locks the device* take a per-device single-writer lock. A conflicting call fails immediately with `busy`; it doesn't queue. Reads never lock.

## Jobs

Commands marked *long-running* don't block. After validation and locking they answer:

```json
← {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":7,"result":{"job":"4b0c…","pending":true}}
```

The job holds the device lock until it ends. Follow it with `jobs.wait` (blocks until it ends, or `timeout_s`), `jobs.get`, or events. Cancel it with `jobs.cancel`: the work stops and the device stays as it was. A job ends `succeeded` (with `result`), `failed` (with `error`, same shape as above) or `cancelled`.

## Events

`events.subscribe {"topics": ["device.", "job."]}` (prefixes; empty = everything) makes the daemon push notifications on that connection:

```json
← {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"event","params":{"topic":"device.boot","data":{"device":"…","stage":"adb_online","progress":0.5}}}
```

Subscribing again replaces the filter. Topics:

| Topic | Data |
|---|---|
| `device.status` | `{device, name, status}`: status is `{state: stopped\|starting\|booting\|running\|stopping\|crashed, …}` |
| `device.boot` | `{device, stage: spawned\|grpc_ready\|adb_online\|booted, progress}` |
| `device.boot_failed` | `{device, error}` |
| `device.crashed` | `{device, report: {kind, reason, exit_code, log, …}}`; never restarted (D9) |
| `device.created`, `device.deleted`, `device.updated` | `{device, name}` |
| `device.hook_failed` | `{device, provider, error}`: a provider's after-boot hook failed |
| `job.started` | `{job, kind, device}` |
| `job.progress` | `{job, progress, message}` |
| `job.finished` | the full job |
| `job.cancelling` | `{job}` |
| `logcat` | `{device, line}` (only after `logcat.follow`) |
| `events.lagged` | `{missed}`: the connection fell behind and events were dropped |

## Connection-scoped methods

These act on the calling connection and aren't in `commands.list`:

| Method | Params | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `hello` | `{version, client?}` | Handshake (above) |
| `commands.list` | — | Every command below, with its params schema |
| `events.subscribe` | `{topics?: string[]}` | Push matching events to this connection |
| `logcat.follow` | `{device, filter?: string[]}` | Push `logcat` events for a running device until the connection closes |
| `daemon.shutdown` | — | Stop the daemon (allowed before `hello`) |

## Commands

Providers register commands with an id, a label, a params JSON Schema and three flags: `destructive` (MCP refuses it unless allowed, D5), `longRunning` and `locksDevice`. The daemon core provides the commands below; `jidr-widgets` (sensors, phone, network, media, snapshots) and `jidr-root` (root modes) add theirs when they land. `commands.list` is always the source of truth.

`docs/decisions/0001-frame-transport.md`:

```md
# ADR-0001: Frame transport for the player

- **Status:** Accepted (Phase 1 spike: **pass**, 2026-10-13)
- **Spike:** a throwaway crate (`spike-display`), removed after this decision; the numbers below are its measurements.

## Context

The player window renders the emulator screen and sends input back. The budget is **≥ 30 fps** at 1080×2400 downscaled to a 400 px-wide window and **≤ 80 ms** median input latency on an M-series Mac. Per D20 we try the simplest path first, inline RGBA frames over gRPC into a Slint `SharedPixelBuffer`, and move to MMAP transport or a wgpu texture import only if the budget is missed. egui is the documented fallback.

## What was measured

Setup: MacBook Pro M1 Pro, emulator 35.6.11, spike-only AVD (API 31 `google_apis` arm64, 1080×2400, 420 dpi, 4 cores, 2 GB), launched `-no-window -no-boot-anim -no-snapshot -no-audio -grpc <port> -grpc-use-token`, Slint 1.18 (default winit + femtovg backend), release build.

Pipeline: `streamScreenshot(RGBA8888, width, height)` → newest-frame slot (one UI hop in flight; newer frames replace older ones) → `slint::invoke_from_event_loop` → `SharedPixelBuffer::<Rgba8Pixel>::clone_from_slice` → `Image`. Input: Slint `TouchArea` → device pixels → client-streaming `streamInputEvent` (touch, pressure 0 on release, `NEVER_EXPIRE`).

- **fps bench** (`--bench fps`): opens Settings, injects alternating 300 ms drags over gRPC for 10 s. "Active fps" = 1 / median frame interval, gaps > 100 ms between drags excluded.
- **latency bench** (`--bench latency`): `show_touches=1`, home screen, 30 taps; time from sending the touch-down to the first frame on the UI thread whose probe pixel changed (the show-taps dot).

| `-gpu` | Frame size | Active fps (median / p10) | Throughput | Frame age (emulator ts → UI) | Touch → changed frame on UI thread (median / p90) | CPU emulator / player |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `host` | 400 px (399×888) | **59.9** / 55.9 | 84 MB/s | 2.0 ms | **13.5 / 16.1 ms** | 280% / 17% |
| `host` | 800 px (799×1777, Retina 2×) | **59.9** / 56.5 | 329 MB/s | 5.4 ms | **13.5 / 25.7 ms** | 315% / 40% |
| `auto` | 800 px | 39.8 / 25.3 | 212 MB/s | 15.4 ms | 31.7 / 43.6 ms | 610% / 26% |
| `auto` | 400 px | ~35 | 49 MB/s | 10.7 ms | — | 583% / 11% |
| `auto` | width only (no downscale, 1080×2400) | 26.6 avg | 276 MB/s | 25.9 ms | — | 545% / 33% |

Estimated input-to-photon with `-gpu host`: 13.5 ms (measured) + up to one 60 Hz vsync to present (≤ 16.7 ms) + host input delivery (a few ms) ≈ **35 ms**, well under 80 ms. The probe doesn't include the OS input path or scanout, so 35 ms is an estimate with those as upper bounds.

## Decision

1. **Inline RGBA8888 over gRPC + Slint `SharedPixelBuffer`.** It passes with a wide margin. MMAP transport and wgpu texture import are **not needed**, and egui stays a fallback only.
2. **Launch emulators with `-gpu host`** on macOS. Under `-no-window`, `auto` falls back to software rendering: 2× the emulator CPU, ~40 fps, 2–3× the latency. The backend (Phase 3b) owns this default. A device setting may override it later (e.g. `swiftshader_indirect` for CI or broken GPU drivers).
3. **Always request both `width` and `height`** in `ImageFormat`. The emulator ignores a width-only request and sends full-resolution frames (finding, emulator 35.6.11). It keeps the aspect ratio and may round down by 1 px (400 → 399×888).
4. **Request frames at the window's physical pixel size** (logical width × scale factor, capped at the device size). Re-subscribe on resize or rotation.
5. **Keep only the newest frame**: one `invoke_from_event_loop` in flight, and frames arriving meanwhile overwrite the slot. The UI never builds a backlog.
6. Frames arrive **top-down** (row 0 = top), despite the proto comment saying "bottom up". No flip is needed.

## Consequences

- The player window (Phase 7c) is built on this path and uses `device.connect_info` for the gRPC endpoint + token.
- The backend (Phase 3b) launches with `-gpu host` by default and exposes the GPU mode in `LaunchOptions`.
- Streaming at 2× Retina costs ~330 MB/s on loopback and ~40% of one core in the player. Acceptable. Re-check if multiple players are open at once.
- CI (Linux KVM, no GPU) needs `-gpu swiftshader_indirect`. CI only runs functional tests, not the fps budget.

## Not verified by the spike

- Manual check "tap Settings and confirm it opens" through a mouse click in the window. The spike's scripted gRPC drags and taps exercise the same input path, but the mouse → `TouchArea` → device-pixel mapping needs a human click. It remains a manual check in the player window.
- Multi-touch, keyboard and rotation. They belong in Phase 7c.

```

`docs/decisions/0002-play-store-root.md`:

```md
# ADR-0002: Full root on Play Store images (Phase 9a)

- **Status:** Accepted (2026-10-14)
- **Date:** 2026-10-13

## Context

D6 and D21 ask for full Magisk support on `google_apis_playstore` images, trying in order: (1) a boot-time grant of the adb shell's uid in Magisk's policy store, (2) an automated tap on Magisk's Grant prompt, (3) a guided tap as a beta fallback.

Play Store images don't allow `adb root`. So the shell can't write Magisk's policy itself the way it can on `google_apis` images, and the first `su` from the shell shows Magisk's prompt on the device.

## Scope

- Options (1) and (2) were **not attempted**. Both grant root to the shell without a person approving Magisk's prompt, so they're left to the maintainer to revisit by hand.
- Option (3) keeps the person in the loop. It is specified below so 9d can ship it as the Play Store beta (D6 fallback).

## Proposed beta flow: guided tap (option 3)

1. Full-root setup runs exactly as on `google_apis` (9d): patched private ramdisk, cold boot, Magisk app install, environment setup, one reboot.
2. Jidr opens the device window and shows one instruction beside the screen: "Magisk will ask to grant root to Shell. Tap Grant." Magisk's own "Forever" option is left to the user.
3. Jidr runs `su -c id` from the adb shell, which raises Magisk's normal prompt. It waits up to 60 s, with a Cancel button.
4. Verify: `adb shell su -c id` → `uid=0` and `su -c 'magisk -v'`. The badge reads "Rooted ✓ · Beta (Play Store image)".
5. Denied or timed out: the badge reads "Root unverified", with "Try again" (repeats step 3) and "Revert" (9d revert).
6. Headless or CLI (`jidr root set magisk` on a Play Store image): the command prints the same instruction and waits; `--json` reports `{"state": "awaiting_user_grant"}` until verified. There is no headless bypass.

Apps keep Magisk's normal per-app prompt (D22). The "auto-grant all" toggle stays opt-in and off.

## Decision

Accepted on 2026-10-14:
- Option (3), the guided tap above, ships as the **Play Store beta for the MVP** (D6 fallback), built in Phase 9d.
- Options (1) and (2) are **deferred to post-MVP**, to be revisited by hand by the maintainer. No AI agent builds them.

## Consequences

- With (3), Play Store full root needs one tap per device, once. `google_apis` images stay zero-touch.
- Phase 9a is Done as a beta pass under this decision: options (1) and (2) were deferred, not tried and failed.

```

`docs/decisions/log.md`:

```md
# Decisions log

Product and architecture decisions made while building the MVP (October 2026). Code comments cite them as `D<n>`. Architecture decisions with more context are the ADRs in this folder (`0001-…`, `0002-…`).

To change a decision, open an issue that names it and explains why; the change lands as a new or amended row here, never as a silent edit elsewhere.

| # | Decision |
|---|---|
| D1 | Name **Jidr** (جذر, "root"). CLI `jidr`, crates `jidr-*`, app `Jidr.app`, site `jidr.ly`. |
| D2 | UI toolkit **Slint** (GPLv3 accepted); possible egui migration later. |
| D3 | Private SDK; Android Studio SDK/AVDs read-only. |
| D4 | Daemon auto-starts on first client, lives while devices run, exits 10 min after the last stops; no launchd agent. |
| D5 | MCP: read/interact/start/stop by default; destructive actions need `--allow-destructive` or an `agent-owned` device. |
| D6 | Play Store + Magisk: pursue full support first (D21), guided-tap beta only as fallback. |
| D7 | Default root mode: `adb` on images that allow it; Magisk one click away and highlighted. |
| D8 | Headless license consent via `--accept-licenses`, per license hash, re-prompt on change. |
| D9 | Dynamic ports (no cap; `adb connect` past ~16); no auto-restart on crash, logs auto-saved, offer cold boot/wipe; per-device single-writer lock. |
| D10 | Own CLI + exit codes, versioned `--json`; no gmtool-compat layer in the MVP. |
| D11 | 🔎 research features ship post-MVP as listed gaps. |
| D12 | Shared folders post-MVP. |
| D13 | Recording: MP4/H.264 via VideoToolbox from the frame stream; audio post-MVP. |
| D14 | GPS map: OpenStreetMap tiles, attribution, configurable URL; GPX/KML replay. |
| D15 | MVP = Apple Silicon macOS only; code stays portable. |
| D16 | Landing page: Astro + Vue islands on Cloudflare Pages. |
| D17 | No telemetry; no auto-updater. Updates come from the Homebrew cask (`brew upgrade --cask jidr`), or from Settings › About › Check for updates, which asks GitHub's latest-release API only when clicked and links the new release (amended in #44). |
| D18 | Split licensing: Apache-2.0 everywhere except `jidr-ui` + `apps/jidr-gui` (GPLv3). |
| D19 | Names/handles as in D1. |
| D20 | Phase 1 spike tests Slint only (`SharedPixelBuffer`, then wgpu import if needed); egui is the documented fallback. |
| D21 | Play Store root R&D order: ramdisk boot-script grant → uiautomator auto-tap → guided-tap beta. |
| D22 | Magisk devices: adb shell auto-granted; apps prompt; opt-in "auto-grant all" per device. |
| D23 | API 29–36 arm64 supported; 28 best-effort; 25–27 not offered. |
| D24 | Generic device profile names; SDK device definitions imported as-is. |
| D25 | No paid tier; GitHub Sponsors (Open Collective later). |
| D26 | Repo stays at `github.com/AbdurahmanAlmehdi/jidr` (the `jidr-dev` org move was dropped on 2026-10-17). The Homebrew cask lives in the `AbdurahmanAlmehdi/homebrew-tap` tap; the MCP Registry name is `io.github.AbdurahmanAlmehdi/jidr`. |
| D27 | Built in three parallel streams after the core platform: A core platform, B player and widgets, C root, release and site. |
| D28 | CI: Linux KVM runners (x86_64 images) for emulator tests on every PR; `cargo xtask e2e-mac` on an Apple Silicon Mac (arm64) before release. |
| D29 | Stop saves a quick-boot snapshot by default; cold boot is separate; root changes force a cold boot; root-tagged snapshots. |
| D30 | Magisk APK cache by SHA-256, `--magisk <path>` offline, `jidr cache prune`, per-device disk usage. |
| D31 | `jidr uninstall [--purge]` + "Remove all data…"; never touches the Studio SDK; removes Jidr MCP config entries. |
| D32 | Signing with the maintainer's Apple Developer ID; unsigned DMG with a CI warning until the signing secrets exist. |
| D33 | English-only MVP, all strings via `@tr`, RTL-checked; Arabic UI post-MVP; Arabic landing page at launch. |
| D34 | Pre-launch "coming soon" site without email capture; brand: a root growing into a phone outline, جذر + Latin wordmark. |
| D35 | Dropped `.zip`: Magisk module install + reboot on Full-root devices; otherwise pushed to `/sdcard/Download` with a note. No image flashing (R12). |
| D36 | Phase 8a adds fingerprint touch/remove (R8), mobile signal bars (R3) and host webcam camera (R7); all other custom-work findings are post-MVP. |
| D37 | Research findings accepted with their stated targets (post-MVP items are GitHub issues labelled `upcoming feature`); R10 Device Link rejected. MVP+ queue after the MVP: R5 build props (Magisk `resetprop`), R12 modules. R6 disk I/O moved to Post-MVP after the proof run (the emulator kernel has no block throttling). |
| D38 | Research proofs ran on a throwaway arm64 AVD. |
| D39 | Brand assets live in `assets/brand/` (regenerated by `assets/brand/build.sh` from the approved symbol). App icons in `apps/jidr-gui/assets/` (`Jidr.icns`, in-app `symbol.svg`, menu-bar template); web set in `assets/brand/web/`, copied into `site/public/`. |
| D40 | R15 WebRTC not needed: ADR-0001 passed with inline RGBA frames. Phase 9d adds `root.module.install` (D35). R5 becomes Phase 9f (MVP+). Repo made public (CI on standard runners is free). |
| D41 | Design adopted: direction **Workbench** (dark-first). Tokens in `docs/design/tokens.json` are the single source; Slint `theme.slint` is generated by `jidr-ui/build.rs` and the site's `tokens.css` by a site script. Fonts Geist / Geist Mono / Noto Kufi Arabic bundled (OFL). Lucide icons. Chosen concepts: launcher 1A (sidebar + detail), device window 4A (docked panel), landing 8A. Index: `docs/design/README.md`. The app icon keeps its approved gradient; the UI uses tokens only. |
| D43 | Agent skills (2026-11-02, Phases 14a–14c) ship in the repo's `skills/` folder, installed with `npx skills add AbdurahmanAlmehdi/jidr`; no npm package. Four skills: `jidr` (basics), `jidr-app-testing`, `jidr-agent-devices` (after 13d), `jidr-root` (after 9d, stream C). `cargo xtask skills-check` keeps them in sync with the CLI. |

`docs/design/PRODUCT.md`:

```md
# Jidr (جذر): product brief for designers

> The source of truth for design work. If anything here seems ambiguous, the decisions in `docs/decisions/log.md` settle it.

## 1. What Jidr is

Jidr (Arabic جذر, *JID-er*, "root") is a **free, open-source Android emulator for the Mac**. It is a desktop app, plus a command-line tool and an AI-agent (MCP) server, that creates and runs virtual Android phones and tablets.

It does what Genymotion Desktop does (a polished device manager, a device window and sensor controls) and adds four things:

1. **One-click rooted devices.** You pick a root mode when you create a device: *None*, *Shell root (adb)* or *Full root (Magisk)*. Jidr does the rest and shows a verified "Rooted" badge. This is the headline feature.
2. **Everything free.** Genymotion's paid features (CLI automation, network profiles, GPS route replay, quick boot, root toggle) cost nothing here.
3. **Agent-native.** Every button is also a CLI command and an MCP tool, so an AI agent can drive a device: screenshot, tap, type, read logs.
4. **Snapshots done right.** Save and restore device states, each tagged with its root mode.

Under the hood it runs Google's open-source Android emulator headless. Jidr's own window shows the screen. We never ship Google's binaries: Jidr downloads them on the user's machine after they accept Google's license.

## 2. Who uses it

| Persona | Wants | Signature moment |
|---|---|---|
| **Sara, mobile developer** | A fast, good-looking emulator that's free; sensors for testing (GPS, battery, network) | Drags an APK onto the device; it installs |
| **Karim, security researcher** | Rooted devices with Magisk, Play Store images, snapshots to roll back | Clicks *Full root*; 60 s later, "Rooted · Magisk 30.7 ✓" |
| **CI pipeline** | Headless create → boot → test → destroy, JSON output | Never sees the UI (CLI only) |
| **AI agent (via MCP)** | Screenshot, tap, read UI tree, logcat | Never sees the UI, but users watch the device window while an agent drives it |

Users are technical, on macOS (Apple Silicon), and often keep the app open all day beside their IDE. They value density, keyboard shortcuts and speed, but the first-run experience must be friendly for someone who has never installed the Android SDK.

## 3. Surfaces

1. **Launcher window**: the device library. Lists devices, their status, Android version, root mode, disk usage; create, start, stop, clone, delete; jobs in progress (downloads, root setup).
2. **First-run setup**: detects whether an Android SDK exists; shows Google's SDK license (must be scrolled and explicitly accepted); downloads the emulator and a first system image with progress.
3. **Create / edit device**: hardware profile, Android version (system image), root mode, RAM, CPU cores, resolution and density, name.
4. **Device window (player)**: the live Android screen (the hero), a vertical toolbar (volume, rotate, back, home, recents, power, screenshot, record, pixel-perfect) and a **widget panel** that opens beside the screen.
5. **Widgets**: Battery · GPS (map, coordinates, GPX/KML route replay) · Rotation and motion sensors · Phone and SMS · Network (Wi-Fi/mobile on/off, speed/delay profiles) · Identifiers · Android controls (D-pad, media keys) · Developer tools (root, show taps, layout bounds, animations) · Biometrics (fingerprint touch) · Clipboard · Microphone input · Snapshots · Logcat.
6. **Root setup flow**: a short, honest progress sequence (download Magisk → patch → reboot → install → verify), with a clear success badge, a clear failure state, and one-click revert.
7. **Settings**: SDK location and disk usage, cache, MCP setup ("Add Jidr to Claude"), map tile source, default root mode, about and licenses.
8. **Landing page (jidr.ly)**: a pre-launch "coming soon" page, then the full marketing site: hero, root showcase, "Genymotion's paid features, free", agent/MCP section, CLI snippet, download, sponsors, Arabic version.

## 4. Non-negotiables

- **The Android screen is the hero** of the device window. Chrome around it is quiet and narrow; nothing overlaps the screen.
- **Root state is unmistakable** wherever a device appears: label + icon, never colour alone. "Verified" vs "Unverified" vs "Failed" must be distinct.
- **Status is honest**: Booting, Running, Stopped, Crashed, Busy (another client is using it) are always visible on device rows.
- **Keyboard-first**: every action has a shortcut or command palette (⌘K) entry.
- **Native macOS feel**: traffic lights, standard menus, standard sheet and popover behaviour; dark mode first-class.
- **Buildable in Slint** (Rust GUI toolkit): solid fills, borders, rounded rects, simple shadows, images, paths; no heavy blur/vibrancy dependencies, no web views.
- **No Google, Android or Genymotion logos or trademarks** in the UI or site (Google SDK license §3.7). Use our own device silhouettes.
- **Honesty about limits**: e.g. "Rooted emulators can't pass Play Integrity" is stated plainly where relevant.
- **RTL-ready**: English-only at launch, but layouts must mirror cleanly for Arabic later.
- **Accessible**: text contrast ≥ 4.5:1, focus rings visible, nothing conveyed by colour alone.

## 5. Statuses (user-facing labels)

| Kind | States (label shown to user) |
|---|---|
| Device | Stopped · Starting… · Booting Android… · Running · Paused · Stopping… · Crashed · Busy (in use by CLI/agent) |
| Root | Not rooted · Shell root (adb) · Full root · Magisk 30.7 · Setting up root… · Rooted ✓ (verified) · Root unverified · Root failed: details · Beta (Play Store image) |
| Job | Queued · Downloading 1.4 / 2.1 GB · Patching · Rebooting · Verifying · Done · Failed · Cancelled |
| Snapshot | Quick boot (auto) · Named snapshot · Taken with: Full root / Shell root / Not rooted |
| SDK | Not installed · Needs license acceptance · Installing · Ready · Update available |

## 6. What the daemon really returns (design within this data)

- **Device**: id, name, profile name, screen W×H and density, Android version + API level (e.g. "Android 15 · API 35"), image tag (Google APIs / Play Store / AOSP), status, root mode + root health + Magisk version + last verified time, RAM, CPU cores, disk usage (GB), adb serial (`emulator-5556`), uptime, last started.
- **Job**: id, kind, device, progress 0–1, bytes done/total, state, error message.
- **Snapshot**: name, created at, size, root mode tag, thumbnail (PNG).
- **Widgets**: battery level and charging state; GPS lat/long/alt/accuracy/bearing; rotation angle; network type + speed/delay profile; Wi-Fi/mobile on/off; clipboard text; Android ID.
- **Logcat**: timestamp, level (V/D/I/W/E/F), tag, pid, message.
- **Not available** (don't design as if they exist; mark as optional ideas if you want them): live CPU/RAM graphs per device, per-app network traffic, cloud devices, accounts or sign-in, team sharing.

## 7. Sample data (use this so screens feel real and agree)

| Device | Profile | Android | Image | Root | Status | Disk |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Pixel-ish 6.1** | Phone 6.1″ FHD+ (1080×2400, 420 dpi) | Android 15 · API 35 | Google APIs | Rooted ✓ · Magisk 30.7 | Running · 2 h 14 m | 6.8 GB |
| **Tablet 11** | Tablet 11″ (1600×2560, 320 dpi) | Android 14 · API 34 | Google APIs | Shell root (adb) | Stopped | 4.1 GB |
| **Play Store test** | Phone 6.1″ FHD+ | Android 13 · API 33 | Play Store | Full root · Beta | Booting Android… 62% | 5.3 GB |
| **CI-runner-03** | Small phone 5″ (720×1280) | Android 11 · API 30 | AOSP | Not rooted | Busy · in use by CLI | 3.0 GB |

- Job: "Downloading Android 16 (API 36) image · 1.4 / 2.1 GB · 2 min left".
- GPS: Tripoli Martyrs' Square, 32.8954, 13.1802; route replay `tripoli-airport-run.gpx` at 2×.
- Battery: 64%, discharging.
- Snapshots on Pixel-ish 6.1: "Clean install" (Full root, 2.1 GB), "Logged in test account" (Full root, 2.4 GB), "Quick boot" (auto).
- Logcat lines: `I/ActivityManager: Start proc 4821:com.example.shop/u0a190`, `W/Magisk: su: request from uid 10190 (com.example.shop)`, `E/AndroidRuntime: FATAL EXCEPTION: main`.
- CLI snippet: `jidr device create "Pixel-ish 6.1" --api 35 --root magisk --wait-boot`.

## 8. Design and brand

The design is done: see `docs/design/README.md` (Workbench direction, tokens, components, final screens).

### Brand

The app icon and symbol are done: see `assets/brand/README.md` (symbol = a root growing into a phone outline; brand blue `#2A88FA → #1267E0`, lilac `#B9A6F7` for the Arabic wordmark).

## 9. Tone

Confident, technical, warm. Short labels. Say what happens ("Reboots the device to finish root setup (about 40 s)"). No hype, no exclamation marks, no emoji in the UI.

```

`docs/design/README.md`:

```md
# Jidr design

Direction **Workbench**: one IDE-like window, dark-first, soft cards, devices open as tabs. Read `system/README.md` first: it holds the voice, colour, status, type, motion, icon and RTL rules.

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Tokens (W3C DTCG, dark and light) | `tokens.json` |
| Design-system rules | `system/README.md` |
| Component specs (50) | `system/components/<Name>/README.md` |
| Component CSS (the app's reduced-motion overrides come from it) | `system/components/bundle.css` |
| Workbench component CSS (the site's styles are pruned from it) | `jidr.css` |
| Product brief | `PRODUCT.md` |
| Brand (icon, symbol, web set) | `../../assets/brand/` |

Chosen concepts: launcher **1A** (sidebar device list and device detail), device window **4A** (docked widget panel), landing page **8A** (headline over the app).

## Implementation rules (D41)

- **One source:** `tokens.json`. Never hand-copy hex values.
  - The **Slint** theme (`crates/jidr-ui/ui/theme.slint`, `export global Theme`) is generated from it by `crates/jidr-ui/build.rs`.
  - The **site's** `site/src/styles/tokens.css` is generated from it by a script in `site/`.
  - Naming: CSS `--jidr-color-surface-raised` → Slint `Theme.surface-raised`. A leading `color-` is dropped in Slint; every other path stays the same.
- **Fonts:** Geist, Geist Mono and Noto Kufi Arabic (all OFL-1.1). Bundle them in the app (`apps/jidr-gui/assets/fonts/`, with licences) because Slint can't fetch web fonts. Self-host them on the site rather than loading Google Fonts.
- **Icons:** Lucide only (ISC). SVGs are loaded with `@image-url` and tinted with `colorize`. Credit Lucide in About › Licenses and the site footer.
- **Brand vs tokens:** the app icon gradient (`#2A88FA → #1267E0`, `assets/brand/`) is the approved icon and stays as is. Inside the UI, use tokens only: accent `jidr-color-accent-*` for actions, root violet `jidr-color-root` for root only. The Arabic wordmark جذر uses `jidr-color-root`.
- Slint constraints the system already respects: no dashed borders, one shadow per element, no web fonts.

```
