`docs/design/system/README.md`:

```md
Jidr (جذر, *JID-er*, "root") is a free, open-source Android emulator for the Mac: a desktop app built in Slint (Rust), a CLI and an MCP server, plus the jidr.ly landing page built in Astro. This system is direction **Workbench**: one window like an IDE, dark-first, soft cards, devices open as tabs. Both products read the same tokens.

## One source, two products

- `tokens.json` here mirrors the product's W3C design-token file. Every name is the product's CSS custom property without the leading `--`: `jidr-color-surface-raised` is `--jidr-color-surface-raised` on the site and `Theme.surface-raised` in Slint (a leading `color-` is dropped in Slint; everything else is the same path).
- Never put a raw hex in a component. Read colours through semantic tokens, and status colours through `jidr-status-<kind>-<state>-*`, never through the shared pairs or `jidr-color-positive` directly.
- The two themes are `dark` (primary) and `light`. Design dark first, then check light; do not invert one into the other.
- Typography composites (`--jidr-type-<role>-size`, `-line-height`, `-weight`, `-letter-spacing`, `-family`) are mirrored in `components/bundle.css` from the type styles below. Reduce Motion overrides live there too.

## Voice and copy

Confident, technical, warm. Short labels, sentence case, no exclamation marks, no emoji in the UI, no "Oops".

- Say what happens and what it costs: "Reboots the device to finish root setup (about 40 s)." Buttons are verbs that match the result; the toast confirms in the past tense ("Deleted Tablet 11").
- State limits plainly where the user decides, not in a help page: "Rooted emulators can't pass Play Integrity." goes on the Full root card and in the inspector.
- Progress is honest: real bytes or real steps, never a fake bar. "Rooted ✓" means Jidr ran `su -c id` and got uid 0; until then the badge says Full root or Root unverified.
- Errors say what went wrong, whether data is safe, and what to do: "Root failed: patch step timed out. The device is unchanged."
- Status labels come from PRODUCT.md §5 exactly: Stopped · Starting… · Booting Android… · Running · Paused · Stopping… · Crashed · Busy (in use by CLI/agent); Not rooted · Shell root (adb) · Full root · Setting up root… · Rooted · Magisk 30.7 · Root unverified · Root failed: reason · Beta.
- No Google, Android or Genymotion logos or trademarks as graphics. "Android" appears only as text naming the OS.

| Write | Not |
|---|---|
| Downloading Android 16 (API 36) image · 1.4 / 2.1 GB · 2 min left | Please wait… |
| Busy · in use by CLI | Unavailable |
| Jidr downloads Google's Android Emulator after you accept Google's license. | Jidr includes the Android Emulator. |

## Colour

- Grounds, back to front: `jidr-color-surface-base` (content), `jidr-color-surface-chrome` (title bar, tabs, sidebar, device toolbar), `jidr-color-surface-raised` (cards, inspector), `jidr-color-surface-control` (buttons, inputs; `-hover`, `-pressed`), `jidr-color-surface-overlay` (popovers, menus). Wells are `jidr-color-surface-sunken` (device stage letterbox, code, map, tracks).
- Text: `jidr-color-text-primary`, `-secondary`, `-tertiary` all hold 4.5:1 on every surface in both themes; each token's note lists the ratios. `jidr-color-text-disabled` is exempt and only used with a non-interactive control.
- Code, serials and package names: `jidr-color-text-code` on `jidr-color-surface-sunken`.
- Accent blue `jidr-color-accent-fill` is for action and selection only. Text on it is `jidr-color-text-on-accent`; hover and pressed get darker in both themes so the pair keeps 4.5:1.
- Root violet `jidr-color-root` means root and nothing else: never a button, link, selection or chart colour. The only solid root plate is the verified badge (`jidr-status-root-strong-*`).
- Control outlines (inputs, checkboxes, radios) use `jidr-color-border-strong` (3:1). Dividers `jidr-color-border-subtle`; card and panel outlines `jidr-color-border-default`.
- Focus: a solid 2 px `jidr-color-focus-ring` outline, 2 px offset (`jidr-border-width-focus`, `jidr-border-focus-offset`), on every focusable element. It holds at least 5:1 on every surface.
- Behind sheets and dialogs: `jidr-color-scrim`. Text selection and selected logcat rows: `jidr-color-selection`.

## Status

Every status has a colour pair, an icon and a label. Statuses that mean the same thing to the user share a pair:

| Pair | Means | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `jidr-status-neutral-*` | idle or ended by the user | Stopped, Paused, Queued, Cancelled, Not rooted, Shell root, SDK Not installed |
| `jidr-status-positive-*` | working as intended | Running, Done, SDK Ready |
| `jidr-status-transition-*` | wait, something is happening | Starting, Booting, Stopping, job running, Installing, Update available |
| `jidr-status-warning-*` | usable with a caveat | Busy, Beta, Needs license acceptance |
| `jidr-status-negative-*` | broken, needs action | Crashed, Root failed, job Failed |
| `jidr-status-root-soft-*` | root configured, not yet proven | Full root, Setting up root, Root unverified |
| `jidr-status-root-strong-*` | root verified | Rooted · Magisk 30.7 |

- Root states are told apart without colour: verified is the only solid plate (badge-check); Full root, Setting up and Unverified are outlined pills with key-round, spinner and circle-help; Failed has a 2 px heavy outline and circle-x plus its reason; Shell root is a filled neutral pill with the terminal glyph; Not rooted is text only with a minus. Beta is a square uppercase tag after the badge, never alone.
- Device status is visible wherever a device appears: rows, cards, tabs, the device window title. Booting carries its percentage, Running its uptime, Busy names its holder.
- No dashed borders anywhere: Slint can't draw them.

## Logcat

Level colours `jidr-logcat-verbose`, `-debug`, `-info`, `-warn`, `-error`, `-fatal` on `jidr-logcat-background`, all at least 4.5:1 in both themes. The level letter always has its own column, and F rows get `jidr-logcat-fatal-row` plus bold, so level never depends on hue. Tag in `jidr-logcat-tag`, timestamp and pid in `jidr-logcat-meta`. Logcat stays LTR in the Arabic build.

## Type

- Geist for UI, Geist Mono for code and live numbers, Noto Kufi Arabic for the RTL build (all OFL-1.1, bundled in the app because Slint can't fetch web fonts).
- Roles: `type-hero` (the one big thing a surface is for: a device name in its detail view, the root result), `type-display` (first-run and empty-state titles), `type-headline` (page title), `type-title` (cards, sheet sections, widgets), `type-body` (13 px, macOS default), `type-label` (buttons, fields, pills, tabs), `type-caption` (metadata).
- `type-code`: serials, ports, package names, CLI (`emulator-5556`, `com.example.shop`). Always LTR.
- `type-metric` and `type-metric-lg`: anything that updates live (64%, 62% boot, 1.4 / 2.1 GB, 32.8954, 13.1802). Geist Mono, because Slint can't switch on Geist's tabular figures; mono figures are tabular by construction.
- Arabic (`type-*-ar`): line heights 1.6–1.75× the size against Latin's 1.2–1.4×, because Kufi has tall ascenders, deep descenders and stacked diacritics. Text sizes go up 1 px; display sizes come down. Letter-spacing is always 0 in Arabic: spacing breaks the joins. Row heights come from density tokens, not line height, so rows keep their height in both scripts.
- Landing page: `type-web-hero` 64/66 at ≥1280 px, 48/52 at 768, `type-web-hero-sm` 40/44 at 390; `type-web-lede` for the subhead; `type-web-body` for running text.

## Space, shape, elevation

- 4 px base: `jidr-space-xs` (4) to `jidr-space-5xl` (96). Components use `sm`/`md`/`lg`; sections `xl` and up.
- Radii: `jidr-radius-pill` for status and root, `jidr-radius-md` (8) for controls and rows, `jidr-radius-lg` (12) for cards, popovers and menus, `jidr-radius-xl` (14) for sheets and dialogs, `jidr-radius-xs` (4) for kbd and tags.
- Elevation: in dark it is surface tint plus `jidr-color-border-default` (`jidr-elevation-1|2|3-surface`, shadows transparent); in light white surfaces with one shadow each (`jidr-elevation-1|2|3-shadow`). Never stack shadows: Slint draws one per element.
- Borders: hairline 1 px everywhere; `jidr-border-width-emphasis` (1.5) only on outlined root badges.
- Density: device list default `jidr-density-default-row-height` (52, two lines) or compact `jidr-density-compact-row-height` (30, one line), toggled with ⌥⌘D.
- App window minimum `jidr-window-launcher-min-width` × `-min-height` (960 × 600). The device window is sized to the device: the screen fits 80% of the display height at first open, then resizes freely down to `jidr-window-device-min-screen-height` (360). Landing breakpoints `jidr-breakpoint-sm|md|lg|xl` (390 / 768 / 1280 / 1440).

## The device screen

- The Android screen is the hero of the device window. Nothing overlaps it; the toolbar is 48 px of icon buttons and the widget panel opens beside it.
- Bezel `jidr-color-surface-device-bezel` with `jidr-frame-<class>-bezel`, `-radius`, `-screen-radius` for phone, small-phone and tablet: a neutral rounded rectangle, no notch, camera, buttons or brand silhouette.
- Fit (default): largest size that fits, aspect kept, continuous scale. Pixel-perfect 1:1 (⌘0): one device pixel per physical pixel; the stage scrolls rather than scaling or cropping.
- Letterbox is `jidr-color-surface-sunken` with nothing drawn on it, at least `jidr-frame-stage-padding` (24) around the bezel. Rotation swaps the frame and re-fits; the window does not resize itself.

## Motion

Subtle and short; nothing bounces or runs longer than 400 ms. Every motion has a Reduce Motion fallback (in Slint `Theme.reduce-motion` from `NSWorkspace.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion`; on the site `prefers-reduced-motion`).

| Motion | Tokens | Reduce Motion |
|---|---|---|
| Hover, press, toggle | `jidr-motion-hover-*` 120 ms | unchanged (colour only) |
| Popover, menu, tooltip | `jidr-motion-popover-*` 160 ms, 4 px rise | 100 ms fade, no rise |
| Sheet | `jidr-motion-sheet-*` 240 ms, 12 px drop | 120 ms crossfade |
| Widget panel, inspector | `jidr-motion-panel-*` 240 ms | instant |
| Status change | `jidr-motion-status-*` 180 ms crossfade | instant swap |
| Job progress | `jidr-motion-progress-*` 240 ms linear | width jumps; numbers still update |
| Root success | `jidr-motion-root-success-*` 400 ms, outline fills to solid once | badge appears solid |
| Skeleton | `jidr-motion-skeleton-*` 1.4 s shimmer | flat fill |
| Spinner | `jidr-motion-spinner-*` 900 ms | static icon; label and % carry the state |

The device screen itself never animates.

## Accent and hero budget

- One hero per surface, set in `type-hero` or `type-web-hero`.
- At most one accent-filled control per surface (a pane, a sheet, a card, a landing section): the primary button or a selected segment, not both.
- Status pairs don't count against the budget, but they are never decoration: no tinted headers or cards to make a section pop.

## Iconography

- Lucide only (ISC licence; credit "Icons by Lucide, ISC licence" in About › Licenses and the site footer). Stroke 1.75 with round caps at every size. In Slint they are SVG files loaded with `@image-url` and tinted with `colorize`.
- Sizes: 14 (`jidr-icon-sm`) inside pills, badges, small buttons and menus; 16 (`jidr-icon-md`) in buttons, sidebar and inputs; 20 (`jidr-icon-lg`) in the device toolbar and empty states.
- Outlined by default. Filled is a state, not a style: only the Running dot, the record button while recording, and the toggle thumb.
- Status icons: square (Stopped), loader-circle (Starting, Booting, Stopping, Setting up, running jobs), filled dot (Running), pause, triangle-alert (Crashed), lock (Busy), minus (Not rooted), terminal (Shell root), key-round (Full root), badge-check (Rooted), circle-help (Unverified), circle-x (Root failed), flask-conical (Beta), clock (Queued), check (Done), x (Failed), ban (Cancelled).
- Mirror in RTL: arrows, back/forward, chevrons, undo/redo, skip, progress, indent. Never mirror: checks, play/pause/record, device rotation, clocks, search, terminal, keys, volume.
- No logo is defined yet; set the name as "Jidr" in Geist Bold with "جذر" in Noto Kufi Arabic SemiBold in `jidr-color-root`.

## Numbers

- Disk, downloads and image sizes: decimal GB (10⁹) with one decimal, matching Finder and About This Mac › Storage ("6.8 GB"). RAM: whole GB meaning 2³⁰ bytes, the convention every RAM spec and the emulator's `hw.ramSize` use ("4 GB"). CLI `--json`: raw bytes.
- Percent without a space (64%); number, no-break space, unit (40 s, 12 m, 2 h 14 m); speed with × (2×).
- Coordinates: signed decimal degrees, latitude first, 4 decimals shown and 6 accepted ("32.8954, 13.1802"); altitude in m, accuracy ± m, bearing in °.
- Logcat timestamps keep logcat's threadtime format (`10-13 14:02:07.318`). UI timestamps: relative day + 24 h time in the Mac's locale ("Today 14:02"), absolute after 7 days.
- Digits stay Western (0–9) in Arabic. Serials, ports, sizes and package names are isolated LTR.

## RTL

Layouts mirror cleanly for the Arabic build: the window (traffic lights included, as macOS does), sidebar, inspector, device toolbar and widget panel swap sides. Logcat, code, CLI, kbd hints and the Android screen do not mirror.

# Button

Primary, secondary, tertiary, destructive and icon buttons.

**Consumer provides:** label (a verb), optional icon and shortcut, state.

- **One accent (primary) button per surface**, for the thing the surface is for. Everything else secondary or tertiary.
- Heights `jidr-control-height-sm|md|lg` (24/30/44). Primary `jidr-color-accent-fill` → hover `-hover` → pressed `-pressed`; all keep 4.5:1 with `jidr-color-text-on-accent`.
- Loading: verb in progress (“Starting…”), spinner replaces the icon, shortcut hidden. Error exists only as Retry after a failed action.
- Icon buttons always have an `aria-label` and a tooltip with the shortcut. Destructive fill is never the default button.

`docs/design/system/components/CreateDeviceSheet/README.md`:

```md
# CreateDeviceSheet

New-device sheet. **A single form, not a stepper.**

Every field has a default, so the common path is name → ⌘↵. A stepper would put four clicks between the user and a device and bury root mode on step three. The form keeps root mode visible, folds rare hardware settings into Advanced, and validates inline.

**Consumer provides:** hardware profiles, installed and downloadable images (with sizes), default root mode.

- Duplicate names show an inline error and disable Create.
- First-run uses the same sheet with the downloaded image preselected.

```

# DeviceCard

A device in the grid view: a stage with our neutral silhouette and status pill, then name, profile, root badge, Android and disk, and one or two actions.

**Consumer provides:** the same device record as DeviceRow.

- At most one accent button per card: Start when stopped. Running devices get a secondary Open; Busy devices get Watch.
- Selected: `jidr-color-accent-fill` outline. Card on `jidr-color-surface-raised`, stage on `jidr-color-surface-sunken`, radius `jidr-radius-lg`.
- Silhouettes are plain rounded rectangles sized by device class. No brand shapes.

```

`docs/design/system/components/DeviceFrame/README.md`:

```md
# DeviceFrame

The bezel around the Android screen, per device class.

- Bezel colour `jidr-color-surface-device-bezel` (dark in both themes, like hardware); sizes `jidr-frame-<class>-bezel`, `-radius`, `-screen-radius`.
- Plain rounded rectangle: no notch, camera, buttons or brand silhouette.
- Bezel stays the same size in window points as the screen scales; minimum gap to the window edge `jidr-frame-stage-padding`.

`docs/design/system/components/DeviceRow/README.md`:

```md
# DeviceRow

A device in the launcher list: silhouette, name with profile · Android · image, status pill, root badge, disk, and inline actions.

**Consumer provides:** the device record from the daemon (name, profile, Android version + API, image tag, status, root mode + health + Magisk version, disk GB), selection, density.

- Default density: two lines, `jidr-density-default-row-height` (52). Compact: one line, `jidr-density-compact-row-height` (30); Magisk version moves to the tooltip.
- Inline actions (Start/Stop, Open, More) appear on hover, focus and selection. Shortcuts: ↵ open, ⌘R start, ⌘. stop, ⌫ delete.
- Status and root are always visible on every row; never hide them to save space.
- Error = crashed: row tinted `jidr-status-negative-container`. Disabled = image deleted.
- Disk uses `type-metric` and stays LTR in Arabic.

`docs/design/system/components/DeviceWindow/README.md`:

```md
# DeviceWindow

The device tab: the live Android screen in our bezel, a vertical toolbar and the widget panel host.

**Consumer provides:** the screen frames, device class, toolbar actions, the open widget.

- The Android screen is the hero. Nothing overlaps it; chrome around it is quiet.
- Toolbar `jidr-window-device-toolbar-width` (48) of 32 px icon buttons; every button has a tooltip with its shortcut.
- Widget panel `jidr-window-device-widget-panel-width` (320), ⌘J. A segmented control switches the four most-used widgets; the rest sit behind ⋯ and in ⌘K.
- Framing: Fit by default (largest size that fits, aspect kept); Pixel-perfect 1:1 (⌘0) scrolls the stage instead of scaling. Letterbox is `jidr-color-surface-sunken`, never decorated.
- In RTL the toolbar and panel swap sides and Back flips; the Android screen itself does not mirror.

# JobRow

A job in progress: download, root patch or verification, with cancel.

**Consumer provides:** job kind, title, progress 0–1, bytes done/total or step index, state, error message.

- The bar follows real bytes or real steps, never time. Unknown length: spinner and step name, no bar.

- Cancel (⌘.) is an icon button; finished jobs swap it for Retry (failed) or nothing, and leave the list after 10 s unless they failed.
- Numbers in `type-metric`.

`docs/design/system/components/LogcatViewer/README.md`:

```md
# LogcatViewer

Live logcat: level filter, search, follow toggle, monospace rows.

**Consumer provides:** the line stream (timestamp, level, tag, pid, message), filter, follow state.

- Columns: timestamp · pid · level · tag · message, in `type-code`. Timestamps keep logcat's threadtime format (`10-13 14:02:07.318`).
- Level colours `jidr-logcat-verbose` … `jidr-logcat-fatal` all hold 4.5:1 on `jidr-logcat-background`. The level letter is its own column and F rows get `jidr-logcat-fatal-row` and bold, so level never depends on hue.
- Level filter is a minimum. Follow pins to the newest line; scrolling up pauses it (⌘F to resume).
- Logcat stays LTR in the Arabic build.

`docs/design/system/components/RootBadge/README.md`:

```md
# RootBadge

Shows a device's root mode and health. Root state is unmistakable without colour: each state has its own label, icon and shape.

**Consumer provides:** root mode, root health, Magisk version, image tag (Play Store ⇒ Beta).

| State | Shape | Icon | Tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not rooted | text only | minus | `jidr-color-text-secondary` |
| Shell root (adb) | filled neutral pill | terminal | `jidr-status-root-shell-*` |
| Full root | outlined pill | key-round | `jidr-status-root-full-*` |
| Setting up root… | outlined pill | loader-circle (spins) | `jidr-status-root-setting-up-*` |
| Rooted · Magisk 30.7 | **solid plate** (the only one) | badge-check | `jidr-status-root-verified-*` |
| Root unverified | outlined pill | circle-help | `jidr-status-root-unverified-*` |
| Root failed: reason | 2 px heavy outline | circle-x | `jidr-status-root-failed-*` |
| Beta | square uppercase tag after the badge, never alone | flask-conical | `jidr-status-root-beta-*` |

- No dashed outlines: Slint can't draw dashed borders.
- Hover shows the last verified time. Failed is always followed by its reason and offers Revert.
- Sizes: 24 px default, 20 px in rows and the sidebar.

```

`docs/design/system/components/StatusPill/README.md`:

```md
# StatusPill

A device's run state as a pill: icon plus label on the state's container colour.

**Consumer provides:** status, plus boot % (Booting), uptime (Running) or holder (Busy: CLI or agent).

- Pairs are shared: Starting, Booting, Stopping use `jidr-status-transition-*` and the spinner; Stopped and Paused use `jidr-status-neutral-*` (icons differ); Running `positive`; Crashed `negative`; Busy `warning`.
- Always read colours through `jidr-status-device-<state>-container` / `-on-container`, never the shared pair directly, so a state can be re-mapped in one place.
- The spinner stops under Reduce Motion; the label and percentage carry the state.

`docs/design/system/components/WindowChrome/README.md`:

```md
# WindowChrome

The launcher window: a title bar with traffic lights and the tab strip (Library plus one tab per open device), a sidebar of devices and jobs, a split content area and an optional inspector.

**Consumer provides:** the device list, open tabs, current selection, and whether the inspector is open.

- Title bar `jidr-window-titlebar-height` (44) on `jidr-color-surface-chrome`. Active tab sits on `jidr-color-surface-base` and joins the content.

- In RTL the whole window mirrors, traffic lights included, as macOS does for right-to-left system languages.
- When the window is inactive the traffic lights turn `jidr-color-border-strong`.

`docs/mcp.md`:

```md
# Jidr for AI agents (MCP)

`jidr mcp` serves the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) on stdio. Agents get every Jidr command plus fast tools for driving a device: look, tap, type, read the UI. It starts the Jidr daemon if it isn't running.

## Add Jidr to Claude

Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add jidr -- jidr mcp
```

Claude Desktop: download `jidr-mcp-<version>-darwin-arm64.mcpb` from the [latest release](https://github.com/AbdurahmanAlmehdi/jidr/releases/latest) and open it, or add Jidr by hand to `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "jidr": { "command": "/opt/homebrew/bin/jidr", "args": ["mcp"] }
  }
}
```

Cursor (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`) takes the same `mcpServers` entry. `jidr uninstall` removes these entries again (D31).

Each release also publishes Jidr to the [MCP Registry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io) as `io.github.AbdurahmanAlmehdi/jidr`, pointing at that `.mcpb`.

## Tools

| Tool | Hints | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `command_list {prefix?}` | read-only | Every Jidr command with its params schema and flags |
| `command_run {command, params, timeout_s?}` | may be destructive | Runs any command; long-running ones (boot, image install) are waited for, up to `timeout_s` (900 s), then returned as a job |
| `jobs_list {all?}`, `jobs_cancel {job}` | read-only / idempotent | Long-running operations |
| `screenshot {device}` | read-only | PNG of the screen fitted in 1024×1024, plus the screen size and scale |
| `tap {device, x, y, coords?}` | interacts | Tap; coordinates are in the screenshot image unless `coords: "device"` |
| `swipe {device, x1, y1, x2, y2, duration_ms?, coords?}` | interacts | Swipe or drag (scroll, open the app drawer) |
| `type_text {device, text, enter?}` | interacts | Type printable ASCII into the focused field |
| `press_key {device, key}` | interacts | `GoHome`, `GoBack`, `AppSwitch`, `Enter`, `Power`, volume, arrows… |
| `ui_dump {device}` | read-only | uiautomator XML: text, ids and bounds to find what to tap |
| `logcat_tail {device, lines?, filter?}` | read-only | Recent log lines (the last N lines that match the filter) |
| `proxy_set {device, host?, port}`, `proxy_clear {device}` | idempotent | The device's global HTTP proxy, for Burp or mitmproxy on the Mac (`host` defaults to `10.0.2.2`, the Mac as the emulator sees it) |

Every tool carries `readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint` and `openWorldHint` annotations. Jidr errors come back as tool results with `isError: true` and structured `{code, message, data}` (codes as in docs/control-protocol.md), so an agent can recover, e.g. start a stopped device after `not_found`.

## Safety policy (D5)

By default an agent can read, interact, start and stop. Commands flagged destructive (`device.delete`, `device.reset`, …) are refused unless:

- the device is **agent-owned**: devices an agent creates through `command_run device.create` are agent-owned automatically, and a person can mark one with `jidr device edit <name> --agent-owned true`; or
- the server runs as `jidr mcp --allow-destructive`.

Refusals carry `data.policy = "D5"`. Connection-level protocol methods (`hello`, `events.subscribe`, `logcat.follow`, `daemon.shutdown`) aren't callable through MCP.

## Measured latency (not gated)

From the five scripted agent tasks (`cargo nextest run -p jidr-mcp --features emulator`, M1 Pro, API 31 arm64): screenshot ~0.4–1.1 s, tap ~0.2–0.4 s, type_text ~0.7–1.2 s, press_key ~0.01–0.1 s, swipe 1–4 s, logcat_tail ~0.2–0.5 s, ui_dump 4–6 s median (uiautomator itself is slow), cold boot via `command_run device.start` 25–32 s.

```

# Parity with Genymotion Desktop

Hand-edited. A row is ✅ only with evidence: a test name or a `file:line`. Report two numbers together, never breadth alone:

- **Breadth**: ✅ rows / all rows.
- **Ready for real work**: a judged estimate, with reasons.

Status: ✅ done with evidence · 🚧 partly done · ⬜ not started · ⏭️ post-MVP (linked issue) · ❌ won't do · 🔎 needs research (D11)

**Breadth:** 26 / 43 ✅ (60%). Of the other 17: 8 🚧, 8 ⏭️, 1 ❌. Five rows are Jidr-only (not in Genymotion); three of them are ✅.

**Ready for real work: about 70% for the core use case, lower for Genymotion power users.**

- **Core use case:** create a device on Apple Silicon, root it, test an app, and automate it from a CLI, CI or an AI agent. Every step has an emulator test, and the whole path passes `cargo xtask e2e-mac` (345 emulator tests plus the CLI, root and SDK-untouched scripts) and CI on API 30, 33 and 35.
- **What holds it back from "ready":**
  - There's no signed release yet; v0.1.0 is in preparation.
  - Quick boot is slower than its target.
  - A few emulator tests are still flaky on shared CI runners.
  - Several paid-tier niches are partial or post-MVP: motion presets, file-based camera, biometric scenarios, network loss and DNS, identifiers, disk limits, gamepad.
  - Fullscreen and clipboard sharing in the player aren't finished.

`docs/root.md`:

```md
# Root modes

Jidr roots your own Android emulators. Root is a first-class device property
(`root_mode: none | adb | magisk`), switched with `jidr root set` and applied
per device — the shared SDK system images are never modified.

| Mode | Images | Mechanism | Verify |
|---|---|---|---|
| `none` | all | stock launch | `adb shell id` → uid 2000 |
| `adb` | `default`, `google_apis`, `aosp_atd` | `adb root` after every boot | `adb shell id` → uid 0 |
| `magisk` | all | patched per-device ramdisk, cold boot | `adb shell su -c id` → uid 0, `su -c 'magisk -v'` |

```bash
jidr root set <device> magisk   # one-click full root
jidr root set <device> adb      # shell root
jidr root set <device> none     # revert either to stock
jidr root verify <device>       # check the live uid against the mode
jidr root status <device>       # stored mode, health, Magisk version
```

> Play Integrity cannot pass on any emulator; Zygisk/DenyList only hides root
> from local checks.

## How Magisk mode works

`root.set magisk` runs the whole setup as one job, with progress and cancel:

1. **Fetch** the pinned Magisk release from the official GitHub release and
   check its SHA-256 (see [below](#magisk-licence)).
2. **Hash** the image's pristine `ramdisk.img`.
3. **Patch** a *per-device* copy on the host with `jidr-cpio`: `init` becomes
   `magiskinit`, the compressed payload goes under `overlay.d/sbin`, and the
   config is recorded in `.backup/.magisk`. The result is written to
   `<avd>/jidr/ramdisk.magisk-<ver>.img` atomically (temp file + rename).
4. **Cold boot** with `-ramdisk <patched>`.
5. **Install** the Magisk app (the release APK is also the manager app).
6. **Set up** `/data/adb/magisk`, then **reboot once** so `magiskd` enables su.
7. **Grant** the adb shell su automatically, then **verify**.

On `google_apis` (and `default` / `aosp_atd`) images this is fully zero-touch:
`adb root` is used to write Magisk's su-policy row for the shell, then adbd is
dropped back so the final check exercises Magisk's own `su`. Apps still get
Magisk's normal per-app prompt; the opt-in "auto-grant all" toggle is off by
default.

## Revert

`root.set none` (or `adb`) on a Magisk device clears `launch.ramdisk`, deletes
the patched file and its metadata, and cold-boots the stock ramdisk. `none` and
`adb` then behave exactly as they do on a fresh device. A failed Magisk setup
leaves the device in the same revertable state (health `failed`, patched file
still present).

## Re-patch

A patched ramdisk records the pristine SHA-256, the Magisk version and APK,
and the build props it was built from. When the image or the version changes
(an image update, or a newer pinned Magisk), the next `root.set magisk` (or the
boot hook) rebuilds the patched copy from the pristine image; a props change
rebuilds it at once. Patches never stack.

## Offline Magisk

To use Magisk without network access, import the official APK once:

```bash
jidr root set <device> magisk --magisk /path/to/Magisk-v30.7.apk
```

The CLI adds the APK to the download cache by SHA-256 and `root.set` uses that
cached copy (`magisk_sha256`) instead of downloading. The SHA-256 is still
checked, so a tampered or wrong file is rejected.

## Auto-grant all (D22)

On a Full-root device the adb shell is always auto-granted `su`. Every other
app gets Magisk's normal allow/deny prompt — unless you opt in per device:

```bash
jidr root auto-grant <device> true    # grant every app root without a prompt
jidr root auto-grant <device> false   # back to the prompt (off by default)
```

`root.auto_grant` stores the flag on the device and, when it is running, sets
Magisk's superuser *automatic response* (`su_auto_response`: `2` = grant,
`0` = prompt) over `adb root`, reading the value back to confirm it. On a
stopped device it stores the flag and applies it on the next boot. Leaving Full
root resets the flag to off. The flag is off by default; Play Integrity is
unaffected.

## Build props (Phase 9f)

A Full-root device can report another identity: `Build.MODEL`, `BRAND`,
`MANUFACTURER`, `DEVICE`, `FINGERPRINT` and `VERSION.SECURITY_PATCH`. In the
GUI, open the player's widget panel → More → Developer tools → Build identity.
From the CLI or an agent:

```bash
jidr call device.props.set '{"device":"Phone","props":{"model":"Pixel 8","brand":"google","security_patch":"2026-10-05"}}'
jidr call device.props.get '{"device":"Phone"}'
jidr call device.props.set '{"device":"Phone","props":{}}'   # back to stock
```

`props` is the whole set: a field left out (or empty) keeps the image's value.
Values are trimmed, at most 256 characters, with no line breaks, and
`security_patch` is `YYYY-MM-DD`. A refused value names its field in
`error.data.field`.

How it works: the emulator's `-prop` only reaches `qemu.*` properties, so the
values are applied by Magisk's `resetprop` at boot. `device.props.set` stores
them in `<avd>/jidr/props.json` and re-patches the per-device ramdisk with the
same Magisk APK. The patch adds `overlay.d/jidr-props.rc`, which Magisk appends
to `init.rc`, and a script in `overlay.d/sbin`. At `post-fs-data`, before
zygote starts, the script runs `resetprop -n` for each property and its
partition copies (`ro.product.model`, `ro.product.vendor.model`, …). Only
identity properties are set, never hardware or HAL ones.

The next start applies them, as a cold boot; `restart_required` is true until
then. Other modes refuse `device.props.set` with `usage`. Reverting root boots
the stock ramdisk, so the stock values come back, and the stored props are
dropped. Play Integrity is unaffected: a changed fingerprint doesn't make an
emulator pass it.

## Play Store images (beta)

`google_apis_playstore` images refuse `adb root`, so the shell grant cannot be
pre-approved. Jidr uses the guided tap from ADR-0002:

1. Full-root setup runs as above (patch, cold boot, app install, environment).
2. Jidr shows "Magisk will ask to grant root to Shell. Tap Grant." and runs
   `su -c id`, which raises Magisk's normal prompt.
3. It waits up to 60 s. Tap Grant, and the shell is granted root.
4. Denied or timed out, the device reports `awaiting_user_grant` with
   **Try again** and **Revert**.

There is no headless bypass on Play Store images; apps keep Magisk's per-app
prompt.

## Magisk licence

Magisk is **GPL-3.0-only**, so Jidr never bundles or redistributes it. It is
downloaded at runtime from
[topjohnwu/Magisk](https://github.com/topjohnwu/Magisk), its SHA-256 is checked
against the pin in `assets/magisk-pins.toml`, and the licence and source link
are shown before the first download. The same clean-room rule applies to the
patch itself: it reproduces Magisk's documented ramdisk layout without copying
its GPL code (see `docs/clean-room.md`).

```

`packaging/homebrew/jidr.rb`:

```rb
# Homebrew cask for the AbdurahmanAlmehdi/homebrew-tap tap:
#   brew install --cask abdurahmanalmehdi/tap/jidr
# release.yml fills in @VERSION@ and @SHA256@ (the DMG's line in
# SHA256SUMS.txt) and pushes the result to Casks/jidr.rb in the tap.
cask "jidr" do
  version "@VERSION@"
  sha256 "@SHA256@"

  url "https://github.com/AbdurahmanAlmehdi/jidr/releases/download/v#{version}/Jidr-#{version}-arm64.dmg"
  name "Jidr"
  desc "Android emulators with one-click rooted devices"
  homepage "https://jidr.ly/"

  livecheck do
    url :url
    strategy :github_latest
  end

  depends_on arch: :arm64
  depends_on macos: :ventura

  app "Jidr.app"
  binary "#{appdir}/Jidr.app/Contents/Helpers/jidr"

  uninstall quit: "ly.jidr.Jidr"

  # `jidr uninstall --purge` (D31) removes devices and the private SDK; zap
  # only removes what Homebrew can see without running Jidr.
  zap trash: [
    "~/Library/Application Support/Jidr",
    "~/Library/Caches/Jidr",
    "~/Library/Logs/Jidr",
  ]
end

`packaging/macos/README.md`:

```md
# macOS packaging

`cargo xtask release` (in `xtask/src/release.rs`) builds `Jidr.app`, `Jidr-<version>-arm64.dmg` and the MCP bundle `jidr-mcp-<version>-darwin-arm64.mcpb` from this folder and `../mcp`.

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `Info.plist.in` | bundle metadata; `@VERSION@` becomes the workspace version |
| `sign.sh` | Developer ID signing (hardened runtime, inside-out) and DMG notarization + staple; `cargo xtask release` calls it when `JIDR_SIGNING_IDENTITY` is set |
| `verify.sh` | Gatekeeper, hardened runtime and the stapled ticket; the release workflow runs it on signed builds. Fails on ad-hoc builds, as expected |
| `../homebrew/jidr.rb` | cask template; `release.yml` fills in the version and checksum and pushes it to `AbdurahmanAlmehdi/homebrew-tap` |
| `../mcp/manifest.json` | MCPB manifest (`@VERSION@`); the bundle holds it, the signed `jidr` as `server/jidr`, the icon and the licences. `jidr-mcp`'s tests check its tool list |
| `../../server.json` | MCP Registry entry; `release.yml` points it at the release's `.mcpb` and publishes it |

Bundle layout:

```
Jidr.app/Contents/
  Info.plist  PkgInfo
  MacOS/Jidr            GUI (apps/jidr-gui, GPL-3.0)
  Helpers/jidr          CLI, daemon and MCP server (apps/jidr, Apache-2.0)
  Resources/Jidr.icns   from apps/jidr-gui/assets/macos (D39)
  Resources/licenses/   LICENSE-APACHE, LICENSE-GPL, NOTICE
```

The CLI lives in `Helpers/` because `MacOS/jidr` and `MacOS/Jidr` are the same path on the default case-insensitive APFS.

```bash
cargo xtask release --dry-run --scan    # local build, DMG, mount check, forbidden-content scan
```

## Releases and signing (D32)

Releases are cut by release-please: every merge to `main` updates a "chore: release vX.Y.Z" pull request (version from conventional commits, `CHANGELOG.md`). Merging it tags the version and publishes the GitHub Release; `.github/workflows/release.yml` then builds the DMG and the `.mcpb` on macOS, signs and notarizes them, runs `verify.sh` and uploads both with `SHA256SUMS.txt`. For a signed build it then pushes `Casks/jidr.rb` to the tap (`brew install --cask abdurahmanalmehdi/tap/jidr`) and publishes `server.json` to the [MCP Registry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io) with GitHub OIDC.

Repository secrets for signing (without them the DMG is ad-hoc signed and the run warns; users then open the app from System Settings › Privacy & Security › Open Anyway):

| Secret | Value |
|---|---|
| `MAC_DEVELOPER_ID_P12_BASE64` | the Developer ID Application certificate and its private key, exported from Keychain Access as a `.p12`, base64-encoded |
| `MAC_DEVELOPER_ID_P12_PASSWORD` | the password chosen when exporting the `.p12` |
| `MAC_NOTARY_KEY_P8_BASE64` | an App Store Connect API key (`.p8`, from App Store Connect › Users and Access › Integrations), base64-encoded |
| `MAC_NOTARY_KEY_ID` | that key's ID |
| `MAC_NOTARY_ISSUER_ID` | that key's issuer ID |
| `RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN` | optional: a fine-grained token with contents and pull-requests write, so the release PR runs CI |
| `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` | a fine-grained token with contents write on `AbdurahmanAlmehdi/homebrew-tap` only; without it the cask isn't updated and the run warns |

Set them without printing anything, for example `base64 -i developer-id.p12 | gh secret set MAC_DEVELOPER_ID_P12_BASE64`, and check the file exists first: if `base64` fails, `gh` stores an empty secret.

To sign and notarize locally: `JIDR_SIGNING_IDENTITY="Developer ID Application: Name (TEAMID)" NOTARY_KEY_PATH=path/to/AuthKey.p8 NOTARY_KEY_ID=… NOTARY_ISSUER_ID=… cargo xtask release --scan`.

The scan fails the build if the bundle or the DMG contains Google SDK binaries, system images or Magisk. Jidr downloads those on the user's machine, never ships them.

```

`packaging/macos/sign.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Developer ID signing and notarization (Phase 12b, D32). `cargo xtask release`
# runs it when JIDR_SIGNING_IDENTITY is set: `app` before the DMG is built,
# `dmg` after.
#
#   packaging/macos/sign.sh app Jidr.app        # hardened runtime, inside-out
#   packaging/macos/sign.sh dmg Jidr-X-arm64.dmg # sign, notarize, staple
#
# Environment:
#   JIDR_SIGNING_IDENTITY   "Developer ID Application: <Name> (<TEAMID>)"
#   NOTARY_KEY_PATH         App Store Connect API key (.p8) for notarytool
#   NOTARY_KEY_ID           its key ID
#   NOTARY_ISSUER_ID        its issuer ID
set -euo pipefail

die() { echo "sign.sh: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
need() { [ -n "${!1:-}" ] || die "$1 is not set"; }

[ $# -eq 2 ] || die "usage: sign.sh app <Jidr.app> | sign.sh dmg <file.dmg>"
kind=$1 target=$2
[ -e "$target" ] || die "$target does not exist"
need JIDR_SIGNING_IDENTITY

sign() {
    codesign --force --timestamp --options runtime \
        --sign "$JIDR_SIGNING_IDENTITY" "$@"
}

case "$kind" in
    app)
        # Inside-out: nested executables first, then the bundle. No --deep.
        sign "$target/Contents/Helpers/jidr"
        sign "$target/Contents/MacOS/Jidr"
        sign "$target"
        codesign --verify --strict --verbose=2 "$target"
        ;;
    dmg)
        need NOTARY_KEY_PATH
        need NOTARY_KEY_ID
        need NOTARY_ISSUER_ID
        [ -f "$NOTARY_KEY_PATH" ] || die "NOTARY_KEY_PATH $NOTARY_KEY_PATH does not exist"
        sign "$target"
        result=$(xcrun notarytool submit "$target" \
            --key "$NOTARY_KEY_PATH" \
            --key-id "$NOTARY_KEY_ID" \
            --issuer "$NOTARY_ISSUER_ID" \
            --wait 2>&1) || die "notarytool failed: $result"
        echo "$result"
        # Check Apple's verdict, not only notarytool's exit code.
        grep -q "status: Accepted" <<<"$result" \
            || die "notarization was not accepted; run 'xcrun notarytool log <id>' with the same key for details"
        xcrun stapler staple "$target"
        ;;
    *)
        die "unknown kind '$kind' (app or dmg)"
        ;;
esac
echo "sign.sh: $kind signed: $target"

```

`packaging/macos/verify.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Gatekeeper checks for a signed, notarized release (Phase 12b validation).
#
#   packaging/macos/verify.sh <Jidr-X-arm64.dmg>
#
# Mounts the DMG read-only and checks the DMG and the app inside it. Exits
# non-zero for ad-hoc (unsigned, 12a) builds: that's expected until 12b.
set -euo pipefail

die() { echo "verify.sh: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
[ $# -eq 1 ] || die "usage: verify.sh <file.dmg>"
dmg=$1
[ -f "$dmg" ] || die "$dmg does not exist"

mnt=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'hdiutil detach "$mnt" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; rmdir "$mnt" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
hdiutil attach -readonly -nobrowse -noautoopen -mountpoint "$mnt" "$dmg" >/dev/null
app="$mnt/Jidr.app"
[ -d "$app" ] || die "no Jidr.app in $dmg"

echo "== DMG signature and ticket"
codesign --verify --strict --verbose=2 "$dmg"
xcrun stapler validate "$dmg"
spctl --assess --type open --context context:primary-signature --verbose=2 "$dmg"

echo "== Jidr.app"
codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2 "$app"
codesign --display --verbose=2 "$app" 2>&1 | grep -E '^(Authority|TeamIdentifier|Runtime)'
codesign --display --verbose=2 "$app" 2>&1 | grep -q 'flags=.*runtime' \
    || die "Jidr.app is not signed with the hardened runtime"
spctl --assess --type execute --verbose=2 "$app"

echo "verify.sh: ok: $dmg is signed, notarized and accepted by Gatekeeper"

```

`scripts/e2e-cli.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# End-to-end CLI run on a real emulator, non-interactive, JSON everywhere:
# create → start (wait for boot) → install → stop → delete → daemon stop.
#
# Env: JIDR_TEST_SDK (SDK holding the image, read-only; default Studio's),
#      JIDR_TEST_IMAGE (sdkmanager package; default API 31 google_apis, host ABI),
#      JIDR_TEST_APK (APK to install; default a sample app from the SDK's images).
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export CARGO_TARGET_DIR="${CARGO_TARGET_DIR:-target}"
cargo build -q -p jidr
# CARGO_TARGET_DIR may be absolute (CI, `cargo xtask e2e-mac` callers) or relative.
case "$CARGO_TARGET_DIR" in /*) TARGET="$CARGO_TARGET_DIR" ;; *) TARGET="$PWD/$CARGO_TARGET_DIR" ;; esac
JIDR="$TARGET/debug/jidr"

case "$(uname -m)" in arm64|aarch64) ABI=arm64-v8a ;; *) ABI=x86_64 ;; esac
SDK="${JIDR_TEST_SDK:-${ANDROID_HOME:-$HOME/Library/Android/sdk}}"
export ANDROID_HOME="$SDK"
IMAGE="${JIDR_TEST_IMAGE:-system-images;android-31;google_apis;$ABI}"
APK="${JIDR_TEST_APK:-$(find "$SDK/system-images" -path '*/data/app/*' -name '*.apk' 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)}"
if [ -z "$APK" ] || [ ! -f "$APK" ]; then
  echo "e2e-cli: no APK to install; set JIDR_TEST_APK" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# A short, private Jidr home (Unix socket paths are limited to ~104 bytes).
JIDR_HOME="$(mktemp -d /tmp/jidr-e2e.XXXXXX)"
export JIDR_HOME
cleanup() {
  # Stops devices, the daemon and any leftover emulator of this run, even
  # after a failure or Ctrl-C (scratch HOME: real MCP configs untouched).
  mkdir -p "$JIDR_HOME/cleanup-home"
  HOME="$JIDR_HOME/cleanup-home" "$JIDR" --quiet uninstall --purge --yes >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  "$JIDR" daemon stop >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  rm -rf "$JIDR_HOME"
}
trap cleanup EXIT
trap 'exit 130' INT TERM

# Runs `jidr --json …`, checks the exit code and that ok == true, prints the result.
step() {
  local name="$1"; shift
  local out code=0
  out="$("$JIDR" --json "$@")" || code=$?
  if [ "$code" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "e2e-cli: FAIL $name (exit $code): $out" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  python3 -I -c 'import json,sys; v=json.loads(sys.stdin.read().strip().splitlines()[-1]); assert v["jidr_json"]==1 and v["ok"] is True, v' <<<"$out" \
    || { echo "e2e-cli: FAIL $name: bad envelope: $out" >&2; exit 1; }
  echo "e2e-cli: ok   $name"
  LAST="$out"
}

field() {  # field <python expression on r = result>
  python3 -I -c "import json,sys; r=json.loads(sys.stdin.read().strip().splitlines()[-1])['result']; print($1)" <<<"$LAST"
}

start=$(date +%s)
step "create"   device create e2e --image "$IMAGE" --profile small-phone-5
step "start"    device start e2e --timeout 300
[ "$(field 'r[0]["status"]["state"]')" = running ] || { echo "e2e-cli: FAIL not running: $LAST" >&2; exit 1; }
echo "e2e-cli:      booted on $(field 'r[0]["runtime"]["adb_serial"]') after $(( $(date +%s) - start )) s"
step "install"  install e2e "$APK"
step "logcat"   logcat e2e -n 20
step "stop"     device stop e2e
step "delete"   device delete e2e --yes
step "list"     device list
[ "$(field 'len(r)')" = 0 ] || { echo "e2e-cli: FAIL device left behind: $LAST" >&2; exit 1; }

# Uninstall --purge (D31) with HOME pointed at a scratch dir, so the real MCP
# configs are never touched; a fake Claude Code config proves the cleanup.
step "create2"  device create e2e2 --image "$IMAGE" --profile small-phone-5
step "start2"   device start e2e2 --timeout 300
FAKE_HOME="$JIDR_HOME/home"
mkdir -p "$FAKE_HOME"
printf '{"mcpServers":{"jidr":{"command":"jidr","args":["mcp"]},"other":{"command":"x"}}}' > "$FAKE_HOME/.claude.json"
LAST="$(HOME="$FAKE_HOME" "$JIDR" --json uninstall --purge --yes)" || { echo "e2e-cli: FAIL uninstall: $LAST" >&2; exit 1; }
echo "e2e-cli: ok   uninstall --purge"
[ "$(field 'r["purged"]')" = True ] || { echo "e2e-cli: FAIL not purged: $LAST" >&2; exit 1; }
for d in data cache logs; do
  [ ! -e "$JIDR_HOME/$d" ] || { echo "e2e-cli: FAIL $JIDR_HOME/$d remains" >&2; exit 1; }
done
python3 -I -c 'import json,sys; c=json.load(open(sys.argv[1])); assert "jidr" not in c["mcpServers"] and "other" in c["mcpServers"], c' "$FAKE_HOME/.claude.json" \
  || { echo "e2e-cli: FAIL MCP entry not removed" >&2; exit 1; }
[ ! -S "$JIDR_HOME/data/daemon.sock" ] || { echo "e2e-cli: FAIL daemon socket remains" >&2; exit 1; }
# No emulator may still be running a Jidr AVD.
python3 -I "$(dirname "$0")/lib/no_jidr_emulators.py" "$JIDR_HOME" \
  || { echo "e2e-cli: FAIL a Jidr emulator is still running" >&2; exit 1; }
echo "e2e-cli: passed in $(( $(date +%s) - start )) s"

```

`scripts/e2e-root.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# End-to-end root cycle on real emulators: none → adb → magisk → none,
# verifying each step and that the shared SDK ramdisk.img is untouched at the
# end (Phase 9d acceptance).
#
# Env: JIDR_TEST_SDK    (SDK holding the images, read-only; default Studio's)
#      JIDR_TEST_IMAGES (space-separated sdkmanager packages; default one
#                        google_apis image for the host ABI — CI passes
#                        API 30/33/35 x86_64 on Linux KVM)
#      JIDR_TEST_MAGISK (optional local Magisk APK; default: download the pin)
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export CARGO_TARGET_DIR="${CARGO_TARGET_DIR:-target}"
cargo build -q -p jidr
# CARGO_TARGET_DIR may be absolute (CI, `cargo xtask e2e-mac` callers) or relative.
case "$CARGO_TARGET_DIR" in /*) TARGET="$CARGO_TARGET_DIR" ;; *) TARGET="$PWD/$CARGO_TARGET_DIR" ;; esac
JIDR="$TARGET/debug/jidr"

case "$(uname -m)" in arm64|aarch64) ABI=arm64-v8a ;; *) ABI=x86_64 ;; esac
SDK="${JIDR_TEST_SDK:-${ANDROID_HOME:-$HOME/Library/Android/sdk}}"
export ANDROID_HOME="$SDK"
IMAGES="${JIDR_TEST_IMAGES:-system-images;android-31;google_apis;$ABI}"

JIDR_HOME="$(mktemp -d /tmp/jidr-e2e-root.XXXXXX)"
export JIDR_HOME
cleanup() {
  local code=$?
  # Stop the daemon first; emulators outlive it and are re-adopted, but the
  # happy path already stopped and deleted the device.
  "$JIDR" daemon stop >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  if [ "$code" -ne 0 ] || [ "${JIDR_E2E_KEEP:-}" = 1 ]; then
    # Keep the evidence: the emulator log that says why a boot hung lives
    # under $JIDR_HOME/logs/devices/<avd>/emulator-*.log. `uninstall --purge`
    # would delete it, so it is skipped here.
    echo "e2e-root: keeping JIDR_HOME=$JIDR_HOME (logs: $JIDR_HOME/logs/devices)" >&2
  else
    mkdir -p "$JIDR_HOME/cleanup-home"
    HOME="$JIDR_HOME/cleanup-home" "$JIDR" --quiet uninstall --purge --yes >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    rm -rf "$JIDR_HOME"
  fi
}
trap cleanup EXIT
trap 'exit 130' INT TERM

# Runs `jidr --json …` and checks ok == true; sets LAST to the last line.
step() {
  local name="$1"; shift
  local out code=0
  out="$("$JIDR" --json "$@")" || code=$?
  if [ "$code" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "e2e-root: FAIL $name (exit $code): $out" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  python3 -I -c 'import json,sys; v=json.loads(sys.stdin.read().strip().splitlines()[-1]); assert v["jidr_json"]==1 and v["ok"] is True, v' <<<"$out" \
    || { echo "e2e-root: FAIL $name: bad envelope: $out" >&2; exit 1; }
  echo "e2e-root: ok   $name"
  LAST="$out"
}

field() {  # field <python expression on r = result>
  python3 -I -c "import json,sys; r=json.loads(sys.stdin.read().strip().splitlines()[-1])['result']; print($1)" <<<"$LAST"
}

# SHA-256 of an image's pristine ramdisk.img, from its sdkmanager package.
pristine_hash() {
  local img="$1"
  local rel
  rel="$(printf '%s' "$img" | tr ';' '/')/ramdisk.img"
  shasum -a 256 "$SDK/$rel" | awk '{print $1}'
}

cycle() {
  local img="$1" dev="e2e-root" before after uid
  before="$(pristine_hash "$img")"
  echo "e2e-root: image $img (pristine ramdisk $before)"

  step "create" device create "$dev" --image "$img" --profile small-phone-5 --root none
  step "start"  device start "$dev" --timeout 300

  # none: the shell is not root.
  step "verify-none" root verify "$dev"
  uid="$(field 'r["uid"]')"
  [ "$uid" != 0 ] || { echo "e2e-root: FAIL none is root ($uid)" >&2; exit 1; }

  # none → adb, live.
  step "set-adb" root set "$dev" adb
  uid="$(field 'r["verification"]["uid"]')"
  [ "$uid" = 0 ] || { echo "e2e-root: FAIL adb uid=$uid" >&2; exit 1; }

  # adb → magisk: the full setup, then `su -c id` must be uid 0.
  if [ -n "${JIDR_TEST_MAGISK:-}" ]; then
    step "set-magisk" root set "$dev" magisk --magisk "$JIDR_TEST_MAGISK"
  else
    step "set-magisk" root set "$dev" magisk
  fi
  uid="$(field 'r["verification"]["uid"]')"
  [ "$uid" = 0 ] || { echo "e2e-root: FAIL magisk su uid=$uid" >&2; exit 1; }
  [ "$(field 'r["verification"]["command"]')" = "su -c id" ] \
    || { echo "e2e-root: FAIL magisk probe: $LAST" >&2; exit 1; }
  echo "e2e-root:      magisk $(field 'r["magisk_version"]')"

  # magisk → none: revert.
  step "set-none" root set "$dev" none
  uid="$(field 'r["verification"]["uid"]')"
  [ "$uid" != 0 ] || { echo "e2e-root: FAIL revert is root ($uid)" >&2; exit 1; }

  step "stop"   device stop "$dev"
  step "delete" device delete "$dev" --yes

  after="$(pristine_hash "$img")"
  [ "$before" = "$after" ] || {
    echo "e2e-root: FAIL SDK ramdisk.img changed: $before → $after" >&2
    exit 1
  }
  echo "e2e-root:      SDK ramdisk.img unchanged"
}

start=$(date +%s)
for img in $IMAGES; do
  cycle "$img"
done
echo "e2e-root: passed in $(( $(date +%s) - start )) s"

```

`scripts/e2e-studio-untouched.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Proves Jidr never writes to Android Studio's SDK or AVDs (D3, D31).
#
#   scripts/e2e-studio-untouched.sh [command...]
#
# Fingerprints every file (path, size, mtime) under the Studio SDK and
# ~/.android/avd, runs the command (default: the jidr-sdk emulator tests and
# scripts/e2e-cli.sh, which ends with `jidr uninstall --purge`),
# and fails if anything changed. AVDs that are running right now are
# skipped, since the emulator legitimately writes to them.
set -euo pipefail

STUDIO_SDK="${JIDR_TEST_SDK:-${ANDROID_HOME:-$HOME/Library/Android/sdk}}"
STUDIO_AVD="${ANDROID_AVD_HOME:-$HOME/.android/avd}"
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR="${CARGO_TARGET_DIR:-target}"

if [ "$#" -eq 0 ]; then
  # Install → use → uninstall --purge on a real emulator, plus the SDK tests.
  set -- sh -c 'cargo nextest run -p jidr-sdk --features emulator --no-tests=pass && scripts/e2e-cli.sh'
fi

if [ ! -d "$STUDIO_SDK" ]; then
  echo "e2e-studio-untouched: no Studio SDK at $STUDIO_SDK; nothing to protect"
  exec "$@"
fi

# AVD dirs held by a live emulator (hardware-qemu.ini.lock with a live pid).
running_avds() {
  for lock in "$STUDIO_AVD"/*.avd/hardware-qemu.ini.lock; do
    [ -e "$lock" ] || continue
    pid=$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$lock" || true)
    if [ -n "$pid" ] && kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
      dirname "$lock"
    fi
  done
}

fingerprint() {
  local excludes=()
  while IFS= read -r dir; do
    excludes+=(-path "$dir" -prune -o)
  done < <(running_avds)
  {
    find "$STUDIO_SDK" -type f -print0
    if [ -d "$STUDIO_AVD" ]; then
      # (bash 3.2 on macOS: an empty array under `set -u` needs this form)
      find "$STUDIO_AVD" ${excludes[@]+"${excludes[@]}"} -type f -print0
    fi
  } | xargs -0 "${STAT[@]}" 2>/dev/null | LC_ALL=C sort
}

if [ "$(uname)" = Darwin ]; then STAT=(stat -f '%N %z %m'); else STAT=(stat -c '%n %s %Y'); fi

tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

echo "e2e-studio-untouched: fingerprinting $STUDIO_SDK and $STUDIO_AVD"
fingerprint > "$tmp/before"
echo "e2e-studio-untouched: $(wc -l < "$tmp/before" | tr -d ' ') files; running: $*"
"$@"
fingerprint > "$tmp/after"

if ! diff -u "$tmp/before" "$tmp/after" > "$tmp/diff"; then
  echo "e2e-studio-untouched: FAIL, Studio files changed:"
  head -50 "$tmp/diff"
  exit 1
fi
echo "e2e-studio-untouched: ok, $(wc -l < "$tmp/after" | tr -d ' ') files unchanged"

```

`scripts/lib/no_jidr_emulators.py`:

```py
"""Exit 1 if a live emulator is running an AVD under the given Jidr home.

usage: python3 -I scripts/lib/no_jidr_emulators.py <JIDR_HOME>
"""

import glob
import os
import sys

home = os.path.realpath(sys.argv[1])
dirs = [
    os.path.expanduser("~/Library/Caches/TemporaryItems/avd/running"),
    os.path.join(os.environ.get("XDG_RUNTIME_DIR", "/nonexistent"), "avd/running"),
    f"/tmp/android-{os.environ.get('USER', '')}/avd/running",
]
for d in dirs:
    for f in glob.glob(os.path.join(d, "pid_*.ini")):
        try:
            vals = dict(line.strip().split("=", 1) for line in open(f) if "=" in line)
            pid = int(os.path.basename(f)[4:-4])
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            continue
        if not os.path.realpath(vals.get("avd.dir", "/")).startswith(home):
            continue
        try:
            os.kill(pid, 0)
        except OSError:
            continue
        print(f"still running: pid {pid} ({vals.get('avd.id')})", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

```

`site/README.md`:

```md
# jidr.ly

The Jidr landing page: Astro (static) for Cloudflare Pages (D16), built to the Workbench design (D41). English at `/`, Arabic (RTL) at `/ar/` (D33). Deployed to Cloudflare Pages (project `jidr`) at https://jidr.ly.

```bash
npm ci
npm run dev          # http://localhost:4321 (generates the styles first)
npm run build        # → dist/ (generates the styles first)
npm test             # tests for the style generator
npm run lighthouse   # Lighthouse CI on dist/ (performance and accessibility ≥ 95)
```

- **Design:** the Workbench landing design, concept 8A (`docs/design/README.md`), in coming-soon, launch and Arabic variants.
- **Phase:** `phase` in `src/config.ts`. `"soon"` (live now) is the coming-soon page; `"launch"` adds the download, agent/MCP, CI snippet and docs sections.
- **Copy:** `src/i18n.ts` holds every string in English and Arabic; components read `Astro.currentLocale`. What depicts the English-only app (the product shot, the Rooted badge, the agent transcript, commands) stays English on both pages.
- **Before launch:** in `src/config.ts`, set `release.version`, `sizeMb` and `sha256` from the published release's `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and `homebrew: true` once the cask exists (Phase 12b). The Download buttons link to `Jidr-<version>-arm64.dmg` on the `v<version>` release.
- **Styles are generated, never hand-edited** (`scripts/build-styles.mjs`, run before `dev` and `build`; outputs are git-ignored):
  - `src/styles/tokens.css`: every token in `docs/design/tokens.json` as a `--jidr-*` custom property, dark and light. That includes the Arabic landing sizes (`--jidr-type-web-*-ar`); a test checks they match the token block of `docs/design/jidr.css`.
  - `src/styles/workbench.css`: the component rules of `docs/design/jidr.css`, pruned to the classes the `.astro` files use. Use a class in a `class="…"` attribute and its rules come along.
  - `src/styles/site.css`: the few page-level rules the design canvas got from its host page, tokens only.
- **Fonts:** Geist, Geist Mono and Noto Kufi Arabic (OFL-1.1), self-hosted from `@fontsource`, only the weights and subsets in use. `src/layouts/Base.astro` has the faces both pages need and preloads each locale's hero faces; `src/pages/ar/index.astro` adds the Kufi faces only the Arabic page uses. Arabic headings use 600, the Arabic type group's weight, so no bold Kufi face loads.
- **Brand assets:** `public/{favicon.svg,favicon.ico,favicon-32.png,apple-touch-icon.png,og-image.png,symbol.svg}` are copies of `assets/brand/web/*` (D39). Re-copy them when `assets/brand/build.sh` changes.
- **Public links:** `src/config.ts`. The repo link moves to the `jidr-dev` org with the repo (D26); the Sponsor buttons appear once `sponsors` is set.
- **Search and AI assistants:** `src/pages/404.astro` (Pages serves it with status 404 for unknown paths), `src/pages/sitemap.xml.ts` (both languages with hreflang), schema.org `SoftwareApplication` data in `src/layouts/Base.astro` (only what's true in the current phase), `public/llms.txt` (a plain-text summary for AI tools) and `public/robots.txt` (allows everyone and names the AI crawlers). Keep `llms.txt` in step with the README.
- **Blog:** a post is a Markdown file in `src/pages/blog/` with `layout: ../../layouts/Post.astro` and a `title`, `description` and `date`. `src/posts.ts` lists them for `/blog/` and the sitemap; add each new post to `llms.txt` under Guides.
- **Rules:** no email capture or analytics (D17, D34); no Google, Android or Genymotion logos; the Genymotion comparison is text only.

```

`site/public/llms.txt`:

```txt
# Jidr (جذر)

> Jidr is a free, open-source Android emulator manager for Apple Silicon Macs, written in Rust: an open-source alternative to Genymotion Desktop. It creates and runs virtual Android phones and tablets from Google's emulator images, roots them in one click (Shell root with `adb root`, or Full root with Magisk, verified with `su -c id`), and ships a desktop app, a CLI with JSON output and an MCP server for AI agents. No accounts, no telemetry, no paid tier.

Jidr is not affiliated with Google or Genymotion.

## What it does

- Devices: create, clone, start, stop and delete virtual devices (API 29–36, arm64). Jidr keeps its own SDK copy and never modifies Android Studio's SDK or AVDs.
- Root: None, Shell root (`adb root`) or Full root (Magisk patched into a per-device copy of the ramdisk, then verified). Revert at any time. Play Store images get a guided beta.
- Widgets: battery, rotation and motion sensors, network (Wi-Fi, mobile data, speed and delay profiles), calls, SMS and signal bars, GPS with GPX/KML route replay, fingerprint, the host webcam as the camera, clipboard, developer toggles.
- Media and state: PNG screenshots, MP4 recordings, snapshots tagged with the root mode they were taken in.
- Build identity: set build properties (model, brand, fingerprint) on Full-root devices.
- Automation: every action is a `jidr` CLI command with `--json` output and stable exit codes; `jidr mcp` lets Claude and other MCP clients see and drive a device (screenshot, tap, type, UI tree, logs).

## Compared with Genymotion Desktop

Full comparison: https://jidr.ly/vs/genymotion/

- Free and open source (Apache-2.0; the desktop app is GPL-3.0-only).
- Includes features Genymotion sells in paid plans: CLI automation, network speed and delay profiles, GPS route replay, quick boot and a root toggle.
- Uses Google's official emulator images and the AOSP emulator, run locally on the Mac.
- Mac only for now (macOS 14 or later on Apple Silicon); no Windows or Linux builds yet.
- Some Genymotion features are planned but not built yet, such as operator and SIM identity, IMEI changes, disk speed limits and gamepad passthrough.

## Install

Requirements: macOS 14 or later on Apple Silicon, and about 10 GB of free disk space for the SDK and one system image.

- Homebrew: `brew install --cask abdurahmanalmehdi/tap/jidr` installs Jidr.app and puts the `jidr` CLI on your PATH. Update with `brew upgrade --cask jidr`.
- DMG: download `Jidr-<version>-arm64.dmg` from the latest release (https://github.com/AbdurahmanAlmehdi/jidr/releases/latest) and drag Jidr to Applications. The CLI is at `/Applications/Jidr.app/Contents/Helpers/jidr`.
- MCP: `claude mcp add jidr -- jidr mcp` for Claude Code; for Claude Desktop, open the `.mcpb` from the latest release. Jidr is in the MCP Registry as `io.github.AbdurahmanAlmehdi/jidr`.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/AbdurahmanAlmehdi/jidr#readme): overview, install, quick start, build from source
- [CLI reference](https://github.com/AbdurahmanAlmehdi/jidr/blob/main/docs/cli.md)
- [MCP tools](https://github.com/AbdurahmanAlmehdi/jidr/blob/main/docs/mcp.md)
- [Root modes](https://github.com/AbdurahmanAlmehdi/jidr/blob/main/docs/root.md)
- [Control protocol](https://github.com/AbdurahmanAlmehdi/jidr/blob/main/docs/control-protocol.md)
- [Feature parity with Genymotion Desktop](https://github.com/AbdurahmanAlmehdi/jidr/blob/main/docs/parity.md)

## Guides

- [How to root the Android emulator on an Apple Silicon Mac](https://jidr.ly/blog/root-android-emulator-apple-silicon/): adb root, Magisk in the ramdisk, verify and revert
- [Driving an Android emulator from an AI agent over MCP](https://jidr.ly/blog/drive-android-from-an-ai-agent-mcp/): setup for Claude Code and Claude Desktop, the tools, a sample session, safety

## Optional

- [Planned features](https://github.com/AbdurahmanAlmehdi/jidr/labels/upcoming%20feature)
- [Contributing](https://github.com/AbdurahmanAlmehdi/jidr/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [Security policy](https://github.com/AbdurahmanAlmehdi/jidr/blob/main/SECURITY.md)

`site/scripts/build-styles.mjs`:

```mjs
// Generates the site's styles from the Workbench design (D41). Runs before
// `astro dev` and `astro build`; the outputs are git-ignored.
//
// - src/styles/tokens.css    every token in docs/design/tokens.json as a
//                            --jidr-* custom property (dark + light)
// - src/styles/workbench.css the component rules of docs/design/jidr.css,
//                            pruned to the classes this site's .astro files use
//
// tokens.json is the single source: no colour or size is typed here.

import { readFileSync, readdirSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync } from "node:fs";
import { dirname, join, relative } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

const site = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");
const design = join(site, "../docs/design");
const out = join(site, "src/styles");

// ---- tokens.css ------------------------------------------------------------

const WEIGHT_NAMES = { 400: "regular", 500: "medium", 600: "semibold", 700: "bold" };

export function tokensCss(t) {
  const base = [];
  const dark = [];
  const light = [];
  const reduced = [];
  // DTCG aliases ({jidr-…}) become var(--jidr-…).
  const resolve = (v) => String(v).replace(/\{(jidr-[\w-]+)\}/g, "var(--$1)");
  const decl = (list, name, value) => list.push(`  --${name}: ${resolve(value)};`);

  // Fonts and type roles.
  for (const [key, family] of Object.entries(t.type.families)) {
    decl(base, `jidr-font-family-${key}`, family);
  }
  const weights = new Set();
  const arabic = t.type.groups.find((g) => g.family === "arabic");
  for (const group of t.type.groups) {
    if (group === arabic) continue;
    for (const s of group.styles) {
      weights.add(s.fontWeight);
      const p = `jidr-${s.name}`;
      decl(base, `${p}-family`, `var(--jidr-font-family-${s.family ?? group.family})`);
      decl(base, `${p}-size`, s.fontSize);
      decl(base, `${p}-weight`, s.fontWeight);
      decl(base, `${p}-line-height`, s.lineHeight);
      decl(base, `${p}-letter-spacing`, s.letterSpacing);
      if (s.name.includes("metric")) decl(base, `${p}-features`, '"tnum"');
      const ar = arabic?.styles.find((a) => a.name === `${s.name}-ar`);
      if (ar) {
        decl(base, `${p}-size-ar`, ar.fontSize);
        decl(base, `${p}-line-height-ar`, ar.lineHeight);
      }
    }
  }
  for (const w of [...weights].sort()) {
    if (WEIGHT_NAMES[w]) decl(base, `jidr-font-weight-${WEIGHT_NAMES[w]}`, w);
  }

  // Colours, then every other group. Themed values ({dark, light}) go to the
  // theme blocks; shadows also expose their colour, y and blur parts.
  const groups = [t.color, ...Object.entries(t)
    .filter(([k, v]) => !["color", "type"].includes(k) && v && Array.isArray(v.tokens))
    .map(([, v]) => v)];
  for (const group of groups) {
    for (const tok of group.tokens) {
      const themed = typeof tok.value === "object";
      for (const [list, theme] of themed ? [[dark, "dark"], [light, "light"]] : [[base, null]]) {
        const value = theme ? tok.value[theme] : tok.value;
        decl(list, tok.name, value);
        if (tok.name.endsWith("-shadow")) {
          const [, y, blur, , color] = String(value).split(/\s+/);
          decl(list, `${tok.name}-color`, color);
          decl(list, `${tok.name}-y`, y);
          decl(list, `${tok.name}-blur`, blur);
        }
      }
      // Reduce Motion, from each motion token's own "Reduced:" note.
      const note = /Reduced:\s*([^.]*)/.exec(tok.usage ?? "")?.[1]?.toLowerCase();
      if (tok.name.startsWith("jidr-motion-") && note) {
        if (tok.name.endsWith("-distance")) decl(reduced, tok.name, "0px");
        else if (/instant|jumps|static/.test(note)) decl(reduced, tok.name, "0ms");
      }
    }
  }

  const block = (sel, lines, scheme) =>
    `${sel} {\n${scheme ? `  color-scheme: ${scheme};\n` : ""}${lines.join("\n")}\n}`;
  return [
    "/* Generated by site/scripts/build-styles.mjs from docs/design/tokens.json. Don't edit. */",
    block(":root", base),
    block(":root,\n.jidr-dark", dark, "dark"),
    `@media (prefers-color-scheme: light) {\n${block(':root:not([data-theme="dark"])', light, "light")}\n}`,
    block(':root[data-theme="light"],\n.jidr-light', light, "light"),
    block(':root[data-theme="dark"]', dark, "dark"),
    reduced.length ? `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {\n${block(":root", reduced)}\n}` : "",
  ].join("\n\n") + "\n";
}

// ---- workbench.css -----------------------------------------------------------

/** Splits CSS into top-level nodes: rules and at-rules (with children for
 * @media/@container/@supports). Comments are dropped. */
export function parseCss(css) {
  css = css.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, "");
  const nodes = [];
  let i = 0;
  while (i < css.length) {
    const open = css.indexOf("{", i);
    if (open === -1) break;
    const prelude = css.slice(i, open).trim();
    let depth = 1;
    let j = open + 1;
    while (j < css.length && depth > 0) {
      if (css[j] === "{") depth++;
      else if (css[j] === "}") depth--;
      j++;
    }
    const body = css.slice(open + 1, j - 1);
    if (/^@(media|container|supports)\b/.test(prelude)) {
      nodes.push({ at: prelude, children: parseCss(body) });
    } else if (prelude.startsWith("@")) {
      nodes.push({ at: prelude, raw: body });
    } else if (prelude) {
      nodes.push({ selector: prelude, body: body.trim() });
    }
    i = j;
  }
  return nodes;
}

function splitSelectors(selector) {
  const parts = [];
  let depth = 0;
  let cur = "";
  for (const ch of selector) {
    if (ch === "(") depth++;
    if (ch === ")") depth--;
    if (ch === "," && depth === 0) {
      parts.push(cur.trim());
      cur = "";
    } else cur += ch;
  }
  if (cur.trim()) parts.push(cur.trim());
  return parts;
}

/** Keeps the selectors whose classes are all in `used` (class-free selectors
 * stay); drops rules left with none, and @keyframes nothing animates. */
export function prune(nodes, used) {
  const keep = (sel) => {
    const classes = sel.replace(/:not\([^)]*\)/g, "").match(/\.[A-Za-z_][\w-]*/g) ?? [];
    return classes.every((c) => used.has(c.slice(1)));
  };
  const walk = (list) =>
    list.flatMap((n) => {
      if (n.children) {
        const children = walk(n.children);
        return children.length ? [{ ...n, children }] : [];
      }
      if (n.raw !== undefined) return [n];
      const sels = splitSelectors(n.selector).filter(keep);
      return sels.length ? [{ ...n, selector: sels.join(",") }] : [];
    });
  const kept = walk(nodes);
  const text = print(kept.filter((n) => !n.at?.startsWith("@keyframes")));
  return kept.filter((n) => {
    const name = /^@keyframes\s+([\w-]+)/.exec(n.at ?? "")?.[1];
    return !name || text.includes(name);
  });
}

export function print(nodes) {
  return nodes
    .map((n) =>
      n.children
        ? `${n.at}{\n${print(n.children)}\n}`
        : n.raw !== undefined
          ? `${n.at}{${n.raw}}`
          : `${n.selector}{${n.body}}`,
    )
    .join("\n");
}

/** Every class named in a `class="…"` attribute of the site's .astro files. */
export function usedClasses(dir) {
  const used = new Set();
  const visit = (d) => {
    for (const e of readdirSync(d, { withFileTypes: true })) {
      const p = join(d, e.name);
      if (e.isDirectory()) visit(p);
      else if (e.name.endsWith(".astro")) {
        for (const m of readFileSync(p, "utf8").matchAll(/\bclass="([^"]*)"/g)) {
          for (const c of m[1].split(/\s+/)) if (/^[A-Za-z_][\w-]*$/.test(c)) used.add(c);
        }
      }
    }
  };
  visit(dir);
  return used;
}

const MARKER = "/* ===================================================================== page chrome */";

function main() {
  mkdirSync(out, { recursive: true });
  const tokens = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(design, "tokens.json"), "utf8"));
  const jidrCss = readFileSync(join(design, "jidr.css"), "utf8");
  writeFileSync(join(out, "tokens.css"), tokensCss(tokens));

  const at = jidrCss.indexOf(MARKER);
  if (at === -1) throw new Error(`jidr.css no longer has the "${MARKER}" marker`);
  const used = usedClasses(join(site, "src"));
  const css = print(prune(parseCss(jidrCss.slice(at)), used));
  writeFileSync(
    join(out, "workbench.css"),
    `/* Generated by site/scripts/build-styles.mjs: the component rules of\n   docs/design/jidr.css that this site uses. Don't edit. */\n${css}\n`,
  );
  console.log(
    `build-styles: ${relative(site, join(out, "tokens.css"))}, ${relative(site, join(out, "workbench.css"))} (${used.size} classes)`,
  );
}

if (process.argv[1] === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) main();

import { parseCss, print, prune, tokensCss } from "./build-styles.mjs";

      {

      { name: "jidr-motion-popover-duration", value: "160ms", usage: "Fade + rise. Reduced: fade only." },
      { name: "jidr-motion-popover-distance", value: "4px", usage: "Fade + rise. Reduced: fade only." },
    ],
  },
};

test("expands type roles with Arabic variants and metric features", () => {
  const css = tokensCss(tokens);
  assert.match(css, /--jidr-font-family-ui: Geist, sans-serif;/);
  assert.match(css, /--jidr-type-hero-family: var\(--jidr-font-family-ui\);/);
  assert.match(css, /--jidr-type-hero-size-ar: 30px;/);
  assert.match(css, /--jidr-type-hero-line-height-ar: 52px;/);
  assert.match(css, /--jidr-type-metric-family: var\(--jidr-font-family-mono\);/);
  assert.match(css, /--jidr-type-metric-features: "tnum";/);
  assert.match(css, /--jidr-font-weight-semibold: 600;/);
  assert.doesNotMatch(css, /type-hero-ar-/);
});

test("resolves DTCG aliases and puts themed values in theme blocks", () => {
  // Regression: aliases were emitted as `{jidr-…}` instead of var(--jidr-…).
  const css = tokensCss(tokens);
  assert.doesNotMatch(css, /\{jidr-/);
  assert.match(css, /--jidr-color-text-link: var\(--jidr-color-accent-text\);/);
  const dark = css.split(":root,\n.jidr-dark {")[1].split("\n}")[0];
  assert.match(dark, /color-scheme: dark/);
  assert.match(dark, /--jidr-color-accent-text: #8fb0ff;/);
  assert.match(css, /:root\[data-theme="light"\],\n\.jidr-light \{\n  color-scheme: light;/);
});

test("splits shadows into colour, y and blur", () => {
  const css = tokensCss(tokens);
  assert.match(css, /--jidr-elevation-3-shadow-color: #12151A33;/);
  assert.match(css, /--jidr-elevation-3-shadow-y: 16px;/);
  assert.match(css, /--jidr-elevation-3-shadow-blur: 40px;/);
});

test("reduced motion follows each token's own note", () => {
  const css = tokensCss(tokens);
  const reduced = css.split("@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)")[1];
  assert.match(reduced, /--jidr-motion-panel-duration: 0ms;/);
  assert.match(reduced, /--jidr-motion-popover-distance: 0px;/);
  assert.doesNotMatch(reduced, /popover-duration|hover-duration/);
});

test("prunes rules to the used classes, keeping at-rules and keyframes in use", () => {
  const css = `
    *{box-sizing:border-box}
    .btn,.btn.is-hover{color:red}
    .unused{color:blue}
    .site .lp-h2{font-size:30px}
    @container (max-width: 760px){.wrap{padding:16px}.gone{x:y}}
    @keyframes spin{to{transform:rotate(1turn)}}
    @keyframes unused-anim{to{opacity:0}}
    .spinner{animation:spin 1s}
  `;
  const out = print(prune(parseCss(css), new Set(["btn", "site", "lp-h2", "wrap"])));
  assert.match(out, /\*\{box-sizing:border-box\}/);
  assert.match(out, /^\.btn\{color:red\}$/m);
  assert.match(out, /\.site \.lp-h2/);
  assert.match(out, /@container \(max-width: 760px\)\{\n\.wrap\{padding:16px\}\n\}/);
  assert.doesNotMatch(out, /unused|gone|is-hover|spinner|@keyframes/);
});

test("the real tokens resolve every variable the design's component CSS uses", () => {
  const design = join(here, "../../docs/design");
  const jidrCss = readFileSync(join(design, "jidr.css"), "utf8");
  const tokens = tokensCss(JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(design, "tokens.json"), "utf8")));
  const defined = new Set([...tokens.matchAll(/(--jidr-[\w-]+):/g)].map((m) => m[1]));
  const comp = jidrCss.split("page chrome */")[1];
  const used = new Set([...comp.matchAll(/var\((--jidr-[\w-]+)/g)].map((m) => m[1]));
  assert.deepEqual([...used].filter((v) => !defined.has(v)), []);
});

// Regression (G13): tokens.json had no Arabic landing sizes, so the RTL hero,
// lede and section titles pointed at undefined variables. The design's token
// block and tokens.json must now agree on every Arabic size.
test("tokens.json carries every Arabic type size jidr.css's token block declares", () => {
  const design = join(here, "../../docs/design");
  const jidrCss = readFileSync(join(design, "jidr.css"), "utf8");
  const tokens = tokensCss(JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(design, "tokens.json"), "utf8")));
  const decls = (css) =>
    new Map([...(/:root\s*\{([^}]*)\}/.exec(css)?.[1] ?? "").matchAll(/(--jidr-type-[\w-]+-ar):\s*([^;]+);/g)]
      .map(([, name, value]) => [name, value.trim()]));
  const want = decls(jidrCss);
  const ours = decls(tokens);
  assert.ok(want.size >= 26, `jidr.css declares ${want.size} Arabic sizes`);
  for (const [name, value] of want) assert.equal(ours.get(name), value, name);
});

`site/src/components/Terminal.astro`:

```astro
---
// A command block (.cli in the design) with a Copy button. The button stays
// hidden without JavaScript or a clipboard; the commands are plain text either
// way. Astro bundles the script once, however many blocks a page has.
import { strings } from "../i18n";

interface Props {
  title: string;
  lines: string[];
}

const { title, lines } = Astro.props;
const t = strings(Astro.currentLocale);
---

<div class="cli">
  <div class="ch">
    <span>{title}</span><span class="grow"></span>
    <button class="btn btn-tertiary btn-sm" type="button" data-copy data-done={t.copy.done} aria-live="polite" hidden>{t.copy.label}</button>
  </div>
  <pre lang="en">{lines.map((line, i) => <>{i > 0 && "\n"}<span class="pr">$ </span>{line}</>)}</pre>
</div>

<script>
  for (const button of document.querySelectorAll<HTMLButtonElement>("[data-copy]")) {
    const pre = button.closest(".cli")?.querySelector("pre");
    if (!pre || !navigator.clipboard) continue;
    // The commands without their "$ " prompts.
    const copy = pre.cloneNode(true) as HTMLElement;
    copy.querySelectorAll(".pr").forEach((p) => p.remove());
    const text = copy.textContent ?? "";
    const label = button.textContent;
    button.hidden = false;
    button.addEventListener("click", async () => {
      try {
        await navigator.clipboard.writeText(text);
      } catch {
        // Clipboard refused: select the commands so ⌘C still works.
        getSelection()?.selectAllChildren(pre);
        return;
      }
      button.textContent = button.dataset.done ?? label;
      setTimeout(() => (button.textContent = label), 2000);
    });
  }
</script>

```

`site/src/config.ts`:

```ts
// What the site shows and where it links. Everything that changes between the
// coming-soon page, launch day and later releases lives here.

// "soon" is the 11a coming-soon page (Star and Sponsor, no download); "launch"
// is the 11b page with the download, agent, CLI and docs sections.
export const phase: "soon" | "launch" = "launch";

// Public links (D1, D25, D26). `sponsors` stays null
// until a GitHub Sponsors profile exists: the Sponsor buttons and section are
// hidden while it's null.
const repo = "https://github.com/AbdurahmanAlmehdi/jidr";
const sponsors: string | null = null;

// The release the Download buttons point at. `xtask release` names the DMG
// `Jidr-<version>-arm64.dmg` and `release.yml` tags it `v<version>`. Fill in
// the size and the SHA-256 from the published release's SHA256SUMS.txt.
export const release = {
  version: "0.2.0", // x-release-please-version
  sizeMb: "20.9",
  sha256: "13b49341c3ff2c860cfdfbd4bfcef4324e6524134f99d4f1fe119dc4a58fbac6",
  // True once release.yml has pushed the cask to the tap (needs the
  // HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN secret); shows the brew install and upgrade lines.
  homebrew: true,
};

export const links = {
  repo,
  sponsors,
  releases: `${repo}/releases`,
  dmg: `${repo}/releases/download/v${release.version}/Jidr-${release.version}-arm64.dmg`,
  doc: (path: string) => `${repo}/blob/main/${path}`,
};

```

`site/src/dates.ts`:

```ts
/** A post's date as `YYYY-MM-DD` and as shown ("17 October 2026"). */
export function postDate(value: string | Date) {
  const date = new Date(value);
  return {
    iso: date.toISOString().slice(0, 10),
    shown: date.toLocaleDateString("en-GB", { day: "numeric", month: "long", year: "numeric", timeZone: "UTC" }),
  };
}
