`site/src/pages/blog/drive-android-from-an-ai-agent-mcp.md`:

```md
---
layout: ../../layouts/Post.astro
title: "Driving an Android emulator from an AI agent over MCP"
description: "Give Claude or any MCP client a real Android device on your Mac: create and boot it, install an app, look at the screen, tap, type and read the logs."
date: 2026-10-17
---

An AI coding agent can write an Android feature, but it usually can't see it run. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) closes that loop: an MCP server exposes tools, and the agent calls them. Give it tools for a real Android device, and it can install the build it just made, look at the screen, tap through the flow and read the crash in logcat.

[Jidr](https://github.com/AbdurahmanAlmehdi/jidr) ships one: `jidr mcp`, an MCP server over stdio for Android emulators on Apple Silicon Macs.

## Setup

Install Jidr (`brew install --cask abdurahmanalmehdi/tap/jidr`, or the DMG from the [release](https://github.com/AbdurahmanAlmehdi/jidr/releases/latest)), then add it to your agent.

Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add jidr -- jidr mcp
```

Claude Desktop: open `jidr-mcp-<version>-darwin-arm64.mcpb` from the release, or add this to `claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "jidr": { "command": "/opt/homebrew/bin/jidr", "args": ["mcp"] }
  }
}
```

Cursor and other clients take the same `command` and `args`. The server starts the Jidr daemon if it isn't running, so there's nothing else to launch.

## The tools

Two tools reach everything Jidr can do: `command_list` returns every command with its JSON Schema, and `command_run` runs one. Long operations, such as booting a device or downloading an image, are waited for up to a timeout and come back as a job otherwise.

The other nine are fast paths for the loop an agent repeats most:

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `screenshot` | PNG of the screen, fitted in 1024×1024, with the scale |
| `tap`, `swipe` | Touch input, in screenshot coordinates by default |
| `type_text`, `press_key` | Text into the focused field; Home, Back, Enter and other keys |
| `ui_dump` | The uiautomator tree: text, resource ids and bounds |
| `logcat_tail` | The last lines of the log, optionally filtered |
| `jobs_list`, `jobs_cancel` | Long-running operations |

Every tool carries MCP's read-only, destructive and idempotent hints, and errors come back as structured results (`not_found`, `busy`, `boot_timeout`, …) that an agent can act on.

## A session

Asked to "check the sign-up screen of my debug build on Android 15", an agent's calls look like this:

```json
{"tool": "command_run", "arguments": {"command": "device.create", "params": {"name": "agent-phone", "image": "35"}}}
{"tool": "command_run", "arguments": {"command": "device.start", "params": {"device": "agent-phone"}}}
{"tool": "command_run", "arguments": {"command": "file.install", "params": {"device": "agent-phone", "apk": "app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk"}}}
{"tool": "command_run", "arguments": {"command": "app.launch", "params": {"device": "agent-phone", "apk": "app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk"}}}
{"tool": "screenshot", "arguments": {"device": "agent-phone"}}
{"tool": "ui_dump", "arguments": {"device": "agent-phone"}}
{"tool": "tap", "arguments": {"device": "agent-phone", "x": 512, "y": 1730, "coords": "device"}}
{"tool": "type_text", "arguments": {"device": "agent-phone", "text": "test@example.com", "enter": true}}
{"tool": "logcat_tail", "arguments": {"device": "agent-phone", "lines": 200, "filter": "AndroidRuntime"}}
```

Two habits make agents much more reliable here:

- **Find targets in `ui_dump`, not in pixels.** The tree gives each view's bounds in device pixels, so the agent can tap the centre of the "Sign up" button with `coords: "device"`. Guessing from a scaled screenshot misses small targets.
- **Check logcat after every step that can crash.** A stack trace under `AndroidRuntime` explains a blank screen faster than another screenshot.

On an M1 Pro, a screenshot takes about 0.4–1.1 s, a tap 0.2–0.4 s and typing 0.7–1.2 s. `ui_dump` is the slow one, at 4–6 s, because uiautomator is. A cold boot takes 25–32 s.

## Safety

An agent with a device can do damage, so destructive commands are refused by default: deleting a device, factory reset, uninstalling an app. They're allowed only on devices the agent created itself (marked agent-owned, as `agent-phone` above) or when you start the server with `jidr mcp --allow-destructive`. A refusal says why, so the agent can ask you instead of retrying.

Root is a device setting like any other. If the task needs it, the agent can call `root.set` with `magisk` and verify it with `root.verify`; the [rooting post](/blog/root-android-emulator-apple-silicon/) explains what that does.

## In CI

The same commands work without an agent: every MCP call has a `jidr` CLI equivalent with `--json` output and stable exit codes, so a flow an agent worked out can become a script on a macOS runner.

## Further reading

- [MCP tools in the Jidr docs](https://github.com/AbdurahmanAlmehdi/jidr/blob/main/docs/mcp.md)
- [The Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io)
- [Jidr's CLI reference](https://github.com/AbdurahmanAlmehdi/jidr/blob/main/docs/cli.md)

`site/src/pages/blog/root-android-emulator-apple-silicon.md`:

```md
---
layout: ../../layouts/Post.astro
title: "How to root the Android emulator on an Apple Silicon Mac"
description: "Shell root with adb root, full root with Magisk patched into the emulator's ramdisk, and how to verify and revert both, on M-series Macs."
date: 2026-10-17
---

Google's Android Emulator runs arm64 system images natively on Apple Silicon, and it's fast. What it doesn't give you is root, and many security, testing and reverse-engineering workflows need it. There are two kinds of root you can have on an emulator, and they solve different problems.

## Shell root: `adb root`

Some system images let `adbd`, the daemon behind `adb shell`, restart as root:

```bash
adb root
adb shell id    # uid=0(root) gid=0(root) …
```

This works on the **Google APIs** (`google_apis`), **Default** (`default`) and **ATD** (`aosp_atd`) images. It doesn't work on **Google Play** (`google_apis_playstore`) images, which are production builds: `adb root` answers "adbd cannot run as root in production builds".

Shell root is enough to read any app's private data, change system settings or run `tcpdump`. But only your shell is root. Apps on the device can't get root, there's no `su` binary, and `adb root` has to be run again after every boot.

## Full root: Magisk in the ramdisk

For apps to request root (a root checker, a Frida server, an app under test that behaves differently when rooted), the device needs `su`. On an emulator the usual way is [Magisk](https://github.com/topjohnwu/Magisk), patched into the boot ramdisk.

The emulator loads the ramdisk from the system image's `ramdisk.img`, a compressed cpio archive whose `init` is the first process Android runs. Magisk's documented layout replaces that `init` with `magiskinit`, adds Magisk's payload under `overlay.d/sbin`, and records its config in `.backup/.magisk`. At boot, `magiskinit` sets up Magisk, then hands over to the real `init`.

Done by hand, it goes like this:

1. Copy the image's `ramdisk.img` somewhere of your own. Never patch the one in the SDK: every device created from that image would boot it.
2. Decompress and unpack the cpio, apply the changes above, repack and recompress it in the same format.
3. Cold boot the emulator with the patched copy: `emulator -avd <name> -ramdisk <patched.img> -no-snapshot-load`.
4. Install the Magisk app, which is also the release APK, and let it finish its environment setup. That needs one more reboot.
5. Grant `su` to the shell (Magisk prompts on the device) and check: `adb shell su -c id`.

Scripts such as rootAVD automate these steps. What they leave to you is keeping track of which ramdisk each device boots, and undoing the patch later.

## Doing it in one step with Jidr

[Jidr](https://github.com/AbdurahmanAlmehdi/jidr) is a free, open-source emulator manager for Apple Silicon Macs that treats root as a device setting:

```bash
jidr image install 35 --accept-licenses   # you accept Google's SDK licence
jidr device create Phone --image 35
jidr root set Phone adb       # shell root, reapplied after every boot
jidr root set Phone magisk    # full root
jidr root verify Phone        # checks the live uid against the mode
jidr root set Phone none      # back to stock
```

`root set Phone magisk` runs the steps above as one job you can follow or cancel:

- It downloads the pinned Magisk release from GitHub and checks its SHA-256. Jidr never bundles Magisk.
- It patches a **per-device** copy of the ramdisk, with its own cpio and compression code, and writes it atomically.
- It cold boots, installs the app, sets up `/data/adb/magisk` and reboots once.
- On images that allow `adb root`, it writes the shell's grant itself, then drops adbd back so the final `su -c id` goes through Magisk's own `su`. On Google Play images it asks you to tap **Grant** once.

Reverting deletes the patched copy and cold boots the stock ramdisk, so a device is never stuck half-rooted. When the image or the pinned Magisk version changes, the next run rebuilds the patch from the pristine ramdisk instead of patching on top of an old one.

The same works from the desktop app (a Root switch on each device) and from an AI agent over MCP.

## What root can't do

No emulator passes Play Integrity, rooted or not: it attests the device's hardware and boot state, which an emulator doesn't have. Magisk's DenyList hides root from local checks only. If your app depends on Play Integrity, test that part on a real device.

Snapshots taken with one root mode can't be restored under another, because the ramdisk differs. Jidr tags each snapshot with its root mode and refuses a mismatch instead of booting a broken device.

## Further reading

- [Root modes in the Jidr docs](https://github.com/AbdurahmanAlmehdi/jidr/blob/main/docs/root.md): the full Magisk flow, auto-grant, build properties, offline Magisk
- [Magisk's installation docs](https://topjohnwu.github.io/Magisk/install.html)
- [Jidr vs Genymotion Desktop](/vs/genymotion/)

// The sitemap: the home page in each language, each listing the others as
// alternates (hreflang) so search engines pair /ar/ with /, plus the
// English-only pages.
import type { APIRoute } from "astro";
import { locales, strings } from "../i18n";
import { posts } from "../posts";

export const GET: APIRoute = ({ site }) => {
  const url = (path: string) => new URL(path, site).href;
  const alternates = [
    ...locales.map((l) => `<xhtml:link rel="alternate" hreflang="${l}" href="${url(strings(l).home)}"/>`),
    `<xhtml:link rel="alternate" hreflang="x-default" href="${url("/")}"/>`,
  ].join("");
  // English-only pages, without language alternates.
  const english = ["/vs/genymotion/", "/blog/", ...posts.map((p) => p.url)];
  const pages = english.map((path) => `<url><loc>${url(path)}</loc></url>`).join("");
  const entries = locales.map((l) => `<url><loc>${url(strings(l).home)}</loc>${alternates}</url>`).join("") + pages;
  const body = `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>\n<urlset xmlns="http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9" xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml">${entries}</urlset>\n`;
  return new Response(body, { headers: { "Content-Type": "application/xml; charset=utf-8" } });
};

```ts
// The blog posts (src/pages/blog/*.md), newest first, for the blog index and
// the sitemap. URLs end in "/", like every other page on the site.
import { postDate } from "./dates";

type Frontmatter = { title: string; description: string; date: string | Date };
type Page = { url: string; frontmatter: Frontmatter };

const pages = Object.values(import.meta.glob<Page>("./pages/blog/*.md", { eager: true }));

export const posts = pages
  .map(({ url, frontmatter }) => ({
    url: url.endsWith("/") ? url : `${url}/`,
    title: frontmatter.title,
    description: frontmatter.description,
    ...postDate(frontmatter.date),
  }))
  .sort((a, b) => b.iso.localeCompare(a.iso));

```

`skills/jidr-app-testing/SKILL.md`:

```md
---
name: jidr-app-testing
description: "Test an Android app on a Jidr emulator: install an APK or run a Flutter or React Native app on the device's adb serial, then check a flow with screenshot, tap, swipe, type and the UI tree, and clean up the devices you created. Use when the user asks to run their Android app on an emulator and check that a screen or flow works, reproduce a bug on a device, or verify a UI change. Needs the jidr skill for creating and starting devices."
---

# Testing an app on a Jidr device

Use the jidr skill to get a running device first. Note its adb serial (`emulator-55xx`): `jidr device list` shows it in the SERIAL column. Use that serial everywhere below, never a guessed `emulator-5554`, which may be a device the user is using.

## 1. Get the app onto the device

An APK:

```bash
jidr install Phone build/app-release.apk --grant     # --grant: all runtime permissions
jidr call app.launch '{"device":"Phone","package":"com.example.app"}'
```

Flutter (debug build with hot reload; the serial is the `-d` id):

```bash
flutter run -d emulator-5556
```

React Native: start Metro, then run `npx react-native run-android` with the serial (`--deviceId emulator-5556` on older CLIs, `--device emulator-5556` on newer ones; `--help` says which). With Expo, `npx expo run:android --device` asks which device to use.

For repeatable runs, turn animations off first:

```bash
jidr call dev.set '{"device":"Phone","animation_scale":0}'
```

## 2. Check the flow: look, act, look again

Repeat until the flow is done: take a screenshot, find the element, act on it, take another screenshot to see what happened. Don't act twice without looking in between.

With the Jidr MCP tools (when connected):

| Step | Tool |
|---|---|
| Look | `screenshot {device}`: the image, fitted in 1024×1024 |
| Find | `ui_dump {device}`: uiautomator XML with `text`, `resource-id` and `bounds` |
| Tap / swipe | `tap {device, x, y}`, `swipe {device, x1, y1, x2, y2}`: coordinates in the screenshot image (or `coords: "device"` for device pixels) |
| Type | `type_text {device, text, enter?}` into the focused field |
| Keys | `press_key {device, key}`: `GoBack`, `GoHome`, `Enter`… |
| Logs | `logcat_tail {device, lines?, filter?}` |

With the CLI and adb (device pixels; the screenshot is full size, so its coordinates match):

```bash
jidr --json call media.screenshot '{"device":"Phone"}'    # read result.path to see it
adb -s emulator-5556 exec-out uiautomator dump /dev/tty     # UI tree
adb -s emulator-5556 shell input tap 540 1200
adb -s emulator-5556 shell input swipe 540 1600 540 600 300
adb -s emulator-5556 shell input text 'hello%sworld'        # %s is a space
jidr call key.press '{"device":"Phone","key":"back"}'
jidr logcat Phone -n 200 --filter flutter:V
```

Tips:

- In the UI tree, `bounds="[x1,y1][x2,y2]"`: tap the centre. Prefer finding elements by `text` or `resource-id` over guessing from the picture.
- `ui_dump` takes several seconds. Use screenshots to follow progress and the tree only to find what to tap.
- If the app crashed or the screen didn't change, read the log before trying again: `jidr logcat Phone -n 200` (look for `FATAL EXCEPTION` or `AndroidRuntime`).
- A rotation check: `jidr call sensor.rotate '{"device":"Phone","angle":90}'`, screenshot, then back to `0`.
- To retry a flow from the same state, save a snapshot before it and load it between tries (`jidr snapshot save Phone start`, `jidr snapshot load Phone start`).

Report what you checked with the final screenshot, and the log lines for any failure.

## 3. Clean up

Delete only the devices you created in this session (D5: devices you create are yours to delete). Leave the user's own devices running and untouched, and say what you removed.

```bash
jidr device stop Phone
jidr device delete Phone --yes
```

If the user wants to keep looking at the result, leave your device running and tell them its name instead.

```

`skills/jidr/SKILL.md`:

```md
---
name: jidr
description: "Run, watch and drive Android emulators with Jidr (CLI `jidr`, the Jidr desktop app, MCP server `jidr mcp`). Use when the user mentions Jidr or a Jidr device, or asks for an Android phone or tablet emulator to run something on, an emulator screenshot, logcat, rotation, snapshots, or starting and stopping a device. For testing an app's flows on a device, also load jidr-app-testing."
---

# Jidr

Jidr (جذر) runs Android emulators, optionally rooted. A daemon owns every device. The desktop app, the `jidr` CLI and the MCP server (`jidr mcp`) are thin clients over the same protocol, so a device started from one shows up in all of them. Today Jidr ships for macOS on Apple Silicon (arm64 images). Docs: https://github.com/AbdurahmanAlmehdi/jidr (`docs/cli.md`, `docs/mcp.md`, `docs/control-protocol.md`).

If `jidr` isn't on the `PATH`, ask the user to install Jidr (https://jidr.ly, or `brew install --cask abdurahmanalmehdi/tap/jidr`). The macOS app also carries the CLI at `Jidr.app/Contents/Helpers/jidr`.

**Prefer the CLI.** It covers every command, needs no setup and works in scripts. `jidr call <method> '<json>'` reaches any protocol command that has no subcommand. A Jidr device is not an Android Studio AVD: `emulator -list-avds` doesn't list it.

## Find or create a device

```bash
jidr device list                 # NAME, STATUS, IMAGE, ROOT, SERIAL (the adb serial while running)
jidr --json device list          # the same as JSON
jidr profile list                # phone-6.1-fhd, phone-6.7-qhd, small-phone-5, tablet-11
jidr image list --installed      # images already downloaded (works offline)
```

Reuse a stopped device whose form factor fits the app. Otherwise create one from an installed image, so nothing has to download:

```bash
jidr -q device create Phone --image 35 --profile phone-6.1-fhd --agent-owned
jidr -q device start Phone --timeout 300    # waits for boot, prints the line with the adb serial
```

- `--image` takes `35`, `35:google_apis`, `35:google_apis_playstore` or a full `system-images;…` package.
- `--agent-owned` marks the device as yours, so you (or the MCP server) may delete it later (D5).
- Installing a new image downloads 1–2 GB and needs the user to accept Google's SDK license. Ask before `jidr image install`, and never pass `--accept-licenses` for them.

## Let the user watch

The daemon runs devices headless. To see the screen, the user opens the Jidr app and then the device's player window (on macOS: `open -a Jidr`). Tell them that's where to look.

## Look, act and read logs

```bash
jidr --json call media.screenshot '{"device":"Phone"}'        # result.path is the PNG; read it to see the screen
jidr call sensor.rotate '{"device":"Phone","angle":90}'       # 0, 90, 180 or 270
jidr call key.press '{"device":"Phone","key":"back"}'         # back, home, recents, enter, power, volume_up…
jidr call app.launch '{"device":"Phone","package":"com.example.app"}'
jidr logcat Phone -n 200 --filter ActivityManager:I
jidr logcat Phone --clear
```

`media.screenshot` takes an optional `"path"`; without it the PNG goes to the user's Pictures/Jidr folder. Taps, swipes, text and the UI tree go through `adb -s <serial> shell input …` or the MCP tools; see jidr-app-testing.

Other protocol commands work the same way through `jidr call`: `network.set`, `gps.set`, `battery.set`, `clipboard.set`, `media.record` / `media.record_stop` and more. `jidr commands` lists them all. A call with a missing param fails with `missing field <name>`, which tells you what to add.

## Snapshots, stop and clean up

```bash
jidr snapshot save Phone before-login
jidr snapshot load Phone before-login
jidr snapshot list Phone
jidr device stop Phone                       # saves the quick-boot state
jidr device delete Phone --yes               # only a device you created
```

## MCP instead of the CLI

If the Jidr MCP server is connected (Claude Code: `claude mcp add jidr -- jidr mcp`), its tools do the same: `command_run` runs any protocol command (`device.create`, `device.start`…), and `screenshot`, `tap`, `swipe`, `type_text`, `press_key`, `ui_dump` and `logcat_tail` drive a device directly. `screenshot` returns the image itself, so you don't need to read a file. Devices created through `command_run device.create` are agent-owned automatically.

## Exit codes (with `--json`)

0 ok · 1 unexpected · 2 usage (bad params, missing `--yes`) · 3 not found or not running (start it) · 4 busy (another job holds the device) · 5 boot timeout · 6 SDK, download or license · 7 root failed · 8 stale daemon (rerun with `--restart-stale`).

## Don't

- Don't delete, reset or wipe a device you didn't create in this session (`device delete`, `device reset`, `app.uninstall`, `snapshot delete`) without asking. Devices you created are yours to clean up; say what you removed.
- Don't stop a device the user is using or watching. Leave the user's devices as you found them.
- Don't change the root mode of the user's devices: `jidr root set` cold-boots them.
- Don't create Jidr devices with Android Studio's tools or in its AVD folder. Jidr keeps its own SDK and devices and only reads Android Studio's.

`xtask/src/license_check.rs`:

```rs
//! Split-licensing guard (D18).
//!
//! Only `jidr-ui` and `jidr-gui` are GPLv3. Every other workspace crate is
//! Apache-2.0 and must never link Slint (GPLv3) or the GPL crates, through
//! normal or build dependencies. Dev-dependencies don't ship, so they're ignored.

use std::collections::{BTreeSet, HashMap, VecDeque};

use anyhow::{Context, Result, bail};
use serde::Deserialize;

/// Workspace crates licensed GPL-3.0-only (they link Slint, D18).
pub const GPL_CRATES: &[&str] = &["jidr-ui", "jidr-gui"];
const GPL_LICENSE: &str = "GPL-3.0-only";
const APACHE_LICENSE: &str = "Apache-2.0";

/// The subset of `cargo metadata --format-version 1` we need.
#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
pub struct Metadata {
    pub packages: Vec<Package>,
    pub workspace_members: Vec<String>,
    pub resolve: Option<Resolve>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
pub struct Package {
    pub id: String,
    pub name: String,
    pub license: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
pub struct Resolve {
    pub nodes: Vec<Node>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
pub struct Node {
    pub id: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub deps: Vec<NodeDep>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
pub struct NodeDep {
    pub pkg: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub dep_kinds: Vec<DepKind>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
pub struct DepKind {
    /// `null` = normal, `"build"`, or `"dev"`.
    pub kind: Option<String>,
}

impl NodeDep {
    fn ships(&self) -> bool {
        // Old cargo versions omit dep_kinds; treat that as a normal dependency.
        self.dep_kinds.is_empty()
            || self
                .dep_kinds
                .iter()
                .any(|k| k.kind.as_deref() != Some("dev"))
    }
}

fn is_gpl_package(name: &str) -> bool {
    name == "slint" || name.starts_with("i-slint-") || GPL_CRATES.contains(&name)
}

/// Returns every violation found; an empty list means the check passed.
pub fn violations(meta: &Metadata) -> Result<Vec<String>> {
    let resolve = meta
        .resolve
        .as_ref()
        .context("cargo metadata has no resolve graph")?;
    let names: HashMap<&str, &Package> = meta.packages.iter().map(|p| (p.id.as_str(), p)).collect();
    let edges: HashMap<&str, Vec<&str>> = resolve
        .nodes
        .iter()
        .map(|n| {
            let deps = n
                .deps
                .iter()
                .filter(|d| d.ships())
                .map(|d| d.pkg.as_str())
                .collect();
            (n.id.as_str(), deps)
        })
        .collect();

    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for member in &meta.workspace_members {
        let pkg = names
            .get(member.as_str())
            .with_context(|| format!("workspace member {member} missing from packages"))?;
        let gpl = GPL_CRATES.contains(&pkg.name.as_str());
        let want = if gpl { GPL_LICENSE } else { APACHE_LICENSE };
        if pkg.license.as_deref() != Some(want) {
            out.push(format!(
                "{}: license is {:?}, expected {want:?} (D18)",
                pkg.name, pkg.license
            ));
        }
        if gpl {
            continue;
        }
        // BFS over shipped dependencies, remembering the path for the report.
        let mut seen = BTreeSet::new();
        let mut queue = VecDeque::from([(member.as_str(), vec![pkg.name.clone()])]);
        while let Some((id, path)) = queue.pop_front() {
            for dep in edges.get(id).into_iter().flatten() {
                if !seen.insert(*dep) {
                    continue;
                }
                let Some(dep_pkg) = names.get(dep) else {
                    continue;
                };
                let mut next = path.clone();
                next.push(dep_pkg.name.clone());
                if is_gpl_package(&dep_pkg.name) {
                    out.push(format!(
                        "{}: Apache-2.0 crate depends on GPL crate `{}` via {}",
                        pkg.name,
                        dep_pkg.name,
                        next.join(" -> ")
                    ));
                } else {
                    queue.push_back((dep, next));
                }
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// Runs `cargo metadata` on the workspace and fails on any violation.
pub fn run() -> Result<()> {
    let output = std::process::Command::new(crate::cargo())
        .args(["metadata", "--format-version", "1", "--locked"])
        .current_dir(crate::workspace_root())
        .output()
        .context("running cargo metadata")?;
    if !output.status.success() {
        bail!(
            "cargo metadata failed: {}",
            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
        );
    }
    let meta: Metadata =
        serde_json::from_slice(&output.stdout).context("parsing cargo metadata output")?;
    let found = violations(&meta)?;
    if found.is_empty() {
        println!(
            "license-check: ok ({} workspace crates)",
            meta.workspace_members.len()
        );
        return Ok(());
    }
    for v in &found {
        println!("license-check: {v}");
    }
    bail!("license-check failed with {} violation(s)", found.len())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// Builds metadata for a tiny workspace. `deps` entries are `(from, to, kind)`.
    fn meta(
        members: &[(&str, &str)],
        externals: &[&str],
        deps: &[(&str, &str, Option<&str>)],
    ) -> Metadata {
        let mut packages: Vec<Package> = members
            .iter()
            .map(|(n, l)| Package {
                id: n.to_string(),
                name: n.to_string(),
                license: Some(l.to_string()),
            })
            .collect();
        packages.extend(externals.iter().map(|n| Package {
            id: n.to_string(),
            name: n.to_string(),
            license: Some("MIT".into()),
        }));
        let nodes = packages
            .iter()
            .map(|p| Node {
                id: p.id.clone(),
                deps: deps
                    .iter()
                    .filter(|(from, _, _)| *from == p.id)
                    .map(|(_, to, kind)| NodeDep {
                        pkg: to.to_string(),
                        dep_kinds: vec![DepKind {
                            kind: kind.map(str::to_string),
                        }],
                    })
                    .collect(),
            })
            .collect();
        Metadata {
            workspace_members: members.iter().map(|(n, _)| n.to_string()).collect(),
            packages,
            resolve: Some(Resolve { nodes }),
        }
    }

    const BASE: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
        ("jidr", "Apache-2.0"),
        ("jidr-client", "Apache-2.0"),
        ("jidr-ui", "GPL-3.0-only"),
        ("jidr-gui", "GPL-3.0-only"),
    ];

    #[test]
    fn clean_workspace_passes() {
        let m = meta(
            BASE,
            &["slint", "serde"],
            &[
                ("jidr", "jidr-client", None),
                ("jidr-client", "serde", None),
                ("jidr-gui", "jidr-ui", None),
                ("jidr-ui", "slint", None),
                ("jidr-ui", "jidr-client", None),
            ],
        );
        assert_eq!(violations(&m).unwrap(), Vec::<String>::new());
    }

    #[test]
    fn slint_added_to_cli_fails() {
        let m = meta(BASE, &["slint"], &[("jidr", "slint", None)]);
        let v = violations(&m).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(v.len(), 1, "{v:?}");
        assert!(v[0].contains("jidr -> slint"), "{v:?}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn transitive_slint_internals_fail() {
        let m = meta(
            BASE,
            &["helper", "i-slint-core"],
            &[
                ("jidr-client", "helper", None),
                ("helper", "i-slint-core", Some("build")),
            ],
        );
        let v = violations(&m).unwrap();
        assert!(
            v.iter()
                .any(|s| s.contains("jidr-client -> helper -> i-slint-core")),
            "{v:?}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn apache_crate_depending_on_gui_crate_fails() {
        let m = meta(BASE, &[], &[("jidr", "jidr-ui", None)]);
        let v = violations(&m).unwrap();
        assert!(v.iter().any(|s| s.contains("GPL crate `jidr-ui`")), "{v:?}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn dev_dependency_on_slint_is_allowed() {
        let m = meta(BASE, &["slint"], &[("jidr", "slint", Some("dev"))]);
        assert!(violations(&m).unwrap().is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn wrong_license_field_fails() {
        let m = meta(&[("jidr", "MIT"), ("jidr-ui", "Apache-2.0")], &[], &[]);
        let v = violations(&m).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(v.len(), 2, "{v:?}");
    }

    /// The real workspace must pass.
    #[test]
    fn current_workspace_passes() {
        run().unwrap();
    }
}

`xtask/src/main.rs`:

```rs
//! `cargo xtask <task>`: build automation for the Jidr workspace.

mod license_check;
mod release;
mod skills;

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::process::{Command, ExitCode};

use anyhow::{Context, Result, bail};

const USAGE: &str = "\
usage: cargo xtask <task>

tasks:
  ci              fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, nextest, license-check, skills-check
  license-check   fail if an Apache-2.0 crate links Slint or the GPL GUI crates (D18)
  skills-check    check skills/*/SKILL.md frontmatter and their `jidr` commands (D43)
  e2e-mac         full arm64 end-to-end gate on Apple Silicon (release gate, D28)
  release         build the macOS release artifacts (Phase 12a)";

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect();
    let result = match args.first().map(String::as_str) {
        Some("ci") => ci(),
        Some("license-check") => license_check::run(),
        Some("skills-check") => skills::run(),
        Some("e2e-mac") => e2e_mac(),
        Some("release") => release::run(&args[1..]),
        Some("-h" | "--help" | "help") => {
            println!("{USAGE}");
            Ok(())
        }
        _ => {
            println!("{USAGE}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    match result {
        Ok(()) => ExitCode::SUCCESS,
        Err(e) => {
            println!("xtask: error: {e:#}");
            ExitCode::FAILURE
        }
    }
}

/// The cargo binary that invoked us (respects rustup overrides).
pub(crate) fn cargo() -> String {
    std::env::var("CARGO").unwrap_or_else(|_| "cargo".into())
}

pub(crate) fn workspace_root() -> PathBuf {
    Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))
        .parent()
        .map(Path::to_path_buf)
        .unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from("."))
}

/// Runs a command in the workspace root and fails if it exits non-zero.
pub(crate) fn run(program: &str, args: &[&str]) -> Result<()> {
    println!("xtask: $ {program} {}", args.join(" "));
    let status = Command::new(program)
        .args(args)
        .current_dir(workspace_root())
        .status()
        .with_context(|| format!("spawning {program}"))?;
    if !status.success() {
        bail!("`{program} {}` failed with {status}", args.join(" "));
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn ci() -> Result<()> {
    let cargo = cargo();
    run(&cargo, &["fmt", "--all", "--check"])?;
    run(
        &cargo,
        &[
            "clippy",
            "--workspace",
            "--all-targets",
            "--all-features",
            "--locked",
            "--",
            "-D",
            "warnings",
        ],
    )?;
    run(
        &cargo,
        &[
            "nextest",
            "run",
            "--workspace",
            "--locked",
            "--no-tests=pass",
        ],
    )?;
    license_check::run()?;
    skills::run()?;
    println!("xtask: ci ok");
    Ok(())
}

/// Release gate on an Apple Silicon Mac: every emulator test on arm64 images, then the
/// end-to-end scripts. Missing scripts fail the gate.
fn e2e_mac() -> Result<()> {
    if !(cfg!(target_os = "macos") && cfg!(target_arch = "aarch64")) {
        bail!("e2e-mac runs only on Apple Silicon macOS");
    }
    let cargo = cargo();
    run(
        &cargo,
        &[
            "nextest",
            "run",
            "--workspace",
            "--features",
            "emulator",
            "--no-tests=pass",
        ],
    )?;
    for script in [
        "scripts/e2e-cli.sh",
        "scripts/e2e-root.sh",
        "scripts/e2e-studio-untouched.sh",
    ] {
        if !workspace_root().join(script).exists() {
            bail!("{script} is missing");
        }
        run("bash", &[script])?;
    }
    println!("xtask: e2e-mac ok");
    Ok(())
}

`xtask/src/release.rs`:

```rs
//! `cargo xtask release`: the macOS release artifacts (Phases 12a and 12b).
//!
//! Builds `jidr` and `jidr-gui` in release mode, assembles `Jidr.app`, packs
//! `Jidr-<version>-arm64.dmg`, mounts it to prove it opens, packs the MCP
//! bundle `jidr-mcp-<version>-darwin-arm64.mcpb` (the signed `jidr` plus
//! `packaging/mcp/manifest.json`) and writes `SHA256SUMS.txt`. With `--scan` it fails if the bundle or the DMG contains
//! anything Jidr must never ship: Google SDK binaries, system images or
//! Magisk (NOTICE, clean-room rules).
//!
//! Only system tools are used (`codesign`, `hdiutil`, `plutil`, `shasum`,
//! `notarytool`), so xtask needs no new dependencies. With
//! `JIDR_SIGNING_IDENTITY` set, the app gets a hardened-runtime Developer ID
//! signature and the DMG is signed, notarized and stapled by
//! `packaging/macos/sign.sh` (which also needs an App Store Connect API key:
//! `NOTARY_KEY_PATH`, `NOTARY_KEY_ID`, `NOTARY_ISSUER_ID`). Without it, or with
//! `--dry-run`, the build is ad-hoc
//! signed and CI gets a warning (D32).

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::process::Command;

use anyhow::{Context, Result, bail};

use crate::{cargo, workspace_root};

const USAGE: &str = "\
usage: cargo xtask release [--dry-run] [--scan] [--out <dir>]

  --dry-run   build and package locally; never sign, even if secrets exist
  --scan      fail if the artifacts contain Google SDK binaries, system images or Magisk
  --out DIR   output directory (default: <target>/release-artifacts)";

/// Env var with the Developer ID identity, e.g.
/// `Developer ID Application: Name (TEAMID)` (Phase 12b).
const SIGNING_IDENTITY_ENV: &str = "JIDR_SIGNING_IDENTITY";

#[derive(Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
struct Options {
    dry_run: bool,
    scan: bool,
    out: Option<PathBuf>,
    help: bool,
}

fn parse_args(args: &[String]) -> Result<Options> {
    let mut opts = Options::default();
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(arg) = it.next() {
        match arg.as_str() {
            "--dry-run" => opts.dry_run = true,
            "--scan" => opts.scan = true,
            "--out" => {
                let dir = it.next().context("--out needs a directory")?;
                opts.out = Some(PathBuf::from(dir));
            }
            "-h" | "--help" => opts.help = true,
            other => bail!("unknown argument `{other}`\n{USAGE}"),
        }
    }
    Ok(opts)
}

pub fn run(args: &[String]) -> Result<()> {
    let opts = parse_args(args)?;
    if opts.help {
        println!("{USAGE}");
        return Ok(());
    }
    if !cfg!(target_os = "macos") {
        bail!("release builds the macOS app and DMG; run it on macOS (D15)");
    }
    let root = workspace_root();
    let version = workspace_version()?;
    let target = target_dir(&root);
    let out = opts
        .out
        .clone()
        .map(|o| if o.is_absolute() { o } else { root.join(o) })
        .unwrap_or_else(|| target.join("release-artifacts"));
    println!("xtask: release {version} → {}", out.display());

    crate::run(
        &cargo(),
        &[
            "build",
            "--release",
            "--locked",
            "-p",
            "jidr",
            "-p",
            "jidr-gui",
        ],
    )?;
    let bin = target.join("release");

    if out.exists() {
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&out).with_context(|| format!("clearing {}", out.display()))?;
    }
    let staging = out.join("staging");
    let app = staging.join("Jidr.app");
    assemble_app(&root, &bin, &app, &version)?;
    let identity = std::env::var(SIGNING_IDENTITY_ENV).ok();
    let signing = signing_mode(identity.as_deref(), opts.dry_run);
    let sign_script = root.join("packaging/macos/sign.sh");
    sign(&app, &signing, &sign_script)?;
    // The bundle reuses the signed CLI; the DMG's notarization covers it.
    let mcpb_name = format!("jidr-mcp-{version}-darwin-arm64.mcpb");
    let mcpb_dir = out.join("mcpb");
    pack_mcpb(
        &root,
        &app.join("Contents/Helpers/jidr"),
        &mcpb_dir,
        &out.join(&mcpb_name),
        &version,
    )?;
    std::os::unix::fs::symlink("/Applications", staging.join("Applications"))
        .context("linking /Applications into the DMG")?;

    let dmg_name = format!("Jidr-{version}-arm64.dmg");
    let dmg = out.join(&dmg_name);
    tool(
        "hdiutil",
        &[
            "create",
            "-volname",
            &format!("Jidr {version}"),
            "-srcfolder",
            &path_str(&staging)?,
            "-fs",
            "APFS",
            "-format",
            "UDZO",
            "-ov",
            &path_str(&dmg)?,
        ],
    )?;
    if signing == Signing::DeveloperId {
        // Sign, notarize and staple before the checksum is taken.
        tool("bash", &[&path_str(&sign_script)?, "dmg", &path_str(&dmg)?])?;
    }

    let mut findings = Vec::new();
    if opts.scan {
        findings.extend(scan_tree(&app)?);
        findings.extend(scan_tree(&mcpb_dir)?);
    }
    findings.extend(check_dmg(&dmg, &out.join("mnt"), opts.scan)?);
    std::fs::remove_dir_all(&staging).ok();
    std::fs::remove_dir_all(&mcpb_dir).ok();

    let sums = tool_output("shasum", &["-a", "256", &dmg_name, &mcpb_name], &out)?;
    std::fs::write(out.join("SHA256SUMS.txt"), &sums)?;
    std::fs::write(out.join("VERSION"), format!("{version}\n"))?;
    print!("{sums}");

    if !findings.is_empty() {
        for f in &findings {
            println!("xtask: scan: {}: {}", f.path.display(), f.reason);
        }
        bail!(
            "{} forbidden file(s) in the release artifacts (Google SDK, system images or Magisk)",
            findings.len()
        );
    }
    if opts.scan {
        println!("xtask: scan ok: no Google SDK binaries, system images or Magisk");
    }
    println!("xtask: release ok: {}", dmg.display());
    Ok(())
}

fn path_str(p: &Path) -> Result<String> {
    p.to_str()
        .map(str::to_owned)
        .with_context(|| format!("non-UTF-8 path {}", p.display()))
}

fn target_dir(root: &Path) -> PathBuf {
    match std::env::var_os("CARGO_TARGET_DIR").map(PathBuf::from) {
        Some(dir) if dir.is_absolute() => dir,
        Some(dir) => root.join(dir),
        None => root.join("target"),
    }
}

/// The version of the `jidr` package (the workspace version).
fn workspace_version() -> Result<String> {
    let out = Command::new(cargo())
        .args(["metadata", "--no-deps", "--format-version", "1"])
        .current_dir(workspace_root())
        .output()
        .context("running cargo metadata")?;
    if !out.status.success() {
        bail!("cargo metadata failed");
    }
    let meta: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&out.stdout)?;
    meta["packages"]
        .as_array()
        .and_then(|pkgs| pkgs.iter().find(|p| p["name"] == "jidr"))
        .and_then(|p| p["version"].as_str())
        .map(str::to_owned)
        .context("package `jidr` not found in cargo metadata")
}

fn tool(program: &str, args: &[&str]) -> Result<()> {
    crate::run(program, args)
}

fn tool_output(program: &str, args: &[&str], dir: &Path) -> Result<String> {
    let out = Command::new(program)
        .args(args)
        .current_dir(dir)
        .output()
        .with_context(|| format!("running {program}"))?;
    if !out.status.success() {
        bail!(
            "`{program} {}` failed: {}",
            args.join(" "),
            String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr).trim()
        );
    }
    Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout).into_owned())
}

fn copy(from: &Path, to: &Path) -> Result<()> {
    if let Some(dir) = to.parent() {
        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir)?;
    }
    std::fs::copy(from, to)
        .with_context(|| format!("copying {} to {}", from.display(), to.display()))?;
    Ok(())
}

/// `Jidr.app` layout. The CLI lives in `Helpers/`: `MacOS/jidr` would collide
/// with `MacOS/Jidr` on case-insensitive APFS.
fn assemble_app(root: &Path, bin: &Path, app: &Path, version: &str) -> Result<()> {
    let contents = app.join("Contents");
    copy(&bin.join("jidr-gui"), &contents.join("MacOS/Jidr"))?;
    copy(&bin.join("jidr"), &contents.join("Helpers/jidr"))?;
    copy(
        &root.join("apps/jidr-gui/assets/macos/Jidr.icns"),
        &contents.join("Resources/Jidr.icns"),
    )?;
    for (from, name) in [
        ("LICENSE-APACHE", "LICENSE-APACHE"),
        ("apps/jidr-gui/LICENSE-GPL", "LICENSE-GPL"),
        ("NOTICE", "NOTICE"),
    ] {
        copy(
            &root.join(from),
            &contents.join("Resources/licenses").join(name),
        )?;
    }
    let template = std::fs::read_to_string(root.join("packaging/macos/Info.plist.in"))
        .context("reading packaging/macos/Info.plist.in")?;
    let plist = contents.join("Info.plist");
    std::fs::write(&plist, render_version(&template, version, "Info.plist.in")?)?;
    std::fs::write(contents.join("PkgInfo"), "APPL????")?;
    tool("plutil", &["-lint", &path_str(&plist)?])
}

/// An MCPB bundle (a zip: `manifest.json`, `server/jidr`, icon, licences)
/// for Claude Desktop and the MCP registries.
fn pack_mcpb(root: &Path, jidr: &Path, dir: &Path, mcpb: &Path, version: &str) -> Result<()> {
    copy(jidr, &dir.join("server/jidr"))?;
    for (from, name) in [
        ("assets/brand/app-icon-512.png", "icon.png"),
        ("LICENSE-APACHE", "LICENSE-APACHE"),
        ("NOTICE", "NOTICE"),
    ] {
        copy(&root.join(from), &dir.join(name))?;
    }
    let template = std::fs::read_to_string(root.join("packaging/mcp/manifest.json"))
        .context("reading packaging/mcp/manifest.json")?;
    let manifest = render_version(&template, version, "manifest.json")?;
    serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&manifest).context("manifest.json is not JSON")?;
    std::fs::write(dir.join("manifest.json"), manifest)?;
    tool_output("zip", &["-X", "-r", "-q", &path_str(mcpb)?, "."], dir)?;
    Ok(())
}

/// Fills `@VERSION@` in a packaging template.
fn render_version(template: &str, version: &str, file: &str) -> Result<String> {
    if !template.contains("@VERSION@") {
        bail!("{file} has no @VERSION@ placeholder");
    }
    if version.is_empty()
        || !version
            .chars()
            .all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '.' || c == '-')
    {
        bail!("invalid version `{version}`");
    }
    Ok(template.replace("@VERSION@", version))
}

/// How the release is signed.
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
enum Signing {
    /// Hardened runtime with the Developer ID identity, then notarization.
    DeveloperId,
    /// Ad-hoc only, with the reason shown as a warning.
    AdHoc(&'static str),
}

fn signing_mode(identity: Option<&str>, dry_run: bool) -> Signing {
    match (identity.filter(|s| !s.is_empty()), dry_run) {
        (_, true) => Signing::AdHoc("dry run: the app is ad-hoc signed only"),
        (Some(_), false) => Signing::DeveloperId,
        (None, false) => Signing::AdHoc(
            "Apple Developer ID secrets are missing; this release is unsigned (ad-hoc). Users open it from System Settings › Privacy & Security › Open Anyway (D32)",
        ),
    }
}

/// Signs the app inside-out: with the Developer ID through `sign.sh`, or
/// ad-hoc.
fn sign(app: &Path, signing: &Signing, sign_script: &Path) -> Result<()> {
    let message = match signing {
        Signing::DeveloperId => {
            return tool("bash", &[&path_str(sign_script)?, "app", &path_str(app)?]);
        }
        Signing::AdHoc(message) => message,
    };
    if std::env::var_os("GITHUB_ACTIONS").is_some() && !message.starts_with("dry run") {
        println!("::warning::{message}");
    } else {
        println!("xtask: warning: {message}");
    }
    for path in [app.join("Contents/Helpers/jidr"), app.to_path_buf()] {
        tool(
            "codesign",
            &[
                "--force",
                "--sign",
                "-",
                "--timestamp=none",
                &path_str(&path)?,
            ],
        )?;
    }
    tool("codesign", &["--verify", "--strict", &path_str(app)?])
}

/// Mounts the DMG read-only, checks the app is there, scans it if asked, and
/// always detaches.
fn check_dmg(dmg: &Path, mountpoint: &Path, scan: bool) -> Result<Vec<Finding>> {
    std::fs::create_dir_all(mountpoint)?;
    tool(
        "hdiutil",
        &[
            "attach",
            "-readonly",
            "-nobrowse",
            "-noautoopen",
            "-mountpoint",
            &path_str(mountpoint)?,
            &path_str(dmg)?,
        ],
    )?;
    let result = (|| {
        if !mountpoint.join("Jidr.app/Contents/MacOS/Jidr").is_file() {
            bail!("the mounted DMG has no Jidr.app");
        }
        if scan {
            scan_tree(mountpoint)
        } else {
            Ok(Vec::new())
        }
    })();
    let detached = tool("hdiutil", &["detach", &path_str(mountpoint)?]);
    let findings = result?;
    detached?;
    std::fs::remove_dir(mountpoint).ok();
    Ok(findings)
}

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
struct Finding {
    path: PathBuf,
    reason: &'static str,
}

/// Walks `root` without following symlinks and classifies every file.
fn scan_tree(root: &Path) -> Result<Vec<Finding>> {
    let mut findings = Vec::new();
    let mut stack = vec![root.to_path_buf()];
    while let Some(dir) = stack.pop() {
        for entry in
            std::fs::read_dir(&dir).with_context(|| format!("reading {}", dir.display()))?
        {
            let entry = entry?;
            let path = entry.path();
            let meta = std::fs::symlink_metadata(&path)?;
            let name = entry.file_name().to_string_lossy().to_lowercase();
            if meta.is_dir() {
                if let Some(reason) = classify_name(&name) {
                    findings.push(Finding {
                        path: path.clone(),
                        reason,
                    });
                }
                stack.push(path);
            } else if meta.is_file() {
                let reason = classify_name(&name).or_else(|| {
                    read_head(&path)
                        .ok()
                        .and_then(|head| classify_content(&head))
                });
                if let Some(reason) = reason {
                    findings.push(Finding { path, reason });
                }
            }
        }
    }
    findings.sort_by(|a, b| a.path.cmp(&b.path));
    Ok(findings)
}

/// Enough of a file to see its magic numbers and an APK's first entries.
fn read_head(path: &Path) -> std::io::Result<Vec<u8>> {
    use std::io::Read;
    let mut head = Vec::new();
    std::fs::File::open(path)?
        .take(64 * 1024)
        .read_to_end(&mut head)?;
    Ok(head)
}

/// Forbidden by file name (lowercased).
fn classify_name(name: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
    const SDK_TOOLS: &[&str] = &[
        "emulator",
        "emulator-check",
        "adb",
        "fastboot",
        "sdkmanager",
        "avdmanager",
        "aapt",
        "aapt2",
        "mksdcard",
    ];
    const IMAGE_WORDS: &[&str] = &[
        "system",
        "vendor",
        "ramdisk",
        "userdata",
        "boot",
        "cache",
        "encryptionkey",
        "product",
    ];
    if name.contains("magisk") {
        return Some("Magisk (GPL-3.0, downloaded at runtime, never bundled)");
    }
    if SDK_TOOLS.contains(&name) || name.starts_with("qemu-system") || name.starts_with("libqemu") {
        return Some(
            "Android SDK / emulator binary (downloaded on the user's machine, never bundled)",
        );
    }
    if name.starts_with("kernel-ranchu") || name == "kernel-qemu" {
        return Some("emulator kernel (system image component)");
    }
    if name.ends_with(".img") && IMAGE_WORDS.iter().any(|w| name.contains(w)) {
        return Some("Android system image");
    }
    if name == "source.properties" || name == "package.xml" {
        return Some("Android SDK package metadata");
    }
    None
}

/// Forbidden by content: formats that only Android payloads use. Jidr's own
/// binaries are Mach-O, so any ELF in a macOS bundle is foreign.
fn classify_content(head: &[u8]) -> Option<&'static str> {
    let starts = |magic: &[u8]| head.starts_with(magic);
    if starts(b"\x7fELF") {
        return Some("ELF binary (Android/Linux code has no place in the macOS app)");
    }
    if starts(b"ANDROID!") || starts(b"VNDRBOOT") {
        return Some("Android boot image");
    }
    if starts(&[0x3a, 0xff, 0x26, 0xed]) {
        return Some("Android sparse image");
    }
    if head.get(1080..1082) == Some(&[0x53, 0xef]) {
        return Some("ext4 filesystem image");
    }
    if starts(&[0x02, 0x21, 0x4c, 0x18]) || starts(b"070701") || starts(b"070702") {
        return Some("ramdisk (lz4-legacy or cpio)");
    }
    if starts(b"dex\n") {
        return Some("Android dex bytecode");
    }
    if starts(b"PK\x03\x04") && contains(head, b"AndroidManifest.xml") {
        return Some("Android APK");
    }
    None
}

fn contains(haystack: &[u8], needle: &[u8]) -> bool {
    haystack.windows(needle.len()).any(|w| w == needle)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    #[test]
    fn signing_follows_the_identity_and_dry_run() {
        use super::{Signing, signing_mode};
        assert_eq!(
            signing_mode(Some("Developer ID Application: A (T)"), false),
            Signing::DeveloperId
        );
        assert!(
            matches!(signing_mode(Some("Developer ID Application: A (T)"), true), Signing::AdHoc(m) if m.starts_with("dry run"))
        );
        assert!(matches!(signing_mode(None, false), Signing::AdHoc(m) if m.contains("missing")));
        assert!(matches!(signing_mode(Some(""), false), Signing::AdHoc(_)));
    }

    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn parses_flags() {
        let args = |a: &[&str]| a.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect::<Vec<_>>();
        let o = parse_args(&args(&["--dry-run", "--scan", "--out", "dist"])).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            o,
            Options {
                dry_run: true,
                scan: true,
                out: Some(PathBuf::from("dist")),
                help: false
            }
        );
        assert!(parse_args(&args(&["--out"])).is_err());
        assert!(parse_args(&args(&["--sign"])).is_err());
        assert!(parse_args(&args(&["-h"])).unwrap().help);
    }

    #[test]
    fn forbidden_names() {
        for name in [
            "magisk.apk",
            "magiskinit",
            "libmagisk64.so",
            "emulator",
            "adb",
            "qemu-system-aarch64-headless",
            "kernel-ranchu",
            "system.img",
            "ramdisk.img",
            "userdata-qemu.img",
            "source.properties",
        ] {
            assert!(classify_name(name).is_some(), "{name}");
        }
        for name in [
            "jidr",
            "jidr.icns",
            "info.plist",
            "license-gpl",
            "notice",
            "disk.img",
        ] {
            assert_eq!(classify_name(name), None, "{name}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn forbidden_content() {
        assert!(classify_content(b"\x7fELF\x02\x01\x01").is_some());
        assert!(classify_content(b"ANDROID!....").is_some());
        assert!(classify_content(&[0x3a, 0xff, 0x26, 0xed, 0, 0]).is_some());
        assert!(classify_content(&[0x02, 0x21, 0x4c, 0x18, 1, 2, 3, 4]).is_some());
        assert!(classify_content(b"070701000493e0").is_some());
        assert!(classify_content(b"dex\n035\0").is_some());
        let mut ext4 = vec![0u8; 2048];
        ext4[1080] = 0x53;
        ext4[1081] = 0xef;
        assert!(classify_content(&ext4).is_some());
        let mut apk = b"PK\x03\x04".to_vec();
        apk.extend_from_slice(b"....AndroidManifest.xml....");
        assert!(classify_content(&apk).is_some());
        // Ours: Mach-O (arm64), a plain zip, plists, text.
        assert_eq!(
            classify_content(&[0xcf, 0xfa, 0xed, 0xfe, 0x0c, 0, 0, 1]),
            None
        );
        assert_eq!(classify_content(b"PK\x03\x04plain.txt"), None);
        assert_eq!(classify_content(b"<?xml version"), None);
        assert_eq!(classify_content(b""), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn scan_finds_planted_payloads_and_ignores_symlinks() {
        let tmp = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("jidr-scan-{}", std::process::id()));
        let app = tmp.join("Jidr.app/Contents");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(app.join("MacOS")).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(app.join("MacOS/Jidr"), [0xcf, 0xfa, 0xed, 0xfe]).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(app.join("Info.plist"), "<?xml").unwrap();
        assert!(scan_tree(&tmp).unwrap().is_empty());

        std::fs::create_dir_all(app.join("Resources/sdk/platform-tools")).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(app.join("Resources/sdk/platform-tools/adb"), b"x").unwrap();
        std::fs::write(app.join("Resources/payload.bin"), b"\x7fELF\x02").unwrap();
        std::os::unix::fs::symlink("/Applications", tmp.join("Applications")).unwrap();
        let found = scan_tree(&tmp).unwrap();
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&tmp).unwrap();
        let names: Vec<_> = found
            .iter()
            .map(|f| f.path.file_name().unwrap().to_string_lossy().into_owned())
            .collect();
        // Sorted by path; the /Applications symlink is not followed or flagged.
        assert_eq!(names, ["payload.bin", "adb"]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn templates_get_the_version() {
        let p = render_version("<string>@VERSION@</string>", "0.1.0", "t").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(p, "<string>0.1.0</string>");
        assert!(render_version("<string/>", "0.1.0", "t").is_err());
        assert!(render_version("@VERSION@", "0.1.0<x>", "t").is_err());
        let manifest = include_str!("../../packaging/mcp/manifest.json");
        assert!(render_version(manifest, "0.1.0", "manifest.json").is_ok());
    }
}

`xtask/src/skills.rs`:

```rs
//! Agent skills check (D43).
//!
//! Every `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` starts with YAML frontmatter: a `name` equal
//! to its folder and a `description` (at most 1024 characters) saying when to
//! use the skill. Every `jidr …` command in a fenced shell block must parse
//! against the real CLI, and every `jidr call <method>` must name a command in
//! the protocol reference, so a renamed subcommand, flag or method fails CI.

use std::collections::BTreeSet;

use anyhow::{Context, Result, bail};
use clap::Parser;
use clap::error::ErrorKind;

use crate::workspace_root;

/// The CLI's clap definition, compiled in as-is. Only `Cli::try_parse_from` is
/// used here; the parsed fields are read by the `jidr` binary itself.
#[allow(dead_code)]
#[path = "../../apps/jidr/src/cli.rs"]
mod cli;

const MAX_DESCRIPTION: usize = 1024;
const MAX_NAME: usize = 64;
const SHELL_FENCES: &[&str] = &["bash", "sh", "shell", "zsh"];

pub fn run() -> Result<()> {
    let root = workspace_root();
    let methods = protocol_methods(
        &std::fs::read_to_string(root.join("docs/control-protocol.md"))
            .context("reading docs/control-protocol.md")?,
    );
    let dir = root.join("skills");
    let mut entries: Vec<_> = std::fs::read_dir(&dir)
        .with_context(|| format!("reading {}", dir.display()))?
        .collect::<std::io::Result<_>>()?;
    entries.sort_by_key(|e| e.file_name());

    let mut problems = Vec::new();
    let mut checked = 0;
    for entry in entries {
        if !entry.file_type()?.is_dir() {
            continue;
        }
        let folder = entry.file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
        let path = entry.path().join("SKILL.md");
        let text = match std::fs::read_to_string(&path) {
            Ok(t) => t,
            Err(e) => {
                problems.push(format!("skills/{folder}/SKILL.md: {e}"));
                continue;
            }
        };
        problems.extend(
            check_skill(&folder, &text, &methods)
                .into_iter()
                .map(|p| format!("skills/{folder}/SKILL.md: {p}")),
        );
        checked += 1;
    }
    if checked == 0 {
        bail!("no skills found in {}", dir.display());
    }
    if !problems.is_empty() {
        for p in &problems {
            println!("xtask: {p}");
        }
        bail!("{} skills problem(s)", problems.len());
    }
    println!("xtask: skills-check ok ({checked} skills)");
    Ok(())
}

/// Every problem in one SKILL.md, with line numbers where they apply.
pub fn check_skill(folder: &str, text: &str, methods: &BTreeSet<String>) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut problems = Vec::new();
    match frontmatter(text) {
        Err(e) => problems.push(e),
        Ok(fm) => {
            match fm.name {
                None => problems.push("frontmatter has no `name`".into()),
                Some(name) if name != folder => {
                    problems.push(format!("name `{name}` must match the folder `{folder}`"))
                }
                Some(name) if !valid_name(&name) => problems.push(format!(
                    "name `{name}` must be 1–{MAX_NAME} lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens"
                )),
                Some(_) => {}
            }
            match fm.description {
                None => problems.push("frontmatter has no `description`".into()),
                Some(d) if d.trim().is_empty() => problems.push("description is empty".into()),
                Some(d) if d.chars().count() > MAX_DESCRIPTION => problems.push(format!(
                    "description is {} characters (max {MAX_DESCRIPTION})",
                    d.chars().count()
                )),
                Some(_) => {}
            }
        }
    }
    for (line, cmd) in jidr_commands(text) {
        if let Err(e) = check_command(&cmd, methods) {
            problems.push(format!("line {line}: `{}`: {e}", cmd.join(" ")));
        }
    }
    problems
}

#[derive(Debug, Default)]
struct Frontmatter {
    name: Option<String>,
    description: Option<String>,
}

/// The `name` and `description` of a `---` delimited frontmatter block. Only
/// single-line `key: value` entries are read (plain, single- or double-quoted).
fn frontmatter(text: &str) -> std::result::Result<Frontmatter, String> {
    let mut lines = text.lines();
    if lines.next().map(str::trim_end) != Some("---") {
        return Err("must start with `---` YAML frontmatter".into());
    }
    let mut fm = Frontmatter::default();
    for line in lines {
        if line.trim_end() == "---" {
            return Ok(fm);
        }
        let Some((key, value)) = line.split_once(':') else {
            continue;
        };
        let value = unquote(value.trim());
        match key.trim() {
            "name" => fm.name = Some(value),
            "description" => {
                if value == ">" || value == "|" || value.starts_with(['>', '|']) {
                    return Err("write `description` on one line".into());
                }
                fm.description = Some(value);
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    Err("frontmatter has no closing `---`".into())
}

fn unquote(v: &str) -> String {
    if v.len() >= 2 && v.starts_with('"') && v.ends_with('"') {
        v[1..v.len() - 1]
            .replace("\\\"", "\"")
            .replace("\\\\", "\\")
    } else if v.len() >= 2 && v.starts_with('\'') && v.ends_with('\'') {
        v[1..v.len() - 1].replace("''", "'")
    } else {
        v.to_string()
    }
}

/// The skills spec's name rule: lowercase alphanumerics and hyphens, no
/// leading, trailing or double hyphen.
fn valid_name(name: &str) -> bool {
    (1..=MAX_NAME).contains(&name.len())
        && name
            .chars()
            .all(|c| c.is_ascii_lowercase() || c.is_ascii_digit() || c == '-')
        && !name.starts_with('-')
        && !name.ends_with('-')
        && !name.contains("--")
}

/// Every command line in a fenced shell block that runs `jidr`, as words
/// (without the `jidr`), with its 1-based line number. Shell operators split a
/// line into commands; comments and redirections are dropped.
fn jidr_commands(text: &str) -> Vec<(usize, Vec<String>)> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut in_shell = false;
    let mut in_fence = false;
    let mut pending: Option<(usize, String)> = None;
    for (i, line) in text.lines().enumerate() {
        let trimmed = line.trim_start();
        if let Some(lang) = trimmed.strip_prefix("```") {
            if in_fence {
                in_fence = false;
                in_shell = false;
            } else {
                in_fence = true;
                in_shell = SHELL_FENCES.contains(&lang.trim());
            }
            continue;
        }
        if !in_shell {
            continue;
        }
        // Join `\` continuations onto the line they started on.
        let (start, mut joined) = pending.take().unwrap_or((i + 1, String::new()));
        if let Some(head) = line.trim_end().strip_suffix('\\') {
            joined.push_str(head);
            joined.push(' ');
            pending = Some((start, joined));
            continue;
        }
        joined.push_str(line);
        for cmd in commands(&joined) {
            if cmd.first().map(String::as_str) == Some("jidr") {
                out.push((start, cmd[1..].to_vec()));
            }
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Splits a shell line into simple commands of unquoted words. Handles single
/// and double quotes, backslash escapes, `#` comments, `|`, `||`, `&&`, `;`,
/// `&`, `$(`/`)` and drops redirections with their targets. Leading
/// `VAR=value` assignments are skipped.
fn commands(line: &str) -> Vec<Vec<String>> {
    let mut cmds = Vec::new();
    let mut words: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut word = String::new();
    let mut in_word = false;
    let mut skip_next = false;
    let mut chars = line.chars().peekable();

    while let Some(c) = chars.next() {
        match c {
            '\'' => {
                in_word = true;
                for q in chars.by_ref() {
                    if q == '\'' {
                        break;
                    }
                    word.push(q);
                }
            }
            '"' => {
                in_word = true;
                while let Some(q) = chars.next() {
                    match q {
                        '"' => break,
                        '\\' => {
                            if let Some(n) = chars.next() {
                                word.push(n);
                            }
                        }
                        _ => word.push(q),
                    }
                }
            }
            '\\' => {
                in_word = true;
                if let Some(n) = chars.next() {
                    word.push(n);
                }
            }
            '#' if !in_word => break,
            ' ' | '\t' => end_word(&mut word, &mut in_word, &mut words, &mut skip_next),
            '|' | '&' | ';' | '(' | ')' => {
                end_word(&mut word, &mut in_word, &mut words, &mut skip_next);
                if !words.is_empty() {
                    cmds.push(std::mem::take(&mut words));
                }
            }
            '$' if chars.peek() == Some(&'(') => {
                end_word(&mut word, &mut in_word, &mut words, &mut skip_next);
                if !words.is_empty() {
                    cmds.push(std::mem::take(&mut words));
                }
            }
            '>' | '<' => {
                // `2>`, `>>`, `2>&1`: the digit before belongs to the redirection.
                if word.chars().all(|d| d.is_ascii_digit()) {
                    word.clear();
                    in_word = false;
                } else {
                    end_word(&mut word, &mut in_word, &mut words, &mut skip_next);
                }
                while matches!(chars.peek(), Some('>' | '&')) {
                    chars.next();
                }
                if chars.peek().is_some_and(|n| n.is_ascii_digit()) {
                    chars.next();
                } else {
                    skip_next = true;
                }
            }
            _ => {
                in_word = true;
                word.push(c);
            }
        }
    }
    end_word(&mut word, &mut in_word, &mut words, &mut skip_next);
    if !words.is_empty() {
        cmds.push(words);
    }
    cmds
}

/// Ends the current word: pushes it, unless it's a redirection target or a
/// leading `VAR=value` assignment.
fn end_word(word: &mut String, in_word: &mut bool, words: &mut Vec<String>, skip: &mut bool) {
    if *in_word {
        if *skip {
            *skip = false;
        } else if !(words.is_empty() && is_assignment(word)) {
            words.push(word.clone());
        }
        word.clear();
        *in_word = false;
    }
}

fn is_assignment(word: &str) -> bool {
    word.split_once('=').is_some_and(|(k, _)| {
        !k.is_empty()
            && k.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '_')
            && !k.starts_with(|c: char| c.is_ascii_digit())
    })
}

/// Parses `jidr <args>` with the real clap definition; `jidr call <method>`
/// must also name a protocol command.
fn check_command(args: &[String], methods: &BTreeSet<String>) -> std::result::Result<(), String> {
    let argv = std::iter::once("jidr").chain(args.iter().map(String::as_str));
    match cli::Cli::try_parse_from(argv) {
        Ok(parsed) => match parsed.cmd {
            cli::Cmd::Call { method, .. } if !methods.contains(&method) => {
                Err(format!("`{method}` is not a protocol command"))
            }
            _ => Ok(()),
        },
        Err(e) if matches!(e.kind(), ErrorKind::DisplayHelp | ErrorKind::DisplayVersion) => Ok(()),
        Err(e) => Err(e
            .render()
            .to_string()
            .lines()
            .next()
            .unwrap_or("does not parse")
            .trim_start_matches("error: ")
            .to_string()),
    }
}

/// Method names from the `#### \`method\`` headings of the protocol reference.
fn protocol_methods(doc: &str) -> BTreeSet<String> {
    doc.lines()
        .filter_map(|l| l.strip_prefix("#### `")?.strip_suffix('`'))
        .map(str::to_string)
        .collect()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn methods() -> BTreeSet<String> {
        ["device.list", "media.screenshot"]
            .into_iter()
            .map(String::from)
            .collect()
    }

    fn skill(frontmatter: &str, body: &str) -> String {
        format!("---\n{frontmatter}\n---\n\n# Title\n\n{body}")
    }

    const OK_FM: &str = "name: jidr\ndescription: Use when the user wants an Android emulator.";

    #[test]
    fn a_valid_skill_passes() {
        let body = "```bash\njidr device list\njidr --json call media.screenshot '{\"device\":\"Phone\"}'\n```\n";
        assert_eq!(
            check_skill("jidr", &skill(OK_FM, body), &methods()),
            Vec::<String>::new()
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn name_must_match_the_folder() {
        let p = check_skill(
            "jidr",
            &skill("name: jidr-basics\ndescription: x", ""),
            &methods(),
        );
        assert_eq!(p, ["name `jidr-basics` must match the folder `jidr`"]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn name_must_follow_the_spec() {
        let p = check_skill(
            "Jidr_X",
            &skill("name: Jidr_X\ndescription: x", ""),
            &methods(),
        );
        assert!(p[0].contains("lowercase letters"), "{p:?}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn description_is_required() {
        let p = check_skill("jidr", &skill("name: jidr", ""), &methods());
        assert_eq!(p, ["frontmatter has no `description`"]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn description_is_at_most_1024_chars() {
        let fm = format!("name: jidr\ndescription: {}", "a".repeat(1025));
        let p = check_skill("jidr", &skill(&fm, ""), &methods());
        assert_eq!(p, ["description is 1025 characters (max 1024)"]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn frontmatter_is_required() {
        let p = check_skill("jidr", "# Jidr\n", &methods());
        assert_eq!(p, ["must start with `---` YAML frontmatter"]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn quoted_values_are_unquoted() {
        let fm = frontmatter("---\nname: \"jidr\"\ndescription: 'it''s fine'\n---\n").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(fm.name.as_deref(), Some("jidr"));
        assert_eq!(fm.description.as_deref(), Some("it's fine"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_unknown_subcommand_fails() {
        let body = "```bash\njidr device lst\n```\n";
        let p = check_skill("jidr", &skill(OK_FM, body), &methods());
        assert_eq!(p.len(), 1, "{p:?}");
        assert!(p[0].starts_with("line 9: `device lst`:"), "{p:?}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_unknown_flag_fails() {
        let body = "```sh\njidr device start Phone --wait\n```\n";
        assert_eq!(
            check_skill("jidr", &skill(OK_FM, body), &methods()).len(),
            1
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_unknown_protocol_method_fails() {
        let body = "```bash\njidr call media.screenshoot '{}'\n```\n";
        let p = check_skill("jidr", &skill(OK_FM, body), &methods());
        assert!(
            p[0].contains("`media.screenshoot` is not a protocol command"),
            "{p:?}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn non_shell_fences_are_ignored() {
        let body = "```json\njidr nonsense\n```\n\njidr nonsense outside a fence\n";
        assert!(check_skill("jidr", &skill(OK_FM, body), &methods()).is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn commands_split_on_operators_and_drop_comments_and_redirections() {
        let cmds = commands(
            r#"SERIAL=x jidr device list 2>/dev/null | grep "a b" && echo $(jidr profile list) # jidr bogus"#,
        );
        assert_eq!(
            cmds,
            [
                vec!["jidr", "device", "list"],
                vec!["grep", "a b"],
                vec!["echo"],
                vec!["jidr", "profile", "list"],
            ]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn continuation_lines_are_joined() {
        let text = "```bash\njidr device create Phone \\\n  --image 35\n```\n";
        assert_eq!(
            jidr_commands(text),
            [(
                2,
                vec![
                    "device".to_string(),
                    "create".into(),
                    "Phone".into(),
                    "--image".into(),
                    "35".into()
                ]
            )]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn protocol_methods_come_from_level_4_headings() {
        let m = protocol_methods("### `device.*`\n\n#### `device.list`\n\ntext `x.y`\n");
        assert_eq!(m.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(), ["device.list"]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_repo_skills_pass() {
        run().unwrap();
    }
}
